name: Clay
text:
clay to breed a clay bee, you must put a clay block beneath the housing. clay bees are the bedrock of many important bee lines. breed them from industrious and diligent.

[note]breeder's notes:

this bee is an ancestor for a diverse group of species. a lot of them have incompatible biome requirements--especially the humidity. while breeding, you'll find that you have to alter the biome from cycle to cycle. you probably want to just earmark a spot that is normal/damp right now if your only option for handling this is to run around with your breeding setup.

you're probably on your way to more interesting production bees, but don't forget that clay dust can be electrolyzed into some useful stuff![/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "forestry:beeprincessge", "tag": {"genome": {"chromosomes": {"0": {"uid0": "gregtech.bee.speciesclay", "uid1": "gregtech.bee.speciesclay"}}}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (forestry:beeprincessge, metadata 0)"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 25, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:25", "name": "lootbag (bees basic)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21219, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 25, "shard": "1f0d195533db23c1", "recipes": 0}, "label": "lootbag (bees basic)"}}}}

name: Coal
Copper
text:
copper the copper bee is the first of the metal lines. there are too many metal breeding lines to cover here, but by now you should be able to use nei to figure out how to breed more bee types. copper bees require a copper block beneath the bee housing. breed them from majestic and clay.

the copper combs have a strong chance of centrifuging into copper dust, but you'll also see a chemical reactor recipe to use hydrochloric acid to get a 1:1 exchange. you have some bee options for getting chlorine so you should think about a sustained hydrochloric acid production line soon. you'll eventually have to use hydrochloric acid and won't have the centrifuge option for later combs. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "forestry:beeprincessge", "tag": {"genome": {"chromosomes": {"0": {"uid0": "gregtech.bee.speciescopper", "uid1": "gregtech.bee.speciescopper"}}}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (forestry:beeprincessge, metadata 0)"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 25, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:25", "name": "lootbag (bees basic)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21219, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 25, "shard": "1f0d195533db23c1", "recipes": 0}, "label": "lootbag (bees basic)"}}}}

name: Essentia
text:
essentia this bee produces nothing directly but instead sacrifices its lifetime to generate liquid essentia for all your magical needs. to do so, however, it requires an apimancer's drainer beneath its housing.

the speed at which the bee produces essentia is affected by its production speed. you have to right-click the drainer with a filled phial of the desired essentia to lock it to that type.

you can breed them from chaotic and ordered bees.

name: Hateful
text:
hateful you can feel the waves of hate radiating out of her eyes. don't even think about getting close without an apiarist suit. must be bred in the nether. breed them from eldritch and infernal.

[note]breeder's notes: infernal bees are used to make both this species and spiteful, which is next in line from hateful. that means you'll probably start winding up with spitefuls while trying to make this species. since this is a progression to more interesting species, you could say it doesn't matter, but:

1. skipping straight to spiteful means not getting this quest done and then losing your progression.
2. maybe you want to do a smoldering bee, which needs this one.

what we recommend is tucking away any spitefuls you get and just act like that didn't happen until you finish this bee. if the princess starts turning spiteful and you don't want to just start a new one, you'd want to pump it with infernal or eldritch (pick one!) until you've cleaned out the spiteful trait.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "forestry:beeprincessge", "tag": {"genome": {"chromosomes": {"0": {"uid0": "magicbees.specieshateful", "uid1": "magicbees.specieshateful"}}}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (forestry:beeprincessge, metadata 0)"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 26, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:26", "name": "lootbag (bees advanced)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21221, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 26, "shard": "9fa6bf04b41dd27d", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (bees advanced)"}}}}

name: Heroic
text:
heroic this one takes a little luck. you'll have to find steadfast drones in chests classified as dungeon chests. note that doesn't mean the chests have to be in a dungeon! you could find one in the middle of some thaumcraft obsidian pillars right on the surface of the overworld. 

heroic bees have the pleasant effect of causing damage to hostile mobs. breed them from steadfast and valiant.

[note]breeder's notes:

name: Infernal
text:
infernal infernal bees are mundane: you get them from hives, and they have no ancestors.

infernal hives are in the nether, surrounded by nether quartz. avoid large nether quartz blobs in ore chunks. instead, look for little pockets of nether quartz. any ghast-infested, open area will show a few dabs of them. alternately, if you're tunneling around, you'll inevitably bump into some of these small pockets.

zombie pigmen will get mad if they spot you nibbling on their quartz, so consider just breaking away the netherrack around the quartz to see that it's a solid cluster that could surround a hive. if so, you are just one or two mining hammer swings away from a likely infernal hive.

there's another way to get these hives: buy them with coins! ka-ching!

their molten combs are nice for a mundane bee. they centrifuge down to refractory wax, which can be used for fireproof wood and refractory capsules.

[warn]infernal bees have an aggressive trait, so they'll damage entities--namely, you--when you are within their territory. you want an apiarist's suit before you start working with them. alternately, if you set them up in an isolated spot, you can just run real fast. this isn't sustainable for all types of aggressive bees, by the way.[/warn]

[note]breeder's notes: you can run these bees in the overworld if you can find a hot/arid climate. when in doubt, place an apiary and look at what it claims the climate is in the upper right of its gui. even if the bee isn't jubilant, but you can get drones out of them for breeding. then you don't have to run back and forth to the nether to run a cycle with a fussy queen while cross-breeding.

use nether wart to keep them happy, and don't forget some soul sand!

they don't cross breed with other mundane bees into stuff like common and cultivated bees, so you can convert another mundane princess to an infernal princess if you have the drones. just take some care with this. for example, if you try this with an arctic princess, you could wind up with an infernal princess that needs a scorching/arid climate, but also needs snow to pollinate.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "forestry:beeprincessge", "tag": {"genome": {"chromosomes": {"0": {"slot": 0, "uid0": "magicbees.speciesinfernal", "uid1": "magicbees.speciesinfernal"}}}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (forestry:beeprincessge, metadata 0)"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "forestry:beedronege", "tag": {"genome": {"chromosomes": {"0": {"slot": 0, "uid0": "magicbees.speciesinfernal", "uid1": "magicbees.speciesinfernal"}}}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (forestry:beedronege, metadata 0)"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 2, "damage": 25, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:25", "name": "lootbag (bees basic)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21219, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 25, "shard": "1f0d195533db23c1", "recipes": 0}, "label": "lootbag (bees basic)"}}}}

name: Monastic
text:
monastic monastic bees aren't found in hives or bred. instead, you will need to find a beekeeper villager and trade with them for it. there are various ways to make more villagers, so do some research.

[note]trader's notes:

beekeeper villagers spawn in houses that have a fenced back yard with apiaries. if the apiaries are missing, the villager didn't spawn. or, well, a player already came along and looted the apiaries. they might have abducted the beekeeper too. the beekeeper should be wearing an apiarist outfit. their initial trades probably don't have this bee. you will have to work up to this by trading what is available. if they require a princess for a trade, an ignoble one is fine. honorable mention goes to the trade of some logs for an apiary. that's so much easier than having to make them yourself! if trades lock up, one trade of the "rightmost" trade should unlock preceding ones so you can keep trying to get this trade to pop up.

you can make a golden lasso at lv tier and run off with the villager. if you do, prepare a heavily-fortified spot. even single-block-wide walls won't keep all zombies away. consider just keeping the beekeeper in the lasso when you're not using them.

beekeeper's notes:

the base fertility for a monastic bee is 1x. that's really annoying. when each cycle ends, you get a princess and a drone. that's it. you don't get surplus stock for carrying on breeding. if you can't just straight up alter the genome, then you can try to convert an arctic princess (or something else with a high fertility) with monastic drones in a way that gives you a higher fertility.

on the flip side, their long life is useful to try to get into production bees so you don't quickly clog up your bee product inventories with drones.

the "monastic line" of bees have other quirks. they'll take stuff like wheat and bookshelves as pollination sources. they can have some nasty aggression habits. they are long-lived, so you want something that cuts their life cycle for breeding--like an oblivion frame. you will start out here with a bee that likes average temperatures and humidity, but that'll drift to outright hellish and arid (but not the nether!) for descendant species.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "forestry:beedronege", "tag": {"genome": {"chromosomes": {"0": {"uid0": "forestry.speciesmonastic", "uid1": "forestry.speciesmonastic"}}}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (forestry:beedronege, metadata 0)"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 25, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:25", "name": "lootbag (bees basic)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21219, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 25, "shard": "1f0d195533db23c1", "recipes": 0}, "label": "lootbag (bees basic)"}}}}

name: Ocean
text:
ocean the ocean bee is bred from diligent and water in an ocean-type biome. note that this doesn't mean literally an ocean. it is any biome that has the ocean tag. the stock terrain generator does not generate oceans in the overworld, but there are a few biomes that carry the tag.

skipping the overworld, you might have luck trying in a twilight forest lake - you'll know you are in the right biome if you see water creepers!

you can dump the biome data in nei by clicking on the nei options button (the wrench), then the tools button, then the data dumps button, and finally the dump button in the biomes category. this creates a "dumps" directory in the root folder of the modpack with a biome.csv file inside of it. try anything that has ocean tagged to it. you can feed these biomes into a nature's compass and see if there are any nearby.

some examples: shield, tropics, twilight lake, and lush swamp.

if you have trouble locating an appropriate spot, you can also purchase ocean bees from the vending machine. breed them from diligent and water.

name: Peat
text:

name: Salt
text:
salt at this point, you may have noticed that these higher-tier metal combs can't be extracted with a centrifuge. instead, you need to pass them through a chemical reactor with some hydrochloric acid. this will leave you in a pickle. here you are, trying to reach post-scarcity, and now you're limited by chlorine.

speaking of pickles, hydrochloric acid is kind of like a pickle, right? after all, you make both with salt! the salt bee is perfect for this. well, the apatite bee line can get you some salt and also some phosphorus for phosphoric acid, but you have to start on ash bees first. meanwhile, you'll likely take care of the salt bee's pre-requisites on your way through getting all the major ores.

breed them from clay and aluminium bees on top of a block of salt.

they will produce salt combs, borax dust, slag combs, and trace lithium combs. the salt combs will require at least an mv-tier centrifuge, but at least it doesn't require processing with acid in a chemical reactor!

[note]breeder's notes:

there are two challenges with this bee:

1. the 5% chance of mutation. you may consider trying the escritoire minigame to get a boost to this chance. if so, favor aluminium drones because you're probably on your way to the other bees derived from aluminium ancestry, and they all only have a 5% chance anyways. they could all use a little boost.

name: Vis
text:
vis vis bees lead to some of the most powerful bees in the whole pack. they require a node within 75m of the bee housing. make sure the lunar phase matches the requirements. breed them from ethereal and infernal.

[note]astronomer's notes: the waxing and waning phases happen on alternating days. the moon starts its next phase at sunrise and will keep to the same phase all day and all night. you want to prepare the day before, get to bed to start the next day, and immediately get to work. also, congratulations if you just learned that the moon in minecraft has phases!

breeder's notes: just because this bee only mutates around specific lunar phases doesn't mean you can't work on them in other phases. to get the mutations to show up at all, yes, you need correct lunar phases. however, you will need a spare infernal or ethereal princess to get started, and you can prep that any day. also, once the vis species trait shows up in some drones and/or a princess, it's just regular cross-breeding to get a pure princess and pure drone. that can be done any day too.

despite the focus on moon phases, you do not need to breed at night to trigger the mutation.

name: Zinc
text:
zinc zinc makes great early game item pipes when mixed into brass. also, these bees have a small chance of producing gallium combs, which is very useful for players needing to make circuits or smd devices. these bees will require a zinc block. breed them from tin and iron.

zinc combs cannot be centrifuged. you now need to use a chemical reactor with some hydrochloric acid.

[note]breeder's notes:

you probably only bred this as a stepping stone into the other metals. nonetheless, that gallium is no joke! the queen will need to be jubilant for you to get those, so you need to match up its temperature and humidity band exactly. your hud will have a note when you are pointed at the apiary about if it's not jubilant. the default band is just normal/normal so any old plain/prairie kind of place will probably do.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "forestry:beeprincessge", "tag": {"genome": {"chromosomes": {"0": {"uid0": "gregtech.bee.specieszinc", "uid1": "gregtech.bee.specieszinc"}}}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (forestry:beeprincessge, metadata 0)"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 26, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:26", "name": "lootbag (bees advanced)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21221, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 26, "shard": "9fa6bf04b41dd27d", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (bees advanced)"}}}}

name: Advanced Coke Oven
text:
advanced coke oven your power needs quadrupled since the last tier, and it's likely that you're not getting charcoal fast enough. instead of adding even more coke ovens, why not build an upgraded version of them?

the caveat is that you won't keep producing creosote alongside the charcoal from now on. it makes for decent power in the appropriate generators, and you might have already used it to produce lubricant. despite that, you can still get creosote from processing in the next steps of this questline, so you can still get it if you need it. with that out of the way, let's move on to the advanced coke oven (aco).

how is it made? the aco needs a lot more steps than the normal coke ovens, steps centered around nether materials, cooked in the ebf and then cooled down. the cooling part is normally the vacuum freezer's job, as you will see later in progression, but you can't build it yet; because of that, you'll have to use ic2 coolant to finish the bricks used in the aco. once you've crafted all the blocks needed for this, you can put it together and start it up, to see what's different from before.

the speed of this new one is 1 charcoal per second, or the equivalent to 90 coke ovens. the cost of this is the loss of the creosote, and also that it needs fuel to work, making it so approximately 1/16 of your charcoal is lost in this step. fortunately, you can automate it with item pipes, and the enderio conduits make it even simpler. input wood, input charcoal, output charcoal.

name: Alcohols Here
Biodiesel Alternative
text:
biodiesel alternative trees are not the only source of power for the renewable enjoyer. you can continue expanding your wood production, but you can also skip the charcoal business entirely. instead of refining crude oil into diesel, you can produce biodiesel from renewable biological oils.

biodiesel generally provides less energy per bucket than diesel, which is the tradeoff for using renewable resources.

there are several ways to produce the required seed oil or fish oil:

cropsnh: grow high-stat canola or oilberries. canola is generally preferred due to its higher throughput than most other seeds.

regular farming: automate crops such as peanuts or other seed-producing crops to obtain seed oil without using cropsnh.

fishing: catch cod or other fish to obtain fish oil.

another good option is to farm goldfish with cropsnh, which yields at least twice as much oil per extraction operation.

[note]crop stats improve the output of cropsnh plants, making them worthwhile if you choose that route, but they are by no means required. whether you use cropsnh, conventional farming, or automated name: Biological Diesel
Burning the Carbon
text:
burning the carbon if you've automated carbon monoxide, you can now burn it directly for eu in a gas turbine. it does not use the steam turbines that the boilers required, which is a good thing for two reasons: steam turbines are less fuel efficient than their gas or combustion alternatives, and steam in itself needs large pipes to move it, being much less power dense than gases or diesels. additionally, you don't even need boilers at all! you can skip them altogether if you invest in this co route.

you also get ashes from this chemical reaction. they can be used in several ways, take a look! {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 32, "damage": 30674, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.01", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.metaitem.01:30674", "name": "carbon monoxide cell", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.metaitem.01", "icon": 40462, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 30674, "shard": "4cc3b1389df3419e", "recipes": 3}, "label": "carbon monoxide cell"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 4, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:4", "name": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21242, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 4, "shard": "3cff4d8e3920defe", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)"}, "1": {"count": 5, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:coinchemist", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:coinchemist:0", "name": "coin "the chemist 1"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "coinchemist", "icon": 20739, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "365f333292e560a7", "recipes": 1}, "label": "coin "the chemist 1""}}}}

name: CBD Into Steam
text:
cbd into steam there are no more diesel-related upgrades for the cbd. to continue using combustion generators, or the lce, you can only make your setup bigger or upgrade energy hatches. there is, however, a more power-dense fuel that uses cbd in its recipe, but there's a catch: it's a solid fuel, to be used in steam boilers, which gives it advantages and disadvantages.

everything from this quest onwards is about those solid fuels. there are two versions, one with additional inputs over the other, and they both follow the same logic: they need to be converted to steam, which is hard to transport, convert into eu and basically require the ev and iv large steam boilers. however, the combination of these fuels and those boilers is much, much more fuel efficient than before, if you are willing to face the additional challenges in this kind of setup.

how does it generally go? if you already have cbd, you can get power from it by putting it directly in combustion generators. in this line, though, you need to automate fuel binder, add blocks of charcoal, coal or coal coke and then put the super fuel in a titanium or tungstensteel large boiler, where you get superheated steam. after that, you need an hp steam turbine multi, followed by a regular steam turbine multi, and the setup is complete.

if you want to continue, then you'll need at least one titanium large boiler. build one. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, name: Carbon, Chemically
text:
carbon, chemically how does all of this organic stuff produce energy, anyways? you burn it, that's how! the heat from that burning heats up water into steam, and this can make a steam turbine spin, generating rotational energy that can directly be converted into electricity with spinning magnetic fields. pretty neat, right? the wood/charcoal provides the combustible material, and the atmosphere provides the oxygen to keep the fire going. with some chemistry, and gtnh magic, we can use these principles to generate power in an alternative way.

it's pretty much magic, really. carbon monoxide (co) is a valid fuel for gas turbines, and it can be made with charcoal and oxygen. the co has more power than the charcoal used to make it, but the additional oxygen will make this step not worth it if you get it from electrolyzing water or centrifuging air, since the eu needed for those crafts will make this process inefficient. there is, however, a more efficient way to automate oxygen production, but you will need crops for it.

your target is sugar and an mv electrolyzer. this will give you oxygen at almost 1000 eu per bucket. each bucket of co produces 24000 eu, made from one charcoal that produces roughly 16000 eu in steam, and costing 560 eu per craft. the whole process gives around 6000 eu of free power per charcoal, around 30% extra power overall!

to get automated sugar from crops, you want sugar beets. sugar canes do the same thing, but with more eu cost to get the sugar. there are other possible ways but, for now, just get loads of sugar. name: Coal Or Charcoal
text:
coal or charcoal the super fuels are blocks of burnable material, like coal blocks, which they need in their crafting recipe. it doesn't have to be coal, though: you can do coal, charcoal or coal coke, and all of them make the same amount of super fuel. however, the amount of fluid fuel used changes based on which kind of block you used, which poses a problem.

(we will ignore lignite coal, since it is by far the worst option. if you want to use it, dealing with the efficiency problem is up to you.)

the problem is this: the amount of eu you save by choosing charcoal instead of the other two is less than the amount of eu that the additional fuel can make. basically, the most efficient option is coal coke, then coal, then charcoal. the easiest option to automate is certainly charcoal, which means this is a choice between ease of automation and fuel efficiency. even if you use charcoal, you will still get more eu from the final fuel than what you used as input.

coal can be automated too, though! there are many ways to do this, but the most popular way of automating items that aren't renewable by default is usually by using either crops or forestry bees, both of which have their own renewable coal. if you never made progress in either of those, keep in mind that they need time and effort to give you good results, but if you have, then they are great options to make this fuel even more efficiently. naturally, you will then turn it into coal coke with pyrolyse ovens, acos or icos.

stock up on either charcoal or coal coke blocks to continue. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, name: Creosote's Work
text:
creosote's work your old pal, creosote oil, is back in the game! that's right, you can get it automatically from charcoal processing again, as you did with the first coke ovens, and what you can do with it is about the same. the two main purposes it has are power generation and lubricant, which you will want to use in cutting machines, and will also be required in some later multiblocks like the large combustion engine and the multiblock miner. using a brewery, you can add some redstone to quickly convert this oil to lubricant and keep it in stock for whatever machine or craft needs it.

alternatively, you can get a bit of extra power from this. the fuel value per bucket is much lower than the big three, but it still has an interesting use. when the semifluid generators were broken, and the creosote wasn't usable in them, there were setups using two max-size lp railcraft boilers to turn the amount you get from one dt into the eu needed to run it, making that step completely free in terms of power. there were some fine details, such as the steam turbines needing to all be lv for the fuel efficiency, but it'd be easier to use semifluid generators from the start. either way, you can at least remove the eu cost from the dt from the equation, if you wish to. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, text:

name: Distilling Benzene
text:
distilling benzene from wood tar, you can selectively filter out the energetic benzene to use as a power source. this tar is like a fluid equivalent of the charcoal, and it actually has a lot of useful chemicals hidden inside: to separate them, the tar needs to be heated up to a temperature that will cause some of its components to evaporate, but not others. this is fractional distillation, and the singleblock distillery, in this case an mv one, can recover only one of the outputs of such distillation.

there is something that is worth considering, though: benzene is not the only useful chemical that can be gotten from wood tar. in hv, you can get all the outputs at the same time, but right now you can only choose one. other options that you might want are toluene and creosote. the former can be used to make tnt, to do implosion compressor crafts, and the latter is useful to make lubricant, if you ran out of it and are not using coke ovens anymore. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, name: Faster Charcoal
Fermented Biomass
text:
fermented biomass after this biomass leaves the pyro, you can input it straight into a dt and it will be separated into its component parts. this is one of the tallest towers that you can make with fully renewable powergen and, sadly, not all outputs are useful. however, you'll still get a nice bang for your buck, if you manage to not get lost in nei in the middle of all this chemistry.

the following quests will explain some important uses for the outputs of this dt recipe. first, however, you need to get it going, which means you need a lot of fermented biomass and a tall enough tower to process it. there is one caveat that you might run into as you try to speed up your machines, which is that saplings don't come fast enough! you can work around this by throwing more plant stuff into the compressor, and how you solve this is really up to you and what you have. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 64, "damage": 30691, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.01", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.metaitem.01:30691", "name": "fermented biomass cell", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.metaitem.01", "icon": 40478, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 30691, "shard": "de8b1e4f3581465b", "recipes": 1}, "label": "fermented biomass cell"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"choices": {"0": {"count": 64, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "ic2:itemcellempty", "resolved": {"id": "i:ic2:itemcellempty:0", "name": "empty cell", "mod": "ic2", "registry": "itemcellempty", "icon": 8488, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "e92cf87ab6208ac5", "recipes": 1701}, "label": "empty cell"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 6, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:6", "name": "lootbag (tier 3 hv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21274, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 6, "shard": "4351b75552afb0b2", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 3 hv)"}}, "ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:choice"}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {}}}

name: Fractioned Benzene
text:
fractioned benzene one of the most important steps is to remove the limitation you had when distilling. wood tar turns into benzene? that's not how it should be, there's much more to get from that tar than what you've been extracting from it. to keep the rest, you need more space in the distillation process, or, more specifically, more height. each of the fluids that can be separated from within the tar will stick at a different height level, sitting on top of all the others that are denser than itself.

basically, you need a multiblock, instead of a singleblock. the distillation tower you will need for this recipe has to be at least 6 blocks tall, with 1 input plus 5 outputs. out of it, you will get benzene, toluene and phenol, which are all viable gases for power alongside being very useful for progression (toluene for compressing with tnt and moving past hv, phenol for crafting circuits in the next tier and other chemical lines). you will also get various types of dimethylbenzene. for now the only one of interest is 1,2-dimethylbenzene which is a part of the pbi line in iv. though even that is unfortunately of little use to you right now. you also get creosote for your lubricant needs, or a little extra power. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, name: Free For All Fertilizer
text:
free for all fertilizer you might have heard of the fertilia crop, which can easily automate the fertilizer input for your crops, if you're using them. why bother, though, when you're already getting it from your dt? that's right, you will also be able to automate fertilizing alongside everything else, which is very important for high-statted crops, making all the inputs (energy, water, fertilizer) automated without any outside inputs. pretty neat, huh?

that said, you might not be using crops at all. in that case, you can electrolyze it, and you'll get a lot of free carbon and calcite dust, which you'll certainly use in future chemistry. you can also use the co2 gas from the dt to get carbon, i guess? it's not very useful. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 256, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "cropsnh:fertilizer", "resolved": {"id": "i:cropsnh:fertilizer:0", "name": "fertilizer", "mod": "cropsnh", "registry": "fertilizer", "icon": 20046, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "0bc8b8d4eff17396", "recipes": 144}, "label": "fertilizer"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 4, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "botania:fertilizer", "resolved": {"id": "i:botania:fertilizer:0", "name": "floral fertilizer", "mod": "botania", "registry": "fertilizer", "icon": 3976, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "698f15e3d16fa54f", "recipes": 6}, "label": "floral fertilizer"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 6, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:6", "name": "lootbag (tier 3 hv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21274, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 6, "shard": "4351b75552afb0b2", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 3 hv)"}, "2": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:coinchemistii", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:coinchemistii:0", "name": "coin "the chemist 100"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "coinchemistii", "icon": 20736, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "fb08f66bce752e14", "recipes": 2}, "label": "coin "the chemist 100""}}}}

name: Further Charcoal Distillation
text:
further charcoal distillation the distillation tower you've recently unlocked can bring forth many, many more outputs than what you've done so far. if you look at nei, you might see that there are other charcoal-related fluids that have recipes in this multi, and this is the time to work with them: doing it all in singleblock distilleries would be very wasteful.

the most important part about getting these fluids is the pyrolyse oven. if you haven't made one, it's highly recommended that you make at least one. you can upgrade both the energy hatch and the coils used in it to keep it up to speed with everything else, no need to build more than one. aside from fulfilling the purpose of the coke oven, to cook wood into charcoal, it gives the choice of which of several fluids it also outputs as it does the processing. most of the options are potentially useful, but a complete benzene setup will prefer charcoal byproducts because they are, essentially, the complete product.

attention: this setup is technically hv, but it's quite expensive. it's fine if you move to ev first before you build this. it is in no way required to progress in hv.

with charcoal byproducts, the full setup involves dting that into wood tar, wood vinegar and wood gas, and then dting all of those into their respective outputs. with one tower for each, you will end up with a quad dt setup, very expensive overall in terms of stainless steel, but with huge savings compared to making 4 separate ones. keep in mind, however, that they will not all have the same height. additionally, wood gas is not as valuable as the other two (although it is a decent ethylene source), so it's also a good idea to make 2 of the 4 dts process that, and burn the wood gas for the little power it can provide.

as a final note, the towers do process things slowly. add distilleries, if you wish, to get specific outputs. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, Green Ethenone
Green Nitric Acid
text:
green nitric acid one half of tnm is nitric acid, which has more paths to reach it than can be listed here. it's basically hydrogen, nitrogen and oxygen merged together, and many compounds made from these things can lead you to nitric acid. how you get this is up to you, but it might be a lot easier if you already automated some distillation tower setups for other renewable resources.

let me explain. nitric acid can be made directly from ammonia and oxygen. o2 has many sources, and you should have already automated it, but ammonia is harder to get: you either make it from nitrogen oxide and dioxide, or you skip all that with a fermented biomass dt, which outputs ammonia directly. that is the fastest way, if you already made that setup, otherwise you'll need to chain several name: Huge Turbines And Loose Mode
text:
huge turbines and loose mode if you are invested in making good iv power from super fuel, you will need a lot of turbine multis. their eu/t at optimal flow is much too low for you to survive with only one or two. however, there are several things you should consider in regards to these turbines, and the fuel you're using.

in summary, this fuel is very, very efficient. turbines can be made faster by losing some efficiency. you have more than enough fuel efficiency to spare!

let's review this in more detail. turbines produce eu based on the flow rate of the fuel that they are consuming. their optimal flow represents the highest fuel efficiency they can reach (140% or 150% for the good turbines in these tiers), but you can increase the flow beyond that point and still get a higher eu/t value. however, the fuel becomes less efficient. a good tradeoff, if you need it.

steam loses efficiency quickly if you do this, though. the right way to pull this off with steam turbines is to switch to loose mode, a mode unique to them, which makes the optimal flow shoot way up at a considerable loss to fuel efficiency. the jump in eu/t is so high, however, that you can replace a whole squadron of turbines with just one or two, as you can see if you look at the turbine items' tooltips.

each setup has their own details, so you will have to work things out and make personal decisions about how you will manage the turbines. just make sure to not let the eu/t value go beyond the maximum that the dynamo hatch can output, or you will waste power! {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 16393, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.02", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.metaitem.02:16393", "name": "oriharukon turbine blade", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.metaitem.02", "icon": 43116, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 16393, "shard": "ba117b3ff3045660", "recipes": 4}, "label": "oriharukon turbine blade"}}}}

name: Large Steel Boiler
text:
large steel boiler direct charcoal consumption is also improved, if you want to go that way. the second large boiler is made out of steel, but needs hv circuits, which you can make in this tier by using polyethylene in the circuit boards. it generates steam at a speed equivalent to 1000 eu/t at 100% fuel efficiency for that steam, which you can't reach with the inefficient steam turbines available to you. it also needs two acos, but it skips any further processing, at an additional cost of heavy pollution that you'll have to deal with in some way.

this is the most "spammable" setup you can make. there are no further upgrades to the large boilers that accept these cheap fuels (the next boilers only accept some more complicated ones), but you can wallshare these to increase the energy input into your processing. the biggest problem, as usual, is transporting the steam to prevent big energy losses across long stretches of cable. this is not the best option, but it can be used. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, name: Mass Distilled Water
text:
mass distilled water water is completely free, that much is obvious. distilled water, though? it's the same input, but it needs a machine to process it into this version, and you best not choose singleblock distilleries to do this, because they are incredibly slow and will never keep up with your demands.

the obvious option is a distillation tower. the less obvious option is a steam turbine multi, which outputs distilled water that is supposedly piped back to where the steam is made. however, there are several steam producers that use regular water, so you can try that? the dt is the simplest and most direct option, though. 3-high is the minimum, so you have to build it like that. it doesn't need a lot of power, it will fill up a tank of any size over time since the water input is completely free. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, name: Methane Stinks
text:
methane stinks the output you'll get the most of, in the fermented biomass dt, is methane. 6/10 of the input amount will become methane, and this makes for the best choice for powering your powergen, even if other outputs can also serve as fuel options. it's important to remember that methane is used in several important chemical lines, such as ptfe and silicone rubber, but you'll get much more of it than you need for those purposes.

the methane you get from one dt can power it 4 times. using 1/4 of your power there, you can fuel the singleblock machines you're using, and the wood automation source as well if you feel like it. regardless, this setup should fuel itself just fine. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 64, "damage": 30715, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.01", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.metaitem.01:30715", "name": "methane cell", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.metaitem.01", "icon": 40495, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 30715, "shard": "bdff4a3ef2571b1b", "recipes": 5}, "label": "methane cell"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 92, "oredict": "", "id": "minecraft:spawn_egg", "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (minecraft:spawn_egg, metadata 92)"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 6, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:6", "name": "lootbag (tier 3 hv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21274, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 6, "shard": "4351b75552afb0b2", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 3 hv)"}, "2": {"count": 2, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:coinchemistii", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:coinchemistii:0", "name": "coin "the chemist 100"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "coinchemistii", "icon": 20736, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "fb08f66bce752e14", "recipes": 2}, "label": "coin "the chemist 100""}}}}

name: Nitrobenzene
text:
nitrobenzene with the chemplant finished, you can slap in the necessary hatches and automate this fuel easily. the titanium gate really is the main obstacle to this improvement, since you can more than triple the power your benzene can make with some cheap additions to it!

name: No Benzene Yet
Normal Or Magic
Phenol's Width
text:
phenol's width this one is not as specialized as toluene is. it's also more likely that you will be producing it in a chemical reactor, or working around it with recipes, if you choose not to use oil or benzene for some reason. you're here, though, so you have all of the possibilities, and all of the advantages of skipping through steps in several important chemical lines that accept phenol, one of the first being epoxy resin. if you check nei, you can more easily see where this chemical can come in handy.

it is true, though, that it isn't as required in hv as toluene is. since both of them are good power options alongside benzene, it's preferable that you burn this one for power between the two, if you have to. in the best situation, you won't need to, but it's also acceptable to burn all of the benzene and some phenol, while the toluene gets converted into its gelled form to make several stacks of name: Pyrolyse Oven
text:
pyrolyse oven some setups really demand space in your base to work properly. you might have thought that when you finished the coke oven automation, but there's also an option in this tier that respects that need for speed by just being a gigantic multiblock: the pyrolyse oven.

in essence, it's the original gregtech large-scale wood processor. it is a massive structure, probably bigger than any other multi you've built before, but it uses simple materials like bronze and steel. if you're able to just throw stacks of those at a controller, you can put this behemoth together and enjoy an alternative to the advanced coke oven that has some extra benefits. unlike any of the other ovens, this one runs on eu, so you need to route your power back here to process the wood you're feeding it.

what makes the pyro valuable? it outputs a fluid alongside the charcoal, which you can process for extra power and/or byproducts. look at nei to see all the alternatives available to you, this multi can usually output several different fluids, but only one at a time, decided by the circuit inside it. the one to choose at this time is wood tar, the same fluid you're extracting from the charcoal. you get a small constant bonus from having built a pyro, which is really nice.

however, the pyro uses coils in a similar way to the ebf, and those coils affect the time each recipe takes: if you're using cupronickel coils, the recipe time is actually 2x what nei says! this might be too slow for your needs, so make sure you check how much charcoal you're getting from here. kanthal coils are available in mv, using the ic2 coolant instead of the vacuum freezer.

you can also boost your pyro by providing nitrogen. there are separate recipes for that in nei. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, name: Renewable Energy
Sapling Power
text:
sapling power wood has been a big part of your power generation, and you might have even used other plants or fish for oil. even if that's true, there is a constant output from your trees that has been left unused all this time: the saplings! no matter which tree you chose to automate, you are surely stockpiling the saplings matching that tree, since there's little that is really useful to do with them. at this point, though, you can set up a decent biomass setup.

to clarify, biomass is just a fluid made from plant stuff. it doesn't need to be saplings, but that's most likely something you have a lot of lying around. on top of that, there are multiple types of biomass, one of them called fermented biomass, which is very similar but different, and the recommended path for you to take, since it needs fewer steps than the alternatives and gets you to the dt recipe just fine.

after this processing line is finished, you will have a lot of new chemicals automated that you won't have from wood tar alone. if you are already processing wood vinegar, you will have several repeat outputs, though. that said, if you complete this line, you will get ethanol + methanol and ammonia, which make the cetane-boosted diesel process much easier. all of these lines interact with each other, and you can get bigger and bigger returns if you automate several at once!

for now, focus on putting together the machines needed to get from saplings to fermented biomass. you will need a compressor, a pulverizer and a pyrolyse oven for this route. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 243, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:243", "name": "advanced compressor ii", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 24565, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 243, "shard": "683b02795833d5c2", "recipes": 1}, "label": "advanced compressor ii"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 303, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:303", "name": "universal macerator", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 24768, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 303, "shard": "e6794a29d1f5292a", "recipes": 1}, "label": "universal macerator"}, "2": {"count": 1, "damage": 15546, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:15546", "name": "pyrolyse oven", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 24065, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 15546, "shard": "01c61146c43cccce", "recipes": 2}, "label": "pyrolyse oven"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:optional_retrieval"}, "1": {"index": 1, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Skipped into Ammonia
Sodium Hydroxide
Sourcing Your Wood
text:
sourcing your wood when it comes to power from wood, your only options so far have been the wood itself and charcoal. both of these are low on energy per item, so you will need a lot of wood to have a decent eu/t output. how, then, can you easily get that much? there are two ways: the automated way, and the non-automated way.

the automated way can be done with one of several machines, but in lv you only have one option: the lv crop manager. it can automatically harvest crops in an area around it and, for this situation, the crop you want is one of several bonsais. you can get them by planting saplings on cropsticks (there is a lot more information about how crops work in the forestry and multifarms page), and most types of saplings are equivalent to one another, although not all of them can be planted as crops. the ones that stand out are spruce, which give a bit more wood than the others, and oak, which give apples alongside the usual wood and saplings, possibly useful for some chemistry later.

the non-automated way can be done earlier, and it only requires two things: an unbreakable lumber axe and trees with a lot of wood, like sacred oak, redwood, or rainforest oak. this axe will chop down (most of) the trees and award you with stacks and stacks of wood, much faster than the automated way, but with more work. this process might be useful in the beginning, but you will have to automate the wood input at some point.

complete one of the tasks and get some wood to continue. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, name: Super Fuel And Boiling
The Benzene Tier
text:
the benzene tier having walked into mv, you are soon going to be able to produce and consume benzene. it's more efficient than burning the charcoal in a boiler, but you will still need to provide a lot of wood to make sure you have consistent, abundant power. it's heavily recommended that you automate this wood input, if you haven't already, possibly with an mv crop manager instead of the lv one, or with the crop harvester.

for automation, you're still stuck with using bonsais, not regular trees. hv will provide a few options that don't need crops, but for now you might want to increase your crop stats by crossbreeding. planting saplings on cropsticks creates 1/1/1 bonsais, which are much slower than their high-stat variants. if you want to invest in crops, you can later use the high stats to get more of the several dozen different items that crops can output, but you should start with stickreed to develop your crop stats, not bonsais.

don't throw away your saplings, either! they will be useful later on, so save up as many as you can.

name: The Most Powerful Biodiesel
The Two Alcohols
text:
the two alcohols the other fluid that mixes in with one of the natural oils to create biodiesel can be one of two siblings: methanol and ethanol. they're very similar, both alcohols composed of carbon atoms surrounded by hydrogen ones, with one oh at the end. they often come from the same source (for example, running wood vinegar or biomass through a distillation tower), but they also have some differences. to produce them from simpler elements in a chemical reactor, you'll need mv tier, which is where you are at.

check nei for all the recipes you can use for either of these. you only need one, so choose whichever alcohol you want to produce. the one you're likely going to produce is methanol. {"0": name: Titanium Chemical Plant
text:
titanium chemical plant this is the difficult part in the whole process. the multi in which nitrobenzene is crafted is the exxonmobil chemical plant, also known as the chemplant, and it is a gigantic 7x7x7 structure with 4 separate upgradable parts to it. even worse, the outer structure uses multiblock machine casings, making the dt look cheap by comparison, and the inside needs a lot of the casings used to craft single blocks.

the difference between them is that the tier of the outer structure that you need is mentioned in the recipe you want to craft, and the tier of the inner structure is generally related to the eu/t of the recipe, minus one tier. this is because, like the ebf and the lcr, you can use 2 energy hatches, so this hv recipe can be made with mv energy hatches. since the inner structure's tier decides the max tier of the hatches used in the chemplant, you can make it out of mv machine casings, which use aluminium.

the outer structure will still need many stacks of titanium, so this is where most of your effort will go. good luck.

[note]technically, you could also make nitrobenzene in an lcr instead of a chemplant. but it is less energy efficient and dilutes your acid. that option was only added for those too weak to handle a name: Toluene's Power
Trees Growing Faster
Two Big Ovens
text:
two big ovens with 19 coke ovens automated, you can sustain two big boilers endlessly. the boilers you want to build for this are specifically the low pressure railcraft boilers, made with iron, each one as big as they can be, a 3x4x3 of the boiler tanks. these multiblocks are expensive, but you will have plenty of power and will consume all the creosote from your coke ovens to keep them running permanently.

[note]these boilers have a high pressure variant, for more information look in the multiblocks tab. this setup is not enough to sustain the high pressure boiler but you can add a few more coke ovens to sustain it if you want.[/note]

the same goes for the large bronze boiler, gregtech's own way of improving on your tiny boilers, but with two added problems: you can't produce charcoal fast enough for it, and it has a terrible efficiency for your creosote, which means most of its power will be wasted.

however, surprise! the gt++ semifluid generators work, and they're very efficient with the creosote. you can use a few of those coupled with a large bronze boiler, but you will still run into the issue of not producing charcoal fast enough unless you do something about it. you can choose this as an option and complete this quest, but it's a more "experimental" alternative that is further into name: Wood Tar
text:
wood tar benzene cannot be extracted directly from charcoal. to get to it, you need to process the extracted fluid, called wood tar. in the past, this was a very slow step, which forced players to spam fluid extractors to keep up with the other parts of their benzene line, but it's a lot faster now. regardless, you still need more than one fluid extractor for each machine used in the step after this one, if you are using lv machines here.

name: Carpenter's Blocks
text:
carpenter's blocks yet another custom block system! carpenter's blocks are crafted blank and placed in-world, and then plain block textures applied to them. the blocks must not be tile entities, so botany blocks don't work correctly with them, but gt stones like red granite, and any colored clay or vanilla glass block will work. some chisel glass types will work, and ztones blocks and tinted glass also work.

the garage door requires a block at the top to hang "down" from, but can pretty much be any length. a redstone signal on any block next to the garage door blocks will open or close the door. the open/close will propagate across multiple vertical doors, so you can set up non-square doors. sneaking and right-clicking with an empty hand will change the door's polarity.

the pressure plates are player-only activation, making them great for doors into your base.

the hatches must be clicked on the side of a block to place. they can be handy for protecting you from crucible...byproducts.

there is a lot more block shapes possible, check nei for "carpenter's" to see the options.

the chisel allows you to chisel blocks while attached to a carpenter's block.

the hammer allows various functions.

hammer on door - changes door shape type
sneak hammer on door - changes from iron to wooden behavior
sneak hammer on lever - changes polarity (which direction is on/off) {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, name: Catwalks
text:
catwalks the catwalks mod adds several cosmetic blocks to deck out your factory.

scaffolds and builder's scaffolds are useful for building up in the air before you get access to flight. they can be climbed like ladders, and break instantly when punched. you will also not fall off of them if you let go of movement keys while climbing. if you right-click the builder's scaffold with a solid block, the scaffold will be replaced by that block.

catwalks can connect to each other to form a wide passageway. you can decorate them by attaching caution tape or rope lights, the latter provide dim lighting.

caged ladders give you a way to move up and down without a risk of falling off. climbing them is much faster than vanilla ladders.

support columns are purely decorative. they connect to each other in all directions. they also work as ladders.

sturdy rails let you run minecart tracks across gaps without supports. right-click the sturdy powered rail with a blowtorch to power it permanently, you don't need a redstone torch. if you don't have enough distractions already, use them to build a rollercoaster!

the blowtorch lets you remove railings or even the floor from a catwalk by right-clicking. use it to make an opening to let you walk onto the catwalk, or if you don't know what an "osha violation" is. the same function can be performed by a gt or forge-compatible wrench, so you don't actually need to make this. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, text:

name: Making Sense of Spaghetti
text:
making sense of spaghetti nobody likes an untidy base. why don't you use some color to organize things a little!
the paint brush, painter, and spray cans can be used to color machines, wires, cables, pipes, wool, stained glass, and more!

colored pipes, wires, and cables can only connect to uncolored cables/pipes/wires, or those of the same color.

input buses and hatches can also be colored, and multiblock machines will enforce input separation based on their colors. inputs of the same color can only see each other, and un-colored inputs work with any color. while outbut buses and hatches can be colored as well, doing so will have no effect on where the machine sends outputs.

any painted block can be painted over with another color, but to remove the color entirely you need to break the block while sneaking or use a can of solvent.

the paint brush is the cheapest to make paint for, only requiring one piece of colored dye.
the painter requires distilled water and a chemical bath to create paint for.
the spray can uses chemical dye, which requires an mv chemical reactor to make.
the color applicator uses paint balls and can store all 16 colors at once.

[note]sneaking while using a spray can or paint brush will color an entire line of blocks![/note]

[note]the priority of colored hatches is the same as the order of vanilla dyes in nei, from highest (black) to lowest (white).[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 1, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "buildcraft|core:paintbrush", "resolved": {"id": "i:buildcraft|core:paintbrush:0", "name": "paintbrush", "mod": "buildcraft|core", "registry": "paintbrush", "icon": 4917, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "b246f32bb9072565", "recipes": 2}, "label": "paintbrush"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "ic2:itemtoolpainter", "resolved": {"id": "i:ic2:itemtoolpainter:0", "name": "painter", "mod": "ic2", "registry": "itemtoolpainter", "icon": 8629, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "5f3ff43ba1d68dca", "recipes": 1}, "label": "painter"}, "2": {"count": 1, "damage": 32402, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.01", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.metaitem.01:32402", "name": "empty spray can", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.metaitem.01", "icon": 40855, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 32402, "shard": "3e04f02d12b9d8c4", "recipes": 18}, "label": "empty spray can"}, "3": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "appliedenergistics2:item.toolcolorapplicator", "tag": {}, "resolved": {"id": "i:appliedenergistics2:item.toolcolorapplicator:0", "name": "color applicator - name: Mo' Hammers Mo' Problems
More Like Ouch-i-tect
text:
more like ouch-i-tect the sawbench can turn most full cube blocks into amazing shapes of various kinds.

right-click with the hammer to rotate 90 degrees. shift-right-click with the hammer to change the orientation of the "bottom" face.

the chisel is used to alter the structure of blocks in various ways. some blocks automatically form connections with adjacent blocks. these connections can be disabled and re-enabled by right-clicking with a chisel near the side that you want to change.

some blocks can have a secondary material applied to them. the secondary material can be removed by right-clicking on the center of the block with a chisel.

you can also right-click on a vanilla glass, glass pane, glowstone or ice block with a chisel to harvest the block without breaking it. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "architecturecraft:sawbench", "resolved": {"id": "i:architecturecraft:sawbench:0", "name": "architect's sawbench", "mod": "architecturecraft", "registry": "sawbench", "icon": 1678, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "e5532fad73bd2cda", "recipes": 1}, "label": "architect's sawbench"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "architecturecraft:hammer", "resolved": {"id": "i:architecturecraft:hammer:0", "name": "architect's hammer", "mod": "architecturecraft", "registry": "hammer", "icon": 1676, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "090ef87f2fca08c9", "recipes": 1}, "label": "architect's hammer"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "architecturecraft:chisel", "resolved": {"id": "i:architecturecraft:chisel:0", "name": "architect's chisel", "mod": "architecturecraft", "registry": "chisel", "icon": 1674, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "fd36d48271cb5941", "recipes": 1}, "label": "architect's chisel"}}}}

name: An Offering To The Gods
text:
an offering to the gods another stargate recipe, another trophy. you know the drill by now: submit two legacy stargates' worth of materials and receive one cute little trophy. 

[note]our journey reaches its latest stop, entering the era of refinement.

the year is 2025, and the game has become more refined than ever before. so refined, in fact, that we may have added a little too much quality of life and accidentally earned this stargate the nickname "ez gate." easy is relative, of course; it was still a stargate, after all.

the matter manipulator has transformed base building and infrastructure expansion, allowing entire structures to be planned, copied, and moved, while nei autocrafting has made early progression considerably faster. et futurum has brought netherite and prismarine to the pack alongside their new processing lines. at the end of progression, the t4 nano forge has provided a much needed alternative to endless t3 spam, while the eoh pity system has made its worst streaks of rng more manageable.

automation has continued to improve, and years of accumulated knowledge have transformed problems that once took entire teams months to solve into well-understood production challenges. outside the pack, the community has created countless calculators, planners, visualizers, and specialized programs for automation, base design, optimization, or simply for fun.

the results have been difficult to ignore. more stargates have been completed during this period than in any previous era, with the recorded gate count on discord passing 1,000 before the release of 2.9.

a team composed of some of the pack's most talented and experienced players completed a full stargate run in only 22 days, 16 hours, and 45 minutes on january 26, 2026, setting a new speedrun record. pxx500 and adam achieved the first documented gatelympics (quintuple) gate during that very same speedrun. 

on the solo end of things, the very first singleplayer gtnh: gods (triple) gate was achieved by sintken on july 2, 2025 and the second was achieved shortly after by lordpeverell on july 24, 2025.

p.s.: here's the list as usual:
-matter manipulator
-spinmatron
-large hadron collider
-latex
-nanochip assembly complex
-bose-einstein condensate line
-exo-foundry
-solar factory
-nano forge t4
-eoh pity system
-super stock replenisher[/note]

p.s. in case you were wondering, 2.7 was the last version where you needed to craft two stargates in order to qualify for a completed run. this requirement was brought down to one stargate in 2.8, but for purposes of this quest you will be making the equivalent of two since the recipe didn't change between versions.

name: Fabricating Solar Systems... in Parallel
text:
fabricating solar systems... in parallel as you've noticed, uxv components are extremely expensive compared to the amount of universium you can currently produce.

the astral array fabricator allows you to run eoh recipes in parallel. you can review the math in the second page of the tooltip.

for a direct answer, you can use this spreadsheet: [url]https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ftfdfmy_uwbtbfoynzarkei90pbhvpbh6m3jhjmac-e/edit?usp=sharing[/url]

[warn]be aware that the eoh will use raw stellar plasma instead of hydrogen and helium if you use astral arrays.[/warn]

[note]make sure you are generating enough power.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "tectech:item.tm.itemastralarrayfabricator", "resolved": {"id": "i:tectech:item.tm.itemastralarrayfabricator:0", "name": "astral array fabricator", "mod": "tectech", "registry": "item.tm.itemastralarrayfabricator", "icon": 51547, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "405af8d490dd8869", "recipes": 1}, "label": "astral array fabricator"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: It Gets to a Point
text:
it gets to a point you are not done with wafers. ok well, now you are, kind of.

infinite wafers are the final tier of raw wafer, forged directly in the god forge. who knew silicon could hold up for this long?

yocto power ics are used in magmatter nanites, max circuits, and uxv energy hatches.

[note]you'll need a uxv laser engraver to cut these.

yocto power ics need to be coated in quark gluon plasma in an exo-foundry, overclocked to reach the max voltage required. this step cannot be done in a mass solidifier.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 32276, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.03", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.metaitem.03:32276", "name": "infinite wafer", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.metaitem.03", "icon": 45697, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 32276, "shard": "782cfecd22e90eac", "recipes": 2}, "label": "infinite wafer"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:optional_retrieval"}, "1": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 1, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 32272, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.03", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.metaitem.03:32272", "name": "ypic wafer", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.metaitem.03", "icon": 45694, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 32272, "shard": "b5890fb09ee7ea55", "recipes": 1}, "label": "ypic wafer"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:optional_retrieval"}, "2": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 2, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 2, "damage": 32273, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.03", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.metaitem.03:32273", "name": "yocto power ic", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.metaitem.03", "icon": 45695, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 32273, "shard": "5bd4e6f4e66da0f4", "recipes": 1}, "label": "yocto power ic"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

text:
max circuits planck-scale circuits, the final circuits in the pack... for now. these max circuits are needed for high end uxv parts and the stargate.

[note]you will need your quantum nac to get started

did you know that planck-scale manifolds, despite being classified as a circuit internally, do not contribute to the calibration of a special nac. planck-scale circuits do, however.[/note]

name: Simulating a Solar System
text: simulating a solar system almost as expensive as the real one, right? not to worry, this stargate and the current are only just the beginning. [note]our journey reaches the current end, entering the uxv, aka eoh era. the year is 2023, and the game continues to be pushed further and further. the eoh exists now, along with machine parts up to uxv. multiblocks have gained endless amounts of quality of life, including sub 1-tick oc, batch mode, void protection, and numerous ae2 additions like crafting input buses, stocking hatches, level maintainers and more. automation has never been easier, yet the goal has never been placed farther. naquadah fuel now has many tiers and can compete into the late-game, even competing with (now fixed) dyson, but outclassed by the huge amount of power a maximized eoh can make (12.8 teu/t!). initially the stargate recipe seemed impossible, requiring months of runtime on hundreds of maximized eohs, requiring some adjustments to be more realistic to attain. after this was changed, the race began again, this time between johny709 and gdcloud. johny burned out towards the end, and gdcloud was surpassed by a silent contender, starstack, being the first to conquer this challenge on the 26th of june, 2023. beyond just the first, this era marked the beginning of the group run era, with large runs such as ballers run (setting this era into motion), bee run (affecting wide change on the nh project and its management as a whole), and cell run 2 (the fastest ever stargate run at the time, only 73 days, popularizing many automation techniques like level maintained lines). additionally, this version saw the first player achieve gtnh gods, reaching stargate in a 3rd run, earned by gdcloud as a part of cell run 2 on the 23rd of june, 2024. later this stargate would see three others reach this goal, ramspace on the 29th of september, 2024, and staffix and serenibyss in a group run on the 17th of november, 2024. p.s.: here's the list as usual: -many new processing multiblocks like hile, fluid shaper, industrial autoclave, etc. -forge of the gods, black hole compressor, antimatter power generation, precise assembler t4 -dtpf convergence, component assembly line tiered bonuses, mega vac subspace cooling, mk5 fusion skips for metastable oganesson -wireless data hatches, wireless optical hatches, uncertainty resolution -artificial universe cells, smart blocking mode[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 1, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, [note]this quest and “see you next time!” are mutually exclusive; completing one will lock the other.

name: Cooking for Blockheads
text:
cooking for blockheads say thanks to mitch for backporting this great mod. you can use it to help you craft new food items. all blocks connected to the kitchen floor (use it as walls too!) are considered part of the same multiblock. countertops will search up two blocks for cabinets to include.

items stored in storages like the cabinet (or your inventory) can be used in recipes. all storage spaces for items are the same, so don't bother making a ton of fridges unless you really want to. supply water to the sink to get water for recipes.

you can store some cooking tools in the oven. you can store the rest on tool racks to auto-use them all in recipes. this includes stuff like the gt soft mallet if you can't make all the pam's tools yet.

the oven has 3 input slots and 3 output slots, and can work on 9 items at once. it's basically a furnace. you can request items be cooked from the cooking table too.

the cooking table will automatically show you all recipes that can be created with the existing ingredients, and you can click on them to craft them. make all the food, and get all the hearts!

you can use dye to color the kitchen, except for the oven.

note that the implementation is not finished, so there are some problems. upgrades like powering the oven with rf/eu are not in yet. and so on. but we finally have a toaster so you can make toast!

name: Laputa I
text:
laputa i the item when used will raise a sphere of land into the air, centered on the selected block. the radius of the sphere and the height elevated are determined by the shard power. the process is not instant, and instead will move each block at a time until every block within a radius is moved. blocks that rely on walls or floors, such as torches and crops, will drop in the process, as the required support is not moved alongside.

name: Mana Fountain
text:
mana fountain the mana fountain allows for quick and seamless automation of mana pool recipes.

you can assemble the multiblock as specified in the lexica botania / nei. after it's assembled, right clicking it using the wand of the forest will show you whether it's complete and the amount of internally stored mana.

you can send the controller mana directly by either using a spreader or a spark much like a mana pool. technically you don't have to use the mana pool in the center of the multiblock for it to function, but it is placed conveniently so that you can (plus, it doesn't hurt to have an extra buffer).

items are allowed to input from any side of the controller, but can only output from the bottom. for early automation, it's recommended to just use hoppers. once you unlock ae2 however you can simply place an interface underneath the controller with the appropriate patterns and it should push and pull items automatically.

[warn]you cannot craft alchemy or conjuration recipes using this multiblock, those are separate multiblocks that you will unlock with more advanced robot arm technology.[/warn]
