name: Magical Base Defense
text:
magical base defense the wand focus: warding can be used to make blocks invincible with right-click. warding may be removed by right-clicking it again. it is not able to ward transparent blocks like glass or non-full blocks like slabs, but there is a block known as warded glass available with the warded arcana research if you want a protected transparent block. it is also unable to ward blocks with tile entities like chests. take note that only the player who warded the block can unward it.

holding a wand with this focus will show an outline on nearby blocks you have warded. they look normal otherwise. warded blocks are [note]completely indestructible[/note] and will produce particle effects similar to runic shielding when a player tries to break them. blocks will lose any special properties when warded: sand or gravel will not fall, grass will not grow, and packed ice will no longer be slippery. warded blocks cannot be affected by any outside influence such as redstone or pistons. the only way to break the warded block is via the owner right-clicking with a wand with this focus.

[note]special note: warded blocks emit light. they can also cause quite a bit of lag if used at scale.[/note]

[note]this focus accepts the following upgrades in the focal manipulator:[/note]
frugal: lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level

name: Plague Inc.
text:
plague inc. the wand focus: pech's curse is a rare wand focus which cannot be crafted by players. it can only be obtained from a pech mage -- either by bartering valuable items or by killing it for its wand to drop. pech mages are rare and the drop chance is quite low, so bartering is recommended. [warn]if attacked, the pech will use this focus against you![/warn]

name: Pocket Dolly
text:
pocket dolly wand focus: dislocation is a very useful focus that allows its user to take and place nearly any block, even tile entities and one that usually can't be moved, like mob spawners, planted crops, and more.

[warn]please use responsibly, and don't move things you shouldn't, like door halves, or some multiblock parts, unless you like the idea of world corruption destroying your world. that said, if you're in sp and make a backup, do whatever you want, just know the risks.[/warn]

it uses:
5 ordo + 5 perditio + 1 terra to take any mundane block.
25 ordo + 25 perditio + 5 terra to take any block with a tile entity (such as a chest).
100 ordo + 100 perditio + 20 terra to take a mob spawner.

name: Scrub, Scrub, Scrub...
text:
scrub, scrub, scrub... the wand focus: flux scrubber is an incredibly useful focus for the messy or insane thaumaturge. it creates a beam that sucks up flux goo and gas.

[note]this focus accepts the following upgrades in the focal manipulator:[/note]
frugal: lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
potency: speeds up flux cleanup
crystallization: drops crystallized potentia when cleaning up flux at level 1. drops crystallized essence of a random aspect at level 2. mutually exclusive with warping and calming
warping: gives its user temporary warp when used to clean flux. mutually exclusive with crystallization

name: Snowball Fight!
text:
snowball fight! the wand focus: frost will launch a ball of ice that can bounce off of blocks and mobs.

frugal: lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
potency: increases damage dealt every level

name: Trade Offer
text:
trade offer wand focus: equal trade is able to switch out blocks in the world with blocks in the player's inventory. shift-right-click on a block to attune the focus to the block. once attuned to a block, left-click on a single block to replace it with the substitute block. right-click will transform a contiguous 5x5x5 area of the same block that has air on at least one side. this can go through thin walls or into caves, so be careful. very useful for upgrading ebf coils or for swapping other blocks that are slow to break like obsidian! it cannot be used to break or place blocks with tile entities like chests.

[note]this focus accepts the following upgrades in the focal manipulator:[/note]
frugal: lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
enlarge: expands the maximum range by 1 block in each direction per level
treasure (level 3): works like vanilla fortune
architect (level 3): allows the focus's working area to be modified with the misc wand toggle keybind. sneaking with the keybind changes which axes are modified. this upgrade also changes the working area to a plane, so be sure to test this upgrade out before committing to it and applying further upgrades
silk touch (level 5): works like vanilla silk touch {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "thaumcraft:focustrade", "resolved": {"id": "i:thaumcraft:focustrade:0", "name": "wand focus: equal trade", "mod": "thaumcraft", "registry": "focustrade", "icon": 12122, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "041737047e567a50", "recipes": 1}, "label": "wand focus: equal trade"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 9, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:9", "name": "lootbag (magic novice)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21280, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 9, "shard": "a84956fa626988d2", "recipes": 0}, "label": "lootbag (magic novice)"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 1, "oredict": "", "id": "thaumcraft:itemlootbag", "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (thaumcraft:itemlootbag, metadata 1)"}}}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 5, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:coindarkwizardi", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:coindarkwizardi:0", "name": "coin "the dark wizard 10"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "coindarkwizardi", "icon": 20753, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "e2cc659550503ae7", "recipes": 2}, "label": "coin "the dark wizard 10""}}}}

name: Collecting the Hybrids
text:
collecting the hybrids if you got lucky and found some bees in a village, put them in their houses next to some trees. over time the bees will slowly pollinate the leaves of the trees. using a grafter you can break the leaf blocks to retrieve a sapling 100%, useful for getting the forestry saplings. this doesn't seem to work with magical trees though. you can trade with villagers to get proven grafters that have a longer lifetime. also investigate magic, you have heard rumors of long lasting grafters available to magicians.

name: Combustion Engine
text:
combustion engine the combustion engine combusts things for power like a car engine does. you need water in it if it's over 100 degrees, or it will explode. don't run out of water! you turn it on with a redstone signal.

your options for fuel are:
oil @30rf/t for a total of 150k
ethanol @40rf/t for a total of 360k
diesel @60rf/t for a total of 1,500k

name: Multifarm: Gearbox
text:
multifarm: gearbox to power your farm and have it automatically harvest crops, you will need at least one farm gearbox to supply power. you can use either rf or eu. if you use eu, make sure to use a cable to allow conversion. farm operations can be hastened with additional gearboxes.

testing has shown that splitting the amps to 4 gearboxes (4a ulv) works better than sending 1a lv to 4 gearboxes.

a max sized cropsnh crop farm (5x4x5) using all space possible with max stat seeds (31/31/31) on a fast crop needs only 6a ulv to keep up.

similarly, a max sized small farm (3x4x3) using all space possible with max stat seeds (31/31/31) on a high tier, moderate speed crop needs only 4a ulv.

sending more power to the same gearbox doesn't work. if it can get to max rf capacity but your farm can't keep up, sending more power won't help, so add more gearboxes.

in addition, you lose 2 eu from the energy emitting device for every amp of ulv (which is only 8 to begin with), so it's not nearly as efficient as using lv or higher. just keep in mind that more a to more gearboxes is better than to the same one.

of course, if you mix your slower crops with your faster ones, you aren't likely to need to min-max to this extent. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, name: Multifarm: Hatch
text:
multifarm: hatch you can supply and extract items from the farm by using farm hatches that are connected to pipe systems.

supplying items
the farm hatch is clever enough to know which item goes where. if an item isn't appropriate for the farm's configuration, the hatch will simply reject it.

extracting items
any item that is harvested by the multifarm is automatically ejected by the farm hatches into inventories or pipes. pipes can be used to extract from other sides. you may need more than one, or a name: Such Pretty Leaves...
THE RAINMAKER
text:
the rainmaker the rainmaker is a forestry block capable of stopping/producing rain & creating thunderstorms.

the rainmaker has no gui, but can be right clicked with 3 different capsules:

iodine capsule: produces rain

phosphoric iodine capsule: produces a thunderstorm

dissipation charge: stops rain

the rainmaker requires around ~30 seconds after activation for the rain and thunderstorm to start.

the dissipation charge will stop the rain after a few seconds until the next activation.  {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "forestry:iodinecapsule", "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (forestry:iodinecapsule, metadata 0)"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "forestry:phosphoriciodinecapsule", "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (forestry:phosphoriciodinecapsule, metadata 0)"}, "2": {"count": 1, "damage": 4, "oredict": "", "id": "forestry:craftingmaterial", "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (forestry:craftingmaterial, metadata 4)"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:optional_retrieval"}, "1": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 1, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 7, "oredict": "", "id": "forestry:factory", "resolved": {"id": "i:forestry:factory:7", "name": "rainmaker", "mod": "forestry", "registry": "factory", "icon": 6770, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 7, "shard": "9f2cc7ff8e71ea80", "recipes": 1}, "label": "rainmaker"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 20, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:20", "name": "lootbag (forest ranger advanced)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21212, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 20, "shard": "f35d56e22ecf78d0", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (forest ranger advanced)"}}}}

name: U-238 Tu-Wait, Seriously?
text:
u-238 tu-wait, seriously? if you want cropsnh crops to work with the multifarm, you now need this. you can get the u-238 from thorium. it also only searches 6 blocks above the farm structure block to prevent lag. so goodbye mf stacking, you always looked dumb, and didn't make any sense.

the largest size supports ~1100 crops, while the smallest supports ~600 depending on your layout if you use it for crops. this is because it will look for crops up to 5 blocks out further than normal in this mode (in the cardinal directions, it's further out in the corners. just try it out, it's hard to describe). they're the same size as in previous versions, so you don't need to rejigger them. name: Advanced Electric Jetpack
text:
advanced electric jetpack the advanced electric jetpack is an upgraded version of the electric jetpack.
while worn in the chest armor slot and charged with eu, it allows the player to fly. it provides no armor protection, but will charge tools being used in the same manner as the advanced lappack from its 3,000,000 eu internal storage.

the advanced electric jetpack is limited to a maximum flying height of y-256.

[note]to turn it on, hit the fly key listed under gravisuite. you can then use space to fly up. to activate hover, hit the ic2 mode key while holding space. will also recharge tools.[/note] {"0": name: Better Boots with a little pizzazz
text:
better boots with a little pizzazz electric boots of the traveller grant you a 2% vis discount along with all the benefits of the regular boots of the traveller.

in addition, they come with a wide variety of new features thanks to our amazing magic devs:

- configurable jump boost: you can choose between 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, or a 100% jump boost.

- configurable speed boost: similar to the jump boost, you can adjust the speed boost percentage to your preference.

- flight inertia: when toggled on, this feature cancels inertia while flying, allowing for precise movement even when traveling at high speeds.

- omnidirectional movement: this toggle lets you decide whether your speed boost applies in all directions or only while running straight ahead.

[note]none of these keybinds are set by default. the easiest way to configure them is to go into options -> controls, turn on the "category" button, and type "thaumic boots." then, assign keys for the features as needed.[/note]

name: Copterpack, More 'Hover' than 'Jet'
text:
copterpack, more 'hover' than 'jet' the copterpack is the first jetpack with a hover mode. it uses several different types of fuels to power it.

buckets of creosote, lava, oil, diesel, cetane, ethanol, and fuel will work.

equip your copterpack, then hold the sneak key and press the adventure backpack action key. you can also switch between hover and normal mode.

max flying height is limited to y-200.

vertical velocity decreases linearly with height after overcoming optimal height - 135 for jetpack and 100 for copter.

name: Electric Jetpack
text:
electric jetpack your first electrical jetpack, it can be charged in any lv machine. you need to hit the ic2 mode-switch key to toggle between normal mode and hover mode while holding down the jump key. when descending, remember to shut off hover mode or else you'll drain your jetpack.

the only limitation is that you can't fly higher than y-185.

for charging on the go, you can craft a charging crystal from ic2 charging components. you have to take the backpack out of the armor slot and put it in your hotbar and activate the charger by sneak-clicking.

later on gt++ charge packs are belts that can charge everything in your inventory including armor. check nei for the recipe.

finally, the gt++ wireless charger will charge everything in your inventory, including the jetpack, from your base at long ranges. a quest is unlocked once you finish your nanosuit. just remember when name: Flippers
Fluid Loader and Unloader
text:
fluid loader and unloader if you plan to automate the oil transport from your oil field far away, you need a fluid loader and unloader. a locking track will stop the train as long as oil is loaded or unloaded.

[note]ps: you should probably use the long distance fluid pipeline once you can make it in lv unless you really love trains.[/note]

full details on how to use these may require online research (gtnh changes the recipes, not normal railcraft functionality), but here is a simple list of things to do:

1. make a loop of track from your base to the oil well.
2. place a locking track near the well, and put a fluid loader two blocks above it. the track should be in locking mode - use a crowbar to change it.
3. use the tank car on the filter in the loader and set it to immediate mode.
4. connect the well to the loader as normal.
5. put a fluid unloader under a locking track at your base, and set it the same as the loader.
6. automate the locomotive similarly - a fluid loader above a steam locomotive set to manual and filtered to the locomotive.

either you got it working, you need to do more research, you realized it moves 32 buckets a trip and decided to just walk, or you can go to discord and ask why anyone would build a train.

item loaders also exist, but the main use for them may be to refuel your locomotive. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, name: Long Distance Power Delivery
text:
long distance power delivery no mage wants to be restricted to short flying times. with this spire from the automagy discipline you can transmit magical energy directly to your flying harness. to get the correct thaumium block, compress 9 ingots to get the gt thaumium block and then chisel that block to get the correct type.

this multiblock requires centi-vis to operate. you can use 2-6 thaumostatic pylons, with additional pylons extending the range. provide the construct aer centi-vis to operate, and it will accept potentia essentia to transfer to flyers. the construct will also accept aer and volatus essentia to increase the range and rate of transfer, respectively. right-click the sides of the controller to name: Minecart
text:
minecart after you craft your first cart the journey can begin...

well, not really. you will need some kind of tracks first.

[note]we here at questbook, inc. do not guarantee the usefulness of minecarts or trains in any way. especially since you can mine out a vein in a single session once you have a hammer and backpacks.[/note]

[warn]warning: unprotected carts can be knocked off their rails by lightning. cover the area with blocks to prevent carts from disappearing.[/warn]

[warn]also, make sure to keep your cart in one chunk, or use chunkloaders covering the whole area the cart works within. loading/unloading chunks may cause carts to disappear or duplicate.[/warn]

[note]you should only make these if you want to have fun with them, as anything they can do is better done by other methods, including the long distance fluid pipeline. excessive minecart and train name: Spare Battery
text:
spare battery the electric jetpack may be useful for flight, but it doesn't seem to last very long. 

if only there was an integrated upgradable battery pack you could keep on your player to extend its range...

oh wait, there is!

the charge pack can be used as a battery pack for charging items both in your hotbar and armor equip to your person. simply place it in the belt bauble slot and it should be fully functional! the hv one should serve you nicely for now.

name: Speed up with the Sash
text:
speed up with the sash the sashes from botania improves your speed passively along with a jump boost and provide step assist all while fitting in your belt slot, how convenient is that?

you will need a method of powering them with either the mana tablet or the mana mirror linked to a pool.

the soujourner sash provides the basic speed boost, jump boost and step assist while the globetrotter provides double the jump height and speed boost.

the planestrider is special since it provides a slowly increasing speed boost as long as you are moving. you can even reach up to 11 times the soujourner sash speed boost!

name: Steam Locomotive
text:
steam locomotive the steam locomotive is much better than the furnace cart. you can control the speed and the direction the locomotive will move. you need to put water and coal inside to make steam to power the locomotive.

you can use a water tank or other water source to refill this locomotive by placing a fluid loader above it at a stop. the loader can be placed either directly above the track, or a block higher to give you clearance when riding the train. (you can't actually ride a train unless you sit in a normal minecart.)

this locomotive runs on any fuel you can burn in a steam boiler, perhaps you will want to use compressed coal blocks or similar. you can use an item loader to refuel it.

once you have stable electricity in mv, you will likely move to the electric locomotive. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, name: Teleporter
text:
teleporter the industrialcraft2 teleporter allows for teleportation between 2 connected teleporters.

name: Travelocity²
text:
travelocity² why walk when you can teleport? this upgrade to the staff of traveling can move you even further, even faster, and will never run out of energy.

right-click:
 * if targeting a travel anchor: teleport to it, 2048 range
 * if looking at a block: teleport to it, 512 range
 * if no block in range: teleport forward, 64 range
 * if looking at a block within 4 range: teleport to the other side of a wall, 16 range
 * no cooldown

shift-right-click:
 * same as right-click, but ignoring travel anchors
 * travel anchors will be hidden from view while holding shift

[note]tip: you won't be able to see travel anchors that are far away, but can still teleport to them if they are in range and chunk-loaded. try using journeymap waypoints to mark anchors![/note]

[note]note: the right-click and shift-right-click actions are fully configurable. check the enderio staff settings configs!
config action values:
 0: do nothing
 1: teleport to look / forward
 2: teleport to anchor
 3: teleport to anchor, or to look / forward if no anchor[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "enderio:itemteleportstaff", "tag": {"energy": 250000}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (enderio:itemteleportstaff, metadata 0)"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Automating Crafting Table Recipes
Better Chassis
Chassis
text:
chassis basic pipes can interact with adjacent blocks, but they also don't do much on their own.

logistics pipes has modules that provide the pipes with more complex functions, but the basic logistics pipes can't make use of them.

to make use of the modules, there are special pipes called chassis.

there are multiple tiers of chassis in logistics pipes. for now, a mk 1, which can hold 1 module, will work.

you can insert modules directly in the chassis by right-clicking said chassis with the module. but if you need to take modules out of a chassis or configure a module in one, you need to right-click the chassis with a wrench to access its ui. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "logisticspipes:item.pipelogisticschassimk1", "resolved": {"id": "i:logisticspipes:item.pipelogisticschassimk1:0", "name": "logistics chassis mk1", "mod": "logisticspipes", "registry": "item.pipelogisticschassimk1", "icon": 8797, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "6140eaf0aea1d652", "recipes": 1}, "label": "logistics chassis mk1"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 4, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:4", "name": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21242, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 4, "shard": "3cff4d8e3920defe", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)"}, "1": {"count": 2, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:cointechniciani", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:cointechniciani:0", "name": "coin "the technician 10"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "cointechniciani", "icon": 20788, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "53205e7d44e6e7e5", "recipes": 2}, "label": "coin "the technician 10""}}}}

name: Fluid Storage
Get Those Machines to Work
text:
get those machines to work most of the recipes are made in all kinds of machines. while a crafting logistics pipe works, it can only hold 1 recipe per pipe.

it is not an issue for logistics crafting tables as it can only hold one crafting table recipes, but it is wasteful to assign only one recipe for one machine.

for machines, use chassis. preferably a higher tier. a mk1 chassis with a crafting module is basically just a crafting logistics pipe.

you can't shift-click recipes from nei so you have to drag the recipe from it. don't worry, you can drag ghost items from nei into the slots in the module to configure it.

you notice there are 3 gray slots at the right. they are for satellite logistics pipes. we will talk about it later.

note: do not use the output face of the machine. the output side blocks all interactions unless you hit it with a screwdriver.

also do not use auto-output, or else the machine will output the item into the pipe and the network will treat the product as an item inserted into the system rather than an item requested by the system and will send it to its storage. every other face except the cover works.

the check mark means you have read the whole thing and should know how machine automation works using lp. the reward of this quest is the knowledge of how to automate gt machine recipes {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: I NEED THAT!!!!!!
Inserting Fluids
text:
inserting fluids sometimes you insert fluid in the system. you need something to get the fluid into the correct buffer other than inserting the fluid into the buffer manually.

there are 2 pipes that can do the job: transfer fluid into a tank connected to a fluid basic pipe allocated to said fluid.

1. logistics fluid extractor pipe. it extracts fluid from connected buffer to the correct big storage tank. it doesn't require a pump but it is slower.

2. logistics fluid insertion pipe. it does not pull fluids from tanks actively, requiring a gt pump if you are using gt tanks, but it can send fluids faster.

name: It gets polymorphic
It's DA BEST
Let this Sink in
text:
let this sink in a well organized storage system is crucial for a logistics system.

with the ability to use modules through a chassis, we can now prepare for storage modules.

logistics pipes uses itemsink modules to assign storage spaces.

this itemsink modules can be used in 2 ways:

1. assign the storage of a connected inventory with at most 9 different kinds of items by setting 9 items as filter on the module.

2. assign a connected inventory as a default route. the default route is a destination for items that have no other valid storage spaces.

note: remember to always check if the default route has additional spaces because items that are stuck in the pipes without a destination will eventually yeet themselves out of the pipes. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 4, "damage": 1, "oredict": "", "id": "logisticspipes:item.itemmodule", "resolved": {"id": "i:logisticspipes:item.itemmodule:1", "name": "itemsink module", "mod": "logisticspipes", "registry": "item.itemmodule", "icon": 8804, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 1, "shard": "6a2f41b9d371e5c8", "recipes": 3}, "label": "itemsink module"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 4, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:4", "name": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21242, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 4, "shard": "3cff4d8e3920defe", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)"}, "1": {"count": 2, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:cointechniciani", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:cointechniciani:0", "name": "coin "the technician 10"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "cointechniciani", "icon": 20788, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "53205e7d44e6e7e5", "recipes": 2}, "label": "coin "the technician 10""}}}}

name: Powering Logistics
text:
powering logistics every system takes power. a logistics pipes network is no exception.

the logistics pipes system runs on an energy called lp, but there are no generators that generate lp.

instead, logistics pipes has a power adapter called the logistics power junction that converts eu into lp. use a basic logistics pipe to connect the power junction to the whole network.

name: Satellites! Wait,... They don't Orbit...
text:
satellites! wait,... they don't orbit... a buffer of 64 per slot is never big enough. just look at red alloy ingot for example. it can only hold 16 recipes worth of redstone at once. you don't really want the items to just zoom around the pipes while waiting for the machine to make room... you want to have a big chest buffering items to be processed.

introducing the satellite logistics pipes. it provides additional input into the recipe incorporating it.

the pipe runs on a numerical frequency system, with the whole server sharing the number pool. this ensures that 2 separate systems can be connected to each other without conflict.

you can "connect" a crafting module with one satellite pipe by selecting the correct frequency of the satellite part. multiple modules can connect to a single satellite pipe.

satellite pipe inputs are the 3 gray slots on the right of the 9 slots of the module. only items in the 3 gray slots will be sent to satellite pipes.

note: ensure your satellite pipe has any frequency other than 0. a satellite pipe with frequency 0 will not work. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "logisticspipes:item.pipeitemssatellitelogistics", "resolved": {"id": "i:logisticspipes:item.pipeitemssatellitelogistics:0", "name": "satellite logistics pipe", "mod": "logisticspipes", "registry": "item.pipeitemssatellitelogistics", "icon": 8793, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "96b88815a351c4cd", "recipes": 1}, "label": "satellite logistics pipe"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 5, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:5", "name": "lootbag (tier 2 mv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21254, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 5, "shard": "86c93816ff53d76b", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 2 mv)"}, "1": {"count": 5, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:cointechniciani", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:cointechniciani:0", "name": "coin "the technician 10"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "cointechniciani", "icon": 20788, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "53205e7d44e6e7e5", "recipes": 2}, "label": "coin "the technician 10""}}}}

name: Sorting Incoming
text:
sorting incoming now that storage spaces are organized and assigned, time to let the network sort the items for us.

there are 2 ways to insert items into the system

1. use an extraction module to extract items into the system. it is slow, but everything that has a valid destination will be sent into the network.

2. use a quicksort module. it extracts a whole stack of items that has a valid destination. this module will ignore items that have no destinations other than the default route though...

it is your choice. pick what you like. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 1, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 3, "oredict": "", "id": "logisticspipes:item.itemmodule", "resolved": {"id": "i:logisticspipes:item.itemmodule:3", "name": "extractor module", "mod": "logisticspipes", "registry": "item.itemmodule", "icon": 8819, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 3, "shard": "68608d134dc7c5cb", "recipes": 3}, "label": "extractor module"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 5, "oredict": "", "id": "logisticspipes:item.itemmodule", "resolved": {"id": "i:logisticspipes:item.itemmodule:5", "name": "quicksort module", "mod": "logisticspipes", "registry": "item.itemmodule", "icon": 8824, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 5, "shard": "efc8430f932a7449", "recipes": 3}, "label": "quicksort module"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 46, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:46", "name": "lootbag (computers)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21251, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 46, "shard": "e8bf0f9d49d142d7", "recipes": 0}, "label": "lootbag (computers)"}, "1": {"count": 3, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:cointechniciani", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:cointechniciani:0", "name": "coin "the technician 10"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "cointechniciani", "icon": 20788, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "53205e7d44e6e7e5", "recipes": 2}, "label": "coin "the technician 10""}}}}

name: The Backbone of the System
text:
the backbone of the system welcome to logistics pipes! this questline is dedicated to this automation mod, which is placed in the mv tier to help manage your chests, crafting and even fluid crafting. it's quite similar to projectred: transportation, but with some differences, particularly in fluid crafting.

here, you can connect chests and machines to a central location, but before you build that central location, you have to get some pipes for connection. the unrouted transport pipe is the first pipe you will ever need in logistics pipes.

they only connect to other pipes and don't have any item routing capabilities, but you will need a ton of them.

warning: do not form junctions with the unrouted transport pipes. items going into an unrouted transport pipe junction will come out of a random exit of the junction. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 64, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "logisticspipes:item.pipeitemsbasictransport", "resolved": {"id": "i:logisticspipes:item.pipeitemsbasictransport:0", "name": "unrouted transport pipe", "mod": "logisticspipes", "registry": "item.pipeitemsbasictransport", "icon": 8781, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "b61054bc5e0a081f", "recipes": 5}, "label": "unrouted transport pipe"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 4, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:4", "name": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21242, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 4, "shard": "3cff4d8e3920defe", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)"}, "1": {"count": 3, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:cointechniciani", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:cointechniciani:0", "name": "coin "the technician 10"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "cointechniciani", "icon": 20788, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "53205e7d44e6e7e5", "recipes": 2}, "label": "coin "the technician 10""}}}}

items and armor get damaged over time.

curse of vampire
mobs become sensitive to sunlight and take more damage.

adds reflection damage to a mob.

name: Curses
text:
curses a curse is a magical powder that attaches itself to an area of blocks, a mob, or a player, crafted using living matter, end powder and specific ingredients.

it can be either placed right on a block or an entity, or thrown. if it gets thrown into a group of entities, it will have a chance to hit more than one at the same time.

curses eventually disappear, but they can be made eternal by crafting them with stardust and an arcane shard. eternal curses will stay forever on blocks and mobs, and longer than normal curses on players.

curses placed on blocks are only visible to the player who cast it, and for a short duration to players affected by it.

getting very close to a curse makes it visible without having it affect you, but it requires extreme carefulness.

it is possible to remove curses by using a potion of purity. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, name: Death Flowers
text:
death flowers the purple flowers found on top of endstone blobs are known as death flowers. they can be planted on end stone, dirt, grass or inside flower pots.

outside the end, the flower will slowly decay, even if in a flower pot.

after some time spent decaying, it starts to occasionally attract angry endermen.

when the flower decays completely, it turns dark, propagates a massive amount of decay to nearby blocks and spawns an energy cluster.

partial decay can be healed a little using end powder. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": name: Ender Towers
Enderpearl Enchantments
text:
enderpearl enchantments enhanced ender pearls are a special version of vanilla ender pearls with one or more special effects (enhancements).

the way to make enhanced pearls is to right-click with end powder in your hand to modify your ender pearl. you can continue adding as many effects to one pearl as you want.

these effects are useful when throwing the pearl, for pearl teleportation effects.

natural occurrence:
it is possible to find pearls with random effects in a dungeon tower's loot chests.

enhancements:
no fall damage (wool)
upon the pearl's landing, the player will not receive any fall damage.

no gravity (feather)
the pearl will not follow the rules of gravity, which makes it possible to throw it straight up. after 10 seconds of flight, the pearl is automatically destroyed without any teleportation or fall damage.

increased range (string)
unlike the no gravity effect, the pearl will fall down due to gravity, but will do so 25% slower. if the pearl has the no gravity effect too, it will override this effect.

double speed (gold nugget)
increases the pearl's speed by a factor of 2, but won't change the flight trajectory. this can be helpful if you are in a bad situation (fell in lava, swarm of mobs around...) and need to be saved very quickly. in combination with the riding effect, you may notice slight stuttering on a server.

explosive (gunpowder)
upon landing, the pearl will explode with radius of 2.7 (tnt has radius of 4). this will not harm the thrower as long as they are far enough from the landing spot.

freeze (snowball)
the pearl will freeze mobs and players within 5 blocks of the landing spot for at least 4 seconds. just as with the explosive effect, this will not affect the thrower unless they throw the pearl close to them, or have the riding effect applied. this effect is also followed by ice cracking sound and snow particles.

riding (lead)
the thrower will "ride" the pearl to its destination. during the ride, if another pearl with this effect is thrown, the previous pearl will destroy itself and deal fall damage (unless no fall damage effect is applied).

trivia:
the enhanced ender pearls can still be used for crafting an eye of ender. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": name: Energy Clusters and the Energy Wand
text:
energy clusters and the energy wand energy clusters, the little glowing orbs you may have seen floating around, have different health levels, which affect the regeneration (or leaking) speed.

clusters can be moved using an energy wand. moving them too far or across dimensions can have negative effects on their health.

blocks that use energy will take it from clusters up to 16 blocks away, and from the environment if placed in the end.

items that use energy automatically refill in the end, or can be used on a cluster to start and stop draining the energy. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, name: Enhanced Brewing Stand
text:
enhanced brewing stand after the altar creation is complete, a player has to place up to 8 matching solid blocks (of any kind) near the altar. these blocks require 1 block of air above them and no solid blocks touching them on the sides and diagonally. these blocks are the pedestals. the dragon essence altar will project purple particles to all the pedestals connected to it.

dropping an item onto the pedestal will place it there. after the item has been placed on top of the pedestal, the altar will start "infusing" the item using dragon essence stored in the altar itself. adding more essence to the altar is done by right-clicking.

infusing makes items repair themselves (this does not work for items that require energy), increases the level of existing enchantments (up to 4 enchantments per item) and can even add new enchantments.

there are two items in this mod that can be obtained only by dragon essence infusion:

enhanced brewing stand - by infusing a vanilla brewing stand, requires 20 pieces of dragon essence.

temple caller - by infusing a vanilla eye of ender, requires 50 pieces of dragon essence. name: Essence Altar
Find all the Ores in the End
text:
find all the ores in the end end powder ore:
generated in the end in between end stone at every height level. when the ore is mined with any type of pickaxe, it will drop one or two pieces of end powder.

endium ore:
rare ore that starts to appear near dungeon towers, and gets more common the further you travel.

igneous rock ore:
generated in the end in the burning mountains and sometimes in the endstone blobs. this block emits lava particles but does no damage to the player. when the ore is mined with an iron pickaxe or better, it will drop one igneous rock.

[note]note: the fortune enchantment does not affect igneous rock ore. however, the silk touch enchantment does work with this block. you can get better output with a macerator.[/note]

instability ore:
generated in the end in the biome islands, especially common in the fiery mines. when the ore is mined with an advanced pickaxe, it has a 40% chance to drop one instability orb, otherwise it breaks without providing any items.

[note]note: the fortune enchantment increases the chance of getting an instability orb by 4% per level, and the silk touch enchantment also works with this block. you can get better output with a forge hammer.[/note]

stardust ore:
generated in the end in the biome islands. when the ore is mined with an advanced pickaxe, it has a chance to drop 0-4 pieces of stardust. even though this ore comes in clusters, two ore blocks from the same cluster can be generated away from each other, making stardust ore a rare resource which requires thorough exploration and mining.

[note]note: the stardust ore block has different textures on its sides.[/note]

sphalerite: often found floating in the open space around endstone blobs. you can macerate it for crushed normal sphalerite. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, text:
infestation remedy infestation remedy is a drinkable (or throwable) item used to shorten effects of the infestation.

obtaining:
the infestation remedy is brewed in an enhanced brewing stand, using silverfish blood as the brewing ingredient and an awkward potion.

usage:
when drunk, the remedy will shorten each of the infestation effects by 150 to 180 seconds.

name: Infused Altar
text:
infused altar you can upgrade your altar with one or more special effects (enhancements).

the way to make an enhanced altar is to right-click your altar with end powder in your hand, then supplying end powder and the enhancement material in the ui. you can continue adding as many effects to one altar as you want.

enhancements:
range (block of lapis)
increase the range at which an item can be infused by the altar.

speed (block of redstone)
increase the working speed of the altar.

efficiency (block of emerald)
reduce the cost of dragon essence used by altar recipes. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, name: Infused Brewing Stand
text:
infused brewing stand a brewing stand with one or more special effects (enhancements).

you can upgrade your enhanced brewing stand with end powder to modify it like other hee items.

you can continue adding as many effects to one brewing stand as you want.

enhancements:
tier (ectoplasm)
your potion can have a higher tier and a longer potion duration than vanilla ones. (tier iv is up to 12 mins)

speed (igneous rock)
increases the speed of the brewing stand.

cost (emerald)
reduces the cost of end powder used in a brewing cycle. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, name: Is This the End? No, it's the END Dimension
text:
is this the end? no, it's the end dimension you investigated the pearls, and managed to reactivate them to become eyes. this has shown you that the source of the disturbance seems to be coming out of the portal frames inside the strongholds, deep underground. they seem strangely drawn towards its mysterious depths. perhaps they can be used to reactivate it?

hint: throwing ender eyes in the air in the overworld will guide you to the nearest stronghold. from time to time ender eyes are destroyed in this process, so make extras. try to do so in a place name: Potion of Instability
text:
potion of instability the potion of instability is a special type of potion, which can be brewed by putting an instability orb into an enhanced brewing stand with an awkward potion. the brewing process requires end powder in the stand's special slot.

usage:
as any other potion, the potion of instability can be drunk (or thrown, if it's a splash potion). unlike regular potions, this potion gives a random potion effect of random tier and duration to each player it affects. it can also apply potion effects which aren't available in vanilla potions, such as jump or hunger.

trivia:
the item tooltip contains ???, as opposed to a potion effect and duration.

you can make splash potions with gunpowder and 3 more end powder as well. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": name: Runes
text:
runes there are 6 types of runes found in the ravaged dungeons on the infested islands:

power
vigor
magic
defense
agility
void

the void rune is less common than other types.

runes are used to create charms, which are crafted in a charm pouch.

basic runes increase attributes, such as strength, speed or health. void rune (gray) gives the louse one of several special and extremely dangerous abilities. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, name: Scorching Pickaxe
text:
scorching pickaxe the scorching pickaxe is a special type of pickaxe that smelts blocks and applies fortune effect to ores.

it only works on smeltable blocks and ores. blocks that smelt into items are affected by fortune, including for example iron ore and cactus.

compatible blocks are also mined much faster.

gt ores are not affected. you can find vanilla ores in the twilight forest inside hollow hills.

name: Spatial Dash Gem
text:
spatial dash gem the spatial dash gem is used for enderpearl-like teleportation.

the spatial dash gem uses energy and can be charged in an energy extraction table. right-clicking with the gem in hand sends a purple beam straight to where the player is aiming. when the beam hits a block, the player will be teleported to it. maximum travel distance is 75 blocks horizontally. the teleportation doesn't hurt the player, unlike ender pearls.

the spatial dash gem always tries to place the player on top of the block, even if the beam hits the side or bottom of it.

the spatial dash gem can teleport the player through 7 solid blocks in a row, making the gem a good way of teleporting through cave walls and ceilings. if the wall is thicker than 7 blocks, the gem then tries to find 2 air blocks inside the wall. if the air blocks are not found, the player will be teleported into a wall, leading to suffocation.

name: TNT Enchantments
text:
tnt enchantments enhanced tnt is a special version of vanilla tnt with one or more special effects (enhancements).

the way to make enhanced tnt is to right-click with end powder in your hand to modify your tnt. you can continue adding as many effects to one tnt as you want.

enhancements:
no block damage (feather)
tnt explodes with no block damage.

no entity damage (slime)
tnt explodes with no entity damage.

extra damage (gunpowder)
tnt explodes with extra damage.

trap (redstone)
tnt explodes when a hostile mob touches or walks over the tnt block.

no clip (enderpearls)
tnt falls through solid blocks and explodes after a few seconds.

fire (igneous rock)
tnt explodes with a big fire spread.

no fuse (redstone torch)
tnt explodes immediately. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 7, "damage": name: Transference Gem
text:
transference gem the transference gem is used to teleport to a marked location.

the transference gem uses energy and can be charged in an energy extraction table. shift-right-clicking on a block with a transference gem in hand will link the gem to that block. the state of the gem itself will then switch to "linked", as seen in its tooltip.

after linking, the player can right-click with a transference gem in hand to teleport to the linked block, using some of the energy stored in the gem.

using f3+h to enable detailed item tooltips makes the transference gem show the exact coordinates and the dimension of the linked location.

once the charge of the transference gem becomes lower than 44%, negative effects will appear:

deflection - the player will be teleported to a random location instead of the linked block.

various negative potion effects, the lower the charge is - the longer they will last:

slowness ii
nausea i
weakness ii
hunger i

endermen - angry endermen will spawn and attack the player.

item drop - a random amount of items in player's inventory will drop to the ground.

storm - will cause a 2-3 minute storm. this is the rarest effect. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, name: Visit the (Enchanted) Homeland Island
Visit the Fiery Island
Visit the Infested Island
text:
visit the infested island the infested islands are mostly a flat biome with occasional hills, long caves and a decent amount of ores. there are 2 variations of the biome - deep and ravaged. both of these variations contain silverfish, infested bats and occasionally endermen.

the deep variation is massively populated with spooky trees that can have faces on them, which are how you get ectoplasm. the ground has all types of infested plants, including thorny bushes.

the ravaged variation has patches of infested plants and occasional spooky trees, but the most important feature is the ravaged dungeon which is an open gate to getting your charms.

about infestation:
simply by standing on the infested end stone, the infestation level will rise. after leaving the area for several minutes, if the infestation level is low, it will reset and won't do any harm to the player.

however, if the infestation level gets high enough, it will trigger one or more potion effects, which include weakness, slowness and mining fatigue, and if the player's level is severe, blindness, confusion and/or poison may take place as well. these effects cannot be cured using milk; however you can drink infestation remedy to shorten them. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, name: Welcome to the End!
text:
welcome to the end! welcome to the end! and more importantly, hardcore ender expansion.

if you've already fought the ender dragon, you'll have noticed that the fight itself was challenging, far more than usual. though much of the island may be destroyed, have no worry, there are plenty of end blobs out there for you to gather ore or endstone from.

first, you will want to gather some end powder, a key catalyst for most of hee. any means of flight is also highly recommended.

hint: press the p key (unless you rebound it) for a key list of information about hee related stuff. once you've looked through it you'll realize you need knowledge in order to unlock pages. looking at blocks or items or certain things will also grant you knowledge. consuming knowledge notes will also grant you knowledge points. here are some for you to get started on. good luck!

you can also search for the adventurer's diary for some lore if you want.

[note]ps: hold shift and whack the egg with a vanilla sword to get it to drop.[/note]

name: A New Home
text:
a new home now that you've destroyed the poor bees' homes, you should build them a new one. the humble bee house will not let your bees mutate into new species. but you'll need the combs anyways for better housing. the production rate isn't too bad, but they cannot be automated.

one tip - put some vanilla saplings near the bee houses. bee houses give a natural boost of 3x to pollination vs better housing. the bees will pollinate them and you might get lucky and start getting some forestry tree crossbreeding. stick with oak and birch trees, they'll give you a nice mix of starter forestry trees.

of course, if you do this without taking precautions, you may find yourself swarmed by laggy butterflies...

you may also notice that bees with the 'flower' type flower spread flowers. this can be used to get, say, lavender, among others. if you don't like them spreading them everywhere, replace the dirt/grass blocks, remove the trait, or reduce the pollination speed/territory. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, name: A Stim a Day Keeps the Doctor Awake
text:
a stim a day keeps the doctor awake supporting circuit boards that can hold 4 electron tubes, the electrical stimulator provides a variety of functions. use a forestry soldering iron on an intricate circuit board to set four slots worth of electron tubes. the tubes' capabilities are listed here as percentages:

iron et -> +0.5 production
diamantine et -> +1.5 production
apatine et -> 1.5x pollination (max 5x)
obsidian et -> 0.8x lifespan
lapis et -> 1.5x lifespan (max 5x)
blazing et -> simulates hellish temperature
golden et -> 1.5x mutation rate (max 5x)
tin et -> 0.4x territory (min 0.1) & -0.1 production
bronze et -> 1.5x territory (max 5x)

genetic decay is also increased by 50% for all of them. this affects how long until ignoble bees die off, so don't worry about it if your bees are pristine.

remember that lifespan is represented by ticks, not time. you need a world accelerator if you want a lifespan that is really less than 1 tick.

[note]breeder's notes:
12x golden ets and 20x obsidian ets across eight of these will make a super breeding party alveary; it will spike your mutation chances while dramatically decreasing lifespan. if you have been using the oblivion frame in an apiary to shorten lifespan for breeding, then this *does not* replace that because you cannot use world accelerators in alvearies. so the shortest you can reduce a bee's life cycle to is 1 tick = 27 seconds. on the other hand, dramatically increasing the mutation rate in the alveary may be faster for crossbreeding.

production apiarist's notes:
alternately, you can slam down three of these with:
* 10x diamantine
* 2x iron
that'll take you right up to the production limit. any higher and you risk your pristine princesses turning ignoble from overwork.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 4, "oredict": "", "id": "extrabees:alveary", "resolved": {"id": "i:extrabees:alveary:4", "name": "electrical stimulator", "mod": "extrabees", "registry": "alveary", "icon": 5454, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 4, "shard": "8d334eba3942e39c", "recipes": 1}, "label": "electrical stimulator"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 8, "damage": 3, "oredict": "", "id": "forestry:thermionictubes", "resolved": {"id": "i:forestry:thermionictubes:3", "name": "iron electron tube", "mod": "forestry", "registry": "thermionictubes", "icon": 7406, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 3, "shard": "216338f0c8d5336f", "recipes": 2}, "label": "iron electron tube"}}}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 26, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:26", "name": "lootbag (bees advanced)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21221, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 26, "shard": "9fa6bf04b41dd27d", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (bees advanced)"}}}}

name: Alvearies
text:
alvearies the alveary is an advanced variant of the apiary. the alveary allows for combs to be produced faster due to its natural speed increase to production (as well as the ability to add up to six frames via the extra bees frame housings) and due to its ability to be modified by other blocks.

it is possible to adjust the internal temperature of the alveary using the alveary heater or alveary fan in order to accommodate bees that require hotter or colder climates.

certain bees will not produce their specialty items unless they are jubilant. this requires matching their preferred temperature/humidity, without any genetic modifiers. some bees also need a block of something beneath them as well.

it is also possible to use mutators to increase chances of mutation, alveary lighting and alveary rain shield to allow bees without the nocturnal and tolerant flyer traits to work during the night and rain, respectively, and the swarmer to use excess royal jelly to create princesses that last for a limited number of generations.

[note]if you're mutating bees that need a specific block in it, you need to place the required block under the middle bottom, and have the one directly above be a normal alveary block.[/note] {"0": text:
are the bees buzzing, or screaming? these frames cause mutations at an increased rate. they're super useful.

about the stats on frames you see when holding shift, you'll note that some have a different number in brackets next to them, this means that this is the maximum they can be stacked. this only applies to the extra bees ones.

the stats on the frames are also multiplicative instead of additive, so after 4 frames in an alveary, soul frames will max out. on the other hand, accelerated frames will take 9 to get there, but you can just keep on going.

name: Breeding Bees Into Oblivion
text:
breeding bees into oblivion if bee breeding is a dice game, then these are the biggest factors you'd control to win:

1. fertility: how many dice you can roll each turn.
2. mutation rate: how good of a roll you need to make.
3. lifespan: how often you can play the game.

the oblivion frame dramatically helps with #3 by reducing the bee's lifespan to the point that you can play the breeding dice game in one "tick" of 27.5 seconds. a bee with the "shortest" lifespan trait cycles for 10 ticks (275 seconds), so you'd minimally cut the cycle by a whole order of magnitude!

you can find oblivion frames in stronghold libraries. this is how you can get them in the early game for very aggressive bee breeding. later, you can make them from dragon eggs. these frames are very precious and you don't want their durability to run out. a typical repair method is to use a thaumic restorer on them.

wait, to find a stronghold reliably, i need some eyes of ender, and that's an hv-tier chemical reactor recipe! if you happen to have a large chemical reactor, remember that it overclocks perfectly, so you can crank er' up with a bunch of mv-tier energy input hatches.

the oblivion bee meta

the oblivion bee meta can be enough to breed most bees quickly. you could do the whole bee breeding quest line with it, but you can ultimately improve on it with alvearies and genetic modification. what you need for this meta is:

1. an apiary
2. an oblivion frame
3. some way to repair the frame (typically: thaumic restorer)
4. a beealyzer and a lot of honey

this is a hands-on process. you don't automatically send the princess and drones back through because you need to watch the oblivion frame's durability. you inspect all the offspring bees after each cycle and hand-pick which to try next after a pass through the beealyzer.

you can accelerate the apiary with a world accelerator. [warn]be sure to protect the world accelerator and supporting equipment from rain![/warn] you can use glass or a breakable clear glass so the apiary can still see the sky while the world accelerator is protected. if you need to use batteries, you can use a state cell to draw out a button pulse to the world accelerator so it runs juuust long enough for an accelerated cycle. {"0": {"autoconsume": lighting - can work day and night
alveary heater - increases temperature a flat 30% each (needs power)
alveary fan - decreases temperature a flat 20% each (needs power)
alveary hygroregulator[sic] - has two modes, water and lava
lava - temp+10%, humidity-20%
water - temp-10%, humidity+20%

unfortunately, there's no way to make them like caves with a block. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, name: Droning On
text:
droning on finally! you can hack bees*! you have two choices, and you will only ever need one. either way you go, you will hatch the modified drone using an incubator that's been loaded with bacteria vector afterwards.

both scale their requirements by the number of genes you intend to apply to a single larvae.

the inoculator

run time: 10 minutes per gene
rf cost: 600,000 rf per gene
rf/t: 50
bacteria vector: 15 mb per gene.

this one has a lower power and recipe cost at the expense of needing bacteria vector, created by incubating bacteria and blaze powder, to transfer the gene into organisms. the consumption for bacteria vector is quite low.

it is also slooooow.. 

the splicer

run time: 1 minute per gene
rf cost: 12,000,000 rf per gene
rf/t: 1,000

the splicer is much like the inoculator in function, however it has the benefit of not requiring any liquid. its power consumption is terrifying compared to the inoculator, but overall it only consumes twice the rf despite gobbling it much faster.

*or trees and flowers via their pollen, or butterflies via their caterpillars. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 1, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 3, "oredict": "", "id": "genetics:machine", "resolved": {"id": "i:genetics:machine:3", "name": "inoculator", "mod": "genetics", "registry": "machine", "icon": 8026, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 3, "shard": "41c41d90ee186e31", "recipes": 1}, "label": "inoculator"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "genetics:advmachine", "resolved": {"id": "i:genetics:advmachine:0", "name": "splicer", "mod": "genetics", "registry": "advmachine", "icon": 8016, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "1b9f522604b557dd", "recipes": 1}, "label": "splicer"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 8, "damage": 772, "oredict": "", "id": "binniecore:containercylinder", "resolved": {"id": "i:binniecore:containercylinder:772", "name": "bacteria vector cylinder", "mod": "binniecore", "registry": "containercylinder", "icon": 3325, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 772, "shard": "ba73856c823ed97f", "recipes": 1}, "label": "bacteria vector cylinder"}}}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 27, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "tag": {"ench": {"0": {"id": 35, "lvl": 3}}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (enhancedlootbags:lootbag, metadata 27)"}}}}

name: Fluorescent Dye
text:
fluorescent dye here is another one requiring ingredients you'll want to passively generate. the sequencer needs one (1) fluorescent dye per gene it sequences. each one is made from one of each tossed into a mixer:

* redstone
* glowstone
* orange dye
* yellow dye
* molten blaze (from blaze powder)

name: Ghetto Biome Changing
text:
ghetto biome changing if you don't want to change the biome to a specific one, and just want a neutral environment for your bees, maybe using nodes is for you. you can try planting a silverwood sapling to get one with a pure node, or use other methods to move one.

keep in mind a 'bare' pure node won't change anything unless it has victus. you can try to use sinister or tainted, but...no refunds. these nodes have a radius of 11. to change the biome back, use an ethereal bloom (radius of 7). keep in mind that both pech and wisps spawn in 'magical' type biomes. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Growth Medium
text:
growth medium the binnie's genetics machines will rely on growth medium in either a little, or a lot. if you can't make too much of it, then you'll need to rely on other passive generation to keep the machines constantly supplied for researching genes. if you can make a lot of growth medium, then you can use it in a closed loop in incubators to duplicate some of the mod's resources you have previously produced just once.

it requires:
* sugar: the easy one here, and remember multiple bee species can produce it too.
* bones (whole bones, not meal): mob farm, animal traps, goofy conversions.
* wood ash: smelt some saplings.
* mulch: there are a lot of ways to do this, but consider peat bees since you're already going for the bees.

this quest is just a little nudge that you should passively produce growth medium, which means being able to passively produce all of these ingredients. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 4, "oredict": "", "id": "genetics:misc", "resolved": {"id": "i:genetics:misc:4", "name": "growth medium", "mod": "genetics", "registry": "misc", "icon": 8033, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 4, "shard": "6d3b88a32a23971f", "recipes": 4}, "label": "growth medium"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 16, "damage": 4, "oredict": "", "id": "genetics:misc", "resolved": {"id": "i:genetics:misc:4", "name": "growth medium", "mod": "genetics", "registry": "misc", "icon": 8033, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 4, "shard": "6d3b88a32a23971f", "recipes": 4}, "label": "growth medium"}}}}

name: IAADDS
text: iaadds aka the mega apiary. it has three primary modes (change with screwdriver) and two operation modes (change with shift+screwdriver): input mode: does not take power. put your queens in the input bus to put them in the internal buffer. output mode: does not take power. will give your bees back to the output bus. operating mode - normal: the processing time is 5 seconds. uses 1 amp luv per queen. all bees are affected by 64x acceleration and 8 production upgrades as well as a genetic stabilizer upgrade. the iaadds also simulates a perfect environment for all bees. you can provide royal jelly to increase the outputs. 1 royal jelly grants 5% bonus per bee. they will be consumed on each start of operation and be applied to that operation only. the maximum bonus is 200%. the normal bee stats still apply of course, though the iaadds is able to provide a perfect environment for any bee. operating mode - swarmer: in this mode you can only insert 1 queen. the iaadds will then slowly produce ignoble princesses for 100 royal jelly per operation. the base processing time is 1 minute but you can overclock this process. the base usage is 1 amp iv. name: Incubator
text:
incubator the incubator is a general production machine that serves two purposes:

1. hatching (modified) larvae into drones at the end of the whole process.
2. heating items and liquids to produce different resources you will need in different parts of the entire research and modification process.

there are up to five different resources you can create from incubators:

1. liquid growth medium: water + growth medium
2. bacteria: liquid growth medium + wheat or more bacteria + growth medium
3. enzyme: bacteria + sugar
4. bacteria vector: bacteria + blaze powder or more bacteria vector + growth medium
5. polymerizing bacteria: bacteria + bonemeal or more polymerizing bacteria + growth medium

three of the recipes can optionally be extended by injecting them with more growth medium instead of using a different ingredient. if you're able to produce a bunch of growth medium, consider "priming" incubators for these outputs and then switching them to use growth medium indefinitely in a feedback loop.

enzyme is usually produced in a pipeline from bacteria, which is in turn produced from liquid growth medium.

bacteria vector is only used by the inoculator to modify larvae, and you don't need it if you use a splicer instead.

ps: you'll also need a source for ethanol for the genepool and the isolator. this technology line has a drinking problem.

pps: blaze powder also comes up with at least fluorescent dye later. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 2, "damage": 2, "oredict": "", "id": "genetics:labmachine", "resolved": {"id": "i:genetics:labmachine:2", "name": "incubator", "mod": "genetics", "registry": "labmachine", "icon": 8020, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 2, "shard": "4432521ea74214e6", "recipes": 1}, "label": "incubator"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 2, "oredict": "", "id": "genetics:labmachine", "resolved": {"id": "i:genetics:labmachine:2", "name": "incubator", "mod": "genetics", "registry": "labmachine", "icon": 8020, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 2, "shard": "4432521ea74214e6", "recipes": 1}, "label": "incubator"}}}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 26, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "tag": {"ench": {"0": {"id": 35, "lvl": 3}}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (enhancedlootbags:lootbag, metadata 26)"}}}}

name: Isolator
text:
isolator the isolator will take ethanol and enzyme to extract a single gene from a candidate bee. sometimes it gets hungry and eats the bee too. don't feed it any bees you won't mind getting destroyed!

you must provide a blank sequence to store the output gene. this will be stored with a "faint" level of strength that can be sequenced slowly, or made stronger to be sequenced faster by passing the sequence through a polymerizer.

the exact gene you get from the bee is going to be a random choice from that bee's genome. you won't know what it is until you run it through the sequencer. it will then be accessible forever in the gene database.

you can wind up isolating the same gene from the same bee multiple times. it's just bad luck. they won't be isolated in any particular order.

the sequencer will drain the container back into a blank sequence, so you can feed them back into the isolator. you only ever need to make a few blank sequences because you can just loop like this indefinitely. if, however, you have a sequenced gene and want to make it blank again immediately, then just run it through your smelting/furnace device of choice. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "genetics:machine", "resolved": {"id": "i:genetics:machine:0", "name": "isolator", "mod": "genetics", "registry": "machine", "icon": 8023, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "38fc3c5af913d437", "recipes": 1}, "label": "isolator"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 5, "oredict": "", "id": "genetics:misc", "resolved": {"id": "i:genetics:misc:5", "name": "blank sequence", "mod": "genetics", "registry": "misc", "icon": 8034, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 5, "shard": "85afc024d34327fc", "recipes": 2}, "label": "blank sequence"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 16, "damage": 5, "oredict": "", "id": "genetics:misc", "resolved": {"id": "i:genetics:misc:5", "name": "blank sequence", "mod": "genetics", "registry": "misc", "icon": 8034, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 5, "shard": "85afc024d34327fc", "recipes": 2}, "label": "blank sequence"}}}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 26, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "tag": {"ench": {"0": {"id": 35, "lvl": 3}}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (enhancedlootbags:lootbag, metadata 26)"}}}}

name: Living It Larvae
text:
living it larvae to play with binnie's genetics with bees, you'll need some larvae, and a hatchery block inside an alveary is the only way to make them. there's a little side perk for having them: they produce at a much faster rate than you'd get from any one species' drones. those leftovers can feed into the gene pool for extra raw dna. just remember to keep a few larvae on standby for the actual genetic modification!

the bee you use in the alveary should be whatever you intend to modify. it can be any kind if you intend to overwrite all the traits, but you probably should have it either be:

1. some new species which will have everything else overwritten.
2. some existing superbee that you want to switch to a new species.

the larvae will eventually be hatched in an incubator into a modified drone based on whatever genetic traits you have inserted into it. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 5, "oredict": "", "id": "extrabees:alveary", "resolved": {"id": "i:extrabees:alveary:5", "name": "hatchery", "mod": "extrabees", "registry": "alveary", "icon": 5455, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 5, "shard": "e28aa12300978aa2", "recipes": 1}, "label": "hatchery"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:optional_retrieval"}} {}

name: Making Bees More Comfortable
text:
making bees more comfortable the acclimatiser can widen the temperature tolerance of a bee. this is technically a little side quest with binnie's genetics machines, but these alterations are permanent and carry into their genome.

note that the bee's species determines its favored temperature for jubilance. you can't use this to make a bee produce secondary products in a different climate.

drones, princesses, queens, and even larvae can go in these machines. this means you can boost one queen and be set for life for that bee.

(you can also use it for pollen, butterflies, caterpillars, plants...)

when a specimen's tolerance has been pushed as far as it can go, that bee will go in the output slot. the typical thing to do here is pipe the bee automatically into another acclimatiser like a little trauma conga line. at the end, the bee should be able to tolerate being anywhere.

here's what you can use for what at what factors:
* temperature down
  * ice: 0.75
  * snowball: 0.15
* temperature up
  * lava (canned!): 0.75
  * blaze powder: 0.5
  * blaze rod: 0.75
* humidity up:
  * water (canned!): 0.75
* humidity down:
  * sand: 0.15

fluid containers are consumed. if only you had a waxy substance in overabundance you could use for throwaway fluids!

[note]the ole' "both trick": if your specimen already has at least up/down 1 for temperature or humidity, acclimatising it in the opposite direction will make it both 1. the trick is that it'll now grow both ways for the price of expanding only in one.

so, if handling canned water and lava is annoying, and you can start with up 1 for temperature and humidity, then you can just bombard it with temperature and humidity lowering steps. it'll switch to both 1 and then eventually both 5 without ever raising temperature or humidity again.

this lets you skip out on canning liquids, you sly dog.

name: Mutatron
text:
