name: Clean Implosions?!
text:
clean implosions?! introducing the bigger (and better) implosion compressor, the electric implosion compressor.

the electric implosion compressor does not need any explosive and only needs electricity, isn't that very nice!

furthermore it gains extra parallels 4^(tier - 1) based on the containment block used in the middle.

tier 1: neutronium block
tier 2: infinity block
tier 3: transcendent metal block
tier 4: spacetime block
tier 5: universium block

[note]the minimum allowed energy hatch tier is one tier below the recipe tier, so you'll want to start with at least 2 uhv energy hatches for now.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, unlike with the singleblock, you get a base 2.5x speed bonus and a 20% eu discount on all recipes. you unlock an extra 5% increase to both speed and eu discount per coil tier.

as a bonus, the ltr provides 8 parallels per voltage tier, and 2 additional parallels per tier of solenoid on top of that.

name: Hulk Smash!
I Think I'm Going to be Sick
text:
i think i'm going to be sick the industrial centrifuge is the best solution for handling the thousands of ores being produced by the multiblock ore drill. you will eventually want to have an array of these running, though one or two is fine to start.

this multiblock gives you 4-8 parallels per voltage tier, operates at 2-3x the speed, and grants a 10% eu discount. this makes it a far better alternative to both singleblock centrifuges and the steam separator.

the parallel and speed modifiers start at their minimums and increase to their maximums as the centrifuge gains momentum.

the centrifuge will gain 1% momentum every 10 ticks while running 
(50s to go from 0% -> 100%)

on the other hand, it will lose 2% momentum every 5 ticks while idle
(12.5s to go from 100% -> 0%) {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, name: Industrial Sledgehammer
Insane Voltage Multiblocks
text:
insane voltage multiblocks upon reaching the land of iv machinery, you can put together even more multis and speed up your automation!

many of the multiblocks from iv tier onwards use special alloys, which either need to be cooked like any ingots you've used before (in a furnace or ebf), but there are also alloys which have to be made in the alloy blast smelter (abs), as a fluid, which then needs to be solidified.

the multis that need abs alloys are further down. to unlock their quests, you will first need to craft the abs itself. however, there is a large assortment of machines you can craft without it, just by having the respective iv singleblock equivalent and some other resources.

those will be here... but you might be able to find some more, if you look closely through nei. good luck! {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: L.A.T.E.X. Cable Coater
text:
l.a.t.e.x. cable coater the laminated application and thermal enclosure exocoater (l.a.t.e.x.) is a multiblock dedicated to coating cables.

you will be making a lot of cables during your playthrough... why bog down your assembler when you can use the latex instead? the latex gives 2x the speed with a 15% eu discount, and generously offers 8 parallels per voltage tier.

if that's not convincing enough, you also get an additive 6.25% rubber discount per item pipe casing tier.

name: STEAM-POWERED BREAKTHROUGH
text:
steam-powered breakthrough you should have quite the collection of single block steam machines by now. while these may have gotten you through processing small amounts of materials, there will be a time when you will have to process a multitude of items. this is where multiblocks come in.

while these multiblocks have a material cost that is way higher than their single block counterparts, they have certain bonuses: they use less steam, and they can process recipes in parallel, which means that a single recipe cycle can craft multiple items at once, if the steam provided is enough to sustain it.

they do however have some quirks that need to be taken care of:

-these multiblocks require very specific i/o blocks, use only those that are part of the quest
-they process up to 8 items, where the basic tier is made of bronze and high pressure tier is made of steel (checkout the multiblock preview in nei which will show you different levels of tiers)
-the tier and amount of parallel processing can be seen via waila if you are looking at the controller block

[note]with this quest, you have started your journey with mass processing. however, don't get too excited quite yet. while there are some multiblocks accessible in the steam age, most of them only unlock in ev or later, including better versions of these multiblocks.[/note] {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Spinmatron-2737
text:
spinmatron-2737 tired of spamming centrifuges already? 

alas, with your newfound zpm technology you can finally fabricate a centrifuge with some real power; the spinmatron-2737!

the spinmatron comes with a litany of advantages compared to the regular centrifuge multiblock, including a 3x speed boost, a 30% reduction in eu usage, and a malleable number of parallels.

unlike the generic turbine that comes stock in a normal centrifuge, the spinmatron graciously allows you to choose the quality of the turbines that go into the machine. you can add between 2-8 turbines depending on the machine tier, each turbine will increase the parallel amount by [4 * turbine material tier]. (you'll want to avoid using smaller, non-huge turbines!)

this efficiency comes at a cost however, and will require [recipe tier * 10] l/s of kerosene in order to run. this can optionally be switched out with biocatalyzed propulsion fluid for a 1.25x parallel multiplier once you've reached uev.

additionally there are three modes that come unique to the spinmatron:

- light -> gives increased speed in exchange for only being able to process [voltage tier - 3] recipes

- normal -> no changes

- heavy -> grants the ability to craft heavy mode dependent recipes in exchange for reducing your parallels by 32x and consuming biocatalyzed propulsion fluid.

[note]checkout the tooltip for more information![/note]

name: You Smell Like a Distillery!
text:
you smell like a distillery! this bad boy will tremendously boost the byproducts of your cracked fuel or pyrolyse oven. this way you can make industrial tnt, polyethylene, polytetrafluoroethylene and other plastics more efficiently. you'll also need this for the platline.

you'll need to make ev circuits in a cleanroom to build this machine.

for hatches, you can choose your own tier. 1 mv energy hatch is enough for most of the useful recipes. 2 mv energy hatches or 1 hv energy hatch will cover almost all the rest. you will also need 1 input hatch, and at least 5 output hatches. an output bus will capture any solid outputs.

nei is not great for determining which cracked fuel option is the best. instead, visit the oil cracking unit wiki page linked below for a complete list of all the fractions in a nice, convenient format!

name: 4x Steel
A Beginner's Guide to Particle Physics
text:
a beginner's guide to particle physics if you've built the source chamber already, you may have noticed that particles aren't produced as items, like gt++ ones are.

instead they're transmitted through beamline pipes from multi to multi, similar to real life.

each stream of particles transmitted, or "beam", has four properties:
- particle: the type of particle carried by the beam
- energy: the amount of energy the particles have
- focus: out of 100, how focused the beam is
- amount: a measure of the number of particles in the beam

note that you can see info about a multi's input and output beams by using a tricorder on the controller.

for the recipes you'll be interested in, i.e. the ones that actually produce items, there'll be a threshold for allowed input beam energy, a minimum focus value, and an amount value which determines recipe time (more on that in the target chamber quest).
take a look some tc recipes for an example of this.

have a higgs boson. to hang on your wall. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 3, "oredict": "", "id": "gtnhlanth:particle", "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (gtnhlanth:particle, metadata 3)"}}}}

name: A Little More Sigma (Squared)
text:
a little more sigma (squared) eventually, your lhc will start making rarer and rarer particles. you may find that they appear in large bursts as single particle packets with very high amounts, but not very often. the beam stabilizer allows you to capture these large packets and redistribute them over time as a continuous series of smaller packets with a lower amount.

name: A Not So Useful Scanner...
A Very Useful Scanner
text:
a very useful scanner the portable scanner is a tool capable of showing advanced information about almost every block in the game. in order to function, the tool needs to be charged first. it can hold up to 400k eu and accept 128 eu/t or less. this is mv tier.

it can scan crops by right-clicking them.

it can scan machines from gregtech, giving information about current progress, the stored energy, efficiency, problems and cpu-load - be sure to check the full chat window for additional details.

for any block in the game it scans, it gives information about its id, metadata, position in the world and hardness value. it also gives information about pollution level in the chunk the scanned block belongs to.

in addition it shows when the cleanroom has reached its 100 percent efficiency level. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 32762, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.01", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.metaitem.01:32762", "name": "portable scanner", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.metaitem.01", "icon": 41155, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 32762, "shard": "92d8f21019478e12", "recipes": 1}, "label": "portable scanner"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"choices": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 5, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:5", "name": "lootbag (tier 2 mv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21254, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 5, "shard": "86c93816ff53d76b", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 2 mv)"}, "1": {"count": 5, "damage": 32764, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.01", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.metaitem.01:32764", "name": "braintech aerospace advanced reinforced duct tape fal-84", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.metaitem.01", "icon": 41157, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 32764, "shard": "6961f59376cbdf7f", "recipes": 5}, "label": "braintech aerospace advanced reinforced duct tape fal-84"}}, "ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:choice"}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 5, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:cointechniciani", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:cointechniciani:0", "name": "coin "the technician 10"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "cointechniciani", "icon": 20788, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "53205e7d44e6e7e5", "recipes": 2}, "label": "coin "the technician 10""}}}}

name: Advanced MB Construction
text:
advanced mb construction the ability to rotate mbs and view a structure hologram has been sto-borrowed from tectech, giving you greater freedom to build the way you want! (until we nerf wallsharing at least)

unlike tt, you can use a normal wrench for this, just aim at the front center of a controller (or one of the other sides if you want to. you just need to aim for the part of the grid with the mark) and right-click or shift-right-click. the first rotates it clockwise, the latter flips it. if you want to change the facing of the controller itself, do that the normal way.

use a multiblock structure hologram projector or mshp to visualize the structure, pay attention to the bottom left for structure details. for multiblocks that accept multiple types of tiered components or have a variable size, the number of mshps you hold in your hand will decide which tier is shown in the hologram.

[note]if you don't get it, try placing a controller, wrenching it, and using the mshp on it.[/note]

while it's now possible to build a sideways ebf, or even build one into the floor, not everything can be rotated.

[note]ps: we did get permission, that was just a little joke.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, name: Air-Filter
text:
air-filter electric air filter

this wonderful multiblock comes in 3 versions: t1 for lv, t2 for late hv and t3 for iv.

it has 2 modes:

- a normal mode, where one chunk is processed at a time in the working area, in order, per pollution cleaning cycle.
- a random mode, where the chunk being cleaned is picked randomly between all the polluted chunks in the working area.
 to cycle between the modes, right-click on the controller with a screwdriver.

the controller can change its working area from 1x1 to (2*tier+1) x (2*tier+1) chunks. to do that, right-click with a screwdriver on the controller while sneaking. the default size is the maximum working area.

the pollution removal calculation is equals (by default) to 30 * bonusmultitier * muffler hatches * turbine eff * multiblock eff * 2.5 ^ effective tier where:

- bonusmultitier is a boost given by the multiblock tier. t1 is 1 (0%), t2 is 1.05 (5%) and t3 is 1.10 (10%)

- muffler hatches is the amount of muffler hatches on the multiblock (up to 8)

- turbine eff is the efficiency of the turbine chosen to run the multi. it won't run if there is no turbine in the controller.

- multiblock eff is the efficiency of the multiblock (100% when no maintenance issue, -10% per issue)

- effective tier is the effective tier of the multi: the minimum tier between the electric tier of the multi and the tier of the muffler hatches.

the pollution cleaning is boosted by two (by default) when using an absorption filter. when added in the input bus, it will be consumed and used for 30 (by default) successful pollution cleaning cycle. if a chunk with no pollution in it is processed, that doesn't count as successful, and the multi decides that a chunk has no pollution if the pollution is below 10k gibbl (by default). after the 30th successful pollution cleaning cycle, the output bus will give a dirty absorption filter.

to know if an absorption filter is present and how many remaining cycles there are, use a portable scanner on the controller.

a pollution cycle lasts 10s, and the cleaning is done every second.

[note]p.s. if you procrastinated making one of these and make a t2 or t3 instead, the quest will still complete![/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, name: Algae Pond
text:
algae pond sustainability. it's not the name of the game... but it could be!

if you've ever wanted to generate many chemicals from a single source, you've probably looked at oil or benzene. however, there's also the algae farm.

each tier, starting from ulv (at 50s per batch) through iv (25s per batch), reduces the time it takes to produce algae by about 5 seconds, and then beyond that each tier will cut the duration in half. the production time can also randomly double or triple, but this happens relatively rarely.

each tier increase also adds to the amount of algae you get in a single cycle, as well as the type of algae produced. each cycle gives out an exact amount as well as a bonus amount 10% of the time. the algae farm also accepts compost, which you can make from the algae itself, to boost the multi's tier by one. this might be expensive at the start, but it's heavily recommended in most cases. you can get regular algae and green algae starting at ulv; brown algae starts appearing at hv, golden-brown algae at ev, and red algae at iv, though higher tier algae appears in very small quantities at first.

to find out more about the exact output quantities and timings, please see the wiki: [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/algae_farm[/url]

the algae can be used for various chemicals like methane, ammonia, sulfuric acid, sodium carbonate, ethylene, lithium chloride, and even some power-generating fluids. you typically need a chemical plant for that. in iv tier you can also combine green algae with glowstone to get glowing coral and make sunnarium from that. if you're curious about all the processing chains, look them up on nei: quests to cover them are coming up, possibly with more recipes that don't need the chemical plant. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": name: An Industrial Mobfarm
text: an industrial mobfarm extreme entity crusher is your newest and probably best spawner/grinder, with this you are not only able to get drops without any tps issues but also with style and extreme efficiency. of course that depends on the quality of your sword; damage, looting, and durability are the only stats that will translate towards the efficacy of the machine. (weapon is optional however, there are spikes in it after all!) will occasionally spawn infernal mobs if possible and will use x8 power with every infernal spawn so you need to take that into account! if you are actively using the blood magic "well of suffering" ritual to power your altar, this multi may be used in combination with it to 'generate' and 'kill' mobs automatically for life essence, so you don't need a setup involving an actual spawner! notes: will generate 120l of liquid xp with every cycle. in case of any problems with multiblock animation just use soldering iron on the machine to disable it. read the tooltip! there are a few unique quality of life settings that you may find of use. name: Assembly Line
text:
assembly line the assembly line (or 'assline') is an important machine for high tier components in luv tier and above for making motors, pistons, robot arms, pumps and many more.

the multiblock can be 5-16 blocks long. the minimum length required depends on the number of components and fluids required by the recipe it's crafting. a length of 11 blocks will fit 80 percent of all recipes in gtnh.

the bottom layer must have on one outer side all the input hatches for fluids (4), in the bottom middle layer input buses for items (10), and on the end 1 output bus. also on the bottom outer layer must be one maintenance hatch. the rest is solid steel machine casings.

the second layer on the outer sides left and right are reinforced glass and in the middle center assembly line casing.

the third layer has on the left and right grate machine casings and in the middle assembler machine casings (note the name change!). the assembly line control block and data access hatch are on the opposite edge from the input hatches - not at the end with the output bus.

the fourth layer is a single line of solid steel machine casings in the middle (11), with two energy hatches for power. once you have it built, you can replace the two iv energy hatches with 1 luv energy hatch.

automating the assline is a difficult challenge! you can use advanced tools like sfm or opencomputers, but maybe you can figure out how to do it with enderio or just ae2.

for more details on using the assembly line, check out the wiki page [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/assembly_line[/url]

[note]btw the input buses are ulv to help with your automating, if you don't want to automate it, you can use higher tier ones, unlike the cal.[/note]

[note]you can have up to 16 input buses. if you use the full 16 you should put the output bus to the side.[/note]

Automation, Tier 1
text:
automation, tier 1 do you want to automate your smeltery because you're planning to make stacks and stacks of glass blocks?

no problem, craft a large bronze pipe and place it under the faucet. make sure to connect the pipe to the faucet using a wrench. now the molten fluid will flow inside the pipe. under or next to the pipe you have to place the casting basins or tables.

a hopper and a chest underneath will auto-output products from the casting blocks.

name: Bacterial Vat
text:
bacterial vat the bacterial vat is a unique multiblock machine with its own recipes. but it also has advanced versions of many brewery recipes.

the vat isn't mandatory in this tier, but there are many useful recipes and you'll need it later on, so let's build one!

all recipes require a culture, some recipes require a specific glass-tier.

the culture is made in a biolab and put in the controller.

name: Better Than Duct Tape
text:
better than duct tape using a soldering iron tool to remove the "burned out circuits" message is cheaper than duct tape.

the soldering iron requires one soldering material item and 10,000 eu. valid soldering materials are fine wires, rods, and ingots made from either tin, lead, or soldering alloy. the soldering iron will consume the first such material it finds in the player's inventory. since you'll likely have more than enough, fine wires of soldering alloy are probably best.

other uses for the soldering iron:

- it will adjust the redstone strength from weak to strong emitted by gt machines.
- while holding it all pipes, wires, and cables will look very small, so that you can see everything past them, and also be sure of the exact connections.
- shift right-clicking on some machines with it will allow you to toggle multi-stack input, which can be very useful for automating certain assembler recipes.

for the other problems other tools are necessary. keep in mind that you can put all needed tools in a toolbox to fix all problems in one click.

possible problems                tool to fix
"pipe is loose."                    wrench
"screws are loose."           screwdriver
"something is stuck."            soft mallet
"platings are dented."           hammer
"circuitry burned out."    soldering iron
"that doesn't belong there."   crowbar

[warn]in order to complete this quest, you'll need to charge the soldering iron after you craft it.
the quest accepts lv, mv, or hv tier soldering irons.[/warn] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 160, "oredict": "craftingtoolsolderingiron", "id": "gregtech:gt.metatool.01", "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (gregtech:gt.metatool.01, metadata 160)"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"choices": {"0": {"count": 3, "damage": 4, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:4", "name": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21242, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 4, "shard": "3cff4d8e3920defe", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)"}, "1": {"count": 64, "damage": 19314, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.02", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.metaitem.02:19314", "name": "fine soldering alloy wire", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.metaitem.02", "icon": 43538, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 19314, "shard": "638f6219c32c05d0", "recipes": 4}, "label": "fine soldering alloy wire"}}, "ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:choice"}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 5, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:cointechniciani", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:cointechniciani:0", "name": "coin "the technician 10"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "cointechniciani", "icon": 20788, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "53205e7d44e6e7e5", "recipes": 2}, "label": "coin "the technician 10""}}}}

name: Catalyzing Miracles
text:
catalyzing miracles the qft uses the kind of catalyst that the chemical plant also does. however, like the plants that have awakened draconium coils or higher, it does not consume the catalyst's durability on recipe finish, behaving more like a real-life catalyst that is regenerated after being used. this makes the catalysts used here more expensive to craft, as was the case with the infinite mutation catalyst for mutated living solder, which is meant to be used only with those coils that make it last forever.

given that there is no durability loss, it would seem only one catalyst needs to be crafted. however, there are two reasons for this to not be true: firstly, each qft recipe uses a different catalyst; secondly, the qft checks for parallels by counting the amount of catalysts it has in its bulk catalyst housing for the recipe in question (limit of 2,147,483,647). this system makes it so that crafting 1 of the correct type of catalyst is required to unlock a recipe, but making more is completely optional and only changes the speed at which the multi crafts, provided it gets enough eu input.

every catalyst needs some of the materials that it unlocks in the qft, which is to say, the original processing line will have to be used to craft the catalyst that allows the player to skip it in the qft. this applies to every recipe, and in turn every line that can be skipped.

to improve the general speed of processing, your one option is to get more parallels with catalysts. the other, more complicated way is to boost the chances of a successful output by adding more energy to the system, but in a special way: instead of using direct eu, using it to create a powerful plasma works to improve the qft processing.

if the correct plasmas are added, the boosting will work, but it is also possible to upgrade the structure itself to perform chemistry skips that are not possible with the base qft. these upgrades rely on more advanced and powerful materials, mainly in the material progression of dtpf recipes. however, those existing materials are not enough, because the quantum stabilization can't be maintained with those “foreign” substances. luckily, the qft itself can produce the items needed to build the upgraded casings, and these items are outputs of some of the skips performed in the multi. it begins by allowing the much simpler production of already-owned materials but, in this process, it unlocks entirely new materials that are useful to improve the structure itself.

there are three new items and four tiers in the structure. the first tier can be built without them, but every new tier needs a new item crafted in the tier before. these outputs are related to the recipe where they can be obtained, and they possess unique characteristics that, in real life, are only theoretical.

the first item you will need to craft is the hyper-stable self-healing adhesive. to craft this material, proceed with the glue/solder recipe by using the adhesion promoter catalyst. additionally, make these other catalysts to prove you're well set in your qft journey. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 16, "oredict": "", "id": "miscutils:item.basicgenericchemitem", "tag": {"catalyst": {"damage": 0, "maxdamage": 50}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (miscutils:item.basicgenericchemitem, metadata 16)"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 17, "oredict": "", "id": "miscutils:item.basicgenericchemitem", "tag": {"catalyst": {"damage": 0, "maxdamage": 50}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (miscutils:item.basicgenericchemitem, metadata 17)"}, "2": {"count": 1, "damage": 19, "oredict": "", "id": "miscutils:item.basicgenericchemitem", "tag": {"catalyst": {"damage": 0, "maxdamage": 50}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (miscutils:item.basicgenericchemitem, metadata 19)"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Cleanroom
text:
cleanroom if you want to make more advanced (and cheaper!) circuits, you will need a cleanroom. the cleanroom is an interesting multiblock, because you will be placing other machines inside of the room!

the cleanroom is a hollow multiblock between 3x4x3 and 15x15x15 (wxhxl) blocks. the base does not need to be a square; a rectangular shape is fine. the top layer is built out of filter machine casings, except for the edges, which are plascrete blocks. the controller needs to be in the center of the top layer. if the width or length of the room are even, then it can be any one of the two (or four) middle blocks. the rest of the structure is built out of plascrete blocks.

up to 30% of those plascrete blocks can be replaced by other valid blocks or materials:

a reinforced door lets you get in and out of the cleanroom. make sure to keep the doors closed, or the cleanroom will rapidly lose efficiency. travel anchors and elevators also work, you can even embed them in the floor if you want to. you can also use ineffable glass as a "door" if you'd prefer.

in order to automate power and item transport through the walls, you can use cable diodes or machine hulls. just be really careful when upgrading your machines to a higher voltage. be sure to remove the machine hulls and diodes and replace them with the new power tier, or else you will be very sad. you don't need to do this for ones you only use to pass items through.

if you want to see inside, you can use any ev+ tier glass (for example, reinforced glass, managlass, or ineffable glass). if the cleanroom does not form, mind the 30% limit: often the problem is that you added too much glass.

finally, the cleanroom itself will need a maintenance and energy hatch to run. the power usage of this multiblock is a bit unusual. it starts out at 40 eu/t and then gradually goes down. but even when it uses 40 eu/t - which is usually mv - a single lv energy hatch suffices, because it accepts two amps of lv power. just keep in mind that this makes the cleanroom an exception, not the rule.

let's build a 5x5x5 room for now. you can expand it later as needed. give it power and let it run until it reaches 100% efficiency. below 100% efficiency, machines inside the cleanroom have a chance to void outputs, so you want to keep the cleanroom running at all times!

any maintenance issue reduces the maximum efficiency by 10%. monitor your cleanroom manually with waila or automatically with either an industrial information panel or a needs maintenance cover connected to a redstone powered light or howler alarm.

[note]multiblocks such as the large chemical reactor or hyper-intensity laser engraver don't need to be in a cleanroom. however, you will still need the cleanroom later on for other machines, like bio labs.[/note]

[note]other helpful hints: you can use an ae wireless connector or a transvector interface for item transport to avoid machine hulls, and use a higher tier energy hatch to reach 100% efficiency faster.[/note]

name: Decay Warehouse
text:
decay warehouse the decay warehouse stores a single type of radioactive isotope and allows it to decay over time. 

the decay speed of the isotope is dependent on its half-life.

isotopes will decay regardless of whether the warehouse is on or powered. 

the warehouse's capacity equals the chest's capacity divided by 400.

capacity of the multiblock for each chest:

super chest i: 10,000
super chest ii: 20,000
super chest iii: 40,000
super chest iv: 80,000
super chest v: 160,000
quantum chest i: 320,000
quantum chest ii: 640,000
quantum chest iii: 1,280,000
quantum chest iv: 2,560,000
quantum chest v: 5,368,000

[note]right click the controller with a screwdriver to dump stored isotopes into an output bus.

right click the controller with a plunger to empty it. [/note]

[warn]the warehouse's contents are voided when the controller is broken[/warn] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 15751, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:15751", "name": "decay warehouse", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 24101, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 15751, "shard": "f3a1757c0090a57d", "recipes": 1}, "label": "decay warehouse"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}, "1": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 1, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 135, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:135", "name": "super chest i", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 23587, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 135, "shard": "0b97a36f949e0633", "recipes": 3}, "label": "super chest i"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:optional_retrieval"}} {}

name: Digging Deep for Water
text:
digging deep for water is the water tank not cutting it anymore? have you set up in a dry biome and are in desperate need of more water? fear not, for the steam water pump can solve your issues! this multiblock is able to produce large amounts of water if fed with steam (1500l/s).

like other steam multiblocks, it can be upgraded by using steel frame boxes instead of bronze ones, which doubles the water output at no additional steam cost.

it is, however, still dependent on how humid the biome you are in is, so keep that in mind.

hint: you can find small lead ore in the nether or full ingots on the lowest floor of roguelike dungeons if you're lucky!

[note]p.s. the optional quest item count includes the cost for the controller. name: Don't Lose That Multiblock Miner!
Don't ask how this works
Draconic Development
Drones are not Drones!
text:
drones are not drones! ...but they can be just as industrious as bees. these new electric companions are the perfect partners for multiblock machines: maintenance, control, management—they can handle it all.

maintenance
the drone centre is a newly developed machine. it requires no power—simply place a drone into the input bus, and it will begin operation.

replacing the maintenance hatch on your multiblock machines with a drone downlink module will connect them to the drone network.

once activated, the drone centre will automatically scan for all downlink modules within range and attempt to establish a connection with them. as long as the drone centre remains active, all connected multiblock machines will [bold]never[/bold] suffer from annoying maintenance issues again!

[note]goodbye, my precious 256x superconductor base ingots that were lost due to maintenance failures...[/note]


entity drones
drones now exist as physical entities, unlocking several new features:

- when a maintenance issue occurs, a drone will deploy from the downlink module and perform a circular inspection flight around the affected machine.
- we've equipped drones with cameras! click the observe button in the gui to access a real-time video feed from the drone. as long as you are in the same dimension, you can connect to the drone regardless of distance.
- while in observation mode, the waila hud provides more information than normal. additionally, aim your crosshair at a machine and press g to remotely open its gui! this currently supports all gt machines and hatches. however, since drones are not equipped with robotic arms, item and fluid slots cannot be interacted with.


group control & statistics
the drone centre provides a powerful machine management interface, supporting grouping, remote observation, batch power control, and machine renaming:

- connected machines can be organized into up to 64 custom groups. groups can be renamed, and a machine may belong to multiple groups.
- after selecting a group, power control actions will be applied to all machines within that group. specifically, shift-clicking the shutdown button will set all machine controller covers to "disable" mode.
- by enabling the built-in production recorder, the drone centre can collect real-time statistics from all connected machines, including eu consumption, item throughput, and fluid throughput. all recorded data is stored directly inside the drone centre.


tiered drones
[warn]drones may crash during operation. the crash probability decreases from tier 1 to tier 3, and tier 3 and tier 4 drones will never crash.[/warn]

don't worry—if a backup drone is available in the input bus, the drone centre will consume it instantly.

using higher-tier drones increases the operating range of the drone centre:

  • drone (t1)
    - range: 128 blocks
    - crash chance: 1/28,800 per second (average ~8 hours)

  • drone (t2)
    - range: 512 blocks
    - crash chance: 1/172,800 per second (average ~48 hours)

  • drone (t3)
    - range: 4,096 blocks
    - crash chance: never

  • drone (t4)
    - range: 4,096 blocks (automatic) / infinite (matching key)
    - crash chance: never
    - cross-dimension: yes


to enable cross-dimensional connections with a t4 drone, configure matching keys on both the drone centre and the downlink module.

the downlink module can copy matching keys using a data stick.

&g&#ffd700&#ff4500our drones can now operate machines across other planets... initiating warp drive!&r


structure
refer to the nei structure preview to construct the new multiblock structure. there is also a new drone model in the centre!

name: EBF Info
text:
ebf info you can use a scanner to manually check how your ebf works, or you can make an information panel from nuclear control and always see the status. make a gt sensor kit and use it on the ebf controller. place the sensor card in your info panel. enable it with a redstone signal.

the gregtech sensor card can monitor gregtech machines like the ebf, turbines, and pyrolyse ovens. this is handy for keeping an eye on maintenance issues for multiblocks.

if you want to put the panels far from the machines they are monitoring, you will need range upgrades.

name: Expert MB-Construction
text:
expert mb-construction right-click the controller while sneaking will invoke an action called survival autoplace. this will attempt to build the multiblock with items from your inventory, provided the area this multi occupies is clear of obstacles. again, like hologram spawning, multiblocks that accept multiple types of tiered components or has variable length, the number of mshps you hold in hand will decide which tier of blocks will be placed. it will place correct amount of hatches for you, but will usually orient the hatches towards you, not perpendicular to the surface. it will just place casings for you if you don't have any hatches in inventory, unless this spot requires the use of a hatch (e.g. the top center spot of ebf).

survival autoplace can also take from your alternative inventories, or items that contain/link to an inventory. currently, this includes:
- adventure backpacks, either worn or as an item in inventory
- ae2 portable cells
- me networks connected via any ae2 wireless terminal with item access capabilities
- forestry backpacks
- ender chest inventory, if you have the ender backpack from backpacks mod. note: ordinary backpacks from the backpacks mod are not supported at the moment. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Focusing Science and Mystery
text:
focusing science and mystery this mechanic is completely optional, and never required for crafting. however, it's greatly incentivized when the number of parallels is high and when crafting the unique items that unlock higher tiers. “focusing”, in general, means to increase the chances of the outputs in a qft recipe, and it can be done in two ways, possibly both at the same time. each method uses a new plasma, both of which are crafted in a t4 fusion reactor by using other plasmas as the inputs, including one t3 plasma for each. these plasmas are neptunium and fermium and they can be used together, or individually.

when neptunium plasma is present, the current recipe can have one of the outputs focused. the specific output is chosen with a circuit in the input bus (this is the only thing circuits do for this multi), where circuit 1 is for the 1st output visible in nei, circuit 2 is for the 2nd output, and so on. it is up to the player to choose which output they want the most out of all the existing ones, and the fact that every recipe has multiple outputs is because of this mechanic.

when an output is successfully focused with neptunium, its chance increases by reducing the chance of all the other outputs. the logic for this change is as follows:

-> without focusing, the chance of each output is 100 / number of outputs;
-> if the casing tier matches the recipe tier, the chance of all other outputs is halved and the sum of those halves is added to the focused output (for example, 20/20/20/20/20 becomes 60/10/10/10/10);
-> if the casing tier is +1 over the recipe tier, halve the other outputs' chance again (for example, 60/10/10/10/10 becomes 80/5/5/5/5);
-> if the casing tier is +2 or +3 over the recipe tier, set the focused output to 100% and the rest to 0%.

in general, this type of focusing doesn't increase the total amount of outputs, save for the new items added with this multi that will come out in smaller quantities. instead, it allows the player to replace less useful outputs with the more useful ones, and this choice is completely up to them, as is the choice of focusing at all.

when fermium plasma is present, the current recipe will have all of its output chances boosted, unless the chance for one of them is 100%, in which case that chance is unchanged. this happens because the boost increases if the output chance before ferm focusing is smaller, and the maximum boost is achieved when the chance is 0%, which happens with high-tier nep focusing.

when an output is successfully focused with fermium, its chance increases based on how far it is from 100% chance. this applies to all the outputs at once, and the logic for this change is as follows:

-> if the casing tier matches the recipe tier, each output gets increased by 1/4 of the "failure" chance (for example, a 50% chance output has a 50% chance of failure, so it gets boosted by 12.5%, becoming 62.5%)
-> if the casing tier is +1 over the recipe tier, each output gets increased by 1/3 of the "failure" chance
-> if the casing tier is +2 or +3 over the recipe tier, each output gets increased by 1/2 of the "failure" chance

with the two plasmas combined and a +2 or +3 over recipe tier, a 5-output recipe would normally have 20/20/20/20/20 chances, but it becomes 100/50/50/50/50.

many lategame multis have parallels, which means they complete the recipe several times at once every time the recipe time is completed, instead of only one, but they require extra eu to achieve this. this makes power the biggest constraint for those multiblocks, and the same happens with the qft, given that recipe inputs are generally very cheap and simple. throwing more power at the machine means more outputs, in general.

given that, a player that wants a faster qft will make more catalysts to unlock more parallels, but each added parallels adds to the other ones, to a cap of 64. focusing, instead, changes output odds, which effectively multiplies the number of outputs per cycle. in terms of speed, a recipe with 4 outputs and 64 parallels runs at the speed of 256 parallels for the focused output if it's nep focused to the maximum of 100%, since it was 25% originally.

this is a lot of saved eu for high-tier, high-parallel qfts, so it is the main reason for focusing, and both plasmas are useful here. however, plasma consumption is not the same regardless of parallels, it instead scales with the square root of the number of correct catalysts for the recipe, which is to say, the number of parallels.

this further applies to the 3 new items that are needed to upgrade the casing tiers. since their output amount is much smaller than usual, they could get a further boost if focusing is being used, to incentivize the plasma mechanic when upgrading the multi. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 64, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "miscutils:itemcellplasmaneptunium", "resolved": {"id": "i:miscutils:itemcellplasmaneptunium:0", "name": "neptunium plasma cell", "mod": "miscutils", "registry": "itemcellplasmaneptunium", "icon": 49655, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "e6ab92bacab57fc2", "recipes": 1}, "label": "neptunium plasma cell"}, "1": {"count": 64, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "miscutils:itemcellplasmafermium", "resolved": {"id": "i:miscutils:itemcellplasmafermium:0", "name": "fermium plasma cell", "mod": "miscutils", "registry": "itemcellplasmafermium", "icon": 49647, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "d9cec7077f38e097", "recipes": 1}, "label": "fermium plasma cell"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Grinding With Wind
text:
grinding with wind the windmill is a grinder that uses the force of wind to macerate items and blocks. you will only get one crushed ore from it sometimes. however it does give a bonus when you try to macerate other things. that bonus depends on the item inserted, for example netherrack has a chance to give two instead of one dust and wheat will always give one and a quarter flour.

the dispensers replace a clay block in the walls. put anything you like in the interior - a bed, stairs, torches, etc.

normal multiblock rules apply - do not cross chunk boundaries with this multiblock.

if this is your first gregtech multiblock, as with all the rest you will need to whack the controller with a soft mallet to activate it.

if you have troubles forming the multiblock, try breaking and replacing the controller block.

the controller can be fed items via hoppers etc. to allow for larger batches. just don't allow the dispenser to fill up or it will void outputs.

the rotor blades will run if the controller is disabled or has no recipe. remove the blades when not in use or else they'll be used up.

speed and output will be affected by wind speed, recipe, and rotor.

macerates 16 items at a time.

high wind speeds will decrease output.

the durability will decrease according to the wind speed. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, name: Helium is Not Just for Balloons
text:
helium is not just for balloons higher tier superconducting wires and energy hatches will require helium. compressing air and liquefying it requires 1802 compressed air cells to get 1 he cell. it's probably better to get it from end stone dust or monazite from the moon. another option is to have a look at your oil processing and see how you can get helium from there.

name: High-Pressure Boiler Tank
text:
high-pressure boiler tank after you make steel you are able to craft a high pressure boiler tank. the upgraded version increases the temperature and produces more steam than the low pressure version. it will take longer to warm up, so make sure to keep it well fed!

extract steam by attaching a pipe to the boiler tank; the boiler will only begin outputting steam once it reaches 50% of its steam capacity.

[note]this is better than the low pressure variant only if you keep it working for very long time, if you intend to turn it on and off all the time this will waste a lot of resources! if you keep it at top temperature it will use ~2x more fuel than low pressure and will give ~4x more steam per sec making it 100% more efficient! if you can't sustain the fuel drain or want a more flexible power source instead use the low pressure variant.[/note]

[warn]actual fuel usage depends on the machine size and other factors such as machine temperature, if you want to know the actual number you will need to test it on your own setup.[/warn] {"0": name: Hundreds of Thousands of eV
text:
hundreds of thousands of ev a linear accelerator (linac) can be used to boost the energy of your beam, provided the beam's particles are charged. you'll need to constantly provide it with coolant for it to run, otherwise you'll have maintenance issues every time it runs dry.

output energy can be increased by increasing eu/t (scales with the cbrt) or increasing length (scales linearly). the latter also decreases focus, however.

focus in turn can be improved by using a better/lower temperature coolant (options listed on tooltip).

name: Infinity Coil Upgrade
text:
infinity coil upgrade smelting with the ferocity of the universe itself.

this unbelievable material seemed impossible to manipulate into a coil block form, even though its properties made this desirable. it is incredibly stable even at extreme temperatures, but this also made it unable to pack together for coils.

however, the situation changed when you thought about using something more intelligent. by integrating a wetware or better uhv circuit, the infinity coil became a reality, controlled by the ever-watching eyes of the circuitry you've spent months to create. from now on, these eyes will watch over your multiblocks.

provides 11701k heat. you could upgrade your ebf, though at this point it's more likely to be for your mbfs or your dtpf. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 16, "damage": 11, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockcasings5", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockcasings5:11", "name": "infinity coil block", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockcasings5", "icon": 22259, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 11, "shard": "d7d804f743617d2e", "recipes": 2}, "label": "infinity coil block"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: It's Time to Get More Steam
text:
it's time to get more steam as soon as you have the ability to store energy in large quantities, it would be necessary to have a way to generate energy in large quantities. you need a large bronze boiler. but in order to make this boiler, you will need a mountain of bronze. this boiler produces 800l of steam per tick. this is enough to run 10 basic steam turbines.

the large boiler can use either water or distilled water. water is consumed at a rate of 1l of water per 160l of steam.

to make a large boiler you must make a 3x3x6 structure with bronze pipe casings in the center of the middle 3 levels. the lowest level must contain at least 1 input hatch, 1 output hatch, 5 fireboxes, 1 muffler, and one maintenance hatch. the lowest level can not contain any plated bricks.

warning: different from other boilers, large boilers must contain water at all times while active. if at any point the boiler runs out of water while it is active, it will explode. {"0": name: Let's Get Crackin!
text:
let's get crackin! cracking oil products like light and heavy fuel with the oil cracker is faster and more efficient than using a chemical reactor, producing 25 to 50 percent more output, depending on which cracking method it's doing (steam does 50%, hydro does 25% but consumes 20% less hydrogen). cracked products will result in additional by-products in the distillation tower. it is a smart idea to get this multiblock since you are going to need tons of industrial tnt from toluene for advanced tier rockets.

the 16 coils form 2 vertical rings of 8 on either side of the controller. the casings between the rings can be replaced with a hatch for steam/hydrogen input. energy hatch and maintenance hatch can replace any of the casings. the input product hatch and output product hatch must replace one of the casings outside of the coils.

hint: only gt/railcraft steam can be used, not ic2 steam. you can use a fluid heater to make it instead of a boiler.

[note]the circuit goes in the controller.[/note]

name: Low-Pressure Boiler Tank
text:
low-pressure boiler tank the low pressure boiler tank is the easiest way to make steam with an rc boiler. the firebox needs this tank on top to produce steam. the bigger the boiler the slower it heats up, but it will produce more steam when heated up.

extract steam by attaching a pipe to the boiler tank; the boiler will only begin outputting steam once it reaches 50% of its steam capacity.

[note]this variant is very useful for inconsistent operation. it has lower efficiency but heats up significantly faster than the high pressure variant meaning the fuel will be used more efficiently at the beginning of the operation, the drawback is that this variant is 50% as efficient as the high pressure one is at max temperature. if instead you want to have a constant high-throughput steam generation use high pressure variant instead.[/note]

[warn]actual fuel usage depends on the machine size and other factors such as machine temperature, if you want to know the actual number you will need to test it on your own setup.[/warn] {"0": name: Neutron Activator
text:
neutron activator the neutron activator is a unique machine that you will use for processing naquadah, and eventually naquadah fuel should you choose to do so.

unlike traditional multis, instead of using a regular energy hatch, this machine relies on a neutron accelerator that will need to be regulated by a sensor hatch. (the neutron accelerator needs to be provided power just like an energy hatch)

the accelerator will increase its neutron kinetic energy (nke) and when the nke is between the requested number which you can see in nei, the machine will work and output the right products. however, if you turn on the neutron activator when nke doesn't meet the requirement, it will still consume your input material but output trash. so be careful with the nke when you run this machine.

when all neutron accelerators aren't running, nke will decrease 72kev/s.

you can enable batch mode with wire cutters.

[note]the more height/speed casings you have, the more inefficient the eu->ev conversion becomes, so you then need more power. the math is as follows: multiply recipe time by 0.9 for each height above 4 and multiply ev you get from your input power by 0.95 for each height above 4.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, name: No More (IC) Engraving
One Fluid Tank to Store it All!!
text:
one fluid tank to store it all!! if you ever thought that the standard super tanks or quantum tanks were still too small then the yottank is the next option.

the yottank compared to the tfft might only be able to store one fluid instead of 25 fluids. however it makes up for this downside by not having to share any of the fluid storage space with any other fluids. it also does not require any energy input or maintenance requirements.

if all you want to do is store a large amount of one fluid type then look no further then the yottank. it has a special me input hatch for ae2 connections while having expandable storage blocks. the tank can be both upgraded with the fluid storage blocks and can be increased in height to hold any more fluid.

so if you want to store your fluid in style then look no further then the yottank.

[note]if you're having issues searching for the fluid storage blocks for the yottank in nei then search for: fluid cell block[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 32014, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:32014", "name": "yottank", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 24964, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 32014, "shard": "bba61bb38fd8389e", "recipes": 1}, "label": "yottank"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}, "1": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 1, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 32015, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:32015", "name": "yothatch", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 24965, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 32015, "shard": "ab6134a969e5b7c5", "recipes": 1}, "label": "yothatch"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:optional_retrieval"}} {}

name: Playing With the Big Boys, Chemically
text:
playing with the big boys, chemically this facility will process certain chemical recipes you'll need later on, like rocket fuels. keep in mind that recipes can only be made after meeting the required chemical plant tier.

it will need a minecart load of resources, so start mining!

catalysts are needed in some recipes, place them in the catalyst housing. they use durability, this includes ones that don't look like it.

[note]you can make silicon carbide in the mixer, you don't need the abs.[/note]

valid solid casings: (determines chemical plant tier for recipes)
1 strong bronze machine casing
2 solid steel machine casing
3 sturdy aluminium machine casing
4 clean stainless steel machine casing
5 stable titanium machine casing
6 robust tungstensteel casing
7 vigorous laurenium machine casing
8 rugged botmium machine casing

valid machine casings: (determines maximum hatch/bus tier)
lv-uhv machine casing, uhv unlocks any hatch/bus.

valid pipe casings: (+2 parallels, -20% chance to consume catalyst durability per pipe casing starting with 2 parallels and 100% chance for the first one.)
bronze
steel
titanium
tungstensteel

all coils from cupronickel to eternal are valid. each one increases speed by +50%, starting at 50% speed for cupronickel.

[note]additionally: if you have at least awakened draconium coils and tungstensteel pipe casings, then no catalyst is consumed at all![/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 998, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:998", "name": "exxonmobil chemical plant", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 25769, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 998, "shard": "ab69f41548b55082", "recipes": 1}, "label": "exxonmobil chemical plant"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 2, "damage": 5, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:5", "name": "lootbag (tier 2 mv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21254, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 5, "shard": "86c93816ff53d76b", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 2 mv)"}}}}

name: Playing with Colors!
text:
playing with colors! multiblock machines enforce input separation based on hatch color. inputs from input buses and input hatches will only interact if they share the same color. un-dyed inputs act as wildcards compatible with any color.

color can be applied using a spray can and removed with a spray can solvent. an infinite spray can becomes available later in progression.

[note]there are a few other items which paint inputs. check out [quest]making sense of spaghetti[/quest] in the building better bases tab for a complete list.[/note]

[note]for more advanced users, note that the priority of dyed hatches is ordered exactly how the vanilla dyes are in nei, from highest (black) to lowest (white).[/note]

name: Producing Solar Panels in BULK!!
text:
producing solar panels in bulk!! [quest]the solar factory![/quest]

the structure has tiers, each of which allow greater production than the previous tier. 

recipes in nei display the minimum wafer tier required. 
wafer tiers: 

monocrystalline
phosphorous
naquadah
europium
americium
photonically prepared
photonically enhanced

machine parallels are based on precise casing tier:

mk-i: 8x
mk-ii: 16x
mk-iii: 32x
mk-iv: 64x

tier 2:

supports multi-amp energy hatches
25% more outputs for every wafer tier above the minimum required.
the bonus to outputs occurs after parallels, but cannot be greater than 100%
lv-luv solar panels can be made without the previous panel, but at a higher cost.

tier 3:

supports laser energy hatches
bonus per increased wafer tier is increased to 50%
zpm-uv solar panels can be made without the previous panel, but at a higher cost. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 367, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:367", "name": "solar factory", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 25050, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 367, "shard": "e131f2a1da1494a1", "recipes": 1}, "label": "solar factory"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Railcraft Steam Power
text:
railcraft steam power as an alternative way to make steam you can use the railcraft boilers. they require at least one firebox.

more than one size is possible: (1x1 which the quest gets you to make) 2x2 and 3x3.

name: Sievert for the Vat
text:
sievert for the vat some vat recipes require a certain sievert (radioactivity) value. so attach this radio hatch to your vat to input radioactive material!

the radio hatch holds rods/long rods of radioactive material and uses them to produce sievert. the input item determines the sievert value and how long it lasts. items stored in the hatch will be used continuously even if machine not active, so make sure you want to craft something before putting items in.

you can check the stats of an inputted item with a portable scanner.

some recipes require [warn]exact[/warn] sievert, you can use the screwdriver to access the radiation shutter control to adjust how much sv is blocked from being sent to the vat. for example, you need 100sv to make seaweed broth, so you'd use naquadah rods, and block off 30sv.

rod stats:
material-sievert-apprx. time until used up
bismuth                 83sv   198s
uranium 235           92sv    80s
uranium 238           92sv    80s
plutonium 239         94sv    66s
plutonium 241         94sv    66s
naquadah             130sv   14.5s
enriched naquadah 140sv   10.5s
naquadria            150sv     8s

there are more radioactive materials than these, but these are the main ones. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 12713, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:12713", "name": "radio hatch", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 23502, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 12713, "shard": "10cf75f8a94c9e3e", "recipes": 1}, "label": "radio hatch"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 23098, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.01", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.metaitem.01:23098", "name": "uranium 238 rod", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.metaitem.01", "icon": 38256, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 23098, "shard": "d4684227fdab119d", "recipes": 9}, "label": "uranium 238 rod"}}}}

name: Something From Nothing
text:
something from nothing void miners are basically the same thing as regular ones, except that they draw from the whole pool of ores for the dimension without there having to be any nearby. in addition, you can speed them up by supplying neon, krypton, xenon, or oganesson.

you can get neon reasonably easily from bartimaeusnek ore from ross 128ba. krypton and xenon can be produced from centrifuging fuel rods. all three can be produced from the ev liquid air distillation method. remember you need the liquid air fluid hatch to actually put in enough liquid air. if you want all the produced gasses from the first 4 slots, you'll need to use the giant output hatch.

to get oganesson, you'll need mk3 fusion.

all four fluids can be replicated, so you'll probably end up doing that.

[note]if you want the deep dark's ores, you have to use a void miner.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 12741, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:12741", "name": "void miner i", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 23518, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 12741, "shard": "8a7a2b58d7d98f99", "recipes": 2}, "label": "void miner i"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Stern-Gerlach, Perhaps?
text:
stern-gerlach, perhaps? the beam splitter allows you to sort your particle beams. the lhc produces output particles randomly, and this machine allows you to sort them into different lanes using the filtered beamline output hatch. it also divides the amount of any particle packet by the number of valid output spots.

[note]for example, if you set one output to protons and two outputs to electrons, then a mixed input beam (with all particles having an amount of 100) will be sorted into 3 beams - one of protons (amount 100) and two of electrons (each amount 50).[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 3017, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:3017", "name": "beam splitter", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 24764, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 3017, "shard": "8662ebd21c284495", "recipes": 2}, "label": "beam splitter"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Synchrotron (No Relation to the Catalyst)
text:
synchrotron (no relation to the catalyst) to actually produce some light for photolithography, you'll need to accelerate your electrons in a synchrotron. like with the linac, providing it with coolant is necessary to keep it running.

you can increase the energy of the produced photons by increasing eu/t, or increasing the tier of all four antenna casings inside.

to improve focus, you can use a better coolant, and the output amount increases with both eu/t and antennae tier.

name: TFFT
text:
tfft the tfft is very useful if you don't want to have a bunch of super tanks, it also has a modular structure so it can be up to x4.33 times bigger than numbers in this quest.

with the tier i storage field block, it consumes 27 eu/t but only has about 0.27x the storage capacity of a super tank i per fluid.

with the tier v storage field block it consumes 1134 eu/t and has about 0.54x the storage capacity of a qt iii per fluid.

with the tier x storage field block it consumes 0eu/t (only tier x uses 0) and has about x3.3 capacity of t7 yottank (divide by 25 to get per 1 fluid)

you can use the multi hatch to access all the fluids at once with an me fluid storage bus or fluid ender conduit.

name: Tier 3 Manipulating
text:
tier 3 manipulating with access to even more advanced materials, you can upgrade your qft to tier 3 by replacing the cosmic fabric manipulator casings with infinity infused manipulator casings. this tier unlocks two powerful new skips: the final naqline skip and the stem cell skip.

this new casing requires even more advanced materials still, including the superconductor rare-earth composite, which can only be crafted in a tier 2 qft. unlike hyper-stable self-healing adhesive, which focused on structural integrity, this composite is designed purely for energy transmission. with automatic self-repair now fully handled, we can shift our focus to increasing the energy flow between components and into the multi itself.

standard superconductors break down under quantum stress - but this composite eliminates all resistance across the outer shell. its precisely layered rare-earth elements create such gradual transitions that quantum flow moves effortlessly, with no losses or destabilizing effects.

name: Tier 4 Manipulating
text:
tier 4 manipulating finally, you have done it! you can now upgrade your qft to the ultimate tier by replacing your infinity infused manipulator casings with spacetime continuum ripper casings. this final upgrade unlocks all skips, including the bio cell skip, the kevlar skip and the radox + xenoxene skip.

even with all previous upgrades, the final leap remained out of reach. chemical skips for foundational components used in the earlier stages of the qft, such as bioware circuits, were still impossible - until now. reaching the theoretical limit of the qft demands a material far beyond anything seen before, hidden deep within the second half of the naquadah line.

the material you require will be your magnum opus - the black body naquadria supersolid. this extraordinary substance acts as a perfect black body - absorbing all radiation without reflection - and behaves as a supersolid, flowing like a fluid with zero viscosity. combining these properties in a single material ensures stable, effortless quantum energy flow at any voltage level, even at the max tier!

with this breakthrough, your qft is fully unlocked, capable of creating components up to the uhv tier. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 236, "damage": 10, "oredict": "", "id": "miscutils:gtplusplus.blockcasings.5", "resolved": {"id": "i:miscutils:gtplusplus.blockcasings.5:10", "name": "spacetime continuum ripper", "mod": "miscutils", "registry": "gtplusplus.blockcasings.5", "icon": 49344, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 10, "shard": "21f639a219feca27", "recipes": 2}, "label": "spacetime continuum ripper"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 27, "oredict": "", "id": "miscutils:item.basicgenericchemitem", "tag": {"catalyst": {"damage": 0, "maxdamage": 50}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (miscutils:item.basicgenericchemitem, metadata 27)"}, "2": {"count": 1, "damage": 26, "oredict": "", "id": "miscutils:item.basicgenericchemitem", "tag": {"catalyst": {"damage": 0, "maxdamage": 50}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (miscutils:item.basicgenericchemitem, metadata 26)"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Time to Drill For Ore!
text:
time to drill for ore! auto miners are nice but you're going to reach a point where you will want mooooooooooooore ores. this multiblock will help with that. it will also pre-macerate your ores and give you a little bonus crushed ores as well.

higher tiers of power will drill faster. you need to upgrade the energy hatch corresponding to the power tier. you will also need an energy hatch, an input hatch, and an output bus - at least mv but you can choose.

later you can upgrade the ore drilling plant so it extracts from more than a 48 block radius. if you don't want to mine that far away, adjust the range with a screwdriver. each tier of the controller also gives 1 bonus fortune for small ores starting at 4. at tier 3 you'll want to spread the wealth to multiple compressed chests!

the multiblock miners have been upgraded so that they will chunkload the area they dig in. they will not chunkload themselves however. they will dig down in the chunk they're in like normal, and then dig up one chunk at a time in other chunks within its range.

you need mining pipes in the controller and drilling fluid in the fluid hatch. you can also feed mining pipes into an input bus.

you'll need to make lots of drilling fluid. 64 is a tiny amount to get started with! plan to make thousands of buckets - perhaps onsite, or pumped in via long distance fluid pipes.

these are gt machines, so remember to protect them (and their power sources!) from rain (and meteors!) on any side. and set a waypoint with journeymap so you don't forget where you placed it! {"0": name: Time to Drill for Oil!
text:
time to drill for oil! pumps are nice but you're going to reach a point where you'll want mooooooooooooore oil. this multiblock will help with that but you'll need to search for oil using a seismic prospector. you can find raw, light, medium, and heavy oil. there's also a chance to find natural gas.

higher tiers of power will drill faster. you need to upgrade the energy hatch corresponding to the power tier.

later you can upgrade the oil drilling rig so it extracts from more than one chunk at a time.

you need mining pipes in the controller. if you need more than 64, you can use an input bus.

these are gt machines, so remember to protect them (and their power sources!) from rain on any side. and set a waypoint with journeymaps so you don't forget where you placed it!

space dims can also have fluids beneath bedrock. for info, check the tips and tricks tab. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, name: Time to Get Some Steel
text:
time to get some steel you need steel? uhh... fine. let's get busy...

the bricked blast furnace (bbf) can share walls with other ones, just like most gt multiblocks. how will this affect the air quality though...

if you are short on stone dust, you can get more by macerating cobblestone.

if you spawn near a biome with hardened clay you can macerate it to get the clay dust you need. you can also use brick blocks from villages to get brick dust in the macerator.

crafting the worktable from forestry can make it easier as you can use all the buckets for crafting in one click. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, name: Using That Algae
Why One Coke Oven When You Can Have Ten?
text:
why one coke oven when you can have ten? your bricked blast furnace uses coal like hell and your steam boilers do too? well it's time to make more coke ovens and automate them a bit. the coke oven hatch, wooden fluid pipes, and tin item pipes will help you reach your goal.

since this is a gt multiblock, it can wallshare bricks and hatches. the amount of bricks required for this quest is the minimum for creating 10 wallshared coke ovens.

remember that tin item pipes require a steel wrench to dismantle them.

[note]search nei for a more efficient way to make coke oven bricks.[/note]

name: You Are Not Prepared... But They Are
text:
you are not prepared... but they are building a smeltery from the ground up can be really tedious and time consuming. how about borrowing one from the locals? they will surely be happy to share it with an unfriendly adventurer that just dismantled their bricked railway station.

the villagers are so dumb that they spent all their seared bricks without adding a few key components like faucets or drains. you still need to craft some smeltery bricks yourselves...

totally not useful tip: if you hold off building this long enough, you will be able to break down seared brick blocks into seared brick items with a forge hammer or extractor.

[note]unfortunately, going down this path means we will not give you quest rewards, since you are already getting this important multiblock for free. check the checkbox to signify your consent.[/note] name: A Green Revolution
text:
a green revolution now that you've made some tools, you can start getting into some real agriculture. get ready to craft many more iron saws...

welcome to cropsnh, the premier passive resource production mo... wait sorry i'm hearing just now that bees do in fact still exist.

anyways, if you want to learn how to till your way to the stargate, with the passive resources needed throughout much of your progression, this is the place to be.

the first step will be obtaining a stock of basic crops which you can breed from. if you don't already have them go steal some from those villagers, or that witch down the hill.

[warn]cropsnh crops do not behave the same as ic2 crops. these quests will walk you through how they work, it's recommended that you give them a read if it's your first time using them.[/warn] {"0": name: A Portable Barrel?
text:
a portable barrel? as an upgrade to the barrels, efr also adds the ever-familiar shulker box! the shulker box allows you to comfortably tote around its contents. you can find the research for them in the new horizons tab of the thaumonomicon.

these have seven additional tiers much like the barrels and chests that give you additional storage space. 

you can dye any tier by shapelessly crafting them with a dye, and undye them by shapelessly crafting them alone. they will retain their inventory. 

[note]there are many ways to obtain shulker shells:
1. fighting shulkers in the twilight forest lich & ghast queen towers.
2. fighting shulkers from the eggs you get from the vending machine.

name: A Quicker Way to Get Around
A Quite Different Storage
A Toolbox For All Your Tools
text:
a toolbox for all your tools as your factory grows, you will need to use your tools to build, configure, and dismantle machines. crafting a toolbox to hold your tools will help.

the field engineer's toolbox allows you to use a tool inside for building and configuring without taking the tool out of the box. right click to open the toolbox and put tools in. then, press the pick block bind (default: middle mouse button) to open a radial menu and select a tool. you can then use the toolbox as if it was that type of tool. pressing pick block while looking at a block will also choose an appropriate tool for the job, skipping the radial menu. sneak and press pick block to deselect a tool quickly.

later on, you can upgrade the toolbox with a battery. this allows the toolbox to recharge electric tools and unlocks the ability for machines and wireless chargers to charge the entire toolbox.

toolboxes can also fix maintenance hatches, using the tools inside. deselect the equipped tool (if any), then right click the maintenance hatch with the toolbox. all of the tools inside will be applied to the maintenance hatch, fixing any problems it might have.

the toolbox requires polyethylene, which is a fluid you likely haven't made before. it's up to you to figure out how to get it. here's a hint: the black gushers of oil found around the world may be
