name: All Alone in the Night
text:
all alone in the night thanks to our amazing devs, you no longer have to use a command block to reload your questbook between updates. this means you'll get all new quests automatically upon updating to a new version of gtnh! isn't that convenient?

if, for whatever reason, you want to manually reload your questbook, you can do so by typing /bq_admin default load in the chat window. you will need to be an admin for it to work, though.

here's another questbook in case you already lost the one you spawned with. don't forget that it can also be viewed at any time by pressing the tilde (~) key if you have not changed its keybind.

name: Appropriate Power
text:
appropriate power whether you used magic, steam, oil or biogas for power until now, you will run into problems as you advance to higher tiers. so you'll need to upgrade your power grid, at least for your ebf(s). so let's start with something more powerful: a nuclear reactor!

if you want to know how they work, refer to the internet or the reactor planner at [url]https://github.com/mauvecloud/ic2expreactorplanner/releases[/url]

note: the eu multiplier is set to 10x in this pack. that means your nuclear reactor is 10 times more efficient. make sure to set the planner to gtnh mode under advanced. also, the base numbers (before 10xing) can be seen on the hover text for all the components.

name: Arc Lamp
text:
arc lamp the arc lamp is a very bright lamp. it is directional - meaning the light it casts is brighter in the direction it is facing. its facing can be rotated using a standard wrench.

including the arc lamp the brightness of blocks which are close to light sources is:

redstone torch: 3-6
torch: 9-12
block of glowstone: 10-13
arc lamp: 13-14

the arc lamp can light up a fairly large area - for example a whole room - at light level 14: it is almost as bright as full sunlight.

the arc lamp also has the interesting property of actively repelling mobs. not only does its light prevent mobs from spawning nearby, but it is so bright that if a mob comes close to the arc lamp the mob will turn around and walk away again. this mob-repellant effect is confirmed to work on: zombies, skeletons, creepers, evolved zombies, evolved skeletons, evolved creepers. it may also work on other types of mobs (confirmation required). but it has no effect on spiders (they are not afraid of sunlight either) or boss mobs. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, name: Balance is Everything
text:
balance is everything you already transcended dimensions, but as your power demands spike to absurd levels, maybe it's time to transcend matter!

using the unbreakable stability of proto-halkonite, harnessing the power of [warn]chaos[/warn] becomes a reality. the  semi-stable antimatter stabilization sequencer introduces the concept of semi-stable antimatter, created from protomatter.

but it's a cruel mistress... fail to manage it, and antimatter could void itself into nothingness.

the semi-stable antimatter is produced in 1 second cycles, the amount generated is based on the total of antimatter currently stocked in its 16 antimatter hatches and consumes equal amounts of proto matter.

each cycle, the base production of antimatter per hatch is:
(1/16)*(antimatter)^(0.5 + c).
then each hatch will pull a random number from a normal distribution of 0.2 + a and a variance of 1, multiplying the base production with it, meaning the total antimatter change may be negative.

this causes an imbalance between the hatches. to properly automate the antimatter production, it's vital to always re-balance the amount of antimatter in the hatches. at the end of each cycle, the lowest amount of antimatter present in hatches is recorded, and any hatch that contains more than the lowest amount loses half the difference!

proper use of stabilization fluids can significantly reduce energy usage and boost production:

it consumes 10,000,000 + (antimatter * 1000)^(1.5 - m) eu/t passively
magnetic stabilization fluids can mitigate the passive instability and have its exponent reduced:
molten purified tengam exponent = 0.1
tachyon-rich fluid exponent = 0.2
molten magmatter exponent = 0.3

for each cycle, the ssass uses (antimatter * 10000)^(1.5 - g) eu
by regulating the gravity containment of the forge, this exponent can also be reduced:
molten spacetime exponent = 0.05
spatially enlarged fluid exponent = 0.10
molten eternity exponent = 0.15

by containing the antimatter more compactly, it is possible to generate larger gains per cycle. containment stabilization fluids alter the exponent in the production formula:
molten shirabon exponent = 0.05
molten mhdcsm exponent = 0.10

by inserting fluids with high energy potential, it's possible to alter antimatter's flow in chaos, making their randomness more favorable. activation stabilization fluids alter the average of the gaussian distribution, lowering the risks of negative changes in antimatter and favoring better gains.
depleted naquadah fuel mk v average = 0.05

name: Basic Bee Stats
text:
basic bee stats there are a couple of basic bees that have good stats you want to breed into your breeding stock.

cave dwelling - rocky - this lets you put the bee housing underneath or inside. handy for putting a chest on top for products.

nocturnal - rocky - this keeps your bees working all night long, and in the dark.

rain tolerant - water - keep producing even when it is raining.

high fertility - wintry - for breeding purposes, you want the maximum number of drones produced.

keep in mind that specialty products from bees require the jubilant state.
to be in this state, a bee needs to have its naturally preferred humidity and temperature. just being able to work due to tolerance traits is not enough.

for example, a salt bee needs warm/normal climate. even if it has +- humidity and temp, it will not produce its salt comb unless it is in a warm/normal climate. use alveary upgrades to make sure it is name: Basic Nuclear Fuel: Thorium
text:
basic nuclear fuel: thorium the weakest of all fuel rods, but very easy to produce, very easy to keep cool and runs twice as long as uranium. it even returns 1/3 of the thorium back later. a perfect "fission and forget" power source.

name: Battery Alloy
text:
battery alloy mixing antimony and lead in the alloy smelter will give you battery alloy. combine it with tin cable and voila, there's your small battery hull.

small = lv, medium = mv, large = hv. it gets weirder after that.

note that if you make the battery alloy in the mixer you need to use dusts, but if you use the alloy smelter you can use either.

name: Bet On The Distillus
text:
bet on the distillus iv brings forth gt++ multis, including an upgrade for the distillation tower called the dangote distillus. its structure is exactly the same as the dt, but it requires a muffler hatch and uses a different controller with a more expensive recipe.

it's also locked behind a luv chemical plant, which makes it a very expensive craft if it is the only use you have for that plant.

that said, it solves the issue of dts being slow, and those are the backbone of many renewable setups. how many quad dts are you going to need for reliable iv/luv power, you might ask? just go for it.

name: Better Questing?
text:
better questing? better questing has a number of useful commands for the questbook (qb) if something goes wrong. you need to have cheats enabled to use them.

/bq_admin default load
use this command to update your qb after you update the modpack. it reloads the quest database from the file. your save file stores a version of the qb that can be different from the one in the file.

/bq_admin edit
toggles editing quests. pressing rmb on the quest will open a context menu to share it or copy its id.

/bq_admin reset all <player>
resets all quests. use this if you want to start over, or are editing the qb. you should specify the player as well if it is a server, otherwise you can skip that part.

/bq_admin reset <id> <player>
resets a specific quest, defined by the quest id. sometimes it may be easier to go into edit mode > designer tool to specify what to reset.

/bq_admin complete <number> <player>
completes a specific quest, similarly to the above. you can still claim the rewards. use this command if a quest is broken, and then report it on github, but please check if it's already reported.

/bq_admin default save
saves changes to the qb after editing it.

/bq_copyquests <playerwithquestscompleted> <newplayer>
if you want to sync the quests with someone in your party, then use this. they won't get any rewards for that though.

/bq_admin hardcore
enables bq3 hardcore mode. you only start with 3 lives, so best of luck. additional life hearts are available in the kill all the things tab.

aside from the consume-type quests, a quest counts for everyone in the party if one person finished it. however, if someone joined your party later, you need to get them up to speed first either through /bq_copyquests above, or manually. otherwise, your quest completion won't count for them because the requirements for that quest are not fulfilled for them.

if your singleplayer world does not have cheats enabled, go to the esc screen, open to lan, then enable cheats. this makes pausing impossible until you reload afterwards. if you host a server, you can run the commands in the command line, without "/". you can also edit the level.dat file, and set 'allowcommands' to 1, but make sure to backup your world before doing that.

[warn]for quests to save properly, you must be online and logged into your mojang account when starting the game. sorry, it's a limitation of better questing.[/warn] {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "minecraft:writable_book", "resolved": {"id": "i:minecraft:writable_book:0", "name": "book and quill", "mod": "minecraft", "registry": "writable_book", "icon": 48727, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "7263c2f6d0ede3bc", "recipes": 1}, "label": "book and quill"}}}}

name: Bio Chamber
Bringing the Biome to You
text:
bringing the biome to you so maybe you can't find a swamp or tropical forest for your crops or bees, or maybe they're too far away so they're inconvenient to get to, or maybe your base is in a colder climate and you have to deal with the constant howls of direwolves. instead of packing up all your stuff and moving somewhere else, why not try changing the biome? there are a couple of different ways to do so in this modpack:

use the arcane terrestrial reformer
-requires ev circuits, tungstensteel, rocket tier iii
-also requires infusion, void metal (sufficient warp), energized node for cv, lots of essentia
-16 block radius
-can only change to a few specific vanilla or thaumcraft biomes
-kind of slow

use ritual of gaia's transformation from blood magic
-requires void metal, infusion, tungstensteel
-requires getting deep into bm (and the warp that comes with it)
-requires 1,000,000 lp, master blood orb, tier 4 altar and awakened activation crystal
-10 block radius, can be exactly specified with bloodstone bricks (either type)
-cannot specify which biome you get, you can only change the temperature/humidity within the 0.0 - 2.0 range and hope
-some biomes may be impossible due to limited range and overlap
-adjust temperature/humidity with items on 8 plinths around the master ritual stone
-need to relog to see changes
-very little documentation or explanation
-fast

use the brew of shifting seasons from witchery
-small range, depends on the level of the brew (power, not dispersal extent)
-biome can be exactly specified
-crafted using the complicated custom brew system
-can add different ingredients to change range of the brew
-at min changes a single block
-at max has about a 3 block (circular) radius
-instant (once you use it)

use the rite of shifting seasons from witchery
-requires stainless steel, greatwood scepter or better for the distillery
-you have to do a bunch of witchery stuff
-not hard once you've done it once
-extremely large range, 16/32/48 block (circular) radius
-biome can be exactly specified
-sometimes fails in specific chunks
-very fast

if you want to know how to use the witchery methods, please go to the look to the edges tab to continue.

psa: the ic2&galacticraft terraformers only change the surface, not the biome itself. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Celestial Gateways
Chemical Pseudo-Altercations
text:
chemical pseudo-altercations learning more about the world and its ways is a sign of wisdom. however, the truly wise are the ones who know what is unimportant and can be skipped. for a true breacher of technology, the constraints of physics and chemistry are not essential. to skip past their technicalities, the quantum force transformer comes into play.

this multi is meant to replicate the most popular and important processing lines in the pack's progression, mostly those related to chemistry. because of recursion in recipes, where earlier tier materials are required to craft higher tier equivalents, there are a lot of early processing lines that stay up through progression. even worse, they often need more and more machines to keep up with increasing speed demands. to save on lag, this multi will do those processing lines in one step and without most of the extra chemicals that are added to purify the inputs into the outputs.

the quantum force transformer (qft) is unlocked in uev, after optical mainframes have been crafted, and with the addition of a single eternal singularity and other materials. it's a tall, 15x15 multiblock with many different casings, including two that are upgradable and decide the two tiers of the multi. although it's available in uev, the upgraded casings require more and more expensive materials, while also unlocking skips for more advanced processing lines. for example, a platline skip can be done in the earliest qft tier, whereas a kevlar skip can only be done in the last tier.

each recipe that the qft has represents a single processing line or a big part of a line. the inputs for the early plastic skip, for example, are the basic components of the plastics on a molecular level (carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, etc.), and not the multi-step chemicals that were used half a dozen tiers earlier. all recipes have 3 or more outputs, and every output has a chance to appear: the chance for each is 100% divided by the number of outputs. to increase it, there are additional mechanics that can be used.

simply put, the qft uses huge amounts of energy and quantum field stabilization to disassemble simple molecules and assemble them into more complex ones, without needing additives or constrained processes. the only addition to the base inputs that the multi requires is a specific catalyst, which the smart circuits use to guide the materials into what they ultimately transform into, but they are never consumed or lost in any way.

this direct process simplifies long processing chains to one step, but it has two consequences: it makes the process expensive, given the extreme conditions needed to undergo the transformation (in a similar way to fusion), but it also generates many different outputs at once, none of which are guaranteed, and it's impossible to choose between them without adding something else into the setup to alter the conditions inside the qft in some way. throwing more energy into the multi won't do anything, and better materials don't seem to work, so what is the next step? that is what the next two quests will answer.

name: Circuit Programming
text:
circuit programming some machines have a very, very large number of recipes. to avoid conflicts, many recipes have programmed circuits to ensure that the correct recipe is used. these programmed circuits are not consumed.

in this modpack, all singleblock gt machines now come with an icon in the gui on the bottom-right that represents a ghost circuit. click it or scroll to choose the number you need. if you do that, you don't have to insert a physical circuit. this is going to be your main option for all single block machines. this option is now also available for input buses of multiblocks, which you will use much later.

there are a few places throughout the modpack where you still need the physical circuits. you can turn an lv circuit into a programmed circuit in the crafting grid and then program it in various ways:

1) find a correct crafting recipe with a screwdriver in nei and use that.

2) right-click while holding the programmed circuit to open an easy menu. you still need to at least have the screwdriver in your inventory though or it won't work. eventually you can also make an electric screwdriver.

3) use the bartworks circuit programmer. it's only available in mv, but it does not use any durability and runs on eu.

4) use the gt++ circuit programmer block. it isn't portable and only available in mv, but it allows for automation.

the tasks in this quest are just the showcase of what programming circuits there are. you can just click the checkmark once you understand how the programmed circuits work. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, name: Compact Storage
Controlling Your Drawers
text:
controlling your drawers now that you have mv circuits and stainless steel, you can make the incredibly handy drawer controller. this block will make any drawers it connects to in a 4-block radius (including the y-axis) and 50 blocks at maximum as part of a multiblock that allows storage (and retrieval with the right setup) to any of the blocks that make it up. this will allow you to dump the contents of your mining trip into a storage system much easier. just hold right-click on the controller front for a second or two, and any items that match what's already in the multiblock will be deposited, while your tools and such won't. just make sure to place your controller last so it registers all the drawers.

you can feed into the controller (and thus the rest of the drawers) with any kind of piping or hopper equivalent. if using it as part of a multifarm or mob farm, make sure to set the contents of the drawers, and lock them with a key so that it properly stores everything in an organized manner. if the drawers' contents aren't set, it will start filling starting from the ones closest. if you wish to have more than one drawer full of an item, put a void upgrade on the drawer further from the controller, and it will fill the first one, then the second.

if you want to go around corners, use the trim drawers to extend the multiblock. if you want to have a second point to dump items into, use the controller slave (one per multiblock, automation only). note that you can use a key on the controller to affect all drawers at once.

once you have an me network, place a storage bus on the controller, and the entire inventory will be accessible from the network, with both storage and retrieval. just remember to set the priority higher than your me drives. if you haven't locked them yet expect all your drawers to fill with random items from your me network.

[warn]using the drawer controller with large amounts of i/o will tank tps! if you're on a server, do not use drawer cubes, or expect the possibility of it being deleted or you getting banned.

additionally, expect all non-backpack interactions to be disabled on the official servers. congratulations, drawer cubists, you ruined it for everyone.[/warn] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "storagedrawers:controller", "resolved": {"id": "i:storagedrawers:controller:0", "name": "drawer controller", "mod": "storagedrawers", "registry": "controller", "icon": 11427, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "ba3dd904b1ecaa7c", "recipes": 1}, "label": "drawer controller"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}, "1": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 1, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "storagedrawers:controllerslave", "resolved": {"id": "i:storagedrawers:controllerslave:0", "name": "controller slave", "mod": "storagedrawers", "registry": "controllerslave", "icon": 11426, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "eea306f50fbc9c3f", "recipes": 1}, "label": "controller slave"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:optional_retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 6, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:6", "name": "lootbag (tier 3 hv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21274, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 6, "shard": "4351b75552afb0b2", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 3 hv)"}}}}

name: Crafting Input Proxy
Crafting, but with Beams!
text:
crafting, but with beams! the beam crafter allows you to craft items using two beam-like inputs! if you are familiar with the target chamber, this works the same way, but with two beams instead of one.

each beam crafting recipe requires two particle inputs. you must provide enough of both types of particles to finish the craft. the progress of a craft in the beam crafter depends entirely on the number of provided particles, but will draw power the entire time. 

[note]this also means that the speed of the craft is entirely dependent on how quickly you can provide particles, and as a result the waila estimate is likely inaccurate.[/note]

failing to provide particles consistently is not an issue! the machine will continue to draw power while it waits for more particles, but you will not lose crafting progress.

[note]if enough of one of the input particles is provided, providing more of that particle has no effect on the progress of the craft.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 3015, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:3015", "name": "beam crafter", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 24762, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 3015, "shard": "d9307d3dd20f78d1", "recipes": 2}, "label": "beam crafter"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Creative Flight With MagLev
text:
creative flight with maglev getting annoyed trying to reach pipes and conduits around your base? look no further than the maglev harness!

with the maglev, you can have creative flight whenever you are within range of a maglev pylon and have the harness equip.

this will work at half of the range when unpowered, you unlock the full range when it's given 1a of it's corresponding tier of power. the maglev will only draw power while you are in-range, not passively. a harness can only be tethered to one pylon at a time, but a pylon can attach to any number of harnesses. will only consume 1a regardless of how many harnesses are tethered to the pylon.

the mv pylon has a 16 block radius (33x33x33 cube centered around the pylon)

the hv pylon has a 32 block radius (65x65x65 cube centered around the pylon)

name: Dark Steel Tools
text:
dark steel tools there are also tools made of dark steel. each of them can receive upgrades. hold shift to get the tooltip which will explain what you need in order to upgrade them.

these tools can also be enchanted like vanilla tools.

the ender will increase wither skull and ender pearl drops. it can be upgraded to teleport the player.

dark shears can be empowered, and then will shear a large area, including leaves. handy for clearing away that giant redwood! maybe you will find other uses for it.

the axe, once empowered, can be recharged wirelessly while in farming station.

the pick? well, it can mine cobalt i guess if you haven't gotten a tool capable of that yet. you could keep it around to use for base decorations if your normal pick is too fast, i suppose. {"0": text:
digging deeper now that you know what an ore chunk is, dig all the way down to bedrock to find if there is a vein located in it.

check out an ore in nei to see where you can find a vein that contains it. search for it and click on it to get this info, among other things.

there are many types of ores, even just for getting one material like iron, so don't stick to only one ore.

you can also search small ores in nei, but not all of them are used. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"amount": 1, "ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "islevels": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:xp"}}

name: Dyson Swarm Ground Unit
text:
dyson swarm ground unit the dyson swarm ground unit multiblock is basically a solar panel, you just insert dyson swarm modules (how many depends on how much energy you want) and get energy out. there are some complications though:
- each hour, n of m modules are destroyed according to this formula: n = m (2 * 0.066) / (exp(-0.00005 * (m - 1))+exp(0.00003 * cps)), where cps is computation per second,
- needs 3.6m l/h of gelid cryotheum.
- up to 10,000 modules can be inserted into a single dyson swarm.
- dyson swarm can only accept up to 100k computation.

name: EBF-Time
text:
ebf-time in order to get aluminium ingots, you need an electric blast furnace. it's another very important step towards victory, so let's get started.

getting the mica for the heating coils might be a little tricky, but you can use a substitute for the first tier of coils.

in order to not scrape by for nickel, check out the quest source of nickel in the novice thaumaturgy tab.

to process the initial recipes, you should have 2 lv energy input hatches receiving up to 4a of 32v total. this is a power-hungry machine so you should be prepared:

1. cables lose some amount of power per block, as shown in their tool tip. put power generation as close as you can to the inputs. uninsulated cables lose more power per block than insulated. pipe steam or fuel to turbines near the energy inputs.
2. if the furnace needs maintenance, it will lose efficiency per maintenance issue and require more power to finish a recipe. the power usage formula is 1/(1-0.1x) where x is the amount of maintenance issues. 

the furnace will void the currently-running recipe it is processing if it runs out of power while operating.

for recipes with a fluid output you need to either enable fluid voiding in the ebf controller block gui or add an output hatch. otherwise the ebf will not start.

before the launch, don't forget to fix maintenance issues and put a programmed circuit if necessary.

if you want a really fancy ebf, you can add more input fluid hatches and store different fluids in each one.

the ebf also has a heat adjustment of 100k for each power tier above or below mv. you can only make lv energy hatches right now, but installing two lv energy hatches will overclock the ebf to mv power, eliminating the 100k penalty and setting the initial heat to 1801k.

as you upgrade your ebf over the course of the game, this heat adjustment will increase. two mv energy hatches (overclocking to hv) will add +100k, two hv energy hatches (overclocking to ev) will give +200k, and so on. coils only set the base value. this adjustment does not apply to the volcanus.

if the pollution gets really bad, check in gt++ multiblocks for a pollution scrubber, or upgrade your muffler.

name: E_TOO_MANY_KEYS
text:
e_too_many_keys error: too many keys to fit a 104 key keyboard.

there are many keybinds in this modpack. to avoid conflicts, most of them are unbound by default. only the ones available from the start are bound. note that nei keybinds are found in the nei menu and not with the rest of the keybinds.

here is the list of what some of them do :

betterquesting
grave - open questbook

draconic evolution
v - place the item you are holding on the block you are looking at

journeymap
b - create a waypoint
ctrl+b - open the waypoint manager
j - open fullscreen map
= - zoom in (works on minimap too)
- - zoom out

share where i am
insert - places a temporary beam where you are looking at that will be seen by you and other players
shift + insert - places a temporary beam where you are that will be seen by you and other players
ctrl + insert - shares the position you are looking at with other players
ctrl + shift + insert - shares your position with other players

waila - shows information about what you are looking at
numpad1 - show/hide the waila hud
numpad3 - shows how to craft what you are looking at
numpad4 - shows the crafting usages of the thing you are looking at

[note]if you have a non-standard keyboard layout, using the java 17-25 version of gtnh might help you in being able to use certain keys for keybinds.[/note] {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "harvestcraft:applejuiceitem", "resolved": {"id": "i:harvestcraft:applejuiceitem:0", "name": "apple juice", "mod": "harvestcraft", "registry": "applejuiceitem", "icon": 47005, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "4b524fe9dcebf5a2", "recipes": 3}, "label": "apple juice"}}}}

name: Eternal Coil Upgrade
text:
eternal coil upgrade beyond spacetime, beyond reality. you have peered into what never existed and brought into a fluid, and then a solid. it has been stabilized, against all odds. when you look at it, you think that you could hold the entire universe in your hand.

in the past, you were able to combine almost all materials into one, through an eternal singularity, an infinitely dense sample of the universe. however, automating this at the scale of the dtpf proved ridiculous, which would have stopped your progress altogether if not for the discovery of the energized tesseract. to physically manifest spacetime itself, you first needed to manifest the fourth spatial dimension, and that is what the tesseract is: a 4-dimensional cube.

cubes! almost everything around you is made out of cubes. you have only glimpsed at the reality of the 4-dimensional world, but you have successfully used it to condensate spacetime, which can be arbitrarily molded into the complete eternal mixture. needless to say, living circuits will not suffice to maintain an infinitely dense, infinitely stable, multi-dimensional material.

currently, the final upgrade with 13501k. this really makes your dtpf shine! {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 16, "damage": 13, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockcasings5", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockcasings5:13", "name": "eternal coil block", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockcasings5", "icon": 22261, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 13, "shard": "db4f49c6461a7066", "recipes": 2}, "label": "eternal coil block"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Exo-Foundry
text:
exo-foundry you didn't think we were going to force you to use the mass solidifier for the rest of the game, did you? imagine being compelled to make hundreds of those for gate... that would just be cruel!

introducing the exo-foundry! 

the exo-foundry is a direct upgrade to the mass solidifier, and just a few of them will be powerful enough to support your infrastructure for the rest of the game. but let's start off with one for now.

there are three separate tiers, and seven different modules. each tier allows you to place more modules on the machine, starting with two at t1 and ending with four at t3. each module has its own special set of abilities, and you can combine them in unique ways to get a foundry that best fits your infrastructure.

the questbook will explain the function of each module type, but the best way to view all of the information together is to use the gui of the foundry itself and the tooltips visible on the individual blocks. 

[note]for even more information regarding the precise mathematics of module combinations and interactions, you can also check out the wiki: name: Exploding Fluids For Power
Faster Basic Crops
text:
faster basic crops welcome to my ted talk, today we talk about the extreme industrial greenhouse.
it is the most advanced and lag free crop farm that will allow you to supply the amount of tea you need.
the machine starts at ev, and can no longer farm cropsnh crops (the industrial farm now handles them).
to see the structure, place the controller on the ground and use a structure hologram to build.
the glass tier limits the energy tier until [note]uv[/note]. with [note]uv[/note] glass you can have an energy tier as high as you want.
there are 3 modes to manage your crops (change with screwdriver):

setup mode (input):
in this mode you can plant your crops in the machine.
just put them in the input bus and enable the machine with a soft mallet.
when the bus is empty, just disable it and change the mode.
keep in mind that there is limited space of slots for your crops depending on the voltage.
with normal crops you start with 1 slot and that multiplies by 2 every tier past ev, every slot can take 64 crops of the same type.

setup mode (output):
this mode allows you to move your greenhouse or upgrade your crops.
when the machine is running in this mode it will output all planted crops in the output bus.

normal operation:
with normal crops it is a straightforward process. base processing time is 5 seconds, at the end of operation all crops are grown and the outputs are added to the output bus. additionally the time is lower every tier past ev (the time is divided by the number of tiers past hv, minimum 1 second. wow)

if you want to grow your crops even faster, then you can use a fertilizer (up to 400% more drops!). machine will take fertilizer from the input buses on start of the operation and will be applied to that operation only. each fertilizer gives +200% per crop. the bonus is applied evenly on crops. examples:
normal mode, 3 wheat seeds, 1 tea seed, you insert 1 fertilizer, you will get +150% wheat drops and +50% tea drops.

additionally, all your crops need water to grow. every single crop drinks 1000l per operation. so for example if you have planted 576 tea seeds at [note]uv[/note] voltage you will need 576000 l per second.

last notes:
the animation can't be disabled.
the lamps can be inverted.
the dirt must be tilled.
if you encounter any issue or have any suggestion please open an issue on github and ping @kuba6000.
this mb was created to farm tea because i wanted to.

name: GT6-Styled Pipes
text:
gt6-styled pipes wondering why new pipes don't always auto-connect? this was changed to make the pipes smarter. you can now use a wrench to connect only the pipes you want. you don't need a plate or a foil to prevent pipes from connecting anymore. the pipes will still autoconnect if you build one onto the other.

pipes transferring anything hotter than a certain amount, like steam, will cause damage to a player touching them. you might want to cover hot pipes to prevent getting hurt. also, if the heat level is higher than the pipe's heat capacity, it will melt.

pressing rmb on a pipe in the center of the 'grid' will enable or disable a connection. it will have an x through it if the connection is enabled. you can do the same to any of the 4 corners to adjust the opposite side. you can similarly connect each of the 4 sides by clicking on the closest box in the grid.

pipes have a free built-in shutter to reduce sloshing. shift-rmb with a wrench on the side you want to prevent input.

pipes attempt to transfer half of their capacity twice per second, so the full capacity per second in total.

large or huge fluid pipes can be a poor man's storage tank, holding large amounts on their own.

for machine outputs, including the boilers and railcraft water tanks - the one made of water tank siding - you will not need pumps. other tanks will need pumps or tinker's construct faucets to move fluids.

you can put covers such as gt oak planks or plates on a pipe as well. normally this prevents connections in that direction, but you can use a screwdriver to enable connections. this lets you make pipes that look nice going through walls. use a crowbar to remove covers. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": name: Heliocast Reinforcement
text:
heliocast reinforcement the heliocast reinforcement (hr) module is the final exo-foundry module unlocked in uiv. 

the hr module finally allows you access to uiv+ fluid solidifier recipes. now you can cool higher tier materials or create advanced reinforced glass types using the foundry.

the hr module is also unique in being able to pair with itself, at a cost. installing three or more hr modules on your foundry will unlock "entropic core" and produce these effects:

- processing values are randomly increased by a factor of entropy, which is rolled independently for each value.
- entropy is a value from 0 to the number of hr modules present (inclusive) and is rolled at the start of every recipe.
- entropy can either severely slow down processing or speed it up, making this pairing random.
- the average entropy values are s=1.5 with 3 hr modules and s=2.0 with 4 hr modules.

at 3 hr, processing values are as follows:

+(s*8) parallels per voltage tier
+(s*100%) speed
-(s*15%) total eu/t
+(s*0.05) oc factor

at 4 hr:

+s overclocks

name: Hello Baron, How's Your Black Gold Today?
text:
hello baron, how's your black gold today? during your travels you may have seen some huge oil spouts. now's the time to make a pump and go collect this black gold into tanks. oil can be burned directly in a combustion generator (onsite to power the pump, perhaps?) or be refined for better fuels and crafting materials.

bring a generator or battery buffer (with full batteries obviously) with you to power the pump. thanks to the advancement of technology the pump can auto output on top. stacking multiple pumps makes them work faster. in that case, oil has to be removed from the bottom of the stack using a pump cover or other means like a conduit.

taller spouts have more oil. but for the lv pump, it's better to use the short spouts if possible since it doesn't have enough range to fully collect the larger ones in the horizontal range. save the taller spouts for mv or hv pumps.

mining pipes are needed for pumping the oil, same as the auto miner. when it hits the bottom (or something in the way), if there's no fluid left to collect, it will start retracting the pipes. same thing if you disable it with a soft mallet. you can also change the range with a screwdriver if there's a reason to do that, like collecting lava in a limited area faster.

these are gt machines, so remember to protect them (and their power sources!) from rain on all sides. and set a waypoint with journeymaps so you don't forget where you placed it!

[note]once you run out of surface oil, you'll want to turn to:
1) oilsands ore, though this is better suited for making heavy oil
2) making oil from logs in a pyrolyze oven
3) bacterial vat (ev+)
4) crops
5) bees
6) underground (ug) oil. dimensions generally have a couple fluids that can be accessed with a multiblock version of the pump, available in mv+[/note]

[note]heavy oil cannot be used until mv for anything except lubricant and burning in semifluid generator since it requires mv distillery.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": name: High Temperature Gas-cooled Reactor
text: high temperature gas-cooled reactor have you heard of gas-cooled reactors? have you heard of pebble bed reactors? well now you have both! the high temperature gas-cooled reactor (htgr) uses specially prepared fuel pellets to heat coolant gas (helium) that's pumped in a closed loop through the reactor and heat exchangers. the reactor requires a constant supply of helium gas and power in order to power the pump that keeps the coolant loop working. this reactor allows the breeding of rare resources (indium, osmium) and fissile materials (u235, pu239, pu241). it can also supply you with lutetium and unlock alternative recipes for europium and americium via the elusive promethium. the disadvantage of this reactor is its expensive nature. pebble reactors work by stuffing the reactor full of pebbles, none of which require rare resources but rather a large amount of common ones. even though a lot can be recycled, you still need to keep the reactor filled to get decent speed. as a reward for this upkeep cost, you get a decent production for many different outputs. [note] notes: htgr has an internal buffer for fuel and gets faster the more fuel you put inside according to the formula eff=1-(1-x)^3 this multi consumes 0.2a iv when operating and this amount increases when lacking helium gas. the amount of helium gas increases with the amount of helium gas stored. the reactor speeds up immensely when supplied with ic2 coolant, water, or both. if the supplied fluid amount is below the maximum, the speed bonus is applied linearly. by typing htgr in nei, you can see all the items that are related to this multiblock. for exact numbers visit name: How the Heck Do I Find Ores?
text:
how the heck do i find ores? gregtech ore generation is based on veins. veins have a fixed height and a rectangular base.

there is a vein every 3 chunks in x and z direction. the veins typically extend into the neighboring chunks and have varying forms. the center point however is very regular. it is based on the chunk number. look at upper left of the screen to find the chunk number. this info is displayed by ingame info xml mod. for now, you need to see chunk info like "chunk x: 3 z: -2".

the 3,-2 is the chunk's address. the ore centers are located at chunk numbers of the form 3n+1 for both x and z. so, 4,7 is an ore center, as well as 10,16, -23,19, and so on. if you are in the right spot ingame info will also say that "this is an ore chunk.".

another useful tool is the nei ore vein overlay which you activate by pressing f9 three times. it shows the 3x3 areas and marks the center blue.

the generation of ore chunks is not related to biomes.

[note]after finding an ore chunk you can view it in your journeymap by clicking the ore icon up top. if you are playing multiplayer and on the same team, you both should be able to see the same prospecting information.[/note] {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "minecraft:iron_ingot", "resolved": {"id": "i:minecraft:iron_ingot:0", "name": "iron ingot", "mod": "minecraft", "registry": "iron_ingot", "icon": 48355, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "b18d0ca861207dec", "recipes": 1434}, "label": "iron ingot"}}}}

text:
hypercooler the hypercooler (hc) module is the first uiv tier module you unlock for the exo-foundry.

the hc module will require one of three different types of coolant be supplied to it via input hatch in exchange for giving overclock bonuses to the foundry. the input hatch can be set in replacement of any cryogenic casing.

allowed coolant types:
1. supercoolant (100l/s) -> 1 overclock
2. spacetime (50l/s) -> 2 overclocks
3. eternity (25l/s) -> 3 overclocks

[note]eternity can not actually be used as a coolant unless paired with another module unlocked later in uxv.[/note]

name: Hypogen Coil Upgrade
text:
hypogen coil upgrade forged from the blood of an ageless dragon, and melded together by the power of fusion beyond what you thought was the reality. no natural element, or combination of elements, could match up to this glowing orange material, not even the awakened draconium you got your hands on before.

what is this blood made of?

what truly happened inside that mk4 fusion reactor? what is this material? it moves on its own, moving as if it is made of slime, however it is boiling to the touch. despite moving as if it is soft and squishy, hypogen is hard to the touch and is incredibly hard to cut or work. it feels out of this world, and it is obvious to you what needs to be done with it.

what were they feeding these dragons?

it absorbs and radiates energy without any effort, but it would be stupid to attempt making coils out of this without assistance. wetware wasn't good enough anymore, and only the most advanced living circuit could withstand the erratic behavior hypogen demonstrates.

provides 12601k heat. almost certainly, this will end up on your dtpf. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 16, "damage": 12, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockcasings5", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockcasings5:12", "name": "hypogen coil block", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockcasings5", "icon": 22260, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 12, "shard": "6c935c2adc0decb0", "recipes": 2}, "label": "hypogen coil block"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Industrial 3D Copying Machine
Industrial Coke Oven
text:
industrial coke oven your ev endeavors might push you into a gt++ multiblock, despite most of those being iv-tier. this happens because the special alloys used to put them together need to be crafted in an alloy blast smelter, which is iv, but the industrial coke oven (ico) does not!

what does it do? it's in the name, it's a really fast coke oven. so fast, in fact, that it can replace a few dozen pyrolyse ovens. it actually takes its recipes from that multi, so you also get the additional fluid, such as charcoal byproducts, alongside the greatly increased processing speed. the caveat is that this multi needs titanium, platinum, and a little bit of tungsten. you can get unprocessed platinum from nickel or meteoric iron & you can get tungsten from processing end stone dust, ender goo or moon dust.

in ev you'll have to stick to the heat resistant casing, which offers 16 parallels. when you unlock hss-s in iv however you can upgrade to the heat proof casings for an upgrade to 32 parallels.

optionally, you can add up to 15 slices to each coke oven for a boost in parallels. +8 per slice when using heat resistant casings, and +16 per slice when using the heat proof casings.

[note]for now, coil tier is irrelevant to the machine's performance, but later on, upgrading to infinity coils+ allows for multi-amp hatches, and using eternal coils allows for unlimited slice name: Industrial Water Purification
Infinite Turbines
text:
infinite turbines some turbine materials are not available for you, either because you don't have the material itself or because the dynamo hatch in the turbine cannot handle the power output from plasma. it will be a different story in uhv, when you can once again quadruple the max output of each turbine, and also unlock infinity as an option for turbines.

huge infinity 300% 6,451,200 eu/t
huge infinity catalyst 231% 1,236,480 eu/t

yes, that's basically it. you can use any material from the previous turbine quests, but when you make the t8 rocket and can mine infinity catalyst, these are the two options. obviously, infinity is much better, but also much more expensive. if you stick with fusion, you will need several of those to push through the endgame. remember that you can input plasma beyond the optimal flow, and get more out of each turbine at the cost of fuel efficiency. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 39, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:39", "name": "uhv dynamo hatch", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 25064, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 39, "shard": "cb188d26d76fc3b3", "recipes": 2}, "label": "uhv dynamo hatch"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

while inconvenient, the water generator runs more consistently.

name: Kinetic Wind Power HV
text:
kinetic wind power hv the kinetic wind generator generates energy from wind power which varies randomly, although certain factors can change this.

unlike the windmill, the kinetic wind generator will require maintenance in the form of rotors. these are needed to run the kinetic wind generator.
once a rotor is placed inside the gui, the block is given sufficient space, and the current wind level is adequate for the current rotor, the kinetic wind generator will begin to generate kinetic energy.

this can be converted into eu by using a kinetic generator attached to the correct face (the black circle).

about wind
first off, the wind strength of a particular area is affected by 3 factors: height, weather, and chance. the higher up in the world you are, the higher the wind level. below y64, there is never enough wind to be used, and kwg's will not function at all. weather will also give boosts; rainy weather will give a 20% boost to normal wind levels, and stormy weather will give a 50% boost. the final factor of chance makes the wind strength vary randomly, however there is a limited range of variation.

the easiest way to check the current wind level in an area is by using a windmeter. wind is strongest at around y160, towards the build limit of y255 there is very little wind, hence no point attempting to run windmills that high. while inconvenient, the wind generator can run anywhere. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, name: Large Hadron Collider
text:
large hadron collider in order to obtain more exotic particles than simple protons, neutrons, and electrons, you will need the large hadron collider. you can use any charged particle as input, sourced from any other beam-like multiblock such as the source chamber.

the lhc's four modules can each produce a different set of particles. for a specific particle to start appearing in the outputs, the collision energy must be greater than the particle's rest mass, shown on its tooltip in nei.

the lhc has two modes: accelerator and collider. 

first, in accelerator mode, it accelerates the input beam to a higher energy. it does this in 1-second cycles, with the beam energy increasing once per cycle by a fixed amount based on how much eu is consumed that cycle. the power draw increases quadratically as the number of completed cycles increases, and linearly if the amount increases. 

you can set a target beam energy and a maximum number of cycles in the ui. if your beam reaches the target beam energy before reaching the maximum cycle count, further completed cycles will repeatedly multiply the beam's current amount by 1.1, which also increases your power draw. once the maximum number of cycles is reached, the lhc automatically switches to collider mode.


in collider mode, the beam is collided with itself to generate all kinds of particles. each lhc module is able to detect and capture a certain subset of particles, depending on which fundamental force the particle can interact with. this also means some particles appear in multiple modules. you can blacklist particles from appearing by using the filtered beamline output hatch.

[note]the collision energy is 2x the accelerated beam energy.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 3013, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:3013", "name": "large hadron collider", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 24760, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 3013, "shard": "26e9d5deee588e9b", "recipes": 2}, "label": "large hadron collider"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Large Molecular Assembler
text:
large molecular assembler the large molecular assembler is exactly how it sounds; a very quick molecular assembler with a much bigger inventory for crafting patterns. 

this can handle up to 1024 crafts per second at the maximum energy usage making it up to 100x faster than a molecular assembler. check out the wiki for specifics: [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/large_molecular_assembler[/url]

the lma controller hooks up directly to your main network in order to function, and all recipes must be placed inside either an input bus or a crafting pattern provider bus in order to be recognized. will not require an output bus.

additionally, you must place a data orb inside of the controller or else it won't function.

[note]it's recommended you use a crafting pattern provider bus since it has more pattern slots and gets recognized by an interface terminal unlike a regular input bus.[/note]

name: Launch Controller
text:
launch controller the launch controller has been modified in gtnh to provide additional functionality. if you launch from a launch pad with the launch controller set up, the countdown will be greatly reduced, and you will teleport directly to the receiving launch pad. it will use half the rocket's fuel up though. this is very useful on laggy servers and can act as an early teleport option if you don't like the magical solutions. you will need to set up a rocket launch pad with launch controller and possibly a fuel loader on either side.

if you don't to use it for yourself, you can also try to use it for the cargo rocket. to use those at full capacity it is necessary to equip a rocket launch pad, to send items, with:

fuel loader
launch controller
cargo loader
and the receiving side with:

fuel loader
launch controller
cargo unloader

it is also possible to use buildcraft pipes to transfer items into the cargo loaders. next step is to set up the frequencies in both launch controllers (i.e. set: a to target b, b to target a). have a look at launch controller to set up the automated launch. the first time you have to right-click the cargo rocket and press launch at the top right corner. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, text:

points to consider:
1) left-click to attempt filling/emptying all fluid containers held on cursor.
2) right-click to attempt filling/emptying one fluid container held on cursor.
3) all fluid containers that can be used in a standard gt tank (e.g. super tanks or the x voltage tanks) are supported, including but not limited to: water bottles, vanilla buckets, ic2 (universal and normal) cells, volumetric flasks, large fluid cells, pressurized fluid tanks, etc.
4) can fill/take less than one cell (1000l or 144l if molten) of fluid if the fluid container supports doing so.
5) it won't check if it's a valid fluid for the machine/recipe, keep that in mind.

name: Main Quests and Secondary Quests
text:
main quests and secondary quests now that you've made it this far, you might notice how the two new quests look different.

the quest with the jagged edges is a main quest - it is linked to other main quests by a thick line. you must complete main quests to unlock the next tier and to progress in general. if you can't progress, go back to previous tiers and look for uncompleted main quests.

the other quest is an optional quest, and is not needed to unlock new tiers. however, optional quests often introduce you to useful items or processes.

what are the coins for? starting in stone age, you can use them to purchase things in a vending machine.

in case you started in a bad biome, here's enough coins to purchase some saplings once you get to the vending machine.

name: Matter Manipulator MKII
text:
matter manipulator mkii the mkii is the penultimate upgrade in the matter manipulator line. it is much more powerful, storing 10x the power, with a range of 128 blocks, and the ability to place 256 blocks/second. in addition to all of the mki features you now unlock two powerful new modes:

- copy / paste: copy a selection of blocks and paste it as many times as you'd like. works best with gt & ae2.

- move: similar to copy / paste, but will physically relocate something already built.

here is a short list of things that are copied / moved with the mm, the more complete list is on the readme, but this should give you a general idea of how versatile it is.

gregtech:
- pipe/cable connections
- machine color
- machine front & output directions
- basic machine settings (auto outputs, etc)
- hatch settings (sorting, stack limiting, etc)
- multi machine settings (void protection, batch mode, etc)
- multi rotation
- covers
- strong redstone output
- custom names
- ghost circuits
- bus/hatch item/fluid lock
- modes (for machines that use the new mode system)
- data stick data
- tectech machine input parameters
- me output bus/hatch capacity

ae2:
- any coloring
- the orientation
- the configuration
- the upgrades
- custom names
- any stored cells (will also automatically configure cells & install their upgrades)
- any patterns (will encode but not decode patterns)
- priority settings
- p2p settings
- oredict / regular filter

advanced copy options: 

when in copy / paste mode, the radial menu has an advanced options sub-menu with two powerful toggles:
  - link to external hubs: when copying wireless connectors that are linked to a hub outside of the copy region, the pasted connectors will stay linked to that original hub.
  - auto-p2p interfaces: replaces me interfaces in the copied region with p2p me tunnels, automatically placing matching tunnels at the source for seamless item routing. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, name: Matter Manipulator MKI
text:
matter manipulator mki the mki is where you really start unlocking the potential of the matter manipulator. it has a 64 block range and a 64 block/second speed limit.

unlike it's prototype predecessor, you now have 3 modes available:

- geometry: places standard blocks in a selected and configurable shape.

- cable: allows you to place ae and gt cables & pipes in lines (and connect them automatically).

- exchange: allows you to swap large swaths of blocks like the tc equal trade focus.

additionally, the mki can connect to your ae network to automatically transfer items and liquids. you can link the tool in your security terminal and use it while within wireless range.

when something is placed in the world, the tool will pull from inventories in this order:
1 - me system
2 - player's inventory
3 - uplink

when something is removed from the world, the tool will push into inventories in this order:
1 - me system
2 - uplink
3 - player's inventory
4 - the ground (items only)

[note]the mki also comes with the ability to remove blocks, so there is no need for another excavation upgrade.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": text:
matter manipulator mkiii the mkiii is the final upgrade in the matter manipulator series, and grants you access to it's most heightened capabilities. with 10x the eu storage as the mkii, it also boasts an unlimited block range and can handle placing 1024 blocks / second.

the mkiii comes with all of the features of the mkii, except now with the ability to also use the quantum uplink, though you won't be able to build that multiblock until uv.

 advanced copy options:

the mkiii unlocks an additional toggle in the advanced options sub-menu:

- auto-proxy cribs: replaces crafting input buses in the copied region with crafting input proxies linked back to the original crib. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, name: Moron's Guide to Better Trees
text:
moron's guide to better trees forestry trees have a variety of attributes. once you get a tree with a useful attribute, you can breed that attribute into other tree species. this way you can get an ultimate tree that combines all the attributes you want - including the type of fruit! you can also extract the genes with gendustry if you can make the machines.

[warn]please do your forestry tree-breeding indoors or underground because butterflies cause lag.[/warn]

keep in mind that for quests, you will need to breed the species "pure", not a hybrid. you should probably save the crossbreeding until after you get all the good ones.

for faster tree breeding, enclose your trees so that butterflies cannot escape, and breed bees with better traits for area and pollination speed. there's also frames too if you can afford it. the sieve may also help if you want to do it more exactly if you can make an alveary. you need either bees or butterflies, trees won't pollinate each other.

trees have the following characteristics:
saplings/fertility: chance of getting a sapling from a destroyed leaf. good for making into biomass or other uses. balsa, gooseberry and sweetgum are what you want.

allele     drop chance
lowest   1%
lower    2.5%
low       3.5%
average 5%
high      10%

[warn]maturation/matures[/warn]: the growth speed of a sapling into a tree. important if you plan to cut it down right away for logs. golden raspberry is the fastest.

allele    time
slowest  10
slower   7
slow      5
average 4
fast      3
faster   2
fastest  ?

height: controls how high the tree grows. giant sequoia is the best, though it may be a little too large.

allele    value
smallest  25%
smaller   50%
small      75%
average 100%
large    125%
larger   150%
largest  175%
gigantic  big

girth: the width of your tree. wider trees have more leaves and logs, but will also need more saplings to begin growing. all saplings must be the same species and girth. the sapling in the nw corner determines the stats of the new tree, and is where bone meal must be applied to mature the tree. the giant sequoia is best here too.

allele/size
1x1
2x2
3x3
4x4

yield: chances of getting a fruit from a destroyed leaf. orchard apple and chili pepper are the best here.

allele     drop chance
lowest   2.5%
lower    5%
low       10%
average 20%
high       30%
higher    ?%

sappiness: controls two things: (1) the rate at which fruit ripens on leaves, and (2) the amount of biomass a sapling produces in the forestry fermenter. each game tick, a leaf block with fruit has a probability of ripening by one step, and higher sappiness values correspond to a higher ripening chance. you can boost the fermenter's output by using honey or fruit juice. blue mahoe and red maple are the best. nei doesn't show recipes for analyzed saplings, and probably hybrids too, in the fermenter.

allele     sappiness  ripening speed
lowest    0.10          1x
lower     0.20          2x
low        0.30          3x
average  0.40          4x
high        0.60          6x
higher    0.80          8x
highest   1.00         10x

allele     fermenter biomass (water)
lowest    50mb
lower     100mb
low        150mb
average  200mb
high        300mb

[warn]fireproof[/warn]: applies to the wood. only the coast and giant sequoia have this.

effect: not used in trees, so it's none for any.

below is more information on some other parameters:

growth: sipiri trees have tropical instead of light, can only be bred in a biome with temperature 90%-190% and humidity 90%-200%, and can only grow in 120%-190% temp and 90%-200% humidity. all other trees just need light to grow.

[note]territory/soil[/note]: all trees have average, whatever that means. probably something related to the below that never really got used.

tolerates: if it can be planted on sand or not. only desert acacia and grandidier's baobab have this. the trait is either plains or plains, desert.

supports: what kind of fruits it can theoretically have. determined by species. only fruits from families listed under this trait can be produced by the tree, regardless of what appears under the tree's fruits trait. there are a number of trees from the extra trees mod that support all 4 types, but none from forestry itself.

fruit: determines what fruit or nut it produces. each fruit/nut provides different advantages:
plum and cherry plum only produces 100l fruit juice, but have a 60% chance of producing mulch in the fluid extractor or squeezer.
papaya produces 600l fruit juice, but only has a 10% chance to produce mulch.
coconuts produce 300l seed oil, but only have a 25% chance to produce mulch.
use a forestry multifarm so you don't have to break the leaf block to get the fruit/nut. set it to manual orchard, and place everything first.

family: tells you what family of the fruit listed under the fruits trait is: pomes, prunes, nuts or jungle. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "minecraft:writable_book", "resolved": {"id": "i:minecraft:writable_book:0", "name": "book and quill", "mod": "minecraft", "registry": "writable_book", "icon": 48727, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "7263c2f6d0ede3bc", "recipes": 1}, "label": "book and quill"}}}}

name: Moron's Guide to Breeding Better Bees
text:
moron's guide to breeding better bees first off, don't be scared by the massive amounts of bees you see here once you unlock the breeding trees. there's even more that aren't included and you'll need nei to find!

ha ha, just kidding - don't panic! the breeding lines unlock bit by bit showing you what you can go for next, mostly from the top to the bottom. the large icons represent particularly powerful bees. many of the basic bees have multiple breeding options, only one is shown on the bee breeding tree.

bees have two sets of traits, active and inactive. the active one affects the behavior of the bee while the inactive one is only relevant for breeding.

every trait further either [warn]dominant[/warn] or recessive, normally respectively colored red and blue. when getting newly bred princesses and drones, check both sets in case you got the desired traits. you can breed the ones with inactive traits to try and make them active in later crosses. a field kit or gt scanner cannot see passive traits, you need a beealyzer for that.

when breeding bees, a good idea is to settle upon a master template bee - a bee that has little to no crossbreeding potential but has all the traits you want - short life, nocturnal, cave dwelling, rain tolerant, humidity tolerance, temperature tolerance, 4x fertility, and so on. once you have that bee, breed a bunch of pure princesses with those traits as both active and inactive. these will be your breeding stock.

when you are trying to get new species, what you want is a drone - this way you can use your "breeding stock" princess with the drone to get new species without the annoying effects or limitations. poorly-crossed princesses can be returned to normal by crossing with breeding stock drones, or just thrown into storage if they now have annoying restrictions. make sure you keep the trait and species you want, and slowly merge the good traits from your breeding stock. you don't have to do this part in an apiary, you can use a bee house to swap around traits. remember that no species mutations occur in a bee house. ignoble bees are good to swap traits because they're mostly disposable - they have a chance to die after 100 breeding cycles, increasing slightly more each generation after that, though genetic stability frames can let them live longer.

once you solidify your species, create a pool of drones. you can use those to convert pristine princesses to the new species. pristine princesses will not die, but they can become ignoble under certain circumstances like using tons of production frames. rocky bees are a great source - all their princesses are always pristine, they have decent traits, and there's a bunch of them underground. if you have an ender quarry, you can collect them with that.

turning two different species traits into a third species trait is a mutation. merely turning one species into another is not. the chance of this happening is shown in the bee breeding tab, as well as the conditions. bees can require things like blocks underneath their structure, certain moon phases, or other things nearby in order for the mutation to happen at all. mutations happen across active-inactive and inactive-active pairs. so if you have an a:b princess that you want to turn into a c:c princess, you want to use an a:b drone. this crosses the princess' active a with the drone's inactive b, and the princess' inactive b with the drone's active a. this gives a shot at mutation for both the active and inactive traits for the resulting princess and drones.

a new bee mutant is considered "pure" or "purebred" when both the active and inactive traits are the new species. this is what you need to complete the breeding quests, but also to retain that species indefinitely. if the mutated trait only appears in one trait, the chance of it carrying is basic cross-breeding and not whatever was required to cause the trait to mutate in the first place. new bee species also have a set of default traits, and the new species will try to manifest these traits. you could start with two species that have compatible climate conditions and wind up with one needing completely different temperature and humidity. you want to encourage traits as you finish breeding the pure bee to get the other traits you want out of it. 

ultimately, the species trait determines what the bee produces and everything else is fair game. all traits can be bred into any bee species, aside from the species itself. species also determines the initial preferred temperature and humidity. species require their preferred temperature and humidity to be in the 'jubilant' state and produce their special drops. you can also mimic this with the alveary or industrial apiary, but increasing tolerances will not work.

advanced frames can provide useful boosts to mutation chances or lifespan reduction for faster breeding cycles. however, the excessive multipliers will increase genetic decay, giving a chance for a pristine princess to become ignoble.

a recommended early-game meta for bee breeding is to find an oblivion frame in a stronghold library, and then a means to keep it repaired like with a thaumic restorer. this rapidly speeds up the turnaround time to turn a queen into offspring. you monitor the process manually at an apiary, and use any additional frames you can to improve the mutation rate. you can push this well past the point you can make alvearies, but there are alveary components that can further improve on this.

it looks complex, because it is! but it's also a lot of dangerous and useful fun! {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"choices": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", name: Moron's Manual for Effective EBFing
text:
moron's manual for effective ebfing welcome to the latest moron's manual, effective ebfing! this manual covers common problems encountered when using the gregtech 1000 electric blast furnace.

setup
when setting up your ebf, make sure to place it a few chunks away from things pollution affects, like farmland. pollution is nobody's friend!

during setup, make sure the center of the ebf is hollow. sometimes things can sneak in there without you noticing, like a thaumcraft light orb!

make sure your muffler hatch is placed on a middle block. the ebf can't work if it is not spreading those delightful odors!

when placing your power hatches, make sure to minimize the distance between any generators and the ebf. especially at lv, those few blocks make a big difference! every amp of energy traveling over a cable loses a little bit - and you'll need as much as you can get! your best setup is to put two generators right next to each hatch, with a 2a cable. if you're poor, you could use 2 battery buffers with 2 batteries each directly attached to each hatch. make sure to top off the buffers' generators. if you make 9 slot battery buffers, you can fill them up over time to get longer running time until you get stable power.

output hatches and buses will automatically push into tanks and inventories placed next to them such as chests or bc tanks.

when building multiple ebfs, the gregtech 1000 electric blast furnace can share walls. this can save you on input, output, and maintenance hatches too. not recommended for energy hatches! {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 8, "damage": 2305, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.01", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.metaitem.01:2305", "name": "steel dust", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.metaitem.01", "icon": 38218, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 2305, "shard": "e8fdd62e0885ed26", "recipes": 431}, "label": "steel dust"}}}}

name: Moron's Manual for Massacring Monsters
text:
moron's manual for massacring monsters if you haven't noticed, this world is a true hellscape full of special mobs and infernals around every corner. unlike in vanilla, a player has to actually stay aware and pay attention to what they are fighting. here are some tips.

if an infernal has vengeance, don't shoot it with your 56-damage crossbow!

a high health infernal with regeneration is hard to kill. even worse if it is a witch that can also heal herself. in those cases, run like hell, or bring a soul vial to capture it and throw it into mount doom.

watch out for zombies with fishing poles - they can pull you to them. and zombies with a bow and arrow - they can shoot you back! {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 8, "damage": 15, "oredict": "", "id": "minecraft:dye", "resolved": {"id": "i:minecraft:dye:15", "name": "bone meal", "mod": "minecraft", "registry": "dye", "icon": 48247, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 15, "shard": "af473578bc18f423", "recipes": 21}, "label": "bone meal"}}}}

heat exchanger: pulls 4 hu/t from the reactor and 12 hu/t from adjacent components.

advanced heat exchanger: pulls 8 hu/t from the reactor and 24 hu/t from adjacent components.

reactor heat exchanger: pulls 72 hu/t from the reactor.
