name: Multiblock Revolution
text:
multiblock revolution the steam machines you have been using until now have served you well, but there will be a time when you need to process even more items. that's where the so-called multiblocks come in. there's a variety of steam multiblocks available to you - go have a look at the mass processing quest tab!

this tab introduces you to a wide range of extremely powerful multiblock machines that can replace your old, worn-out singleblocks (and some that can replace your old multiblocks!). many of these new machines will require you to handle additional mechanics and requirements, but it will be worth it!

here are some terms you should be familiar with as you enter the world of multiblocks:

overclock (oc):
whenever a machine is running a recipe of a lower tier than it's energy hatch it will gain a speed boost at the cost of more energy usage.

imperfect overclock (aka. normal, 2/4 oc):
for each tier above recipe machine will be 2x faster at the cost of 4x energy (2/4 oc)

perfect overclock (often phrased as "does not lose efficiency when overclocked", 4/4 oc):
some machines conditionally (or unconditionally) perform perfect overclocks. in this case, the machine will be 4x as fast, but it will run at 4x the eu/t (4/4 oc), leading to both increased speed and no net increase in the total eu usage!

parallel (often phrased as "processes x items"):
machines which parallel act as if they are running multiple of themselves - that is to say, they are able to perform multiple of the same recipe at the same time, using the recipe's eu/t multiplied by the number of parallels. machines which parallel will [warn]prioritize[/warn] this behavior over overclocking, which is good for you! parallels are more efficient.

input separation:
refers to a machine's behavior when choosing inputs for a recipe. with input separation on, you must have all required items for a recipe in one bus. with input separation off, you can split item inputs of a recipe between multiple busses.

[note]when working with multiblocks, if power is interrupted during operation, your inputs will be lost forever... careful![/note] {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "harvestcraft:limejellysandwichitem", "resolved": {"id": "i:harvestcraft:limejellysandwichitem:0", "name": "lime jelly sandwich", "mod": "harvestcraft", "registry": "limejellysandwichitem", "icon": 47420, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "6f8dd1f579451a16", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lime jelly sandwich"}}}}

name: Mushroom Biomes? Why Are There So Many?
NEI Next Level Recipe Search
text:
nei next level recipe search there are even more nei search options!

if you are scrolling through recipes, you might have noticed the magnifier symbol on the top, left to the page number. clicking it opens the recipe search field. a search term you enter here will filter all the current recipes to the ones where an input or output matches the term. an easy way to narrow down all screwdriver recipes to just the one from a particular material you want!

if you use "extended+" search mode the recipe search becomes even more powerful!

here backticks `` are used around the search queries, but you don't need them when searching.

by default the search works like in the extended mode, searching in any of the inputs and outputs of a recipe. so if you search a recipe by `-dust`, it will return all recipes where there's at least one item that doesn't have "dust".

let's say you want to search only in inputs. put < before your search query to do that. for example: `<iron` returns all the recipes with "iron" in one of the inputs, `<steel@gregtech` returns the recipes with at least one item from any mod containing gregtech in their name, using "steel".

but then, if you search by `<-dust` it still returns the recipes with "dust" on the left. why is that? because < searches among all items. so if there's one item that doesn't have "dust", then it would still match the recipe, even if the rest of the inputs are dusts.

to solve this, use <& instead. like this: `<&-dust`. it returns all the recipes without "dust" among the inputs! <& sets a strict condition on all inputs, unlike < that sets a condition on any input.

to filter the outputs use > and >&. they work the same way, but allow you to filter the outputs of a recipe. so `>gold` gives you the recipes with at least one output with "gold". and `>&gold` gives you the recipes with "gold" in every outputted item.

want to combine multiple conditions? sure, just put them one after another in any order. e.g. you could search for `<iron>steel`, `<& -$dust < cell`, `>&-dust cell`.

or even for `dust>cell`. here the non-prefixed part works like default, searching among all items from the inputs and outputs. so this query returns the recipes with "dust" in one of the inputs or outputs and "cell" in one of the outputs.

in some recipes you might have items that don't belong to inputs or outputs. in order to filter them use `^` and `^&` respectively.

you can add spaces for readability too, because (unless you have space mode on) spaces can be used anywhere while in extended+ mode. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:cointechnician", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:cointechnician:0", "name": "coin "the technician 1"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "cointechnician", "icon": 20789, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "d12081e875e5268a", "recipes": 1}, "label": "coin "the technician 1""}}}}

name: NEI Next Level Search
text:
nei next level search nei search got improved even further!

select a search mode extended+ to try it out!

extended+ works pretty much like extended, but it doesn't support * and ? expanding in the names. also the following symbols have to be escaped with a `\`: `-` (dash) `<` and `>` (less-than and more-than) `^` (caret) `{` and `}` (curly brackets) `|` (vertical bar) `\` (backslash) ` ` (space) `"` (quote) alongside with the prefixes that you have enabled like @ or $.

examples: @electro\-magic, iron\ ingot, pb\&j.

extended+ adds some qol to your everyday search experience and an improved recipe search (next quest). in the following backticks `` are used around the search queries. you don't need them when searching.

want to search for something without having to put a backslash before every other symbol? use quotes! you could use a quote inside quotes too, but you would have to escape it. like this: `"\""`.

use curly brackets {} to group conditions. searching for `{mytryl|manasteel} hammer head` would show you hammer heads made out of mytryl or manasteel.

space is no longer necessary to use. so `{mytryl|manasteel}hammer` works too!

there's a space mode support, so if you want your spaces to work literally turn it on!

quotes no longer require a closing quote. so you could search for `"iron ingot` and it would work! you still do need a quote if you want your quotes to end though.

regex syntax got simplified (though the old one is still supported). now instead of `r/some regex/` you could search for `/some regex` and it would work too! you still do need a slash if you want your regex to end. regex doesn't require escaping, the same way quotes don't, with the only exception being the `/`. so to find a slash with a regex you would search with `/\/`.

you can use quotes or regex after prefix to search with them instead of a plain text. for example, use `@"chest minecarts` to search for items from the iron chest minecarts mod. or `@/chest minecarts` to do the same with a regex. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:cointechnician", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:cointechnician:0", "name": "coin "the technician 1"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "cointechnician", "icon": 20789, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "d12081e875e5268a", "recipes": 1}, "label": "coin "the technician 1""}}}}

name: NEI is EVEN MORE POWERFUL NOW?
text:
nei is even more powerful now? nei now automatically collapses similar items into one slot making browsing much faster! to collapse/uncollapse a group use alt+lmb.
you can also create your own presets with custom groups!

[note]you can disable this functionality in nei settings.[/note]

also now nei has jei-like advanced search:

@ - search by mod (@minecraft)

[note]there are even more special characters that you can use but most of them are off by default (e.g. no need to use # to search in tooltip), below are all the special characters, check which ones are on/off in nei settings.

space is used as a logical and between different conditions
# - search by tooltip (#uv-tier)
& - search by id: (extratrees:door)
$ - search by ore dictionary ($ore)
% - search by subsets (%block)
| - logical or. multi-item search (wrench|hammer)
- - logical not. exclude items that match the following expression (-@minecraft)
" - multiple words wrapped in quotes are treated as one condition rather than several ("white stained glass")

search mode (apply on search parts, not full string):
plain - simple string
extended - allow only ?, * rules (by default)
regex - allow full regex

in extended search mode:
? - any character (@min?craft)
* - any few characters (@m*ft = @minecraft)
r/.../ - standard java regex (@r/m\w{6}ft/ = @minecraft)[/note]

[note]you can disable this functionality in nei settings.[/note]

you can add bookmarks with the a key while hovering over an item, also:
hold shift to bookmark the whole recipe
hold ctrl to bookmark number of items
hold shift + ctrl to bookmark both recipe and all the number of all the items it contains {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:cointechnician", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:cointechnician:0", "name": "coin "the technician 1"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "cointechnician", "icon": 20789, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "d12081e875e5268a", "recipes": 1}, "label": "coin "the technician 1""}}}}

name: NEI is More Powerful Than You Imagine
text:
nei is more powerful than you imagine nei has some really nice advanced features too.

clicking lmb or pressing r on an item shows the recipes to create it. rmb or u show recipes that use the item. backspace moves you back to the previously browsed recipe.

hold shift to stop the oredict cycling through items, and to show the oredict entries for the current item under your cursor.

search using @ to find all items from that mod; for example, @thaumcraft will list all thaumcraft items and blocks.

you can combine multiple search terms with a space. @thaumcraft table will search for anything with table in the name or description, in the mod thaumcraft.

it has even more advanced features than mentioned here and many configuration options, you can look in the nei option menu under inventory to find a few. here you can change more things about how the search works (like using regex), toggle collapsible items or the item zoom panel, or configure the history panel to your liking. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:coinsmith", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:coinsmith:0", "name": "coin "blacksmith 1"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "coinsmith", "icon": 20774, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "1bcd43c03cd0e821", "recipes": 1}, "label": "coin "blacksmith 1""}}}}

name: Neutronium Compressor
text:
neutronium compressor in order to compress singularities and eventually infinity catalysts, you'll need the strongest compressor yet: the neutronium compressor. this multiblock channels and controls extreme amounts of pressure through carefully calibrated active neutronium casings, but the sheer magnitude of pressure is too much to produce blocks or superdense plates, as any regular material inserted into the device will be compressed down to a singularity. more advanced singularities should be possible in theory, but you'll need something even stronger...

text:

text:

name: Not Enough Items - Now with Bookmarks and Recent History!
text:
not enough items - now with bookmarks and recent history! more like too many items! here are some tips for using nei.

when you have your inventory open, you can type the search terms in the text bar at the bottom. make sure your gui size is set correctly, or you won't be able to see it. double-click the bar to highlight any matching items in your inventory or inventories you're looking at. handy for searching for a specific ore, as they tend to look the same!

even better, you can use t to search nearby inventories, which will emit some particles.

we have also provided the special y command to look for a machine in the world, in case you've forgotten where you placed that advanced circuit assembler.

we now have an extra-fancy bookmark feature! the default key is a, but can be changed in the nei config window. bookmarks will be on the left side of the inventory, and you can look up their recipes or uses as normal. to move a bookmark, drag it with shift+lmb. you can even bookmark entire recipes with shift+a or recipes with amounts using ctrl+shift+a.

pressing o will hide nei, useful for fancy screenshots. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:coinadventure", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:coinadventure:0", "name": "coin "the explorer 1"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "coinadventure", "icon": 20723, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "29bd4b98fe0b00ba", "recipes": 1}, "label": "coin "the explorer 1""}}}}

name: Numbers in the Corner?
text:
numbers in the corner? what's with the numbers in the corner? that is the in-game info (igi) mod. some of the info it gives is useful right away, some of it shines later on in progression.

for now, the most important thing it does is showing if you are in an ore chunk. further quests will explain what it means.

if you want to hide it, type "/igi disable" in the chat. type "/igi enable" if you want to turn it back on.

the command "/igi config" opens the configuration window to control its position, scale, and size.

the command "/xu_tps" from the mod extra utilities toggles numbers to measure ticktime in milliseconds and the tps (ticks per second). tps is a measure of how well your server is running. the ideal tps is 20.00 (meaning a ticktime of at most 50.00). if your tps is less than 15, things are going to start lagging noticeably. at 10 or less tps, it is going to be hard to play.
the tooltip shows three types of measurement: instantaneous, average, and worst-case. each one first shows the ticktime and then the tps in brackets.

if you need suggestions on solving tps problems, feel free to ask for help in the gtnh discord.

while gtnh comes with recommended default settings, in particular when it comes to balance, there are many commands and configurations to customize your experience. they range from accessibility or debug tools to visual customization all the way to various cheats. you can find a small overview on [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/commands_and_configurations[/url]. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "biomesoplenty:food", "resolved": {"id": "i:biomesoplenty:food:0", "name": "berry", "mod": "biomesoplenty", "registry": "food", "icon": 3440, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "930414d8a114239f", "recipes": 0}, "label": "berry"}}}}

name: Obtaining Ender Pearls
text:
obtaining ender pearls you can hunt endermen the vanilla way to get a chance at ender pearls, you can purchase endermen spawn eggs, or try your luck in the end.

or you can get cruel, and stuff one into a smeltery to melt it down into delicious liquid ender and cast pearls from it.

you monster.

some of the dungeons have spawner of enderman, so you can do whatever you want with it.

to prevent endermen from teleporting, make sure to cover the smeltery so they don't see the sky.

if you manage to put a regenerating endermen in there, tag it so it doesn't despawn, and make sure your smeltery is not in a claimed chunk on a server.

name: PCB Factory
text:
pcb factory using a chemical reactor to create circuit boards has become quite inefficient... it's time for a proper solution! after some research you have found a more efficient method; a factory designed to print out circuit boards.

the pcb factory is able to use a wide range of plastics to create circuit boards ready to be used. the printing mechanism overheats when it tries to overclock currently, so i will have to find a way to make that work later. boards with neurons on them will also require a modification before they can be made, but that shouldn't be hard to achieve.

trace size: the trace size represents the lines between components, which are needed to transmit the electrical signals on the circuit. one can make it smaller to slow down the machine, but use less resources, or make it bigger to make it faster, but use more resources.

formulas:
- 10000/(tracesize/100) production
- recipeduration/tracesize^2 time

[note]similar to the water line, additional modules of the pcb factory can connect to one another using a data stick[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, text:

for the structure casings, you find that using infinity as a frame and enriched holmium as the protection layer works well. it can be allowed to let through nanites to go into the printer base so that extra material can be directly removed instead of trying to go slower.

with this new upgrade you can finally use tier 2 recipes. additionally, by placing extra nanites into the nanite containment bus, you can boost your parallel amount by amount^.75 up to 256 parallels.

name: Powerfail Notifications
text:
powerfail notifications congratulations on your first ebf!

throughout your gtnh gameplay you will end up creating hundreds of multiblocks, and will very likely run into a multitude of power failures at some point. 

fortunately, we have a dedicated system for helping you stay informed of exactly when and where these power failures occur (though the 'why' portion is up to you to figure out!).

when a multiblock powerfails, you will receive a notification in chat, in addition to a visible icon on screen, and an icon visible on your map. 

you can clear these notifications by:
- clicking into the multiblock that has powerfailed
- deleting the notification in journeymap
- typing /powerfails clear

for those playing multiplayer, anyone who is on your team will receive the same notifications. one person clearing a notification should clear it for all players.

[note]this feature uses the same team system as wireless eu. use </gtnhteam invite [player name]> to team up.[/note]

all of these features can be turned off in the gregtech config. if you want the on screen icon to disappear use /powerfails hide. for all in-game options use /powerfails help. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Power in the Ether
text:
power in the ether these new hatches allow you to wirelessly store and receive energy from any location in any dimension. they can be placed in any existing multi block structure and will function as normal energy hatches. 

additionally, the wireless covers can be used for singleblock machines such as a world accelerator or a biolab.

the wireless network can store a total of 2^(2^31) eu, far exceeding even a max tier lsc.

you can share a wireless network with others by adding them to your network with /gt global_energy_join user1 user2. this will make user1 use user2's energy when interacting with the global network. you can leave a network at any time by doing /gt global_energy_join your_name your_name.

you cannot connect wires to these blocks. these are also designed to be highly lag efficient, meaning eu is added at large intervals to prevent needless calculations from occurring. this will also save you some tps lag from vast wire networks.

[note]if your calculator is giving up, 2^(2^31) is a number with 646,456,994 digits.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 206, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:206", "name": "ulv wireless energy hatch", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 24438, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 206, "shard": "313af2c8b087f3bc", "recipes": 2}, "label": "ulv wireless energy hatch"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}, "1": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 1, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 32383, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.01", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.metaitem.01:32383", "name": "lv wireless energy cover", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.metaitem.01", "icon": 40836, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 32383, "shard": "bdcc901e29575e9d", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lv wireless energy cover"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:optional_retrieval"}} {}

name: Precise Assembler
Proto-Volt Stabilizer
text:
proto-volt stabilizer the proto-volt stabilizer (pvs) module is one of the first three modules you unlock right away for use in the exo-foundry.

the pvs module is a welcome addition for those who want to save power. it will give an eu discount equal to (100 - ((100 - 10x) * 0.8^x))% where x is the number of pvs modules installed to the foundry. 

so, for a t1 foundry, you can attain a 28% eu discount with one pvs module, and a 49% eu discount with two.

[note]this can be combined with other modules unlocked in the future for further eu discounts and other special effects![/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, name: Prototype Matter Manipulator
text:
prototype matter manipulator the matter manipulator is an extremely powerful tool that you can use during your entire playthrough. it is essentially a survival version of world-edit that is custom made for the gtnh player's convenience.

as you might expect, the prototype matter manipulator is the least powerful, most rudimentary version. you can only use the geometry mode to create and manipulate shapes for use in building. you will [warn]not[/warn] be able to remove blocks until you install an upgrade unlocked in ev.

you can find detailed information from the developer on: [url]https://github.com/gtnewhorizons/mattermanipulator/blob/master/readme.md[/url]

but the best way to learn about it is to use it! experiment with the ui and become familiar with how it works.

name: Quantum Uplink
text:
quantum uplink the quantum uplink is a multi made specifically for the matter manipulator that is unlocked with the aid of uv tech. 

this allows the matter manipulator to connect to your me system over an infinite range, and across dimensions. the tool can be linked by placing it into the controller while the uplink is active. the uplink will take a continuous 1a of zpm power to function.

additionally, you can now use it to create fake me patterns upon selecting an area. this will make it quick to order all of the parts needed for copy & pasting in an area. 

[warn]the uplink is powerful, but at a cost. moving all items / fluids from the ae system will cost a small amount of plasma per transfer.

name: Safety First
text:
safety first for those new to gregtech, here are some tips and warnings about electricity.

machines don't like being out in the rain, and will start fires nearby. fires next to a machine have a random chance of an explosion. also, sending a higher voltage than a machine's tier causes an explosion. or several, if you pack things together, like many people. sending more amps than a machine can use doesn't harm anything though.

sending too high a voltage or too many amps down a cable will cause the cable to burn up and start fires, which may then cause machine explosions. make sure the number of amps provided by generators and buffers to a cable does not exceed the amps it is capable of carrying.

a generator that supplies 1a can possibly feed multiple machines, if their recipes require less than the full voltage. for example, macerators processing ore only need 2 eu/t, so you could run several from a single 1a generator, as long as the wires aren't too long. why does that matter? because there's loss for every amp for every block, listed on the wire/cable. note that cables are better than wires. but be careful! sometimes a recipe needs a lot more eu than you expect, like a macerator sand -> quartz dust recipe.

most machines only use 1a, however there are exceptions, such as the thermal centrifuge, world accelerators, and the uum machines. note that machines can accept more amps than they use (usually 2) in order to top up their energy supply, especially if they didn't receive most of the amp because of loss (mostly a problem in lv). the formula is (eu/t of recipe * 2) / voltage tier + 1. keep this in mind when deciding on cables.

some machines are specifically there to help you deal with multiple amps, such as battery buffers, transformers, and diodes. check out the quest tab storing and transforming eu for more on those.

if you want to send more amps, use a larger cable or a superconductor (mv+, but ulv and lv have their own lossless cables). you can use laser hatches much later to send even more. there even are wireless options, but not right now.

a single block machine starved of eu will restart progress but not lose the recipe items. a multiblock machine will lose the items.

note that any block that emits eu has loss when doing so: 2 ^ (tier-1) per amp. so 1 eu at lv, 2 eu at mv, and so on. using large numbers of battery buffers in a row is thus very wasteful of your power. you have to be careful with losses when making your first ebf later in lv, maybe rather power them directly? of course, if you want to keep your amps topped up over longer distances, you'll need to place bbs occasionally to 'top up' the amps, though this is less the case the further ingame you get, as the loss becomes less of something to worry about.

if this info isn't enough for you, head on over to [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/electricity[/url] to read more.

if you prefer to learn via video there are also great youtube resources such as hamcorp's electricity guide: [url]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lpdpy8j-4qy[/url] {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "miscutils:itemhattinfoil", "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (miscutils:itemhattinfoil, metadata 0)"}}}}

name: Sending the Power Back
text:
sending the power back kinetic generator compatibility has been improved so that you no longer need transformers, you can connect directly with a cable. but why not use your transformer to send the power back to base more efficiently, it's a loss of about 97eu per hv amp just going from 160 straight down to 63 without it. if you transform up (after going through 1 block of cable to transform it to gt power), you only lose about 97eu per ev amp, which saves 4x the energy in regard to cable loss.

name: Sentient Overclocker
text:
sentient overclocker the sentient overclocker (so) module is the sixth module of the exo-foundry, and the only one unlocked in umv.

the so module, as you might imagine, increases the overclock factor of the foundry by 0.35. this means that for every overclock provided to this machine, it will give a 35% speed boost. 

for example, if your foundry has 1 overclock it should run at 2x base speed. however with this module it would instead run at 2.35x base speed (235%). this then compounds if another overclock is added, so instead of running at 2x the speed of the first overclock, it will run again at 2.35x the speed of the first overclock, bringing it to a total of 5.52x speed (552%).

additionally, this module can pair with the proto-volt stabilizer (pvs) module to unlock "harmonic efficiency" giving the foundry a 50% eu discount and an additional 0.1 overclock factor (2.45x instead of 2.35x).

name: Smelt All the Things...
text:
smelt all the things... smelting up to eight items at once sounds nice? with a bit of bronze & steel you can make a steam hearth for all your furnace needs!

aside from having 8x the parallels and 25% more speed, it's also significantly less steam intensive (per parallel) than the high pressure steam furnace. not only that, but depending on your input you can further increase your speed bonus by taking advantage of two special modes: blasting and smoking.

in blast mode, the steam hearth will smelt at 2x speed & use 2x steam for all metals, just like with the efr blast furnace. 

in smoke mode, the steam hearth will smelt at 2x speed & use 2x steam for all food-based recipes, just like with the efr smoker.

upgrading this multiblock to its high pressure variant also gives 2x speed & 2x steam usage.

[note]you can use a screwdriver to quickly swap between modes on the machine![/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, name: Steam-a-licious!
text:
steam-a-licious! you've almost made it. one last crafting step is required in order to advance to tier 1. keep going!

this steam turbine generates electricity from steam. the power source you've been using is the same, but from this point on you will generate eu, and bring it to your machines via cables, instead of bringing the steam directly to them. luckily, electric machines don't need an exhaust port, and they are considerably more efficient than bronze machines.

at a later point, you will most likely switch from steam to another fuel, though.

name: Streamlined Casters
text:
streamlined casters the streamlined casters (sc) module is one of the first three modules you unlock right away for use in the exo-foundry.

the sc module functions as a powerful 150% speed bonus for the foundry. if that's not enough for you, you can further amplify by another 150% for every sc module you install.

if this module paired with superdense casting basins (scb) module, you will unlock the "optimum production" bonus for 6 extra parallels per voltage tier and a further 75% speed increase.

lead boots allows you to walk under water, prevents you from swimming, and may cause excessive blub. bring along potions of water breathing.
slimy shoes reduces fall damage.

name: Turbine Time
text:
turbine time your fancy new large plasma turbine will need a rotor to go inside of it. you can make it out of any gt material, but the best right now is normal draconium.

[warn]always test in creative or the gtnh power planner (linked below) first![/warn]
[url]https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ftfdfmy_uwbtbfoynzarkei90pbhvpbh6m3jhjmac-e/edit?usp=dsharing[/url]

when using turbines, be careful of flow rates. to find the optimal flow rate manually, divide the optimal energy flow rate listed on the turbine, by the plasma's energy density (eu/l). you can also scan the multiblock's controller while feeding it a minimal amount of plasma to see what the optimal flow is. make sure to use a fluid regulator set to this flow rate for highest fuel efficiency, or go beyond it to get more eu/t at a lower efficiency. plasma turbines are the best at retaining efficiency beyond the optimal flow.

if you go beyond the optimal flow, you will get a higher eu/t value, but less fuel efficiency, and the maximum eu/t value depends on the turbine type and its overflow efficiency tier. for this type of turbine, tier 1 reaches the max at 250% of optimal flow to produce 158% of the eu/t, tier 2 reaches the max at 400% of optimal flow to produce 214% of the eu/t and tier 3 reaches the max at 550% of optimal flow to produce 301% of the eu/t. the closer you get to this maximum, the more fuel efficiency you're throwing away. the choice is yours!

name: Two Million Turbines
text:
two million turbines hopefully, not more than a handful. the objective here is for each of them to output close to 2 million eu/t.

how can you get there? look at the uv dynamo hatch's recipe and you have your new objective. when you arrive there, each turbine that is equipped with that impressive block will be able to output up to 2,097,152 eu/t, which again opens you up to new turbine opportunities. some good choices at this point are as follows:

large cosmic neutronium 225% 1,360,800 eu/t
large ichorium 225% 1,360,800 eu/t (very durable)
large awakened draconium 195% 491,400 eu/t
large trinium 185% 1,451,840 eu/t

at this point, you might consider building more t1 fusion reactors to process other materials. even if you stop the reactor you're using to generate this plasma, the eu cost of restarting it is less than 1 bucket of plasma, so it's probably not that big of a deal.

[note]at this point, you really should be looking into the xl turbine chain, from xl supercritical to dense to normal steam.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 38, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:38", "name": "uv dynamo hatch", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 25058, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 38, "shard": "de2a8905d4085a63", "recipes": 2}, "label": "uv dynamo hatch"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: UV Power Per Turbine
text:
uv power per turbine once you progress enough in zpm to make zpm dynamo hatches, you can increase each turbine's output to 524,288 eu/t. at this number, you'll be a lot less limited by the turbine material, and it's possible to increase the total power output of one fusion reactor considerably. you can cover the total helium plasma output from one reactor with 3 plasma turbines, if you choose the right materials:

large high durability compound steel 235% 473,759 eu/t
large atomic separation catalyst 206% 409,663 eu/t
large adamantium 206% 413,280 eu/t
large draconium 175% 220,500 eu/t (durable)
large neutronium 165% 249,480 eu/t (very durable)

the power output and final efficiency can vary a lot, based on which turbines you're using. some of them, like ichorium and neutronium, last basically forever, while others will need to be replaced from time to time but offer higher efficiency. if you want to get more power per turbine, to reach closer to the dynamo's limit, you can increase the flow of plasma to the turbine, but be careful! you can't go beyond the dynamo's limit, and you will also lose efficiency as you increase the flow amount. more concrete values for efficiency loss can be found in the plasma turbine quest in the luv page.

[note]also, check out the xl plasma turbine.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 37, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:37", "name": "zpm dynamo hatch", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 25052, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 37, "shard": "f894e6e47f6d4598", "recipes": 2}, "label": "zpm dynamo hatch"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Universal Collapser
text:
universal collapser the universal collapser (uc) module is the final module unlock for the exo-foundry.

the uc module quadruples power consumption and processing speed, allows uiv+ recipe processing, and increases the minimum number of casings by 15, leaving space for only 10 inputs (without an scb module installed). only one uc module can be installed per foundry.

this becomes much more powerful if paired with the hypercooler (hc) module to achieve "realized potential", allowing eternity to be used as a coolant. using eternity as a coolant grants an additional 3 overclocks. the pairing also doubles both power consumption and processing speed.

name: Venting Heat
text:
venting heat heat vents are a passive way to remove heat from your reactor. their performance is measured in heat units per tick (hu/t), and there are a few different types that all work slightly differently.

these heat vents simply cool themselves after absorbing heat from adjacent fuel rods and heat exchangers:

heat vent: cools itself by 6 hu/t

advanced heat vent: cools itself by 12 hu/t

these heat vents absorb heat and cool themselves much like the ones above, but they also pull heat directly from the reactor core to themselves:

reactor heat vent: cools itself by 5 hu/t and the reactor by 5 hu/t

overclocked heat vent: cools itself by 20 hu/t and the reactor by 36 hu/t[note]since it pulls more heat from the reactor than it dissipates, these are prone to melting if their heat is not balanced by a heat exchanger[/note]

the component heat vent works differently to the other vents. rather than absorbing heat and cooling itself or the reactor, it simply cools adjacent components (but not fuel rods) by 4 hu/t {"0": text:

lapis - fortune on kills

name: Working Table 2.0
text:
working table 2.0 a manual crafting table which remembers the last nine used recipes. left-click one of the recipes shown in the right-hand side to automatically fill in the crafting grid. right-click to lock a memorized recipe and prevent a newer recipe from bumping it off.

resources need to go into the internal inventory. the crafting matrix is only a visual representation.

the forestry worktable is super-useful, and can reduce the tedium of many common jobs because you can click-drag across a row of items, and it will use tools in its own inventory to continue crafting.

specifically:
making <item x> with <bucket of y> - put all the ingredients into the table, and if the recipe is selected, shift-click the result to craft them all at once (until you run out)
making fresh water for pam's - same as above, but no second item
making clay bricks - the wooden form is automatically reused
making anything that uses a tool - also automatically reused, while consuming durability

[warn]warning: stored recipes will be lost if the worktable is broken! to avoid this, move it using a dolly.[/warn]

name: pH Neutralization
Bees Template
text:
bees template get the princess bee and reward bag in nei first.
copy this quest.
press icon and set the icon to the bee.
change the name, description, and rewards.

press task, and select the stone, and replace it with the princess.
before closing, select the ... next to the bee name and press raw nbt
go into tag, genome, chromosomes. the first one is the name and must stay.
go inside there and delete the first entry, keep both of the species so players
must have purebreeds.
delete the rest of the chromosomes.
delete the rest of the entries for genome.

press requirements. remove the infinity unlock requirement and select the required bee quests. use the common bees quest if nothing applies.

change show:hidden to show:normal.

to reduce waste in the questbook file ideally you should also go into the advanced options, then press ... for the icon, and remove unnecessary nbt there as well. just leave the species as above.

name: Adding More Functions
Alleviating Warp
text:
alleviating warp when you get poisoned or withered a bit of milk solves the problem. why not create something akin to milk, but for warp effects?

briar gives a bit of an answer to that. these two block tall plants, which require good light to grow, will produce briar seed bags when harvested. those can be combined with sugar and a suitable container in an arcane workbench to create rosehip syrup.

rosehip syrup stacks up to 16 and can be used the same as milk, also removing some (though not all) warp effects as well as flux flue and flux phage.

the plant has a strange life cycle where the seed pods will first appear as yellow dots, turn pink as they start to mature, then disappear, only to return fully matured. still, if it works, it works. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "thaumicbases:briar", "resolved": {"id": "i:thaumicbases:briar:0", "name": "briar", "mod": "thaumicbases", "registry": "briar", "icon": 51570, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "e8339530e451c876", "recipes": 1}, "label": "briar"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}, "1": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 1, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "thaumicbases:rosehipsyrup", "resolved": {"id": "i:thaumicbases:rosehipsyrup:0", "name": "rosehip syrup", "mod": "thaumicbases", "registry": "rosehipsyrup", "icon": 51690, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "537109686e31a39f", "recipes": 1}, "label": "rosehip syrup"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 4, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "thaumcraft:itemessence", "resolved": {"id": "i:thaumcraft:itemessence:0", "name": "glass phial", "mod": "thaumcraft", "registry": "itemessence", "icon": 12160, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "29ac04cd2c8f2bfa", "recipes": 2}, "label": "glass phial"}, "1": {"count": 4, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "minecraft:sugar", "resolved": {"id": "i:minecraft:sugar:0", "name": "sugar", "mod": "minecraft", "registry": "sugar", "icon": 48679, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "bdad2aa3940c6b73", "recipes": 8}, "label": "sugar"}}}}

name: Comparing at a Distance
Counting Items
text:
counting items the remote comparator makes it significantly easier to get comparator signals out of whatever block you want, but looking at your storage chests you can't help but see no reason to bother. so what if they're nearly full? you want to know what they're nearly full of.

tally boxes can be pointed at a container - either directly or, using a remote comparator, remotely - and given a runic whitelist that specifies conditions where you want a tally box to send a redstone signal. quantity, metadata and nbt matching are options, as is using a basic name filter.

note that the redstone side is always opposite the reading side, and remote comparators must be placed on top of tally boxes to work together, meaning redstone is always output on the down face in that case.

name: Cursed Earth
Division Sigil
text:
division sigil find a sigil in a chest? get one from the wither? you've heard about a ritual to activate it.

you need an enchantment table, 8 redstone dust, a weapon, and an animal you want to sacrifice. catching and holding it with a golden lasso would be the easiest way. check in lv for the golden lasso quest if you haven't completed it yet.

place your enchantment table on a grass field and surround it with redstone dust. at midnight, place the animal on or near the table and kill it. you can check with the sigil if it's time yet by right-clicking it on the enchantment table. of course you also need to have your sigil on you.

name: Essentia Filtering
text:
essentia filtering this nifty little device will filter essentia out of an alchemical crucible or alchemical boiler. once it has received a single unit of any type, it will only accept this type until it is completely empty. you can place more than one on top of an alchemical furnace, and you should. try to have one per essentia type in the item you're melting on a furnace.

name: Essentia Storage
text:
essentia storage at long last, you have all the tools to smelt items into essentia, keep it stable, and store it for later use.

the last step was creating warded jars, relatively simple creations that keep essentia in a quasi-liquid state, which makes it easier to keep essentia from turning into flux. unlike phials, which must hold 8 essentia exactly to keep it stable, warded jars can store anywhere from 1 to 64 essentia.

these warded jars are safe to pick up and carry around, which you suspect will not be the case for most objects storing much more essentia than these jars do. right-click them with a label to filter that jar to a specific type of essentia. use a preset label if the jar is still empty.

sneak-right-click with an empty hand to remove a label from a jar, or void the essentia it contains if it doesn't have a label. voiding essentia from jars will not generate flux, because... magic, i guess. it's very convenient, so just politely don't question it too much. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 8, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "thaumcraft:blockjar", "resolved": {"id": "i:thaumcraft:blockjar:0", "name": "warded jar", "mod": "thaumcraft", "registry": "blockjar", "icon": 12553, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "b86b141e37a20f5d", "recipes": 1}, "label": "warded jar"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}, "1": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 1, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 8, "damage": 13, "oredict": "", "id": "thaumcraft:itemresource", "resolved": {"id": "i:thaumcraft:itemresource:13", "name": "jar label", "mod": "thaumcraft", "registry": "itemresource", "icon": 12337, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 13, "shard": "e1aa70f66c388de2", "recipes": 2}, "label": "jar label"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 8, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "thaumcraft:blockjar", "resolved": {"id": "i:thaumcraft:blockjar:0", "name": "warded jar", "mod": "thaumcraft", "registry": "blockjar", "icon": 12553, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "b86b141e37a20f5d", "recipes": 1}, "label": "warded jar"}}}}

name: Growing Auram
text:
growing auram one essentia you might have a hard time gathering is auram. maybe you've gotten some from ethereal essence, which is dropped by the flying balls of light that rarely show up in the nether, or some from nodes. but that is hardly a good supply. the aurelia plant can resolve this.

when a full moon is visible overhead, aurelia flowers will open up their petals presumably to feed off of the light. significant for you is that they will occasionally shed these petals, which can be collected off the ground as a dense source of auram essentia.

you should make sure the ground near the flower is level and clear, so you'll be able to collect the petals later. the flower itself is simply planted on grass, not farmland, so no need to have a water source nearby either.

[note]gaia wart is also a growable source of auram essentia. it has a quest in the green revolution quest tab.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "thaumicbases:aurelia", "resolved": {"id": "i:thaumicbases:aurelia:0", "name": "aurelia", "mod": "thaumicbases", "registry": "aurelia", "icon": 51564, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "c8a0e85d82011160", "recipes": 1}, "label": "aurelia"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 5, "oredict": "", "id": "thaumicbases:resource", "resolved": {"id": "i:thaumicbases:resource:5", "name": "aurelia petal", "mod": "thaumicbases", "registry": "resource", "icon": 51670, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 5, "shard": "97dac451cf6731a6", "recipes": 0}, "label": "aurelia petal"}}}}

name: Growing your own Knowledge!
I Can See Everything
text:
i can see everything with your new wand, you can make goggles of revealing. you can now see nodes clearly, more so than with the thaumometer, but all the time! additionally, the goggles give you a 5 percent vis discount.

simple lens upgrades will grant you various seeing abilities as well.

later you can make more advanced goggles and even integrate the goggles into advanced armors.

name: Infused Stones
text:
infused stones this whole place here is filled with magic. no matter where you look at, it's just everywhere. you wonder what happens to regular stone if it's exposed to large amounts of magic for such a long time. maybe it's time to go mining?

there are 3 veins. there's amber and cinnabar in each. they aren't super useful, but make sure to keep hold of some at least.

even when you find these infused stones, they won't drop the infused shards you desperately need. rather, you have to process the raw ores themselves. the easiest way to do that is to throw these raw ores in your forge hammer.

later when you have a sifter, you can sift purified ores for more shards. an autoclave can also turn shard dust into a shard. maybe there's a magical way to do the same thing? {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, name: Keeping Out the Riff-Raff
text:
keeping out the riff-raff you're starting to get tired of having to build everything like some kind of fortress just to make sure no unwanted guests come in. sure, that's just the nature of living in a world where infinite hoards of restless undead haunt every other dark corner, but is having a secure entryway that isn't conveniently door-shaped too much to ask?

not anymore. paving stone of warding, assuming nothing sits on top of it, will project a two block tall invisible force-field above itself that block non-player mobs from passing through, at least the common riff-raff. as a bonus spiders cannot climb the force-field, so no need for overhangs to keep them out too.

that said, since the force-field cannot tell an arrow fired by you from one fired at you, mundane objects will still pass through regardless. and the force-field does as much to block line of sight as the term invisible would suggest.

of course, you're not concerned about that part. being able to shoot things with your crossbow while they can't reach you is very much in your favor, all told. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 4, "damage": 3, "oredict": "", "id": "thaumcraft:blockcosmeticsolid", "resolved": {"id": "i:thaumcraft:blockcosmeticsolid:3", "name": "paving stone of warding", "mod": "thaumcraft", "registry": "blockcosmeticsolid", "icon": 12521, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 3, "shard": "5dff30bacc796bfd", "recipes": 1}, "label": "paving stone of warding"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 4, "damage": 3, "oredict": "", "id": "thaumcraft:blockcosmeticsolid", "resolved": {"id": "i:thaumcraft:blockcosmeticsolid:3", "name": "paving stone of warding", "mod": "thaumcraft", "registry": "blockcosmeticsolid", "icon": 12521, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 3, "shard": "5dff30bacc796bfd", "recipes": 1}, "label": "paving stone of warding"}}}}

name: Scanning Made Easy
text:
scanning made easy we get it; the early-game of thaumcraft requires a lot of research and you don't want to throw every one of your 1000 items on the ground and scan them for aspects. that's why we added 2 cool qol features which makes this tedious task very quick and easy.

1. you don't actually have to throw the item on the ground. you can scan it directly from your inventory! simply hover your thaumometer over the item you want to scan, and after a short duration it will be scanned.

2. you've probably accumulated dozens of double chests full of junk that you don't want to sift through and scan, so there's a second feature now: scanning entire chests! simply shift right-click while hovering over a chest with your thaumometer and it'll scan every item inside of the chest. though before you can do so you have to learn a bit more about deconstruction in the thaumonomicon.

[note]hint: to unlock the research to scan entire chests, go to your thaumonomicon, open "basic information" (the first tab), and complete this research path: research -> research expertise -> deconstruction table -> container scanning.[/note] {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "thaumcraft:itemlootbag", "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (thaumcraft:itemlootbag, metadata 0)"}}}}

name: Taint Warnings
text:
taint warnings now that you have started using vis in the form of essentia, a warning about taint.

vis in the state of essentia is unstable if not stored properly. left alone too long, or emptied out of the crucible, essentia will break down. but not into vis. rather, it will turn into flux.

flux manifests as a liquid or a gas, but is, itself, only a nuisance. thaumaturges exposed to the stuff can end up getting flux flue, a condition which makes it harder to channel vis, but it is only temporary.

larger concentrations of flux will solidify into thaumic slimes, bizarre creatures that try to merge with each other to grow larger. they can be dangerous, but are no less susceptible to crossbow bolts than most things.

however, if too much flux is allowed to linger for too long, it will corrupt the land and solidify into tendrils. this is a manifestation of the blight called taint. fibrous tendrils (as well as condensed blocks thereof) spread the tainted lands, feeding on the magic it twists. nodes are especially vulnerable, becoming tainted themselves if exposed to this twisted magic.

destroying the tendrils stops the spread, but unless all are destroyed this is only temporary. a more effective solution is to destroy the tainted land itself, as outside this specific biome tendrils quickly starve and die off.

if you are exceedingly careless with your crucible you can, in fact, create tainted lands. so you would be wise to try wasting as little essentia as possible, and clean up any you do waste. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Thaumic Dendrology
text:
thaumic dendrology thaumcraft saplings can be quite useful early on, now that you have access to infusion you can create them. each type has a special trait:

golden oak - drops golden apples as opposed to regular apples.

nether - creates a miniature nether biome upon placement that can spawn mobs- be careful! placing the leaves from this tree on top of a block will cause that block to turn into its nether counterpart.

ender - creates a miniature end biome upon placement that can also spawn mobs. placing the leaves from this tree on top of a block will cause that block to turn into its end counterpart. (a great source of endstone)

peaceful - gathers passive creatures underneath its leaves. the types of animals attracted depends on the biome its planted in. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, name: The Burden of Knowledge
text:
the burden of knowledge have you made too many mistakes and researched yourself into a corner by getting too much warp with no way to get rid of it? do you wish you could just start everything over? the [warn]potion of blissful oblivion[/warn] is the solution you are looking for.

at the cost of your knowledge of [warn]all research, all discovered aspects, all knowledge points in the research table, and everything scanned with a thaumometer[/warn], all of your warp will be removed. it won't do anything about warp from armor, so you might still get minor warp events if you're wearing any warpy armor. be absolutely certain you know what you are doing before you drink this.

keep in mind that there are better alternatives for dealing with warp (which you can see in the adept thaumaturgy tab). this is just the cheapest one.

[note]it's also a rather decent source of strontio.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "warptheory:item.warptheory.oblivionpotion", "resolved": {"id": "i:warptheory:item.warptheory.oblivionpotion:0", "name": "potion of blissful oblivion", "mod": "warptheory", "registry": "item.warptheory.oblivionpotion", "icon": 13217, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "d712cde9a00e6c0b", "recipes": 1}, "label": "potion of blissful oblivion"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "thaumcraft:itemlootbag", "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (thaumcraft:itemlootbag, metadata 0)"}, "1": {"count": 8, "damage": 9, "oredict": "", "id": "thaumcraft:itemresource", "resolved": {"id": "i:thaumcraft:itemresource:9", "name": "knowledge fragment", "mod": "thaumcraft", "registry": "itemresource", "icon": 12420, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 9, "shard": "771f42d7bd430138", "recipes": 1}, "label": "knowledge fragment"}}}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 5, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:coindarkwizard", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:coindarkwizard:0", "name": "coin "the dark wizard 1"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "coindarkwizard", "icon": 20754, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "557384ac0b019618", "recipes": 1}, "label": "coin "the dark wizard 1""}}}}

name: Timewood Tree
text:
timewood tree the timewood clock is a special block that can be obtained in the twilight forest. it can be used to accelerate vanilla crops in a 16 block radius, making farms significantly faster and more efficient.

to get one, you must explore inside the massive twilight forest trees and search the loot chests hidden within them. there is a small chance to find a tree of time sapling. the clock generates hidden inside the tree after it grows.
[warn]
after growing the tree, you will need a silk touch tool to obtain the timewood clock itself.[/warn]
[note]

name: Tube Madness
text:
tube madness so you want to move essentia from your alchemical furnace to your warded jars without getting it all gunked up with different essentia types?

well you came to the right place, with the use of buffered tubes and your handy wand you can move your essentia in tubes to fill all your jars without having to manually break and replace one jar at a time.

to create a simple setup place the buffered tubes in a main line from your arcane alembic with tubes coming out of the main buffered tube line. these standard tubes will then go directly into a warded jar. to get the essentia to flow correctly into the buffered tubes, shift-right-click the output side of the buffered tube with your wand until it is red. this will change the band to a red band which will limit the suction of the essentia.

the essentia will be forced from the buffered tube to a normal tube then into your warded jars. chain your buffered tubes as needed until all your warded jars will fit.

note: this system will get gunked up with essentia if any of your warded jars are full!

if you would like more information please check out the guide 'a thaumaturge guide to laying pipe' by xlstadal for more in-depth thaumcraft 4 tube knowledge.

name: Understanding Wand Progression
text:
understanding wand progression more advanced thaumcraft recipes require larger and larger amounts of vis that your initial wands can't handle. you need to progress bit by bit to increase your capabilities. the progression is two-fold:

first, you need to craft more advanced wands, the greatwood wand is next. and secondly, you need to improve your crafting discounts. they reduce the vis cost of crafts and thus also let you craft higher vis recipes.

in your progression you will need to rely on both aspects. better wands and higher discounts. however, as you progress, there are many different ways on how to proceed. some ways focus more on discounts, others more on wands. therefore, the questbook can only give you some general advice.

for example, when making a new wand type, it is always cheapest to first make it with iron caps and then try to improve it afterwards. one way you can improve your wand is by swapping the cores & caps for higher tiers as you unlock them (see "substitution" research). however, if you are able to obtain enough discounts you can directly make the wand with gold caps or better, skipping the iron capped wand altogether.

but before all these options really open up, let us work on that greatwood wand! {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Warp Warnings
text:
warp warnings thaumcraft offers considerable power from its devices and tools. but power comes with a price.... that price is represented by warp: a corruption of the character's mind and soul, inflicting progressively more dire effects upon them.

while the effects of warp can range from annoying to deadly, accumulating enough of it can also grant you access to greater power... at the cost of increasing madness, and attention from dark powers. at least, others may call it madness... but is it truly insanity, when the voices in your head grant useful knowledge?

warp theory adds a bunch of new warp effects to the player. be very careful because you don't want to spawn a wither in your base.

[note]if you're still early on in your thaumcraft journey, warp shouldn't be something that scares you away from progressing further. you'll only stumble upon dangerous warp effects once you've done a lot of research. if you still wanna play it safe, make sure to avoid research that's labeled with "forbidden knowledge" [/note]

name: Convocation of the Damned
text:
convocation of the damned time to open a portal to the demonic realm. what could possibly go wrong? (it's recommended to do this ritual in a space dimension, as the demon city spreads up to 1000x1000 blocks)

[note]you should also be starting the ritual from the ground rather than in the air for the best results![/note]

requirements:
- 15m lp (archmage blood orb and >= 13 runes of the orb)
- 8 crystal belljars (one filled with each of: magicales, potentia, incendium, terrae, tenebrae, sanctus, aether, and aquasalus)
- 1 sacrifice (bottle a lesser demon/elemental in a soul vial)
- 1 master ritual stone, 128 ritual stones, and 1 blood altar
- 1 awakened activation crystal

steps to the ritual:
1. use a ritual diviner to place all the ritual stones.
2. place the belljars atop the 8 pillars surrounding the center.
3. link the belljars to the master ritual stone.
4. place the blood altar on top of the master ritual stone.
5. start the ritual with the awakened activation crystal.
6. the belljars are drained of their reagents.
7. kill the lesser demon/elemental with a dagger of sacrifice.
8. the demon portal is opened.

for more details and images, visit [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/convocation_of_the_damned[/url]

name: Incense Crucible
text:
incense crucible the forefather of the 1.12.2 incense altar.

the bonuses it gives are mostly similar, but the way it works is completely different.
each incense is meant to be tiered one after another. currently you can only use wood ash and byrrus (red).

white smoke will come out when there is an incense in the crucible, and the crucible will light up when it finds a player to increase the incense value of.
once the player has an incense value greater than 0, their sacrificial knife will get super-charged, allowing the player to completely sacrifice all of their hearts but one.

putting wood ash in the crucible will increase the incense value from 0 to 400.
byrrus increases it from 400 to 800. it cannot get you from 0 to 800 alone.

the lp you get from self-sacrifice will get a boost depending on your incense value.

lp = 200lp * heartsacrificed * incensemodifier

incensemodifier = 1 + incensevalue * 0.001 {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": name: Paying the Highest Price
text:
paying the highest price when regular magic just isn't enough, you need something... stronger. which is paid with blood. your blood, and maybe others'.

in tier 1 you only need to place the blood altar. plan for the configuration to grow in size up to 23x23 for a single altar.

keep in mind that you get less blood, and use more when crafting in gtnh. plan for pain and frustration too.

the altar has a 10,000l blood tank, plus a 1,000l i/o buffer (you can pump in and out, but the rate is pitifully low at the start). blood will flow to the i/o buffer until it's full, so be aware of that before your first craft. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "awwayoftime:altar", "resolved": {"id": "i:awwayoftime:altar:0", "name": "altar of gregoriust's blood", "mod": "awwayoftime", "registry": "altar", "icon": 1505, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "4b69d02d82d79e35", "recipes": 1}, "label": "altar of gregoriust's blood"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 16, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:16", "name": "lootbag (bm novice)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21202, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 16, "shard": "67d93dc1c215e12e", "recipes": 0}, "label": "lootbag (bm novice)"}}}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:coinbloodii", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:coinbloodii:0", "name": "coin "the vampire 100"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "coinbloodii", "icon": 20731, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "262ca2165a21f503", "recipes": 2}, "label": "coin "the vampire 100""}}}}

name: Portable Battery...
text:
portable battery... using this binds it to you (expect to do that a lot), and consumes one heart while depositing 200lp in your 'soul network'. you can draw upon the soul network for anything that needs lp such as alchemy or rituals. if you want to automate it, you can put it into your altar for a 1:1 conversion of blood.

the highest tier orb you have bound will be considered the maximum limit to lp in your network, but you'll need to put it into the appropriately tiered altar to keep absorbing blood. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "awwayoftime:weakbloodorb", "resolved": {"id": "i:awwayoftime:weakbloodorb:0", "name": "weak blood orb", "mod": "awwayoftime", "registry": "weakbloodorb", "icon": 1652, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "66ea93e59b59f053", "recipes": 0}, "label": "weak blood orb"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 16, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:16", "name": "lootbag (bm novice)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21202, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 16, "shard": "67d93dc1c215e12e", "recipes": 0}, "label": "lootbag (bm novice)"}}}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 5, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:coinbloodi", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:coinbloodi:0", "name": "coin "the vampire 10"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "coinbloodi", "icon": 20733, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "afe84e6983e1e128", "recipes": 2}, "label": "coin "the vampire 10""}}}}

name: Ritual of Gaia's Transformation
text:
ritual of gaia's transformation the ritual of gaia's transformation is the blood magic way of changing biomes. it consists of 116 ritual stones, including the dusk ones, and requires an awakened activation crystal.

to use the ritual, simply activate it, and it will transform an area up to 21x21.

if you want to change the biome you get from the ritual, use arcane plinths. the ritual starts from 0.5 humidity and 0.5 temperature, then consumes the items placed on the plinths to increase or decrease those values. it also starts by assuming a range of 0.1 is acceptable in both directions.

the items that modify these values are as follows:
- sand -> humidity -0.1
- sandstone -> humidity -0.2
- netherrack -> humidity -0.4
- lapis -> humidity +0.1
- water bucket -> humidity +0.2
- lapis block -> humidity +0.4
- coal -> temperature +0.1
- coal block -> temperature +0.2
- lava bucket -> temperature +0.4
- snowball -> temperature -0.1
- snow block -> temperature -0.2
- ice block -> temperature -0.4

once you have used the items to reach your desired environment, the ritual will give you a biome from it. if there are multiple biomes with that humidity and temperature, you can use wool to determine the exact one, for up to 17 conflicting biomes. if the ritual cannot find a valid biome, it will default to plains.

some cool ones include, but are not limited to:
- sky (also known as end) -> orange wool
- eldritch -> cyan wool
- eerie -> light gray wool
- tf forest -> pink wool
- sacred springs -> yellow wool
- tainted land -> purple or blue wool
- moon -> 0% humidity, no wool
- mars flat -> 0% humidity, white wool
- asteroids -> 0% humidity, orange wool
- space -> 0% humidity, magenta wool
- toxic everglades -> 70% humidity, no wool

name: Summon the Meteor!
text:
summon the meteor! the mark of the falling tower is among the most powerful magic you can achieve in gtnh. it allows you to summon a huge meteor full of various gt ores right where you want it. all you need is a particular catalyst item and a good amount of lp. even better, you sometimes get access to ores before you could get them normally! check out nei for all the possible meteors. for example you can start by looking at the uses of a pufferfish.

the meteor requires at least a singular block to see the sky above the master ritual stone. you can use the alchemical component terrae to increase the radius of the meteor by 1. using orbis terrae increases the radius by 2.

the meteor deals some damage but it does not deal environmental/block damage. just be weary if you have villagers or important mobs nearby. the size of the meteor also increases the damage & radius by an enormous amount.

multiblock miners can mine out the various ores spawned from the meteor, but there are other options too! {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0,
