name: RP-1 Rocket Fuel
text:
rp-1 rocket fuel one option to fuel your t1 and t2 rocket is rp-1 rocket fuel. first, you'll need either diesel or coal tar. coal tar is the better option in the long run, since you'll need the other products of distilling it to make other rocket fuels, but for now you can use diesel.

[note]if you're using diesel, you need 20 cells, if using coal tar, you need 30. unless you use a dt, in which case it doesn't divide evenly anymore.[/note]

distill it in the distillery to get kerosene, then distill it again to get rp-1. you'll need a chemical plant for the last step.

rp-1 rocket fuel is a t4 240 eu/t recipe, so you'll need to make the chemical plant out of stainless steel and hv machine casings.

since there is no oxygen in space, you will also need an oxidizer. but since the galacticraft rocket can only take one fluid we have simplified that a bit. just combine liquid oxygen and rp-1 to make the fully functional rp-1 rocket fuel.

if you're confused about how to use/make the chemical plant, refer to the manual with the same name or the quest in the gt++ quest tab.

[note]ps: you can also use rocket fuels for power in rocket engines, or the rocketdyne f-1a engine multi.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 1, name: Rocket Fuel
text:
rocket fuel for every flight the rocket needs some fuel. so refine some fuel for your rocket.
this quest chain will guide you through the progression of rocket fuels.

for your t1 & t2 rockets you have 2 options. you can either use cetane-boosted diesel or make rp-1 rocket fuel.

for the moon, a full rocket leaving from the overworld should have enough fuel left to make it back, but you might want to take extra just in case.

[note]rocket fuel usage is not based on the destination nor the type of fuel used. rather, it is based on the tier of the rocket, with higher tiers both storing more fuel, and consuming less. also, the gravity of the planet affects how much fuel is used, with lower gravity locations using less fuel to launch.[/note] {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Rocket Launch Pad
text:
rocket launch pad every rocket needs a launch pad. build a 3x3 launch pad and place your rocket on top of it.

storms and other events that affect entities can knock your rocket off (but not lightning warp anymore), so make sure to not leave it alone.

[warn]before liftoff, make sure you clear the airspace above you![/warn]

be sure to check out [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/moon_travel_checklist[/url] for a departure checklist!

[note]also note that they emit pollution, lots of it. so either put it far from your base, or use a scrubber while launching. you probably won't have to worry until t4 or so though.[/note] {"0": name: Serious Upgrades
text:
serious upgrades so if you thought 'hey, the purple stuff wasn't that bad, why not make the green?', well, first of all, you may need professional help. second, you're going to need to be in zpm to make the casings you need, full stop. you need a zpm abs for the components, so come back once you've made a zpm energy hatch.

you can probably figure most of it out on your own, but keep in mind that some of the materials need to be created in the abs, solidified, macerated, and then used in another abs recipe. the examples here are hastelloy-n for lafium compound and, rhenium for laurenium. rhenium itself is made with a nonstandard abs recipe. you also need dysprosium which requires either making rare earth (iii) or going to the toxic everglades. you'll also need either rare earth (ii) or rare earth (iii) for ytterbium unless, again, you visit the everglades for it. [warn]the everglades ore veins might be very hard to find, due to their rarity.[/warn] you could also get ytterbium from almandine ore if you are willing to try gt++ milling and froth flotation.

have fun with that!

name: Sleeping in Space
text:
sleeping in space the cryogenic chamber is used to sleep on other planets and skip long nighttimes. it can be used at any time, even during the daytime, and in any dimension, including the overworld.

using the chamber during the daytime will skip the time to the next sunrise, except on the asteroids dimension where the sun is always locked on west.

once the player has used the cryogenic chamber, there is a 300 second cooldown before they can use it again. breaking and replacing the chamber, or trying to use a different chamber, will not reset the cooldown unless the player dies.

the chamber does not require energy to work. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": name: Slimeling
text:
slimeling the slimeling is a utility mob that spawns from slimeling eggs found on the surface of mars. it shares some features from vanilla wolves and mules: it can be tamed and attacks mobs that threaten its owners, and can be equipped with a special chest to transport items.

as an allied mob, slimelings will actively help and follow the player-owner and will attempt to protect them. they can also have a neutral behavior, that is, they can attack if provoked or hurt by non-owners.

items that you can feed slimelings with:

boat
cooked fish
gunpowder
gold ingot
redstone repeater
wooden door

slimelings can be equipped by their owners with a slimeling inventory bag to transport items.

to complete this quest get any one of the eggs - note you may need a heavy duty pickaxe. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, name: Space Pumping
text:
space pumping at some point you may have wondered: there are these enormous gas planets in the solar system - could there be a way to "harvest" them? indeed there is. by constructing the "planetary gas siphon" multiblock, you are able to pump from the infinite supply of gas found on jupiter, saturn, uranus, and neptune. you just need to build a space station around a gas planet to get close enough to reach the gas without falling into it.

different gases can be extracted by pumping at different depths which is controlled by a programmed circuit. you need to supply (64 * depth) mining pipes to reach the selected depth.

while operational, the multiblock needs d*4^(t+2) eu/t where t is the tier of the space station and d is the depth.

you do not need a minimum tier of coil to siphon particular gas types, but you will get a 10% speed boost per coil tier.

you probably also want a good overview of what you can get with your planetary gas siphon, and the tiers of the gas giants. so here we go:

jupiter (tier 3)
1 hydrogen - 15000 l/s
2 helium - 500 l/s
3 nitrogen - 300 l/s
4 oxygen - 200 l/s

saturn (tier 5)
1 hydrogen - 18000 l/s
2 helium - 800 l/s
3 oxygen - 500 l/s
4 liquid oxygen - 150 l/s

uranus (tier 5)
1 deuterium - 5000 l/s
2 neon - 450 l/s
3 argon - 250 l/s
4 krypton - 100 l/s

neptune (tier 6)
1 tritium - 3000 l/s
2 helium-3 - 500 l/s
3 ammonia - 400 l/s
4 xenon - 350 l/s {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 15559, name: Space Station
text:
space station you can build a space station if you want. you can add up to four spin thrusters to your station to rotate it.

days on space stations last longer than on the overworld, so you can generate more solar power.

you can build space stations here:
1. moon - t1
2. mars - t2
3. jupiter - t3
4. venus - t4
5. saturn - t5
6. uranus - t5
7. neptune - t6

each retrieval task in this quest corresponds (in order) to the resources you will need in order to build a space station at one of the planets listed above. the "t#" afterwards refers to the tier of rocket you will need to get there.

[note]you will need to complete at least one task to complete this quest![/note]

[warn]it is likely that you will lose your rocket when flying back to earth or another space station. make sure you have an alternative way to return (some form of teleportation) or use another name: Battery Buffer
text:
battery buffer batteries work pretty much the same in a battery buffer as in a regular machine's battery slot. battery buffers are used to buffer power to stabilize output.

they come in different sizes: 1, 4, 9(!) and 16 slots. they can draw 2a and output 1a per battery inserted - watch your wire amperage! cables come in 1x, 2x, 4x, 8x, 12x, and 16x, with tin transferring 1a per size. make sure not to mess up, or your cable will melt, becoming a fire, and possibly an explosion.

remember that there's loss when outputting eu from any gt machine, so putting 4 4-slot ones in a row loses 8 power compared to 2 from 1 16-slot one. and this is for every amp too.

[note]you can import batteries into one, but only empty acid batteries can be exported from one. no, you can't get around this.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 171, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:171", "name": "low voltage battery buffer", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 24253, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 171, "shard": "78f7f30211eff705", "recipes": 1}, "label": "low voltage battery buffer"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 4, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:4", "name": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21242, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 4, "shard": "3cff4d8e3920defe", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)"}}}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 3, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:cointechniciani", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:cointechniciani:0", "name": "coin "the technician 10"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "cointechniciani", "icon": 20788, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "53205e7d44e6e7e5", "recipes": 2}, "label": "coin "the technician 10""}}}}

name: Gotta Pump It Up
text:
gotta pump it up if you made it this far you may have already noticed that you cannot pour vanilla water into the dam. that's what a hydroenergy pump is for. this multi-block exists in multiple tiers and will allow you to reach higher water levels (= more energy capacity). provide the pump with vanilla water as input and pipe the fluid output into the dam. then the dam will slowly fill up. if the dam is full or full for a pump's voltage tier, it will void the water and energy.

name: Infinite Energy Storage
text:
infinite energy storage you shouldn't click on links from strangers! although this sounds like clickbait it is true. from a certain point of view.

use the (potential) force! and store energy that way. simply construct a dam and flood vast areas with water. you may add energy to your storage by pumping more water into it or just drain it back into energy whenever you need. this works especially well with fluctuating energy sources like wind, water, and solar. or you dump excess energy into it so you can use it another time. the capacity is huge and the choice is yours.

sounds great! but...? - indeed. there is a catch: pumps and turbines will have efficiency correlated loss. still interested? let's get to crafting!

the multi-block has an unusual shape: the back is open. the lake will spawn inside the multi-block and spread block-by-block as far as it can/is allowed. it will replace plants like water (make sure to secure your crops!) but not replace any solid blocks. additionally, you can specify limits in any direction. the water will never spread past these limits. you can set those limits in a second gui by right-clicking the controller with a screwdriver.

when you enter a limit, it will correct itself to the nearest valid setting. especially if you try to spread past the server limits. you may talk your admin into raising these limits (these limits are designed to limit griefing). further, water is not able to spread into foreign towns.
you will also find 3 magical buttons in the top-right of this gui. from left to right: the first will slowly despawn the lake blocks. you can use this to shrink the lake if it spread past a barrier for example. the multi-block will also initialize with this configuration so there is no accidental flooding. the second and third buttons will slowly spawn more lake blocks. additionally, the second button will render those lake blocks pink so you see where they are so you may plug holes and such. in this "debug" mode you can walk/breathe/act in the lake like in air. this should make it easy to create a sunken village for decoration purposes. the third button is for normal operations so you can see the water and enjoy a swim in your energy buffer.

of course, there is also a normal gui (simple right-click). it shows you the energy stored in the dam. to reach higher water levels you are required to use stronger pumps. for this purpose, you may configure the voltage tier of the gui with a circuit in the circuit slot. don't worry: it is only optical. you cannot void any energy if you set a low voltage tier. it is only for the player information. you may give it a try with the reward you earn...

if you have any further questions, find missing information, or have suggestions please do not hesitate to post on the official gt new horizons discord. please add '@sinth0r4s' to your post to make sure i'll see it.

[warn]a warning though: there have been a lot of mentions of bugs and even world corruptions caused by the hydro dam. use at your own risk. if you have more detailed information, please report these name: Low Voltage Transformer
text:
low voltage transformer it is possible to run mv machines while still in lv - build a transformer and use 4 power sources 32 eu/t to power one 128 eu/t machine.

it transforms power up or down, depending on the mode, which you can switch with a soft mallet. step-up means 4a lv in, 1a mv out, while step-down means the reverse.

make sure you understand the following if you prefer your base not being a crater:
a step-down mode is the default one. in this mode, the large dot is the input. in a step-up mode, it's the output. do not mix it up. lv machines that receive mv power will explode.

if the transformer is connected to power, or was in the past, then do not change the mode with stuff connected. it's better to break and place it again to get rid of the stored power rather than rotate it with the wrench and blow things up. make sure to also disconnect the nearby wires with a wire cutter.

as a reminder, machines don't blow up if they are given more amps than they can consume. they blow up from higher voltage tier. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 21, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:21", "name": "low voltage transformer", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 24460, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 21, "shard": "039135de87a56f71", "recipes": 3}, "label": "low voltage transformer"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 4, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:4", "name": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21242, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 4, "shard": "3cff4d8e3920defe", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)"}}}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 3, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:cointechniciani", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:cointechniciani:0", "name": "coin "the technician 10"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "cointechniciani", "icon": 20788, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "53205e7d44e6e7e5", "recipes": 2}, "label": "coin "the technician 10""}}}}

name: One BILLION EU
Power Goggles
text:
power goggles wanna see how your lsc is doing but don't want to run to it or your information panel every time? get yourself a pair of power goggles to see your energy storage straight from the hud!

by default the goggles are unlinked and will monitor the amount of energy in your wireless network.

to link the goggles to an lsc, right+click the controller with the goggles in your hand. shift+right click air to unlink.

if you wish to move or modify the display you can do so by opening the power goggles config menu!

[warn]make sure to check your keybinds! there's also a keybind for toggling the power chart!

or, if you don't wanna deal with that, you can use the /powergoggles command[/warn] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.power_goggles", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.power_goggles:0", "name": "power goggles", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.power_goggles", "icon": 22086, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "9d29dcb0ec0c90bb", "recipes": 1}, "label": "power goggles"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Take charge!
text:
take charge! the lapotronic supercapacitor is your best option for massive power storage.

it can have maintenance issues which increase its power loss by 20% more each, so try not to let that slide. though at most it's still only 2.2%

for the first, smallest one, you'll need the following, plus an energy hatch and a dynamo. remember that you can get your lapos back if you run the capacitor through an unpackager. finally a reason to make one!

you can use laser hatches, that can output very high amperage. you need at least uv glass to use them.

your lsc can hold between 300 meu and 25.38 geu using only the ev capacitors. remember that you need more than half the blocks to be non-empty capacitors for it to be valid. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, name: Wireless Power!?
text:
wireless power!? are you sick and tired of having cables all around your base? are you tired of having to upgrade your cables constantly to handle different amperage amounts? are you a fan of lightning bolts zapping around your base?

then this multiblock is for you, the tesla tower comes with high amperage output and full tectech energy hatch support with this powerful multiblock.

to get started you will need to fill the tower with capacitors matching the tier of the primary tesla windings within the capacitor bank. the tesla winding determines the tier of power that the tower transfers power at and the amount of capacitors determines the maximum amperage that can be output.

a total of 16 capacitors can be placed into one capacitor bank so you might need many banks depending on your power needs.

once the tower is constructed click open the controller to configure the maximum transfer distance of the tower to fit the needs of your base. the range setting is currently buggy which means that at least for now you can do so without needing any plasmas. this option is called “tesla towers transfer radius setting”.

now that your tower is all configured how do you get power out of it to your machines? well i am glad you asked. to get power to the machines of the base you will need to use the tesla coil covers. place them on the tops of your machines, energy hatches and even transformers to get power flowing from the tower. energy hatches are a bit picky however and the hatch likes to be facing upwards to receive power.

[warn]warning! the tesla tower will output only one tier of amp such as ev, iv etc. when upgrading the primary tesla windings, please make sure to check that all of your coil covers and transceivers in the base can handle the upgraded power. failure to do so will result in a machine explosion.[/warn]

name: A Summary of Crossbreeding
text:
a summary of crossbreeding when crops breed, the resulting stats are the average of the parents' stats plus a random value between -2 and 4.

essentially, the variation in stats is a fixed (-2 -> +4). if all parents have fertilizer in them, stat loss is prevented in all cases (0 -> 4). 

deterministic breeding is similar to how bees work, where you must bring the right species together. some situations require more than two parents.

[note]advanced crops (mv and above materials) will require the breeding machine.[/note]

most crops will also have access to breeding pools. breeding pools are like a set of tags associated with each crop. when breeding, if none of the parents produce a deterministic mutation, but some share one or more breeding pools, a random mutation may occur. the resulting offspring will always be a species tagged with one of the shared pools.

[note]once you've obtained your first 31/31/31 seed, it can be helpful to use these random pool mutations to collect many different types of crops.[/note] {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Breeding With Technology
text:
breeding with technology the crop breeder is a single-block machine that allows you to breed new crops deterministically. it will consume the parent seeds, some enriched fertilizer and a catalyst item for material-based crops.

the stats of an offspring created by the breeder will always be the rounded down average of seeds that were consumed to create it. [note]breeding two or more maxed-out crops will always give a maxed-out offspring.[/note]

the enriched fertilizer cost is 144l per tier of the offspring crop + 72l for each stat point on the new seed. so a 31/31/31 tier 5 offspring would cost roughly 7.4kl to breed.

some crops require a minimum machine tier to be bred:
- iridine, osmianth and stargatium are all iv recipes
- titania is ev
- bauxia is mv
- an hv machine is required to breed 31/31/31

[note]success chance starts at 40% and increases by 10% for every tier past lv, meaning that at zpm, it's guaranteed. a failed breed will void the parent seeds used.[/note]

as a final note: when two crops share breeding requirements (ie tearstalks and evil ore), be careful to insert the seeds in the proper order as to not trigger the mutation with fewer parents.

you only need one of the machines for this quest. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 1, "requireditems": name: Crop Nutrients
text:
crop nutrients the speed at which a crop grows is based on its nutrient score. there are a number of different ways to obtain nutrient points for your crops, but to keep your crops from getting sick try to make sure they are always receiving at least a couple of the below bonuses:

- +10 points can be gained from having water in your crop sticks (scales 1-10 based on hydration level).
- +10 points can be gained from having fertilizer in your crop sticks (scales 1-10 based on fertilizer level).
- +2 points can be gained from allowing the crop to see the sky.
       - crops in the industrial farm will always have this bonus.
- +28 points can be gained from preferred biome tags
       - [warn]if no preferred tags are found[/warn], high humidity will give up to +14 points. 
       - see more on this in the environmental preferences quest.

all crops have a base nutrient score of 5.

you can check the nutrient score of a crop by using a portable scanner on any crop sticks or industrial farm controller, even if it's empty.

crop tier determines the nutrient score requirements for growth. 
the following cutoffs apply:

tier 4 - last tier where crops can be planted anywhere

tier 5 - last tier where crops can be planted anywhere as long as they can see the sky

tier 11 - last tier where crop can be anywhere as long as crops are in an 80%+ humidity biome

tier 12 - last tier where crops can be anywhere as long as crops are in a 80%+ humidity biome and can see the sky {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Crop Stats
text:
crop stats a key part of cropsnh is improving the stats of your crops. there is always a chance for this to occur whenever a new crop grows - whether by self propagation or crossing...

growth:
improves growth speed
- increases the number of progress points per growth tick by up to about 525% with some variation depending on the tier of the crop.
can cause weeds to spawn
- when growth is above 23 (or 7 for necrobloom), crops will begin spreading weeds and diseases to nearby crops.
- you can prevent this by either using weed-ex or by increasing the resistance stat so it's equal to or above the growth stat.

gain:
improves harvest size
- up to 2.5x per harvest at 31 gain.
- has a gain/100 chance of increasing the stack size of any drop by 1.

resistance:
improves seed harvest chances
- a resistance of 10 will guarantee a seed drop when harvesting a mature crop with a reinforced spade.
- this scales by rate of resistance/10:
  - 20: 2 seeds
  - 25: 2 seeds + 50% chance for a 3rd
  - 31: 3 seeds + 10% chance for a 4th
- a resistance of 31 will guarantee a seed drop even without a spade.
increases weed resistance
- when a crop's growth is above 23, resistance will prevent weed spreading as long as it's greater than or equal to the growth stat.
improves a crop's resistance to diseases
- each point reduces a crop's chance of becoming infected.
- with 31 resistance, crops are immune to diseases.
this includes sickness from lack of nutrient score, however, the crop still will not grow without the necessary nutrient level being reached.

name: Crop Sticks
text:
crop sticks to do anything in cropsnh, you first need crop sticks. these will act as the supports for your plants to grow upon. empty crop sticks can be doubled by right-clicking another crop stick onto them. these double-crop sticks allow you to breed any adjacent mature crops.

as new species grow on your crop sticks, you can harvest them by right-clicking, which won't remove the seed. left-clicking harvests the crop and removes it, potentially dropping a seed depending on the resistance. spades will help you improve your chances of obtaining seeds when you do this, as will the resistance trait.

[note]the chance to drop a seed from any crop without a spade is measured
as resistance/31. so crops with a maxed resistance stat will always drop a seed when broken.[/note]

[warn]note in nei the varying types of soil, sub-soil, and environmental requirements for different crops![/warn]

if you're already an experienced farmhand, collect a single stonelily seed and i'll let you skip subsequent introductory trainings for now. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 32, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "cropsnh:cropsticks", "resolved": {"id": "i:cropsnh:cropsticks:0", "name": "crop sticks", "mod": "cropsnh", "registry": "cropsticks", "icon": 19946, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "899a889345ee16aa", "recipes": 2}, "label": "crop sticks"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"choices": {"0": {"count": 8, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "cropsnh:fertilizer", "resolved": {"id": "i:cropsnh:fertilizer:0", "name": "fertilizer", "mod": "cropsnh", "registry": "fertilizer", "icon": 20046, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "0bc8b8d4eff17396", "recipes": 144}, "label": "fertilizer"}, "1": {"count": 32, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "cropsnh:cropsticks", "resolved": {"id": "i:cropsnh:cropsticks:0", "name": "crop sticks", "mod": "cropsnh", "registry": "cropsticks", "icon": 19946, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "899a889345ee16aa", "recipes": 2}, "label": "crop sticks"}}, "ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:choice"}}

name: End Stone Lilies
text:
end stone lilies once you can actually get your hands on some endstone, these babies will allow for a lot of high level passive material production.

since enderbloom requires end stone lily to be bred deterministically and end stone lily requires enderbloom for its deterministic mutation, you'll need to use your mastery of the mutation pools to obtain either of them.

[note]tip #1: if you're lost and don't know what to do, remember that you can trigger pool mutation even when breeding 2 crops of the same species together.[/note]

[note]tip #2: also remember that crops require all their growth requirements to be met in order to breed, even when breeding via mutation pools.[/note]

[note]tip #3: this requirement can actually be used to filter the outcome of a pool mutation so that only a subset of them may appear. though this doesn't actually reduce number of crops that can be picked from the pools shared by the parents. (and therefore doesn't directly increase your chance of getting what you want).[/note]

[note]tip #4: if you want to properly increase your chance of getting something through mutation pools, try lowering the number of shared pools between the parents.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "cropsnh:genericseed", "tag": {"crop": "cropsnh:endstonelily", "scan": 1}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (cropsnh:genericseed, metadata 0)"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 59, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "tag": {"ench": {"0": {"id": 35, "lvl": 3}}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (enhancedlootbags:lootbag, metadata 59)"}}}}

name: Enriched Fertilizer
text:
enriched fertilizer enriched fertilizer allows you to advance to the next stage of crop technology! 

it is used in countless ways moving forward, for example:

- apply it to your crops for more efficient fertilization.
- used to breed novel crops in the crop breeder.
- used to replicate seeds in the seed generator.

enriched fertilizer is 10 times more potent than regular fertilizer when applied.

- with a crop manager, a single unit of fluid adds 10 fertilizer units to the machine's internal storage.
- with an industrial farm, you only need to provide 1/10th of the amount indicated on the tooltips. (except when using a fertilization unit.)

it will always be superior to the item based fertilizers of the past, so moving forward you should be using it whenever possible.

when using the crop breeder or seed generator, the enriched fertilizer recipe costs scale with the stats of the resulting seeds. [warn]keep this in mind as early tier machines all have a lower than usual fluid capacity.[/warn] you'll need at least hv machines in order to create maxed seeds. by default nei shows you the costs for a maxed seed, so keep this in mind when looking up recipes. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 8, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "cropsnh:enrichedfertilizercell", "resolved": {"id": "i:cropsnh:enrichedfertilizercell:0", "name": "enriched fertilizer cell", "mod": "cropsnh", "registry": "enrichedfertilizercell", "icon": 20015, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "4e71df776bdfca77", "recipes": 2}, "label": "enriched fertilizer cell"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 16, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "botania:fertilizer", "resolved": {"id": "i:botania:fertilizer:0", "name": "floral fertilizer", "mod": "botania", "registry": "fertilizer", "icon": 3976, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "698f15e3d16fa54f", "recipes": 6}, "label": "floral fertilizer"}, "1": {"count": 16, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "forestry:fertilizercompound", "resolved": {"id": "i:forestry:fertilizercompound:0", "name": "fertilizer", "mod": "forestry", "registry": "fertilizercompound", "icon": 6830, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "693de06a027a5762", "recipes": 13}, "label": "fertilizer"}, "2": {"count": 16, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "cropsnh:fertilizer", "resolved": {"id": "i:cropsnh:fertilizer:0", "name": "fertilizer", "mod": "cropsnh", "registry": "fertilizer", "icon": 20046, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "0bc8b8d4eff17396", "recipes": 144}, "label": "fertilizer"}}}}

name: Environmental Preferences
text:
environmental preferences each crop has a set of preferred biome tags. these can be viewed in nei along with the other growth requirements.

having the proper biome tags will provide a significant nutrient point boost to your crops (+14 points per tag).

you can only benefit from up to 2 biome tags (+28 points).

it is possible to emulate a single preferred biome tag by planting your crops in a high-humidity location. the bonus scales linearly with humidity between 50% and 80%. values below 50% provide no bonus, while values above 80% will hit the cap at an equivalent of 1 preferred biome tag (+14 points).

if any favored biome tag is present in the current biome, the high humidity bonus will be ignored.


the nature's compass will allow you to view the tags of each biome as subtext within its menu. sorting biomes by tags is the simplest method. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Gene Extractor
text:
gene extractor the crop gene extractor and crop synthesizers can be made in ev and allows you to create new seeds using uu-matter and a few data orbs.

crop gene extractor
the crop gene extractor is used to extract "genes" from a crop. you can control which gene is extracted from a crop by using a programmed circuit:
1. species
2. growth
3. gain
4. resistance

extracting will usually have a base recipe time of 150 seconds (with the exception of the species gene, taking 300 seconds at base)

crop synthesizer
the crop synthesizer is used to create new seeds from the extracted genes at the cost of some uu-matter.

the uu-matter cost will depend on the stats and tier of the seed being synthesized.
- 750l per crop tier.
- 100l per stat point on the seed.

name: Last Universal Common Seed
text:
last universal common seed before going further into cropsnh, there is but one chore i need you to do. to prevent future hardship, collect a fully statted 31/31/31 seed.

this may seem daunting at first, but with enough blood, sweat, and bonemeal (see the fertilizer quest), you can do it. i believe in you!

ensure you pick a species which is related via mutation pools and determinism to other crops you want. if you don't know what to choose, may i suggest the potato or cactus crops which will give you access to the root or danger pools respectively.

while there is a reason behind keeping some seeds low statted (lowering enriched fertilizer costs in machines), the time saved by working with max stat crops compared to low stat crops is just too significant to ignore.

name: Multiblock Farming
text:
multiblock farming now this... this is how you show those b**keepers what's what. 

the industrial farm (if) is a long term, scalable, solution to crop production. at its most basic, it will grow, harvest, and hydrate your crops, but with several upgrades and tier based size scaling, it is not a simple machine to make use of. the if has three modes:

input - pulls seeds and sub-soil blocks into the machine from an input bus.
farm - grows the seeds and pushes products into an output bus.
output - exports the seeds and undersoil blocks from the machine into an output bus.

you can cycle through them in the machine menu by clicking on the mode button.

to start, you should construct the most basic if possible. once you've done that, place your seeds (and any relevant sub-soil blocks) into the input bus. 

[warn]seeds that have sub-soil requirements won't be inserted into the farm unless a block of the sub-soil is also available to the machine. the sub-soil block doesn't need to be in the same input bus as the seeds for it to work.[/warn]

once you've input your seeds (and sub-soil blocks), you can begin using farm mode to grow your crops.

when you wish to switch out seeds, enter output mode before re-inserting the new seeds via the input mode.

the length of your if is controlled by the tier of your seed bed. an mv farm will require mv seed beds and therefore can only have one row of seed beds. this also means you can only insert one upgrade block (by replacing the wooden frame on the top layer). each subsequent tier of seed bed increases the length of the machine, the base power consumption, the number of upgrades you can install and the number of seeds that can be inserted into the controller.

[note]the power, water and fertilizer consumption of the industrial farm do not scale with the number of seeds inside the farm, so there is no benefit to running the farm under capacity.[/note]

crops grown in the industrial farm are assumed to grow in the following environment:
- they have sky access (+2 nutrient points)
- they have 200 water (+10 nutrient points)
- they have 200 fertilizer when using fertilizer (+10 nutrient points)
- the biome at the location of the controller controls the biome tags and humidity with the biome tags added by the env modules (up to +28 nutrient points) {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, name: Mutation Titration
text:
mutation titration before going any further you really should craft a lot,[note] and i mean a lot[/note], of crop sticks. hope you like chopping trees and crafting saws! you should've seen the old recipe...

each of the adjacent quest groupings represent a different category of crops found within the mod. if you haven't yet, i would highly recommend you review the in depth guide quests focusing on [warn]crop stats[/warn] and [warn]crop nutrients[/warn].

while not every crop will produce a useful harvest, they very well may deterministically breed into a useful crop or open up a useful pool. so don't throw away new species just because they don't seem immediately useful.

certain crops need more than just two parents to breed. for those crops, simply surround a single double cropstick with all 3-4 crops needed and continue as normal.

name: Renewable Oil - No Diagenesis Required
text:
renewable oil - no diagenesis required oil from crops? makes as much sense as oil from bees!

if you're looking for passive oil before the mv crop breeder, there is another crop that can help but it is much slower.

[warn]you can't use an mv crop breeder or seed generator in order to breed 31/31/31 seeds since their fluid capacity is too low.[/warn]

you'll need to follow these steps in order to get your hands on oil-berry seeds if your parents have maxed stats:

1. down-stat one of the parents via manual breeding.
2. use a spade to get some spare seeds.
3. use the lower stat seeds to create an oil berry seed using the mv crop breeder.
4. max out the stats of the oil berry seed like you originally did when you got your first maxed crop.
5. use a spade to farm enough seeds to fill your fields.

alternatively, if you don't want to bother with this process you can just wait until you can get your hands on the hv breeder and seed generator.

[note]if you want to go with the mv route, using random breeding is the easiest way to get your hands on a mid-stat version of the parents. for oil berry, the simplest solution simply involves breeding withereed with a 1/1/1 sugar cane until you breed a new mid-stat withereed.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "cropsnh:genericseed", "tag": {"crop": "cropsnh:oilberry", "scan": 1}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (cropsnh:genericseed, metadata 0)"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 64, "damage": 30707, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.01", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.metaitem.01:30707", "name": "oil cell", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.metaitem.01", "icon": 40487, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 30707, "shard": "8590ff8dc580e95c", "recipes": 2}, "label": "oil cell"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 59, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "tag": {"ench": {"0": {"id": 35, "lvl": 3}}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (enhancedlootbags:lootbag, metadata 59)"}}}}

name: Seed Generator
text:
seed generator the seed generator is a single-block machine that can clone most existing seeds (with some very rare exceptions).

in order to clone a seed, you'll need to provide the following:
- 36l of enriched fertilizer per stat point; so a 31/31/31 seed will require just under 3.4kl of enriched fertilizer per seed.
- some crops may require an additional catalyst item based on the material produced by the seed.

the seed generator has an nei tab so feel free to consult it.

the fluid storage capacity of the seed generator is much smaller than most machines, [note]you'll need at least an hv machine to replicate crops with maxed stats.[/note]

name: Speed Up Your Plant Growth
text:
speed up your plant growth fertilizer is a foundational resource to produce and consume when farming. it has two key uses:

first, it speeds up crop growth by boosting the nutrient score.

second, it prevents stat loss during crop breeding. this simply prevents stat loss; it doesn't increase the likelihood of a stat increase.

four separate items can be used to apply fertilizer to your crops, each providing a different amount of fertilizer points:

- crops nh fertilizer: 100 points
- forestry compost: 50 points
- forestry fertilizer: 25 points
- bone meal: 5 points

[note]while bone meal may seem weak, its ability to still prevent stat loss when breeding is key if you intend to start crops before you can make a chemical reactor.[/note]

the crop managers and the industrial farm both also accept liquid fertilizers. there are currently two of them:

- fertilizer: 1 point per l
- enriched fertilizer: 10 points per l {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": name: Sweet Tooth
Taking Pools Seriously
text:
taking pools seriously with that 31/31/31 seed now in hand you will (ideally) never have to complete 
the entire statting process again. 

once replicated, you can cross this perfect seed with itself (keep them fertilized!) to access the pools that it has access to! this is the intended path for early game crop discovery. while it is much more random than deterministic breeding, it will let you collect a wider range of species quicker.

keep in mind that: when pool breeding occurs, the offspring has a chance to be any crop found within any of the pools shared by 2 or more of the parent crops.the mutation selection occurs prior to the check for environment. in practice this means that if you're searching for a specific species in say, the food pool, it will take much longer to appear than one in the reed pool because there are fewer alternative species. [warn]no matter the environment.[/warn]

once you've gotten your hands on a solid number of species, deterministic breeding becomes a simpler and more effective method for obtaining new species. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 8, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:coinfarmer", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:coinfarmer:0", "name": "coin "the farmer 1"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "coinfarmer", "icon": 20759, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "7ce27110202bd8ec", "recipes": 1}, "label": "coin "the farmer 1""}}}}

only one fertilization unit is allowed per industrial farm

[note]the growth speed increase is applied as a final multiplier. this means that it's even more effective when used in conjunction with other upgrades.[/note]

name: Tools Of The Trade 5 - Electronic Scanning
Tools of the Trade 1 - Less Dirty Hands
text:
tools of the trade 1 - less dirty hands this tool is a combined trowel, hoe, and shovel. the basic spade will allow you to easily clear weeds from your sticks, till soil, and potentially obtain bonus seeds from simply harvesting the crops (right-click) without breaking them. each point of resistance increases the chance of getting a seed when harvesting with the basic spade as follows:

1 resist = 3%

name: Tools of the Trade 4 - Reinforced Spade
text:
tools of the trade 4 - reinforced spade the reinforced spade will do everything the basic spade does, but better. it further increases your chances of bonus seeds based on the resistance stat. every ten points of resistance increases the minimum seed drop by one. that means:

1 resist = 10% seed drop
10 resist = 1 guaranteed seed drop
15 resist = 1 guaranteed seed drop + 50% chance for a second seed drop!
31 resist = 3 guaranteed seed drops + 10% chance for a fourth seed drop!!

time to scale up farmhand.

text:
weeds weeds will show up from time to time on empty single or double crop sticks. they will spread from there and sicken all your precious crops, so clear weeds with your spade (or fist) before you start desiring to reload the last backup.

text:

name: A Better Way to Find Items
text:
a better way to find items nei has a built in search feature for finding an item stored in an inventory nearby. a stockroom catalog can give you a list of everything stored in your inventories.

sneak-right-click a block with an inventory (a chest, bookcase, barrel, anything with an inventory) to add that inventory to the list of inventories for the catalog to keep track of.

sneak-right-click the same block again to remove that block from the list.

a small particle effect will render on any block that has been selected with the catalog when holding the stockroom catalog to let you know that block is being tracked.

right-click to open the gui and see the list. you can sort the list in ascending or descending order by quantity (count) or alphabetical order.

you can also see a list of all the inventories that have a particular item and easily add the location of one of those inventories to a stockroom catalog so you can easily find your stuff.

the stockroom catalog can also be copied with the typesetting table and printing press.

click on the title to change it to anything so you can custom label your stockroom catalog.

click on the small chest icons on the right hand side of each listing to open the inventory list view.

if you want, you can craft a waypoint compass and use that to point you towards the chest. since we have journeymaps and nei, it's not really necessary.

name: Advanced Solar Boilers
text:
advanced solar boilers once you have some steam machines, you can make advanced solar boilers. they have more steam output per second. otherwise they are the same as simple solar boilers.

fill it with water on the bottom side to produce steam. unlike the other boilers, this only outputs steam on the output port side.

hint: the advanced solar boiler calcifies and becomes less efficient over time - but it will only drop to 120l/s, not 40l/s, like the simple solar boiler. later on you can consider using distilled water to avoid calcification.

name: Basic Crafting: Machine Hulls
text:
basic crafting: machine hulls all machines need a hull to keep their private parts together. good news is: they are crafted in the same way for every tier, only the materials change.

as noted on the tooltip, you can also use a machine hull to pass eu through, at 1a. this can be useful for a 1a diode on thermos servers, splitting cables from 4a->1a or in a cleanroom later. you can name: Better Than Iron
text:
better than iron but not as good as steel. mostly, this is used in machine hulls, or in tools if you don't want to use steel up for that.

to make cast iron, you either need to use a tinkers' smeltery to melt some iron ingots down and cast them into iron nuggets, or use an iron ingot and a saw to craft iron nuggets. then put these in a furnace to get cast iron nuggets. with the compressor, you can compress the nuggets into ingots.

hint: crushed or purified iron ore (not a mixed version like pyrite; look for iron ore in chalcopyrite veins) can be smelted directly into iron nuggets. 

you can optionally use an alloy smelter to turn iron ingots into nuggets faster than a smeltery. 

later on, you can use an arc furnace to make cast iron ingots directly. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, name: How Can I Carry All These Items?
text:
how can i carry all these items? after you made your first steel, you are able to craft a small backpack. it has 36 slots, which is a bit more than a small chest. later you can make it even larger.

you can have at most four of these backpacks in your inventory.

you can put one on your back and set it to automatically pick up stuff. in your controls, check that the command "open backpacks" has a key and doesn't have conflicts. the key only works after the backpack is added to the back slot, which can be done by using shift+<open backpacks key>.

you can rename your backpack by pressing shift+rmb when holding it in your hand. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, name: How to Open Your Wooden Doors?
text:
how to open your wooden doors? wooden doors make your house safer. let's craft some wooden pressure plates and buttons to open these doors.

doors will open when they receive a redstone signal, and close again after it stops. if you place the plates on either side of a door, it will open when you step on it. or a monster does. double doors will open together.

you'll need to use oak for this quest. purchase some saplings from the vending machine if you don't have any nearby.

pressure plates will send a redstone signal when an entity is on top of them. there are different types, like items or not, or mobs/player/any entity/etc.

buttons will emit one for about 2 seconds before resetting.

levers will emit a signal until switched back off. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": name: Lit Way to Get Charred
text:
lit way to get charred the "charcoal pile igniter" is an alternative option for mass-producing charcoal. it does not consume any power or steam, but generates a lot of pollution. follow the steps below to get it working.

1. build a brick floor no bigger than 11x11 in size.
2. place 1-5 layers of logs atop the brick floor. no air gaps allowed.
3. place the charcoal pile igniter above the top-center log.
4. surround the remaining logs in dirt or grass.
5. the charcoal pile igniter immediately starts processing
6. after some time, the logs are converted to brittle charcoal blocks.
7. break the blocks with an axe for the charcoal (luck/fortune has no effect on the drop rates).

if this is your first multiblock, read the extended tooltip (hold shift) for construction requirements, or visit [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/charcoal_pile_igniter[/url] for more name: Lucifer's Little Helper
Macerator v1.0!
text:
macerator v1.0! finally you are able to make a device that will replace your mortar. however, the "no-durability" feature of this device comes with a cost: you need 2 diamonds for the grinding heads.

the macerator will double your ore output. put ores through it instead of smelting directly.

note: remember, don't block the output port and don't stand behind it.

name: More Advanced Alloys
text:
more advanced alloys your smeltery does a great job mixing metals into alloys, but it's not very efficient, and limited in its complexity. you need something new, so why not put your steam to some use? the alloy smelter can make bronze for you directly, using ingots, dusts, or even nuggets. you can make a nugget mold as well to turn ingots into nuggets if you have steel.

it might also come in handy when processing raw rubber. you should keep an eye on recipes to see when machines offer better options to make items...

[note]note: like all steam machines, the output port is a steam outlet when recipes complete. it must not be blocked. also, steam is hot, remember? change the output side by whacking the machine with a wrench. the 3x3 grid will show you which side the output will move to when you whack it.[/note]

you can empty the machine by putting a hopper beneath it.

[warn]warning: the alloy smelter recipes take a lot of steam.[/warn] do them one by one until you understand how fast you use steam, and how much you will need buffered. large pipes are a decent "poor man's" buffer, and the boiler can hold quite a bit of steam, as well as the machine itself. once you get a little further along, make a larger steam buffer with an iron or steel railcraft tank. {"0": name: THE NETHER
text:
the nether now more dangerous with extra hardcore infernal mobs. have fun and take care. remember that the flint and steel can take a few times to work, but there are other ways to make fire ...

be sure to bring a tough companion along to keep you alive. if you have no friends, why not make an iron golem and push it through first, or bring the materials for more along with you?

also, when you die here, not if, your graves will spawn skeletons because of the darkness. make sure you light up areas where you might die, and when recovering graves light up the area first so that you don't end up dying over and over and making a mess.

watch out for some mobs! they'll take minimal damage from any weapon that is not their weakness. so if you seem to not be doing much damage, you probably aren't! think about other options to hurt/kill name: Tame an Ocelot to Get a Friend
text:
tame an ocelot to get a friend once you have the required materials, you will need to find an ocelot to tame.

ocelots can be found in jungle biomes.

if you are having trouble finding an ocelot, you can always summon an ocelot using a spawn egg.

you can tame an ocelot by giving it a raw fish. so add the raw fish to your inventory and select the raw fish in your hotbar.

just like vanilla minecraft, a tamed ocelot turns into a cat. the cat will repel creepers.

tip: make sure you are in a large space when trying to tame the ocelot so that the ocelot has lots of room to move. if you are in a space that is too small, you will not be able to tame the ocelot.

next, while holding the raw fish, do not move. if you move, you will scare away the ocelot. if you are very still, the ocelot will eventually notice the fish in your hand and begin to walk over to name: The Power of the Sun
text:
the power of the sun the sun has quite a bit of power, so why not use it to produce steam?

fill it with water on the bottom side to produce steam. unlike the other boilers, this only outputs steam on the output port side.

you need silver from small ores to craft solar boilers. later in lv you can get much more in the twilight forest.

hint: the simple solar boiler calcifies and becomes less efficient over time, dropping down to a minimum of 40l/s. later on you can consider using distilled water to avoid calcification. {"0": {"allowanvil": 0, "allowcraft": 1, "allowcraftedfromstatistics": 0, "allowsmelt": 1, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 105, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:105", "name": "simple solar boiler", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 22687, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 105, "shard": "4ecb2c447d1cdaf3", "recipes": 2}, "label": "simple solar boiler"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:crafting"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 2, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "harvestcraft:papayajellysandwichitem", "resolved": {"id": "i:harvestcraft:papayajellysandwichitem:0", "name": "papaya jelly sandwich", "mod": "harvestcraft", "registry": "papayajellysandwichitem", "icon": 47557, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "709cf76b0b5fc2b6", "recipes": 1}, "label": "papaya jelly sandwich"}}}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 10, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:cointechnician", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:cointechnician:0", "name": "coin "the technician 1"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "cointechnician", "icon": 20789, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "d12081e875e5268a", "recipes": 1}, "label": "coin "the technician 1""}}}}

name: The one book to rule them all
text:
the one book to rule them all this tome can store multiple documentation books from other mods. it will be empty when crafted, but you can add books by combining it with the desired book in a crafting grid.

right-clicking with the tome in hand will open an interface showing all the added books; clicking on a book will transform the tome into the selected book. to revert it back to the tome, left-click while sneaking.

to retrieve a stored book, transform the tome into the desired book and throw it away while sneaking - this will drop the selected book and leave the tome in your inventory.

[warn]some warnings:

the extended version of the book of biomes from witchery is not compatible with this tome.

you should not throw it through the botania portal. the elves might steal your tome and return only their own copy of the lexica botania.[/warn] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "akashictome:tome", "resolved": {"id": "i:akashictome:tome:0", "name": "akashic tome", "mod": "akashictome", "registry": "tome", "icon": 14202, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "80f3ae390ca1f6b3", "recipes": 1}, "label": "akashic tome"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 16, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "minecraft:paper", "resolved": {"id": "i:minecraft:paper:0", "name": "paper", "mod": "minecraft", "registry": "paper", "icon": 48428, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "33f0cf9790b0d253", "recipes": 13}, "label": "paper"}}}}

name: Underground Geodes
text:
underground geodes you can find amethyst blocks, crystals, and calcite blocks in underground geodes. 

during the steam age, calcite blocks become incredibly useful because you can put them into a forge hammer to obtain valuable calcite dust, which is used for crafting the bricked blast furnace. they can usually be found between y-levels 5 and 46.

amethyst can also be mined and used as a source of silicon dioxide. one amethyst block drops 9 amethyst dust, making it a great option for obtaining silicon dioxide.
[note]

name: Animal Farms
text:
animal farms trying to get some leather or wool? you'd probably need to spend a lot of time hunting animals and traveling around, or you could simply make a farm to get a decent amount of leather, wool, and meat close to home. make sure you don't put too many animals in the pen or they will overcrowd and kill each other. this happens to villagers as well.

animals will prioritize moving towards grass blocks over any other blocks, and if there's no grass blocks around, they prefer lit blocks over dark blocks. you can encourage animals to stay in pens, or at least not crowd the edges, by removing grass from around both sides of the fence and under it, and by placing a torch in the center of the pen. for sheep that need the grass to eat, which reduces time to mature and replaces sheared wool instantly, place it in the center of a cleared out area with a border of non-grass.

also, large quantities can cause server lag, especially if they are bumping into each other a lot. so if you are in multiplayer, make sure you limit animals to no more than roughly one per block for small entities like chickens and one per two blocks for large entities like cows.

as an alternative, most animal and mob drops can be obtained from less laggy cropsnh farms. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, name: Coins! Coins! Coins!
text:
coins! coins! coins! finally, a use for all of these coins!

the vending machine is a unique multiblock that allows you to exchange coins for valuable resources. you will progressively unlock new trades as you complete quests. quests that unlock vending machine trades upon completion will show this information under the section labeled "associated vending machine exchanges".

alternatively you can click "u" on the vending machine in nei to see all available trades and what quests they are unlocked by. if an item can be traded for it will show up when clicking "r" under the vending machine tab.

you can put your coins directly into the input and they will appear in the internal storage. additional inputs (including non-consumable) should be placed here as well. there is also a button for ejecting the coins if you need to reclaim them. breaking the vending machine will not cause the coins to fall out or get deleted, they will be there when you replace it.

you can also share coins between a team. using the /gtnhteam command you can team with other players and switch at will between using either your personal wallet, or your team wallet. additionally, while in a team you can purchase vm items on behalf of a teammate.

name: Creosote
Divine Rod of the Gods?
text:
divine rod of the gods? the ore finder wand reduces the tedium of locating needed veins. if you're not sure how to craft magnetic iron rod for it, check its shapeless crafting tab in nei.

once you put an ore sample into the wand, it will tell you if this ore is nearby. when you get close to the target, you will hear the sound, and the wand will tilt down to the point of being upside-down if there's a lot of target ore nearby.

use nei to figure out which ore is the best for your search. if you don't have the needed ore, some basic ones can be purchased in the vending machine.

open the wand's inventory with shift+rmb when looking at the ground. put the sample ore into the slot.
the rod has a 60-block range both up and down, so it can miss a vein that is located very low or if you are above the sea level.

the rod appears to work based on the gt's material system, so anything of the same material will work.
that includes crushed ores, dusts, ingots, gems, rods, you name it. for things that don't belong to a particular material, the rod appears to search only for that exact block - for instance, you won't detect small ores with the usual ore block.

if the detected ore is a part of a vein, you will see a discovery message in the chat, and the vein will be automatically logged into the visual prospecting tab of your journey map.

the wand also works from inventory and hotbar, so you don't need to be actively holding it, but you get style points if you do.

the ore in the wand is stored with the player, not the wand. in other words, remove the ore if you want to give the wand to your teammate.

the ore finder wand doesn't work in space! the vast cosmic energies of the sun interfere with its inner workings! or the devs want you to use something more complicated than a stick. you choose. {"0": magnetite veins (y 60-180)

name: Important Tools
text:
important tools in order to craft even basic machines, you'll need new tools. most of them can be replaced by machines later. for now, you should become familiar with each of their recipes, as you will need a lot of these tools, starting today.

your new tools can also be used to make railcraft water tanks, a very useful multiblock considering the finite water feature.

there are also electric versions of the tools, you can upgrade later if you want. also, there are many versions of the tools, they generally follow the same rules as tinkers parts in terms of how good they are, similarly to turbines. you can look at the spreadsheet for more info on gt tool stats.

for this quest, you can use whatever materials you want. the gem version of the saw is crafted differently to metal versions. higher tier tools need steel or tungstensteel rods instead of sticks.

[note]if you want to know the recipe for a tool using your specific material, be sure to take advantage of the magnifying glass icon at the top of the list of tools seen from viewing the recipe in nei so you can search for the material easily. name: Making Better Tools
text:
making better tools with zinc and copper, you can create a material with a higher melting temperature - brass - which can be used to cast better tools.

for that, you need a smeltery. see the multiblock goals tab for details. you can also grab some extra blocks from some villages, but they don't count towards the quest.

alternatively, there are also one-time-use clay casts available.

you can then use your fancy bronze to make better tools with a higher mining level.

remember, you need to use the pickaxe a bit to gather mining xp if you want the full mining level on your bronze pickaxe. certain tool upgrades can give that directly if you have an upgrade slot name: More Food, More Hearts
text:
more food, more hearts so, food is great, right? but what's even greater is eating tons of it! too boring and pointless you say? well, what if i told you, that you can get extra hearts just by expanding your palate. you get 1 point for every half shank of hunger from a food eaten, and after 50 points, you get 1 extra heart! now you have a reason to make all those pam's foods. each food contributes its shank-value once. eating something from a lunch box counts as if you took it out and ate it manually.

if you want to see what foods you've eaten, you can use the food journal, but it's clunky. realistically, you want to use nei to both see foods eaten and not eaten. you can search for 'not yet eaten' to see foods left, and 'assisted' to see foods eaten. you need to have started diminishing returns first to see this.

if it doesn't work, go to nei options at bottom-left when the inventory is open, then click on inventory, and change search mode to regex. then restart your client and try searching again.

there are also two commands:

/foodlist size
tells you the overall progress, and the progress to the next heart.

/foodlist sync <playername>
sync your food progression with the server if it gets out of sync. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "harvestcraft:friedchickenitem", "resolved": {"id": "i:harvestcraft:friedchickenitem:0", "name": "fried chicken", "mod": "harvestcraft", "registry": "friedchickenitem", "icon": 47286, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "684c9cdd0a34d8a3", "recipes": 1}, "label": "fried chicken"}}}}

name: Need More Space?
text:
need more space? as you might know: tanned leather is more resistant and good enough for a backpack. let's get a digger's backpack and a miner's backpack. each pack holds different items. so use both for your first true back-packed mining experience.

some tips:
- you can change a backpack's mode with sneak + right click while holding it. default mode picks up items from the ground, resupply mode fills matching stacks in your inventory from the backpack, and locked mode prevents the backpack from accepting items.

- you can hover over a backpack in your inventory and press the "activate item in inventory" hotkey (g by default) to open it directly. this does not work while the backpack is in your hotbar.

- while holding a backpack, you can use sneak + right click on a chest, drawer, or any other block face that accepts items to transfer the backpack's contents into that inventory. this can be used to name: No Self-Healing Tools Here...Yet
text:
no self-healing tools here...yet in this pack you have to first gain expertise in thaumcraft to craft the tinker's construct ball of moss. go and become a dangerous wizard, and you'll gain the power needed to craft the ball of moss and make your tools heal themselves. of course, you need to get to the twilight forest and get some aluminium ingots before you can begin. the ball of moss is in the gtnh tab of the thaumonomicon, and requires infusion. there are many other great things in the thaumonomicon, but be wary of warp.

have a beer to prepare for your long journey. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 2, "damage": 32119, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.02", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.metaitem.02:32119", "name": "beer", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.metaitem.02", "icon": 45034, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 32119, "shard": "25494b842971752c", "recipes": 1}, "label": "beer"}}}}

name: Redstone, Early Game Processing
text:
redstone, early game processing are you wondering how to process raw redstone ore without a macerator?

use the hammer in the crafting table to get some crushed redstone ore from your raw redstone ore. after that, use the hammer in the crafting table again to get some impure redstone dust.

lastly, fill a cauldron with water and drop the whole stack of dust into it, either manually or by pressing ctrl+q. the cauldron can handle the entire stack with the same amount of water. you will get pure redstone dust for your redstone needs.

you could also take the hammer with you on your mining trip and break the redstone ore with it directly to get crushed redstone ore, thus skipping the raw redstone ore. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, name: The power of prospecting!
text:
the power of prospecting! at the top of your map screen (j by default) there are multiple tabs, some of them will be very useful and will save you a ton of searching!

gt oreveins - this tab will keep track of the veins for you, to save a vein to map right-click a naturally generated ore (some tools can't right-click)
gt underground fluids - this will help you later (mv)
tc nodes - this tab will keep track of thaumcraft nodes for you (you need to scan them first)

[note]small ores are not part of veins and thus do not uncover a vein on the map. however veins generate extra small ores related to the vein in their chunks, so they can still be useful in your search (though not all small ores are related to a nearby vein so don't be fooled).[/note]

[note]another great interaction is that you can use the nei search bar in highlight mode (double-click it) and then go to the map screen to get the matching uncovered ore veins highlighted![/note] {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "harvestcraft:herbbutterparsnipsitem", "resolved": {"id": "i:harvestcraft:herbbutterparsnipsitem:0", "name": "herb butter parsnips", "mod": "harvestcraft", "registry": "herbbutterparsnipsitem", "icon": 47365, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "795a3169d0df9c90", "recipes": 1}, "label": "herb butter parsnips"}}}}

name: When All You Have is a Hammer...
text:
when all you have is a hammer... ...the whole world looks like a nail. 

when looking for good tool materials, see "gregtech material tools" tab in nei. remember that nei bookmarks are your friends.

the gt tools each have special uses.

screwdriver - used on covers to change their behavior or on machines to change their input mode.

wrench - used to change the output direction on a gt machine, or to break it. can also disconnect/connect pipes or enable their built in shutter.

crowbar - remove covers from machines or pipes.

wire cutters - connecting/disconnecting/breaking wires/cables.

soft mallet - turning machines on/off.

hammer - prospecting for ores in a limited way in front of you, smashing ore blocks into crushed ores, and muffling machine sounds.

plunger - drain fluids from a machine or tank

[note]on a side note, tin pipes need a steel wrench to dismantle, so don't place them randomly, and pay attention to material levels![/note] {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: You Shall Proceed
Your First Flint Sword
Your First Tool
text:
your first tool when your tinkers tables are ready, you can craft your first real tool. if you didn't find a village yet to grab some parts from the chest, you can only craft flint tools.

let's start with a pickaxe, an axe, and a shovel.

keep in mind that most of the original tool parts from tinker's construct are not shown in nei. that doesn't mean that you can't craft them - use the tooltips on patterns and molds as guidance.

your new tools are weak at first, but the more you use them the better they will get. you get a modifier slot after some levels, needing more as you level it up. they will level up to level 99 if you play long enough, with 20 modifier slots. tool parts can be replaced for a bit of level xp, however the tool must be fully repaired first.

you need to level up the mining level each time you replace the parts to unleash the full power of the pickaxe. stone->copper for this pickaxe. if you manage to get a zombie, skeleton, or creeper head, you can use it to skip the level-up process. this doesn't use up a modifier level, but does change the look until you change the pickaxe part out.

item=usable when mining level is x or less
zombie=1
skeleton=2
creeper=4
wither skeleton=7
nether star=8

you could use a paper binding to add an extra modifier, but you will also get modifiers with tool levels. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, name: Dimensional Breach Imminent
text:
dimensional breach imminent at last, you have done it. the dtpf is a mighty multiblock fueled by large amounts of power and catalyst. running it constantly for 8 hours or longer reduces catalyst consumption by 50%, so you will want to find a way to automate this to save on expensive catalyst.

you will need 2112 coil blocks in total. accepted coil tiers are

- awakened draconium
- infinity
- hypogen
- eternal

while you can start with awakened draconium coils, you will need at least infinity coils to make tesseracts for uiv, so it may be worth it to skip to those immediately

name: Dragonblood
text:
dragonblood for your first batch of hypogen you will need some dragonblood. maybe you already have some lying around somewhere from killing the dragon a long time ago. you have 2 other options though. bees and the de fusion crafter.

for the bee path you have to go very deep into the breeding tree, but maybe you have already done that? check the bee breeding tab either way.

in the de fusion crafter you have 2 recipes. the better one uses an infinity egg from witchery. without any witchery you can also just use a normal dragon egg for the weaker recipe.

once you have a bit of hypogen you can then use that as a starting point to make more in your dtpf without any dragonblood. i don't know why it works that way, complain to colen.

however, you will still need more dragonblood eventually for umv superconductors.

[note]there is actually another way to get dragonblood which is similar to the de fusion crafter recipes but in the mixer instead. it's even slower and less resource efficient. in particular, the dragon egg does not survive the process. so only use that if you are absolutely trying to avoid magic and bees.[/note]

[note]just a reminder: a fluid task just needs you to have the fluid in some container in your inventory. name: Dreams of Rainbow... Stargates?
text:
dreams of rainbow... stargates? uev energy hatches? great! time for stargate trophy number two.
once again, to get your trophy you have to submit two stargates' worth of materials.

trophy number two brings us to chapter two of our journey through gtnhs past, the early uev era.

the year 2022 has just begun and the uev tier, albeit still quite empty, has become more useful than before. uev-umv energy hatches now have proper recipes (although with uev parts) and optical smds are a thing now, hooray.
there finally are better powergen options than regular plasma turbine spam, namely naq fuel and compact fusions + xl plasma turbine spam. technically dyson too, but that is horribly bugged and its 'legit' power output reasonably can't exceed around 6 billion eu/t (around the same as a compact mk4 running helium plasma).
some useful newly introduced multis are the prass, mcr & mega oil cracker and overclocks past max voltage are possible on megas now.
stargate has once again become a distant goal, as it now requires exorbitant amounts of infinity catalyst and bio circuits, requiring the player to utilize the new tech to its fullest.

two players, phineasor & gdcloud were determined to be first to completing this goal, and after months of a close friendly race, the winner had been decided. 
gdcloud won the race and conquered this round of nerfs on the 27th of may, 2022.

p.s.: once again, if you want to be faithful to the challenge, try completing it without these additions:
-pcb factory, space elevator, component assemblyline, aal, eec, eig, mabs
-any bee related gt machines
-any uev or above multis (except weak dyson and naq refineries)
-leg
-sub 1-tick oc, batch mode, inbuilt void protection on multis
-level maintainer, ae fluid crafting, stocking buses/hatches, crafting input buses, me output hatches

p.p.s.: again the chaotic capacitor banks have been left out for the same reason as stated in the uv gate quest. oh and the stargate parts used to be uxv recipes, but since umv hatches are not
