name: Haha, Spinny Ingot
text:
haha, spinny ingot transcendent metal is the primary metal used in uiv components.

this metal is a bit different from the ones you have been processing so far. you need to macerate your tesseracts to get the dust and then blast it at such high temperatures that you'll need a coolant to help manage the heat.

due to the impossible nature of the tesseract particles, you'll need a medium to enable them to form 3d shapes. tungsten, for some reason, works very well for this purpose.

the ingot itself is also not very stable; therefore, a coating of titansteel must be applied during the cooling process.

[note]consider passively generating it. this process is slow.[/note]

[note]you may proceed to uiv now. best of luck.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 2, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 11581, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.01", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.metaitem.01:11581", "name": "transcendent metal ingot", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.metaitem.01", "icon": 36506, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 11581, "shard": "3d8da57644149d65", "recipes": 36}, "label": "transcendent metal ingot"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: NAC™: Advanced Routing Package
text:
nac™: advanced routing package sometimes, basic automation isn't enough. we've heard you - we are now offering the advanced routing package to allow more complex automation of your components!

the nanopart splitter allows splitting, merging and filtering of your components between different colored vci and vco hatches. in the configuration gui, you can define rules such as:
- merging any colors of your choice into one color
- evenly splitting inputs from one color into many output colors
- filtering specific components from one color to another
and many more!

if you purchase in the next 72 hours, this package is 50% off! please... make a nac™ for crystal circuits, cals aren't as good we promise...

name: NAC™: Optical Package
text:
nac™: optical package you may have noticed that optical circuits the way you're used to in the cal and assembly line are far more expensive than any other circuit line. the nac™ has just the solution for you!

we are offering the new optical package, allowing for much more efficient production of your optical circuits! see the attached owner's manual for installation instructions.

an external review has been conducted and has found the company not responsible for changes to other methods of producing optical circuits. the benefits of a nac™ for optical circuits are merely coincidental.

optically optimized organizer owner's manual

the optically optimized organizer requires two different grades of purified water to function. however, these are not just an extra running cost! each grade of water 3 and above provides a bonus to the module's running stats:
- grade 3 (1000l/s): 0.8x water cost (applies to both)
- grade 4 (800l/s): 0.6x water cost (applies to both)
- grade 5 (800l/s): 0.9x recipe duration modifier
- grade 6 (600l/s): 0.7x recipe duration modifier
- grade 7 (600l/s): 0.9x recipe eu cost
- grade 8 (400l/s): 0.7x recipe eu cost

water is only consumed while the module is running. similar water bonuses (such as grade 5 + grade 6) can be applied together.

the nac™ will track the most recent 100,000 circuits crafted, and can be calibrated to a specific circuit type by reaching a certain percentage of circuits of this type. at 60% (60,000) optical circuits crafted, the nac™ will become "fully calibrated" to optical circuits.

once that has been met, the bonuses from each chosen water type are applied twice. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 9512, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:9512", "name": "optically optimized organizer", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 25749, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 9512, "shard": "4f5424454b19c7d6", "recipes": 1}, "label": "optically optimized organizer"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 2030, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.01", "tag": {"repaircost": 2, "display": {"name": "chrom dust"}}, "resolved": null, "label": "chrom dust"}}}}

name: The Final Frontier!
text:
the final frontier! with the mothership (see the space race tab for how to build one) you can visit the truly last system: the amun-ra system. it has six planets and moons you can visit, each with at least one unique ore vein.

anubis
infinity catalyst vein (neutronium, adamantium, infinity catalyst, bedrockium)

horus
cosmic neutronium vein (neutronium, cosmic neutronium, black plutonium, bedrockium)

maahes
naquadria vein (naquadah, enriched naquadah, naquadria, trinium)

mehen belt
awakened draconium vein (draconium, draconium, awakened draconium, nether star)

neper
dilithium (dilithium, dilithium, mysterious crystal, vinteum)

seth
raw tengam (raw tengam, raw tengam, electrotine, samarium)

name: A Diode, But For Condensate
text:
a diode, but for condensate at this scale, moving condensate is no longer a matter of pressure or pipe capacity. every connected conduit becomes part of the same quantum network, allowing its contents to be observed and extracted from anywhere. what you need is a way to impose direction upon something that does not particularly care which way it travels.

like the theoretical demon whose name it bears, the maxwell gate separates one state from another. networks connected to its output may observe and pull condensate from the input, while the input remains blind to everything beyond the gate. a filter in the controller can further restrict this passage to a single type of condensate.

there is one exception: the entanglement apparatus sees the gate backwards. it may only push condensate from the output network toward the input network.

[note]the maxwell gate is optional. it does not move condensate by itself; it only controls which side may access it.[/note]

the middle path: antimatter

[note]this path makes the other two paths easier to scale by giving you more power to burn.[/note]

the bottom path: the forge of the gods

name: Assembly To The MAX+
text:
assembly to the max+ the observation array is less an assembler than an enormous quantum router. it draws condensate from every containment field visible to its network, supplies power to its linked teleportation nodes, and presents those nodes with the nanites demanded by each stage of their recipes. up to sixteen nodes may be linked to one array, with their combined energy cost paid here.

the nanites are never consumed, but they must be exchanged constantly. providing a higher tier than requested actually slows processing, while mixing nanite types causes the entire collection to behave as the lowest tier present. precision, not brute force, is the key.

[warn]more than three unrequested condensates on the network will immediately fail every active recipe. even fewer contaminants significantly reduce processing speed.[/warn]

[note]running the same recipe across synchronized nodes is strongly recommended. different recipes may request incompatible nanites and contaminate one another's condensate network.[/note] {"0": name: Fluid^2 Extractor
text:
fluid^2 extractor welcome to the bec line! it's recommended you read the wiki for full context on these machines: [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/bose-einstein_condensate_line[/url]

until now, manufacturing has been a matter of imposing order upon matter: heat it, compress it, shape it, and force its atoms into the arrangement you require. but the materials ahead of you have become too complex for such crude methods. no amount of mechanical precision can control every particle individually.

at temperatures approaching absolute zero, another possibility emerges. as a cloud of bosons loses its thermal motion, the quantum waves describing its particles spread and begin to overlap. enough of them eventually occupy the same low energy state that the cloud ceases to behave like a collection of independent particles. instead, it acts as a single coherent quantum system: a bose-einstein condensate.

the first step is using the entanglement apparatus to convert ordinary fluids into entangled condensate by brute-forcing this delicate state on an industrial scale. it cannot overclock; instead, it expands the experiment across unlimited parallels, processing as much material as the supplied power can sustain. multi-amp and laser energy hatches will be necessary if you intend to feed the rest of the bec line at any meaningful rate.

different fluids may be entangled simultaneously, although the entire batch runs for the duration of the slowest active conversion.

[note]insert ordinary fluids through the input hatch at the front. entangled condensate leaves through the bec hatch at the rear and is pushed into the connected containment field network.[/note]

[note]the apparatus does not check whether sufficient storage is available before processing. use a bec detector hatch to disable it before your containment fields overflow and begin voiding name: Project Godforge
text:
project godforge with your research now complete, you have finally constructed it - the forge of the gods.

the forge of the gods is an immensely powerful structure constructed around a stabilized neutron star - it is so advanced that its full capabilities are not yet understood. however, through continued use, one can slowly upgrade and expand the range of abilities of the forge, and learn the power hidden in the most extreme parts of the universe: [note]graviton shards[/note].

this esoteric material can only be found where conventional matter and degenerate neutronium crust matter on the surface of a neutron star meet. at this point in space, gravitons are far more common and irradiate this material mixture to create highly unstable graviton shards, which can be used to internally upgrade the forge. while these shards cannot yet exist outside the extreme conditions of the forge, with continued research and utilization it may be possible to eventually isolate and extract them outside the forge - but for what purpose?

name: Pseudostable Black Hole Containment Field
text:
pseudostable black hole containment field as the materials around you achieve transcendental properties, you have found that traditional modes of compression like pistons or gases will not be enough to compact them as densely as you require.

the solution? using the sheer force of gravity. by using extreme amounts of explosive force on your fourth-dimensionally engineered tesseracts, you can tear tiny rifts in the fabric of space, enough to create a seed which can birth a black hole. if you can build a machine which can harness it, it will be able to compress even the strongest materials to the most dense states possible.

taming a black hole is no easy task - even with all of your precautions, it defies your efforts to stabilize it and attempts to collapse itself constantly. meaningfully extending the lifespan of the black hole will be extremely difficult. by bending spacetime through carefully aligned glass, you can reverse the flow of hawking radiation back into the black hole and keep it completely stable - problematically, however, the amount of spacetime required to maintain this process increases at an exponential rate.

as the black hole decays, it becomes even more powerful - but be wary, as it will eventually become unstable and you will no longer be able to recover your items from the edge of the event horizon. to safely close the black hole and restart this process, you have engineered a collapser out of the same fourth-dimensional materials.

[note]the pseudostable black hole containment field is the most powerful compressor in the game, capable of creating superdense plates out of any material, as well as being able to perform more advanced neutronium compressor recipes that will save incredible amounts of resources.[/note]

name: Quantum Tank X
text:
quantum tank x a bose-einstein condensate cannot simply be poured into a larger tank. its particles have surrendered their individual identities, behaving as a single coherent quantum state. storing it requires continuously forcing that state to remain confined and the moment that force disappears, so does everything you stored.

the containment field holds every variety of entangled condensate on its network. its field strength determines both its capacity and its appetite for power: every unit of strength provides another litre of storage while consuming another eu/t. the contents cannot be partitioned or filtered, so careful monitoring will be essential.

exceeding the configured capacity does not stop more condensate from entering. instead, the unstable field begins destroying 11% of every stored condensate each second until it returns below the limit.

[warn]a power failure or manually disabling the machine immediately voids the entire contents of the containment field. keep its power supply exceptionally reliable.[/warn]

[note]a bec detector hatch can monitor total or filtered condensate levels and disable the entanglement apparatus before the field overflows.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, name: Tier 11 (UIV)
text:
tier 11 (uiv) now that you've enjoyed your exotic cookies, let's keep going, shall we?

welcome to insanely ultimate voltage, a very fun tier with many new large multiblocks to play with! at first, this tier is mainly about solving your dtpf catalyst problems and getting to eternal coils. afterward, you are introduced to late game content like the forge of the gods, the bose-einstein condensate apparatus, and the black hole compressor that you will use until the end of the modpack!

this tier also introduces a few qol additions, like the crafting input proxy, uncertainty resolver, and the thaumometric essentia cell.

you also gain access to the dyson swarm and the semi-stable antimatter stabilization sequencer, two incredibly powerful ways to generate power. {"0": {"index": 1, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Transcendent Plasma Mixer
text:
transcendent plasma mixer definitely consider making one.

the transcendent plasma mixer is a powerful asset for all your dtpf catalyst needs.

the base processing time is always 5 seconds. you can specify the number of parallels the machine can run in the gui.

each parallel additively increases the power requirement, so you don't lose any efficiency while increasing production!

[note]most of your power will go here. consider upgrading your naquadah fuel or creating the dyson swarm.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 1006, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:1006", "name": "transcendent plasma mixer", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 22677, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 1006, "shard": "f041b3b3431812ec", "recipes": 2}, "label": "transcendent plasma mixer"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Tunnels Of Light
text:
tunnels of light despite its name, the teleportation node does not send your components elsewhere to be assembled. the entire recipe is processed inside the node; power, condensate, and nanites are brought to it remotely by the observation array.

once the solid inputs arrive, the node begins processing immediately, even if the required condensate has not yet been provided. the observation array must deliver everything before the recipe completes, or the process fails and the inputs are lost. there is no energy hatch on the node; its full power cost is paid through the linked observation array.

the line-of-sight hatches on the node and observation array must face one another, share the same y-level, and be no more than 128 blocks apart. no cable is required between them.

[note]increasing parallels only allows larger batches. processing speed falls proportionally, so total throughput does not increase. scale the line by building additional teleportation nodes name: A Second Ring has Hit the Godforge
A Solder Singularity
An Eye at the End of Time
text: an eye at the end of time so you have made yourself an eternal dtpf or hopefully a few, and now it is time for the push to the next tier, uxv. introducing the final multiblock in the game, and by far the most expensive. it introduces 4 new materials: raw stellar plasma, white and black dwarf matter and finally universium. it has 3 different tiered casings with 9 tiers each: spacetime compression field generator: - determines the tier of the planet block that can be run and decreases the processing time by 3% per tier. time dilation field generator: - decreases recipe time by 50% per tier, while decreasing the chance of a recipe succeeding by 9.25% per tier. stabilisation field generator: - increases the chance of a recipe succeeding by 5% per tier, while decreasing the output of a recipe by 5% per tier. lower tier stabilization field generators have a power output penalty. finding the best setup of different casing tiers might be a hard task, so use this calculator to evaluate setups and visualize drops: [url]https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ftfdfmy_uwbtbfoynzarkei90pbhvpbh6m3jhjmac-e/edit?usp=sharing[/url] [note]be sure to read the tooltip of the eye of harmony controller, it explains everything in detail! depending on your gui scale it might have multiple pages.[/note] [note]well... it explains mostly everything. the eye of harmony has an inbuilt pity system to make sure you don't lose your mind. here's a quick rundown on how it operates: (all chances are decimals here) there is a counter c that starts at the current recipe success chance p. if a recipe fails, (1-p)*p is added to c. if c reaches >= 1, the next roll is guaranteed to succeed and c resets to p. if a recipe succeeds before c reaches >= 1, it resets in a similar manner. if you switch recipes, c will be reset to p of the new recipe, even if the next roll would be a guarantee. the guarantee can be canceled out by overflow penalties as they apply after the pity does. however, they do not reset c, so the guarantee is shifted to the next recipe cycle. if parallels are > 1, pity doesn't apply.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, name: Convergence
text:
convergence running your dimensionally transcendent plasma forge for an extended period [note](8 hours)[/note] allows the multidimensional spaces to align perfectly.

with your newly acquired technology, you can now tap into these spaces in perfect sync, enabling your plasma forges to operate at incredible speeds.

the transdimensional alignment matrix allows the dtpf to run with perfect overclocks. to achieve this, you need a full discount, and the extra power cost is offset by using more of the same catalyst.

overall, it is more efficient and totally worth it.

this process is extremely catalyst-hungry. ensure you're producing enough to sustain it.

for recipes without a catalyst, you must specify the catalyst in the gui by right-clicking the convergence button, otherwise it will default to crude.[/note]

[note]math for the curious:

to clear up what exactly happens in the background, here's an explanation on how the extra catalyst values are calculated using an example:

the example recipe of choice is the molten neutronium recipe using prosaic catalyst, running at 64a umv (8,589,934,592 eu/t).
the recipe uses 14,753l of prosaic catalyst and 36,484,545,600 eu per recipe without ocs or the catalyst discount. with the discount, the catalyst amount gets cut in half, meaning 7,376.5l of catalyst, which are rounded to 7,376l, and due to the 64a umv the machine is supplied with the recipe overclocks 3 times, meaning each recipe actually uses 36,484,545,600 * 2^3 = 291,876,364,800 eu.

knowing the amount of ocs and the base voltage of the recipe, the difference of the needed eu per recipe with and without perfect oc can be calculated, that being 291,876,364,800 - 36,484,545,600 = 255,391,819,200 extra eu due to imperfect ocs.
to get the value of needed extra catalyst, this extra eu value has to be divided by the energy density of the relevant catalyst, prosaic in this case.

the division equates to 255,391,819,200 eu / 66,768,460 eu/l = 3,825.037 l, rounded to 3,825l extra prosaic catalyst per recipe. for the final step, this value has to be multiplied by 0.5 as it's affected by the discount, meaning the total extra catalyst that gets added to the recipe is 3,825l * 0.5 = 1,912.5 l, rounded to 1,912l.

to summarize it all in a formula:
amount extra catalyst per recipe = (b * ((2^x) - 1))/2l
where:
b is base total eu of the recipe
x is the number of overclocks
l is the eu/l of the relevant catalyst [/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 32758, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metaitem.03", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.metaitem.03:32758", "name": "transdimensional alignment matrix", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.metaitem.03", "icon": 45742, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 32758, "shard": "6cf1bd5ee5f7ca75", "recipes": 1}, "label": "transdimensional alignment matrix"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Magnetic Monopole Matter
text:
magnetic monopole matter with total mastery of the forge of the gods achieved, it is possible to begin a new universe-spanning initiative. it is now possible to quantize and extract graviton shards for use outside the forge in powerful new technological endeavors; produce the most exotic plasmas beyond merely periodic elements; and most importantly, begin to understand the immense power of magmatter, a form of matter made entirely of magnetic monopoles with density and stability billions of times that of conventional bosonic matter. it is with this development you realize that the completion of the forge was not the end goal, but merely a stepping stone to universal transcendence.

[note]required for uxv components, magmatter is the second material the heliofusion exoticizer can create, and will require a second module. read the godforge information in the ui for more information on how to automate this.[/note]

[note]the creation of magmatter requires the ee upgrade.[/note]

name: Stars, So Many Stars
text:
stars, so many stars eternal coils? perfect time for stargate trophy number three.
you know the drill, you give 2 stargates' worth of stuff, you get your trophy. simple as that.

[note]our journey through time continues onwards, entering the umv, aka dtpf era.

surprisingly, it still is the year 2022, but there have been a huge amount of changes since our last stop in the uev era. the dtpf exists now, hypogen & eternal coils included, and machine parts up to umv thus are craftable. wireless energy is a thing now too, both the lsc and the regular hatch kind, and ae2fc is in the pack, allowing direct fluid crafting (meaning no more volumetric flask shuffling).
the power situation hasn't changed much since the uev era, except for dyson being even more bugged and giving free uncapped infinite power (abusing this was obviously labeled as bugabuse).
some other new useful things are the mabs, integrated ore factory, space elevator, uiv and umv singleblocks, eig, eec, industrial & mega apiary, yottanks, stocking buses, data bank chaining and the draconic fusion crafter.
the stargate's cost has now skyrocketed far more than ever before, marking the beginning of this new era of gt:nh endgame, the era of expansion.

this time around the leading gdcloud was challenged by the team neo caelestia, who were progressing at a staggering speed, inching ever closer to being first to gate, but ultimately weren't able to fully catch up and thus gdcloud once again was first to conquer the challenge on the 19th of november, 2022.

p.s.: you know how this works, right? here's the list:
-pcb factory, component assemblyline, aal, transcendent plasma mixer, eoh, qft
-multi-amp wireless hatches
-sub 1-tick oc, batch mode, inbuilt void protection on multis
-level maintainer, stocking hatches, crafting input buses

name: Stellar Catalyst
Storing Computation in the Cloud
Subspace Cooling
text:
subspace cooling cooling exotic ingots proves to be a much bigger challenge than smelting them.

fortunately, reinforcing some of the casings with your new materials allows you to inject exotic coolants that capture extreme heat in miniature tears of spacetime, helping to cool your ingots a bit faster.

with subspace cooling, you can enable the vacuum freezer to achieve perfect overclocks… at a cost.

tier 1 will consume spacetime in liquid form at [warn]75 l/s[/warn] and allow for 1 perfect overclock.

[note]this cost is very high but static, remaining the same for each recipe being run. so, be selective about cooling your ingots.

the faster the recipes, the more efficient the cost, so find your optimal balance.[/note]

name: What is this, Tekxit?
text:
what is this, tekxit? the immense heat of the god forge and its modules allow for ideas themselves to be melted down.

two clashing ideologies, forced to coexist. hexanite is born.

a fusion of magic and technology, the ultimate concoction, a volatile one. even the god forge struggles to merge them perfectly. a mess of ideas needs a host, something familiar to bind them together.

[note]redstone plasma requires the god forge to be melted, while ichorium only needs a fluid extractor. you are sure to have lots of ichorium dust lying around from your space miners.

it is recommended to cast these materials in an exo-foundry, as the long wait times and high volume of use cannot be supported in a mass solidifier[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, name: Analyzing the Soil
text:
analyzing the soil tired of looking for ores by hand? want to find underground oil that will last a long time? a seismic prospector will tell you the ores in the surrounding chunks in a (sorta) handy book you can read, and also the underground fluids beneath you. it doesn't need to be powered.

to determine which kind of fluid there is in the chunk you need to scan the soil by right-clicking an advanced seismic prospector with 2 powderbarrels, 4 glyceryl trinitate cells, 8 itnt or 16 tnt. this one doesn't explode the user too on use. features! there are four types of oil or natural gas for the overworld. see the quest in tips and tricks once you've made an oil drill.

1) right-click explosives.
2) use a single data stick to extract the data by right-clicking on it after the animation has finished. each will hold one result.
3) next you need to put the data stick in a gt scanner to have it analyzed.
4) place the analyzed data stick in the bottom right slot of a printer and add 3 paper in the top left slot and make sure you have at least 144l squid ink in it.
5) take the printed pages and combine it with a piece of leather in an assembling machine filled with at least 20 mb of refined glue.

[note]tada![/note] now you have a book with detailed info about the chunks you scanned. visual prospecting adds the information to your map the moment you make the book.

data sticks are not easy (or possible) to make right now, so do not lose them. you can put it in a crafting table to erase it when done.

ore locations are given as the center of the chunk. ores that are marginal in that chunk may not be found in the center but on an edge. look at where ores are located and determine the center of the vein. at higher tiers, it scans more chunks for ores. if you just want to know about fluids, use the lower tier version so the book isn't as long.

each underground fluid field is 8x8 chunks. this starts at 0,0 and continues for 8 chunks east and south, containing 64 chunks. not all fields have anything in them though. within the field the amount can vary +/- 25 percent. the amount reported in the book is the minimum and maximum per field across all chunks in the field. the prospector reports on 3x3 fields (as in, 9 fields of 8x8 chunks) at all tiers with the center field where the seismic prospector is located. fluid extraction rate depends on many factors, check the wiki for details. in general, anything above 300 is really good. the name: Ardite and Cobalt
Auto Mining
text:
auto mining automatic mining in lv tier? wow! this nifty machine will collect ores for you, which can be helpful especially in the nether, as it won't anger pigmen.

place up to two stacks of mining pipes in the right slots. each pipe can go 1 block, and allow the miner to dig 1 block further. if you're above y64, you may need to pipe more in.

this machine only needs 8 eu/t to work, so lv batteries in a batbuff work ok if you don't want to make another generator.

the miner searches for ores in a 17x17 block work area (adjustable with a screwdriver), and comes with a level 1 fortune bonus! great for gathering additional small ores!

don't forget to cover it up! these are gt machines, so remember to protect them (and their power sources!) from rain on all sides. and set a waypoint with journeymap so you don't forget where you placed it if you place it far away! you'll need to chunkload the miner if you want it to keep working when you're not there. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 679, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:679", "name": "basic miner", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 25493, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 679, "shard": "dcd9f78e79d36e1c", "recipes": 1}, "label": "basic miner"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 16, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "ic2:blockminingpipe", "resolved": {"id": "i:ic2:blockminingpipe:0", "name": "mining pipe", "mod": "ic2", "registry": "blockminingpipe", "icon": 8409, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "128111a589af3cce", "recipes": 19}, "label": "mining pipe"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 4, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:4", "name": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21242, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 4, "shard": "3cff4d8e3920defe", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)"}}}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 20, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:cointechnician", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:cointechnician:0", "name": "coin "the technician 1"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "cointechnician", "icon": 20789, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "d12081e875e5268a", "recipes": 1}, "label": "coin "the technician 1""}}}}

name: Better Gallium and Arsenic Sources
text:
better gallium and arsenic sources there are a couple of ways to increase your gallium.

1. find tico zinc gravel ore and process it to get gallium.

2. breed zinc bees and react the gallium combs with hydrochloric acid. the bee is not too deep in the breeding progression and the processing only requires lv.

3. use crops under the green revolution tab to get galvania leaves, to 4x your zinc and sphalerite crushed ores to purified ores.

4. use the hv macerator on the centrifuged ores to get a 10 percent chance of a whole gallium dust.

5. use plentiful bauxite ores from the moon.

6. kill redcaps/redcap sappers in twilight forest. also kobolds drop arsenic.

7. duplicate nugget with thaumcraft. this requires taboo researches, so you might not want to do this.

for arsenic, cobaltite ore in the twilight forest is a great source for more information go to the quest "cobalt and arsenic from cobaltite".

cobaltite can also be multiplied 4x by the crop nickelback. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 37, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockores2", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockores2:37", "name": "gallium ore", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockores2", "icon": 26562, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 37, "shard": "20ec31b678590cfb", "recipes": 0}, "label": "gallium ore"}}}}

name: Biomes Everywhere, But Not the One You Want?
text:
biomes everywhere, but not the one you want? tired of searching all over the map for that bamboo forest or tropical rainforest? desperate for clay dust and need to find a canyon or mesa biome? nature's compass will lead you to the biome you're looking for, if it's within its range.

the compass menu has the following functionality:
* when sorted by: name, you can filter the list by name or its parts. the search is case-insensitive.
* you can search by keys and their combinations. for instance, name: bamboo, climate: warm, bh: -1.8, tag: forest.
all available keys are:
name,
climate [hellish, hot, warm, normal, cold, icy],
baseheight | bh (float, can be negative),
heightvariation | hv (float),
rainfall | rain (float),
temperature | temp (float),
humidity [damp, normal, arid],
tags.

some things to keep in mind:
* biomes from other dimensions show up on the list, don't bother searching for those unless you're in that dimension.
* in general, the full list has biomes that are not generated by realistic world generator, like sunflower plains.
* radius 10000 means it couldn't find the biome. in this case after the initial search, its menu will show only the biomes in the 10k radius. use shift+rmb to see the whole list again.
* you can try again at a different location - the range is 10k from your current position.
* artificially created biomes count, so remove them if you want to find a natural one.
* there's lots of different 'versions' of biomes under the same category, so if you want a tropical one for tropical bees, there are actually a bunch of places you can get it.
* for those who don't mind the freeze when searching, the radius can be changed in a config. the hud position can also be changed in the config. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "naturescompass:naturescompass", "tag": {}, "resolved": {"id": "i:naturescompass:naturescompass:0", "name": "nature's compass", "mod": "naturescompass", "registry": "naturescompass", "icon": 51334, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "00808d77cb900a7a", "recipes": 1}, "label": "nature's compass"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 4, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:4", "name": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21242, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 4, "shard": "3cff4d8e3920defe", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)"}}}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 15, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:coinbees", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:coinbees:0", "name": "coin "the beekeeper 1"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "coinbees", "icon": 20728, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "0f07c3ec5018dde9", "recipes": 1}, "label": "coin "the beekeeper 1""}, "1": {"count": 15, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:coinforestry", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:coinforestry:0", "name": "coin "the forest ranger 1"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "coinforestry", "icon": 20769, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "09c5f2397ce37ba2", "recipes": 1}, "label": "coin "the forest ranger 1""}}}}

text:

- they stack up to 64 items per slot, making it possible to store 2,048,000 l in a single slot!

- tanks can be placed on top of each other to form a connected tower. when filling higher tanks, the fluid will automatically flow down. you can also drain fluid from higher tanks even if the fluid is only stored in tanks below.

- you can use an empty cell, a large fluid cell or any other fluid container to fill or drain a tank on right click. if the fluid container in your hand is not empty, right-click will always try to fill the tank from it.

[warn]note: the tank keeps its contents only when shift-right-clicked with a wrench. 
breaking it with a pickaxe will void the stored fluid.[/warn] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, name: Choices, Choices
text:
choices, choices need a map on fuel choices? well, we don't have that, but we have suggestions. you can use steam up to iv, but beyond mv it gets pretty painful.

in lv you can start refining oil for either light fuel for a combustion generator or refinery gas for a gas turbine. or you can use creosote in a semi-fluid generator.

once you hit mv, you can switch from steam to renewable benzene (gas) from your logs. other renewable alternatives are fish oil or seed oil based bio diesel (combustion). seed oil can be sourced from pam's peanuts, canola or forestry tree nuts.

at mv you can also upgrade your light fuel with heavy fuel to get diesel. when you reach hv turn diesel or bio diesel into cetane boosted diesel. in ev, you can make high octane gasoline (hog), but it's complex, and you'll need to rejigger your whole oil distillation setup, since it uses different fluids than cetane does.

ev introduces the large gas turbine, large steam turbine, large hp steam turbine, and large combustion engine, which are more efficient versions of the earlier ones. the first 3 require turbines.

you can also make nukes, or wind and water kinetics.

for low-power operations, or dedicated players willing to set up autocrafting, you can begin using solar panels at mv. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "harvestcraft:sundayroastitem", "resolved": {"id": "i:harvestcraft:sundayroastitem:0", "name": "sunday roast", "mod": "harvestcraft", "registry": "sundayroastitem", "icon": 47767, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "3f2ce997df278c52", "recipes": 1}, "label": "sunday roast"}}}}

name: Diodes
text:
diodes good circuits need diodes. there are two main ways to craft them. you can crush the gallium arsenide crystals to dust and combine that with fine copper wires and molten glass. once you have solar grade silicon you can use it to make silicon wafers in your ebf to make even more. note that the wafers are much more efficient on gallium and arsenic, so even a reduced amount is still worth it.

make sure you check all the nei recipes for advanced items instead of just using the first one you find. you can use annealed copper wires and polyethylene to increase your output even more. {"0": name: Enderman Smelterman
text:
enderman smelterman need enderpearls? getting them by killing endermen can be dangerous. instead of doing that, put an enderman into a smeltery with hot fluids and use a gem cast to get guaranteed pearls.

the higher the hit points, the longer they'll last, so the more pearls you get. if you can find a regenerating enderman, or an enderman spawner, you'll have all the pearls you would ever want. later on with enderio you can even create your own powered spawner to make endermen on-demand. or just place it in the end and move the mobs inside.

use a nametag on a regenerating enderman to make sure he doesn't despawn. you'll want to keep him from seeing the sky or else he'll teleport away.

if you haven't found a regen enderman yet, you can buy enderman spawn eggs to put into your smeltery with coins. maybe you'll get lucky and get a regenerating one. as a slightly more volatile alternative, an ender creeper works too. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "minecraft:name_tag", "resolved": {"id": "i:minecraft:name_tag:0", "name": "name tag", "mod": "minecraft", "registry": "name_tag", "icon": 48400, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "7f35c5297276e939", "recipes": 2}, "label": "name tag"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 58, "oredict": "", "id": "minecraft:spawn_egg", "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (minecraft:spawn_egg, metadata 58)"}}}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 30, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:coinsmith", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:coinsmith:0", "name": "coin "blacksmith 1"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "coinsmith", "icon": 20774, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "1bcd43c03cd0e821", "recipes": 1}, "label": "coin "blacksmith 1""}}}}

name: Firestone Ore/Dust
text:
firestone ore/dust firestone ore is used to make some bc machines like the filler, and some other stuff. unfortunately, it's in the nether...at the bottom of the lava ocean!

here are some tips for finding it:

-firestone only spawns in deep lava, at least 6 deep. it will only replace netherrack, so a fjord filled with soulsand won't have any. can you think of ways to check the lava depth, and what's down there?
-alternatively, if you keep your head at just the correct height above the lava and at the correct angle, you'll be able to see underneath it - surely there must be a hovering jetpack?
-...or just look for the biome when your cursor is over the jm map. hell is the default one that has netherrack.

firestone can be mined with the gt miners, if you place it within horizontal range. firestone ore and products will cause random fires to start nearby, so get it into a backpack quickly!

name: Gallium Arsenide Crystal
text:
gallium arsenide crystal the diode requires gallium arsenide, and you may be wondering how to get gallium or arsenic this early in the game.

sphalerite and zinc are the primary sources of gallium at this tier.

you can find sphalerite in sulfur veins at y 5-20, and the small zinc ores in the overworld or the nether at y 80-210. you won't find much on the overworld because of obvious reasons. to get additional zinc crushed ore drops, use a tinker's construct tool with the luck (fortune) enchant on it, probably the best use for all that lapis you got while looking for calcite. or use a miner, if you don't mind how slow it is.

- sphalerite can be electrolyzed for a small chance of a gallium dust. better put in a lot or you might get unlucky.
- zinc crushed ore can be washed and then thermal centrifuged or forge hammered and then centrifuged. but you don't always get the crushed ore as a drop, the impure dust doesn't give gallium.

you can get arsenic from realgar small ores in the nether at y 15-85. centrifuge the dusts in a centrifuge.

other sources are tinker's construct cobalt ore in the nether and cobaltite ore in the twilight forest. you can use your ebf for that. you also need to level up your pickaxe to ardite or make an ironwood pickaxe or lv miner to harvest cobalt ore.

another way to get gallium and arsenic is with xp buckets in a crafting grid if you're really desperate.

with your ebf you can combine these two dusts to make a gallium arsenide crystal. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, name: Getting Ready for Tier 2, MV
text:
getting ready for tier 2, mv in order to proceed forward, you need to get raw aluminum. a lot of it. but for now, 8 is enough to complete this quest.

your first option is alumina dust. probably the best source for alumina is clay or hardened clay from canyons, however you need an mv machine for that, so you need to find an alternative until you have enough dust for your initial setup. for now, you can get it by centrifuging various impure piles from your ores or by smelting ruby, sapphire, or green sapphire in an ebf with carbon. check the ebf quest in the multiblock goals.

you will also need an ebf to turn the alumina into aluminium ingots. for that you need cryolite. go visit the twilight forest for that and find a cryolite vein. the related quest "lead, galena, silver and cryolite" is in the novice thaumaturgy tab.

your second option is to use aluminium dust. however, you can not smelt that directly yet, even if you have an ebf. that will require higher heat levels. for now, you will have to either use a tinker's smeltery or a gt compressor to turn the dust into raw aluminium which you can then smelt into ingots in the ebf.

by the time you've completed this, you'll probably be done with most of the tab, but you'll still need good circuits (mv) to actually open up the next tier if you haven't done that yet.

you might also want to check the getting around and without dying tabs for new unlocks. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, text:

this machine allows you to filter by machine recipe type and allows you to effortlessly set up automations. to use it simply put a machine of any type into the gui to create a filter, e.g. a macerator will allow the machine to only accept items that can be macerated. the same machine can be used to create an inverse filter (a button in the gui) that will allow you to exclude all items that can be name: Handle Resources Like a Bo$$ #2
Handle Tiny Piles Like a K1ng
text:
handle tiny piles like a k1ng don't you hate having to manually compress all those tiny piles? well, let me show you how to automate that. a combination of type filter, chest buffer (or super buffer in hv) and packager frees you from that annoying task. the chest buffer can hold up to 9 stacks of tiny piles and the super buffer can hold 256 stacks of tiny dusts, which is more than enough. you can set its mode with a screwdriver on the output side. set it to 9 to export 9 tiny piles at a time and let the packager compress these into regular dusts.

[note]when you unlock them, super buffers can be lag sources, so be careful to keep them as empty as possible. if you end up using a multiblock packager, be sure to change the buffer from stocking name: Hey DJ, Mix it!
text:
hey dj, mix it! the mixer is a very useful device. you can mix all kinds of fluids and items. useful to prevent dust from falling to the ground when crafting - most mixer recipes give a slight boost over hand crafting!

you get +3 slots in the ev+ versions, this one has 6.

you can use the battery slot and other extra slots in the gui to store anything you like!

name: Keeping things organized
text:
keeping things organized are you tired of storing shapes and/or molds near your extruders and solidifiers instead of inside them? today must be your lucky day, because these item holders let you do exactly that!

they allow your machines to hold a small number of extra items, though each slot can only store one item at a time. there are three versions of this cover, each offering a different amount of storage:

basic item holder: 9 slots
good item holder: 12 slots
advanced item holder: 15 slots

[note]if that's still not enough space and you are already using the highest tier, you can simply attach multiple holders to your machine of choice.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, name: Long Distance Fluid Pipeline
text:
long distance fluid pipeline wouldn't it be great if you could transport your oil from a far away oil spout or oil field by pipes to your base?

this is not a problem anymore. connect your setup on the start and end point with a long distance fluid pipeline block. in between use the associated pipe blocks - the total distance between endpoints must be more than 64 blocks apart (4 or more chunks). there can only be one start and end point per pipeline.

to actually connect it, you need to align the start ldfp block such that the arrows are facing inwards, and the opposite side of it has a ldfpp block. put a pump on the side of the block that has the arrows and set to import. it will now attempt to import fluid to the endpoint ldfp. this will go as fast as you can put fluid into it.

do the opposite on the far side, except you don't need a pump.

now you only need to chunkload the start and end points and the fluid will be "teleported" to you.

of course, later on you'll probably use ender tanks to actually teleport the fluid, especially from other dims.

this setup is lag-free in the pipe blocks, so it's useful in your base as well if you want to reduce lag. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, name: Node Upgrades
text:
node upgrades nodes can take many upgrades. for now, try building a world interaction upgrade. with it, you can set up simple autocrafting.

put a wiu in a transfer node attached to a crafting table. on the other side of the table, the 3x3 area is now treated as a crafting grid. place items in inventories on the other side and if they make a valid recipe, the wiu will craft it. to speed it up, you will need to wait until hv for stainless steel.

also, if you place a node on a block of cobble that has lava and water next to it, and a wiu in it, it will produce cobble for you automatically. use upgrades to get more at a time and faster.

name: Personal Chunkloading
text:
personal chunkloading let's craft a personal chunkloader. it will load a 3x3 chunk area. you need ender fragments, ender pearls, or coins to power the chunkloader.

personal anchors can be powered with ender fragments for 1h, ender pearls for 4 hours, and a varying amount depending on the coin used.

personal anchors are loaded once the owner visits, and stays loaded while the player is logged in.

passive anchors are loaded once the owner visits, and stays loaded until the server resets.

name: Prison Gangs are Obsolete
text:
prison gangs are obsolete want lots of cobble, stone, obsidian, or another type of rock? this is the machine for you!

cobble: water and lava on the side.
stone: water on the side, lava on top.
obsidian: lava on top or side, water on side, and redstone in the machine.
netherrack: lava on top or side, water on side, and glowstone in the machine.
basalt: lava on side, soul sand below, and one packed ice in the machine.
cobbled deepslate: lava on side, soul sand below, and one magma block in the machine.

you of course need to power it. if you don't want to spend power on cobble, do it the exu way with the wiu.

you need to toggle the ghost circuit to circuit 1 or 6 depending on the recipe, check nei. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, name: Reading the Grid
text:
reading the grid while the gt eu meter can inspect one cable or machine at a time, troubleshooting a large power network that way quickly becomes rather tedious. if only there was a dedicated tool for that...

the network analyzer displays the entire connected eu network directly in the world, allowing you to follow power from generators to machines and identify dangerous sections before they become craters.

right-click a gt cable to bind the analyzer to its network, then keep it in your hand to display the overlay. you can also use it on a multiblock controller to inspect the networks connected to all of its energy and dynamo hatches.

you can shift-right-click to cycle through its five modes:
- topology displays the complete network and its worst case condition.
- critical displays only overloaded or otherwise dangerous sections.
- active displays cables that are currently carrying amperage.
- amperage compares the expected load with each cable’s capacity.
- voltage displays expected cable loss and warns about cables or machines receiving excessive voltage.

orange nodes are power sources, cyan nodes are consumers, and green nodes are forks in the network. gray indicates an idle or unknown section, green is safe, yellow warns of significant voltage loss, and red indicates an overload, a cable that may burn, or a machine that may explode.

look directly at a node to see more detailed information about amperage, voltage loss, and any detected problems.

[note]amperage mode displays the potential load of the connected machines, while active mode shows what is actually carrying power at that moment.[/note]

[warn]machines from other mods cannot always report their real amperage requirements. the analyzer must estimate their consumption, so readings for ic2 machines, reactors, and other non-gt consumers name: Refined Firestone
text:
refined firestone cut firestone is the basic shape for producing refined firestone.
use a diamond or firestone lens for cutting.
it is then fired with lava in the ebf.

lastly it is thrown into lava and charged by absorbing lava blocks around it.
it needs 5000 lava blocks to be fully charged, so a large lava lake is required, preferably in the nether.

this is most often used to heat up steam boilers very quickly or as a fuel. additionally, it can function as a flint and steel.

[note]if the firestone breaks, it can be repaired with lava in the ebf and recharged.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 1, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, this early, you will have to use a chemical reactor to crack it, but later on there's a dedicated multiblock for this purpose, the oil cracker. for best ethylene results, you should severely name: Sulfuric Acid
text:
sulfuric acid combining sulfur trioxide and water in the chemical reactor will give you sulfuric acid for your single use acid batteries. you'll need to make sulfur dioxide first.

on the other hand if you've made some light fuel you'll have some spare hydrogen sulfide you can also turn into sulfuric acid (after a couple steps), and if you've automated it, you'll be drowning in it honestly. once you can make an lcr, you can skip directly from hs to sa in one step. keep in mind that you'll need all that acid for making stuff instead of for single use batteries by then. {"0": name: Thermal Centrifuge
text:
thermal centrifuge a machine to get different byproducts out of your crushed or purified ore dust. it's useful for getting a bit of gallium out of crushed zinc ore for your diodes needed in good circuits.

when you have ic2 nuclear reactors and want to recycle your depleted fuel rods, it's the only way to do so.

if you can't produce the 2a of lv power for this machine right now, wait until you get to mv and use transformers to power an lv version.

in lv, you can obtain the same ore byproducts via different methods. the thermal centrifuge only becomes really important in hv when you can combine it with the hv macerator.

name: Time to Dry Out the Nether
text:
time to dry out the nether pumps can do more than pump oil and water. you can go to the nether and pump lava from the huge lava lakes too.

once you reach hv, lava can be centrifuged for silicon dioxide, magnesia, quicklime, gold, sapphire, and tantalite. you can get silicon, magnesium, calcium, gold, aluminium, manganese, tantalum, and oxygen out of them.

this is a good use for your lv pumps once you upgrade to mv pumps for oil. if you get into thaumcraft or blood magic, there are ways to produce lava with magic unlimitedly and easily too.

name: Welcome to Tier 1, LV
text:
welcome to tier 1, lv why, hello there! it seems you've made it into the electrical age. don't be so quick to throw away your steam machines, you'll probably want to keep using them for a while.

to make your life easier, you'll want to focus on getting a wiremill and bender first... once you suffer through making all the machine components.

after that, the polarizer, assembler, lathe, and chemical reactor+fluid solidifier (for rubber) all help make things cheaper.

lv machines are more energy-efficient than their steam counterparts because steam machines convert steam to power with 50% efficiency, when the starting lv steam turbine has 85% efficiency.

text:

name: Your Oil is Too Crude? Refine it!
text:
your oil is too crude? refine it! burning oil in the combustion generator is a very inefficient way of producing power. every bucket/cell of oil only gives you 20,000 eu. time to refine it.

you'll need to use a circuit to pick which of the products you want. later on you can make a distillation tower to get all of them, but that's far away for now.

you can also distill many other fluids! there are two that are useful, but take a long time to distill, so you should set them up in advance:

name: You're Gonna Hate This #2
text:
you're gonna hate this #2 the second item you'll need a lot of. when you want to get fluid out of tanks you'll need one.

attach it to fluid pipes or gt machines/blocks. adjust the flow direction and redstone behavior with a screwdriver. place it on the side facing the tank or machine. when looking at a pipe or machine, you can use the grid to place it on a side already touching another thing. you can use the grid with a screwdriver to adjust a cover on that side as well.

when a gt pipe or machine has any cover, including a pump cover, wrenching the machine back into an item keeps the cover on that machine. the cover stays with the machine in the same direction when it is placed down again. this way you can arrange pump and conveyor covers on a machine outside a tight spot and place it there. to remove covers, use the crowbar.

it can also be further upgraded into a fluid regulator that allows precise control of fluid transfer speed.

name: All Those Chunks, All in a Row
text:
all those chunks, all in a row sometimes you don't want a 3x3 area chunkloaded, but a long straight line instead. this can be handy for rail lines or power lines going across long distances. an anchor sentinel can perform this function. right-click on a chunk loader with a crowbar, and it will activate. go in any straight line from the chunkloader and place the anchor and hit it with the crowbar. those chunks, up to 25x1, will now remain loaded.

name: Conduit Probe
text:
conduit probe the conduit probe is an incredibly useful tool for managing and troubleshooting your ender io conduit networks.

it features two modes:

• probe mode
right-click an energy conduit to view detailed network information
right-click an item conduit to simulate item transport using the item in your hand
right-click a redstone conduit to see connection details, including signal levels sent and received

• copy/paste mode
shift + right-click a conduit connection to copy its settings
right-click another conduit to paste those settings

this is especially useful when configuring multiple machines with identical setups and helps prevent mistakes.

you can switch between modes by: using shift + mouse wheel, or pressing the yeta wrench mode keybind (unbound by default) while holding the probe. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "enderio:itemconduitprobe", "resolved": {"id": "i:enderio:itemconduitprobe:0", "name": "conduit probe", "mod": "enderio", "registry": "itemconduitprobe", "icon": 5350, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "3b65e909cdf1638b", "recipes": 1}, "label": "conduit probe"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 5, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:5", "name": "lootbag (tier 2 mv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21254, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 5, "shard": "86c93816ff53d76b", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 2 mv)"}}}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 25, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:cointechnician", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:cointechnician:0", "name": "coin "the technician 1"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "cointechnician", "icon": 20789, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "d12081e875e5268a", "recipes": 1}, "label": "coin "the technician 1""}}}}

name: Gut-Enough For You? Bet You Thought Newspapers Were Dead!
text:
gut-enough for you? bet you thought newspapers were dead! when used together, the typesetting table and printing press allow you to duplicate enchanted books. you'll need a lot of xp, so either build a mob grinder or get farming. a fortune iii book, for example, requires 40 levels to convert into an enchanted plate.

to use the typesetting table, place a print press chase in the top slot and an enchanted book in the bottom left slot. sneak right-click the enchanted book to convert it into an enchanted plate if you have enough xp.

to use the printing press, place an enchanted plate in the center of the machine, ink sacs on the top metal plate, and books on the bottom left side of the counter. it immediately starts processing without any power or redstone signal.

wearing reading glasses, tinted glasses, or a monocle will display more information about these blocks when looking at them.

each enchanted plate can make three enchanted books before breaking, but the trick is to make two books and then repair it in a thaumic restorer for unlimited uses.

name: Molten Polyethylene
text:
molten polyethylene polyethylene is made out of ethylene and oxygen in a chemical reactor. molten polyethylene cells hold 144l, perfect for 1 ingot or plate.
if you want precise amounts, you can use a volumetric flask once you electrolyze some boron from borax.

you may have started getting damaged from holding the cells. if you have, put your glove baubles back on. all molten cells cause damage and store 144l. mostly, molten cells come from metal-type materials, or stuff that was melted. excuse me, fluid extracted, whatever that's supposed to mean.

if you have the materials, you can use 12 ethylene cells and 83 oxygen cells to make 124 cells of polyethylene.

name: Ore Processing, Kind Of...
text:
ore processing, kind of... the endless war between macerators and sag mills rages on eternally, so why does it matter which one you choose?

hv macerators are still required for the final byproducts on many ore chains, but a sag mill still shines through with upgraded grinding heads! sag mills are the perfect machine for getting the most from your ores without using bees and crops. you can get bonus outputs with tungsten grinding heads, but that doesn't mean you can dupe materials (like ingots) with it. plus for many of them you'll get the final output directly without any need for further processing. handy for processing redstone to get chrome!

it's great for lead, copper, tin, silver, nickel, redstone, ruby, lapis, certus quartz, and malachite ores. other ores will give you better outputs as well if you use a good enough head.

even coal, charcoal, bones, wheat, ender pearls, and charcoal non-ores will give bonus outputs.

that said, the gt ones are still way faster later on. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "enderio:blocksagmill", "resolved": {"id": "i:enderio:blocksagmill:0", "name": "sag mill", "mod": "enderio", "registry": "blocksagmill", "icon": 5281, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "3a30b9df5c88910d", "recipes": 1}, "label": "sag mill"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"choices": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "enderio:itemmachinepart", "resolved": {"id": "i:enderio:itemmachinepart:0", "name": "machine chassis", "mod": "enderio", "registry": "itemmachinepart", "icon": 5395, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "ff37a727ed981c04", "recipes": 3}, "label": "machine chassis"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 5, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:5", "name": "lootbag (tier 2 mv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21254, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 5, "shard": "86c93816ff53d76b", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 2 mv)"}}, "ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:choice"}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 25, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:cointechnician", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:cointechnician:0", "name": "coin "the technician 1"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "cointechnician", "icon": 20789, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "d12081e875e5268a", "recipes": 1}, "label": "coin "the technician 1""}}}}

name: Passive Chunkloading
text:
passive chunkloading using the mv bender you can finally press dense plates. so let's craft a passive chunkloader. it will also load a 3x3 chunk area. you need ender pearls or coins to power the chunkloader.

passive anchors will run for 1 hour off of an ender pearl, and a varying amount depending on the coin used.

name: Pipes, Pipes Everywhere
text:
pipes, pipes everywhere now that you're in mv, you'll want to start automating polyethylene, oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen, rubber, charcoal, etc. faster item pipes will help with transporting items quicker around your base. for now, use your spiffy new extruder to craft some brass item pipes.

the reward - restrictive item pipes - allow you to prioritize destinations. locations on the other side of a restrictive pipe are treated as much further away than locations on the same side of a pipe. very handy when you want overflow (or non-matching) items to go somewhere else!

for higher tiers, look up "item pipe" in nei or use the wiki: [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/fluid_%26_item_pipes[/url]

name: Portable Prospecting Tool
text:
portable prospecting tool now that you have some tech, you've discovered a way to prospect for ores.

unfortunately, the tech to make it repairable or rechargeable doesn't work, so you'll have to make a new one each time it breaks. it does work better at higher tiers and lasts longer with better materials.

it doesn't make a convenient book like the seismic prospector, but you can look at the results of scanning on the map, thanks to visual prospecting.

it can be hard to choose a good material for the basic prospector. here are some good choices for you in their respective tiers, the size searched, and the average amount of veins they can scan:

lv vanadiumsteel 3x3 - 50
mv vanadiumsteel 3x3 - 213
hv vibrant alloy 5x5 - 299
ev shadow metal 7x7 - 1080
iv oriharukon 7x7 - 2649

as you can see, the prospectors become better and better with each tier, but it might also be worth looking around for better materials.

good luck. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 4, "oredict": ruby electrolyzing ruby is a good source for chrome and a little alumina. once you get low on ruby, you can centrifuge redstone to get more.

text:
simple rf power: liquids this generator requires both water as coolant, and a burnable liquid as fuel. the amount of power it produces depends on the type of liquid used.

oil                5                          30                               150
hootch          6                          60                               360
ethanol        15                          40                               600
fire water    15                          80                              1200
diesel/fuel   25                          60                              1500

name: Simple RF power: Solid
text:
simple rf power: solid by simply burning coal as fuel, this machine produces rf power. enough for a basic machine setup. this machine will also accept compressed and multiple-compressed blocks. want to burn something for 250+ days? also, with double or octadic capacitors the output will increase and efficiency will improve.

gt wiring can convert eu to rf, but not the other way around. note that with the enet changes a gt wire network will need at least one gt energy consumer - a machine hull of the matching voltage will work.

ender io machines and gt cables and wires can be left safely out in the rain.

it might be useful for genetics machines since they consume excessive power when attached to gt wiring - forestry and enderio machines work fine (except for the thermionic fabricator). or use a name: Stainless Taking Too Long?
text:
stainless taking too long? time for a second ebf!

you can make ingots faster in 3 ways - better coils, higher tier energy hatches, or adding more furnaces. it's probably time to add a second ebf to your base.

multiblock machines can share casings, mufflers, and input/output hatches/buses, but not maintenance hatches (you can share the auto ones though). you can share energy hatches, but only if you can supply enough power to all machines it's a part of.

remember, pollution will be very high with two ebfs active at once! watch out for high pollution effects. use the best mufflers available and don't place the ebfs in the same chunk as farmland or other high pollution machines like pyrolyse ovens and large boilers. maybe it is time to do something more active?

you can use whatever coils you have lying around, but you certainly want to start searching for mica if you haven't found any yet. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": name: String Theory?
Super Tank I
text:
super tank i this tank works the same as the smaller gt tanks, but holds way more. specifically, 4,000,000l. only make this for things you need tons of, lv circuits are expensive after all.

now you can store the same amount of fluids a steel 5x5 railcraft tank contains in a single block.

[note]a lot of nice functionality has been added to super and quantum tanks. you can now pick them up with a wrench without voiding the fluids! super tanks (but not quantum) will give you heavy debuffs though, so better prepare some milk.

if you actually want to void the fluids you can crouch while using the wrench.

they now also have optional automatic fluid output, fluid locking, overflow void mode, or full void mode. and all that with a nice and simple gui. quite the impactful change i would say.[/note] {"0": name: There Can Be Only One...
Tier 2 (MV)
text:
tier 2 (mv) the mv machine hull needs aluminium. you're also gonna need aluminium for every mv machine part, so keep that ebf truckin'.

here are some tips on where to start:
- mv electrolyzer makes getting aluminium easier.
- mv extruder makes parts cheaper.
- mv miner saves your time.

have you read the quest safety first for details about mixing tiers?
sending mv to an lv machine causes it to explode.
sending mv voltage over lv cables causes them to melt, which causes fire that will likely cause the machines to blow up.
additionally, recipes done in a tier higher than the original one (not ulv, ulv counts as lv) are overclocked (oc'd). the oc'd recipes use 4x power but complete 2x faster. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 12, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:12", "name": "mv machine hull", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 23286, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 12, "shard": "7e3381090fb5a971", "recipes": 2}, "label": "mv machine hull"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 4, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:4", "name": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21242, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 4, "shard": "3cff4d8e3920defe", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 1 lv)"}}}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 5, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:cointechniciani", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:cointechniciani:0", "name": "coin "the technician 10"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "cointechniciani", "icon": 20788, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "53205e7d44e6e7e5", "recipes": 2}, "label": "coin "the technician 10""}}}}

name: Way Two: Pyrolyse Oven
Welcome to the Church of Benzene
text:
welcome to the church of benzene if you made it to mv using steam, you're probably wondering how to survive going further. one option is to switch to light fuel, discussed in lv. another option is to use benzene. benzene is made from wood tar. there are a couple of pathways for that. both start with logs from trees.

one path is to use coke ovens or advanced coke ovens to make charcoal, and fluid-extract wood tar from it. then distill the wood tar to make benzene. this method produces less pollution, but will also provide less benzene.

the second path is to use the pyrolyze oven multiblock and nitrogen gas to extract wood tar and charcoal. fluid-extract the charcoal for additional wood tar. then proceed as above. this method will create pollution from the pyrolyze oven, but will provide more benzene per log.

excess wood tar can also be turned into toluene, a key ingredient for explosives that you'll need later on to make rockets.

if you use the charcoal byproducts recipe, you can get a plethora of useful byproducts as well, but you'll need 4 dts.

name: Chloroform
Chunkloading
text:
chunkloading with your hv assembler you can craft a world anchor. so let's make one. it will again load a 3x3 chunk area.

you need coins to power the world anchor, it will run a varying amount depending on the coin used.

personal anchors are loaded once the owner visits, and stay loaded while the player is logged in.

passive anchors are loaded once the owner visits, and stay loaded until the server resets.

[warn]world anchors[/warn] are always loaded, even after a server reset.

[note]check with server operators in case world anchors are disabled. on the official servers, world anchors are currently disabled to keep tps high.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "railcraft:machine.alpha", "resolved": {"id": "i:railcraft:machine.alpha:0", "name": "world anchor", "mod": "railcraft", "registry": "machine.alpha", "icon": 10307, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "e9ac74bc569ddc8e", "recipes": 1}, "label": "world anchor"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 4, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:coinchunkloadertierii", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:coinchunkloadertierii:0", "name": "chunkloader coin tier ii", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "coinchunkloadertierii", "icon": 20741, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "cd9b64da067270e4", "recipes": 1}, "label": "chunkloader coin tier ii"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 6, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:6", "name": "lootbag (tier 3 hv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21274, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 6, "shard": "4351b75552afb0b2", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 3 hv)"}}}, "1": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 1, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 5, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "dreamcraft:cointechniciani", "resolved": {"id": "i:dreamcraft:cointechniciani:0", "name": "coin "the technician 10"", "mod": "dreamcraft", "registry": "cointechniciani", "icon": 20788, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "53205e7d44e6e7e5", "recipes": 2}, "label": "coin "the technician 10""}}}}

name: Fluid Heater
Fluoro-who now?
text:
fluoro-who now? fluorophlogopite is the industrial answer to mica-based foils, and something you'll want to start investing in as higher tier coils cost increasingly more foil to make.

the recipe for making raw fluorophlogopite dust is done in the mv mixer. while all of the new dusts involved may look a little daunting, they're not that bad. you will need the following:

- some variant of quartz dust: any one of quartz sand, quartzite, nether quartz, or certus quartz
- alumina
- potassiumfluorosilicate, which is made in two steps by combining rock salt, hydrofluoric acid, and raw silicon
- potassium carbonate, made by combining potassium dust and oxygen (or potash to cover both) with carbon dioxide in a chemical reactor

the exact ratios of each ingredient depend on the form of quartz that you're using, as does the exact amount of raw dust that you get from the recipe.

[note]technically, this process is entirely optional, but highly recommended. the raw dust is also used in zpm, but mica can be substituted for that use case if you would like.[/note] {"0": name: HV Bender
text:
hv bender an hv bender is 4x faster than your lv bender, but it also opens up an important recipe - tin cans!

with this bender you can turn tin casings into tin cans. using the tin cans with food in a canner will make canned food. this can stack up to 64, and will fully restore your shanks - no need to rotate food types anymore! you will eat as much as you need with one click. one drawback is you will no longer get the well fed buff with its slight health regen bonus, nor will you gain more hearts from eating new food. also, these cans don't fit in the lunch bag or lunch box so you don't need those anymore. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, text:
