name: Performing Chemical Experiments at HV Level
text:
performing chemical experiments at hv level there are a number of chemical recipes that are unlocked with an hv chemical reactor; you will finally be able to make ender eyes, ammonia, gelled toluene, and plenty of other useful components. 

alternatively, if you're up for it, you can head over to the mass processing tab and build yourself a large chemical reactor (lcr) instead! in addition to having a more efficient overclock, the lcr can input multiple liquids so you won't need to mess with those pesky cells any longer. 

[note]if you choose to go the lcr route, be sure to take a look at the ptfe questline just ahead of this one, starting with "teflon don".[/note]

name: Personal Dimension
text:
personal dimension tired of mobs in your base? want to build somewhere... different? probably in a personal dimension? then this is your chance.

when you first activate the portal, you can configure the world to your liking: it can be a void world, or a superflat world made up of any blocks you find available on the list.

be careful! once you configure the world, you can only change the cosmetic settings such as sky color by shift-right-clicking the portal.

editing world generation settings after the world is created is only possible if a server administrator unlocks it for you via the /pspace allow-worldgen-change dimid command.

[note]ps: the last millenium is also a void dimension you could use.[/note]

if you're used to the buggy garden/void dimensions from utilityworlds, this is now a new mod that should resolve most of the previously known issues with blood magic, etc. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "personalspace:personalportal", "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (personalspace:personalportal, metadata 0)"}}}}

name: Recycle for the Environment

name: Teflon Don
text:
teflon don to make ptfe, aka teflon, you only need a few steps.

the first one is hydrofluoric acid. if you haven't reached the moon yet, the best sources for fluorine might be cryolite. other options are treating sand or sandstone in a chemical plant for some fluorite ore, and centrifuging stone dust or black granite dust for biotite. you can also get small amounts from lepidolite in salt veins and mica. mix it with some hydrogen to get hydrofluoric acid.

if you have reached the moon, you can also process bastnasite ore.

name: The Creation of Life
text:
the creation of life by utilizing large amounts of energy, you're able to reactivate those broken spawners you may have found in the past. if you haven't, you should get one of them now.

if the broken spawner isn't of the type of mob you want to spawn, you'll need to do some extra work. capture one in a soul vial, then use that and the broken spawner in the soul binder to change the type. this takes forever, and also levels.

combine a bs with your powered spawner in an anvil to set the type for it to spawn. then you just gotta power it up!

if you set it to capture mode, you can make souls of a specific mob without any danger.

name: UUMatter
text:
uumatter now you can actually make the uum with a mass fabricator. well, technically you could make it without uua, but that's way more expensive. to make sure it only runs with uua, put a programmed circuit (any value) in the machine's slot. uumatter can be used for some very specific things, such as replicating some materials (check nei, mostly/all periodic table), used with crops to create an ore, some specific high-level recipes need it, and...you can also sit in it to get regen.

the energy usage and overclocking of the mass fabricator is different from the usual gt way. to have fixed eu to uum ratios for all tiers, the machine does 2/2 oc. it also starts with a very high amperage in lv. the following chart should make it more clear:

tier  amps       eu/t         time
lv     8a         256          160
mv     4a         512           80
hv     2a        1024           40
ev     1a        2048           20
iv     0.5a      4096           10
etc.

put in power (and hopefully uua), and out comes uum.

for now, just stockpile the uu matter. you need data orbs to use the replicator, and that's explained next tier.

name: Bigger Drums
text:
bigger drums now that you have drums, you want them larger? already??

well, in that case, you better start collecting or making cobblestone, by the tens of thousands. and making explosives too.

compress the cobblestone in an assembler first using circuit 9, then run them through the implosion compressor until you get quadruple compressed cobblestone. do that four times, and then another pass through the assembler with a diamond block, and there you have it - one bedrockium ingot.

now do that 5 more times, and you can make yourself a bedrockium drum.

64k buckets of portable fluid. perfect for your new ore drill!

[note]there's also a bedrockium ore much later on if you're lazy. by then you probably won't want the drums though.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 1, "oredict": "", "id": "extrautilities:drum", "resolved": {"id": "i:extrautilities:drum:1", "name": "bedrockium drum", "mod": "extrautilities", "registry": "drum", "icon": 6509, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 1, "shard": "18bafb9ea92c2aeb", "recipes": 1}, "label": "bedrockium drum"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 3, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "extrautilities:bedrockiumingot", "resolved": {"id": "i:extrautilities:bedrockiumingot:0", "name": "bedrockium ingot", "mod": "extrautilities", "registry": "bedrockiumingot", "icon": 6241, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "ab29b504c4dd6dd3", "recipes": 0}, "label": "bedrockium ingot"}}}}

text:

some items you might want to replicate include:
indium
platline metals like iridium and osmium
neon, krypton, xenon from liquid air distilling
oganesson

name: Dealing with Radiation
text:
dealing with radiation nuclear materials cause two types of radiation effects. one is a large number of standard debuffs. these can be removed the normal ways, with milk or gaia wart or other methods that imitate them.

the other effect is a special radiation unique debuff. this gets applied the longer you hold onto the radioactive item. severely radioactive items can apply minutes of this deadly debuff. regeneration might delay the inevitable death, but most regeneration sources aren't fast enough or long enough to keep you alive. you can try using an amulet of remedium to get rid of the effects. you should have one from your moon trip, if not you'll have to dive into thaumcraft to make one. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Indium
Just Enough Tungstensteel For Your Rocket
text:
just enough tungstensteel for your rocket ok, now you can:

1) turn the tungsten trioxide into hot tungsten ingots in the ebf with some carbon
2) keep going for ts

we want ts, so put some hydrogen along with the tungsten trioxide in your ebf to get rid of the oxygen.

combine your pure tungsten with steel in a mixer to get tungstensteel. then ebf and then freeze it to get the tungstensteel ingot.

some of tungstensteel dust you don't need to smelt as you will want to use it for hss-g!

[note]note that tungsten trioxide to tungsten ingot has reduced smelt time. this does not apply to the pure version. you're gonna need a bunch of it in iv as well as the ts, so keep this in name: Power of the Sun from Nuclear
text:
power of the sun from nuclear your good old singleblock molecular transformer is gone. so, how do you obtain sunnarium? well, there are a couple of ways, but at ev you'll need to radiate glowstone and convert it to sunnarium.

the glowstone rod will slowly charge up if you put it next to any fuel rod in your ic2 reactor. the exact charging speed is (number of rods adjacent) * (floor(hull temperature/3000) + 1) per second. a dual rod counts as 2 rods, and a quad fuel rod counts as 4 rods for this purpose. the glowstone rod will neither emit heat, nor cause other components to emit more heat. you can treat this rod as reactor plating in the ic2 reactor planner.

as you can see, the speed is directly proportional to hull temperature and adjacent rods. at the very extreme, you can fully charge up a glowstone rod in less than half a minute and output one sunnarium every 10 seconds (on average, since cells aren't charged at the same speed due to their different positions), but that requires a very considerable amount of resources to set up. it also involves a vacuum freezer to cool down the coolant cells and running the reactor at 66000+ hull temperature. balance your needs and your resource situation wisely.

the wiki has good advice for reactor planning: [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/nuclear_reactors[/url]

replace the containment reactor plating with actual glowstone rods and you should be good to go. you can also use fewer reactor chambers by using less plating. enjoy! {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, name: Pulverize the Planet
text:
pulverize the planet literally. you can grind the rock of most planets, to get a chance for...stuff. it depends on the planet. does consume quite a bit of power, but can really help you out.

for tungstate, you can centrifuge previously macerated moon dust, macerate end stone with an hv+ macerator and then centrifuge it, or centrifuge endergoo (found all over the end, does not give back buckets).

if you want to make your rocket, you need to get at least a little before you can get to a planet with the ore. however, keep in mind that you'll need an ebf with tpv coils to smelt tungstensteel dust into the ingot!

name: Radon Decay
text:
radon decay radon is needed for ev emitters and sensors.

you can get radium-226 from sifting thorium, pitchblende, uraninite, or uranium 238. it needs 4500 seconds, or 75 mins, to decay, and it will debuff you unless you have complete hazmat protection. it's a good idea to make a lead-lined box and let the radium decay there.

thorium can be obtained from the nether, whereas the other 3 ores are locked after the tier 2 rocket. however, thorium gives a much smaller chance of getting radium, so you'll need a good amount of it to continue.

after it decays, you can electrolyze radon out of it and progress into the next circuit line. however, you will not be able to do the radon loop here, that can only be done with plutonium 239.

name: The Redstone Sniffer
text:
the redstone sniffer ever wonder where your redstone transmitters are? or wish they were labeled? maybe your teammate placed one down, didn't tell you, and now you're stuck wondering what private frequency they placed it on?

now, you have a way to do all of that.

introducing the redstone sniffer!

for regular wireless redstone, the sniffer will list all currently used frequencies, tell you whether that frequency is private, and give you an option to label it.

for advanced wireless covers, the sniffer will additionally tell you where that cover is currently located, including in other dimensions, and offer you the option to highlight it (and teleport to it if you have op). {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.item_redstone_sniffer", "tag": {"last_page": 1}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (gregtech:gt.item_redstone_sniffer, metadata 0)"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 7, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:7", "name": "lootbag (tier 4 ev)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21276, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 7, "shard": "128329d33b3c2bec", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 4 ev)"}}}}

name: Tier 4 (EV)
text:
tier 4 (ev) the main goal here is to get a tier 2 rocket and reach mars. you also might want to rethink your power setup, as more and more machines will be upgraded. this quest set will teach you about a couple of options you have regarding power production, but it's recommended that you check out the how to generate power tab for more options and information.

name: A Small Reward: The Infinite Spray Can
text:
a small reward: the infinite spray can congratulations! you have completed the platinum line. not many players have the perseverance to accomplish this task. a small reward is in order!

the [note]infinite spray can[/note] never runs out of paint, and contains all sixteen colors (as well as solvent!) of course, line mode and ring of loki support are included. there are also many convenience features. middle-click to open a color choice gui. middle-click a painted block to copy its color to the spray can. left-click to cycle the active color (sneak to go backwards.) sneak-middle-click to lock the can; while locked, you can't accidentally change the color. sneak-middle-click to unlock.

you can also hold it in your offhand to automatically spray any colorable block you place with your main hand.

naturally, you'll have to craft the infinite spray can yourself. it's a dire crafting recipe, so hopefully you have a dire crafting table. it requires a lot of platinum line materials, of course. and, apparently, a rainbow cactus, so a small detour into magic will be necessary. and a bunch of random-looking ae2 parts. and an iv world accelerator. and... a fence?

text:

name: Chemical Reactions at IV Level
text:
chemical reactions at iv level high tier chemical recipes need a high tier iv chemical reactor.

alternatively you can use your large chemical reactor with either two ev energy hatches or one iv energy hatch.

[note]...which you can make after you finish the platline. have fun![/note]

if you missed it or forgot, hold a stack of the platline dust to skip the quests in between.

you can also skip the pbi chem quests, but you need to hold 128 sheets in your hand. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Long term planner?
text:
long term planner? well get ready for a processing line.

first you need to react thorium dust with hydrofluoric acid and eight buckets of nitric acid. i hope you have a nitric acid setup.

then react the thorium nitrate with sodium hydroxide to produce thorium hydroxide. then react with even more hydrofluoric acid to get thorium tetrafluoride.

then pump it into a centrifuge to separate the normal thorium away from the thorium 232. sadly it is still in a liquid form so you will need to blast it with zinc chloride and calcium.

then finally use your blast furnace again for the zn-th alloy ingot to separate the zinc from the thorium 232 to obtain the thorium 232 dust and even get your zinc back in fluid form.

name: Monazite
text:
monazite welcome to lanthanide processing!
it'll be a fun journey, whether you like it or not :p

first off get some monazite. this is only to get you started,
as you're going to need a ton to truly reap the rewards
of this line.

you'll then need to combine it with nitric acid in the digester multiblock,
to get its mud form.
yes, this is a very nitric acid hungry process!

[note]to skip all of the monazite quests hold a stack of each of these in your hand:

- zirconium dust / ingot
- hafnium dust / ingot
- cerium dust / ingot
- samarium dust / ingot[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 60, name: More Samarium!
text:
more samarium! if you have a stable samarium resource acquisition, refining samarium ore should be the best way to get samarium.

as the first step, dissolve some samarium ore concentrate dust or crushed samarium ore (you probably don't have access to this option yet) in nitric acid in a digester to get muddy samarium rare earth solution. thorium and phosphate are retained in the form of a solid slag powder.

then transfer the muddy solution to a dissolution tank and continue to soak it in nitric acid. the undissolved powder is then meticulously filtered out, yielding some cerium.

then dilute the result with water to adjust the ph. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": name: Repreci... what?
text:
repreci... what? reprecipitated! it means you have separated a solid from a solution/suspension, then dissolved it again, and then separated it again.

combine the original palladium enriched ammonia with palladium metallic powder. this will get you palladium salt again, but also reprecipitated palladium.

from now on you should skip the first step, it's not necessary anymore as this gives the same thing, but more. you do need to find a way to combine the dusts automatically though.

when/if you run out of palladium enriched ammonia, you can make more by adding ammonia to palladium metallic powder. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": name: Thorium 232?
text:
thorium 232? so you were looking at thorium 232 and wondering how to make it?

you could centrifuge it using a long recipe with a horrible output chance, but there are better ways to obtain it.

there are three processing paths, although the third is not unlocked until after you unlock fusion and gain access to the neutron activator.

the first path requires the chemical plant multiblock, which you may not be familiar with. it is the fastest path, requiring only two steps to obtain thorium 232, but it requires borax. you can obtain borax by mining salt veins (as a byproduct), from bees, or through cropsnh.

the second path is a six-step processing chain that requires chemical reactors, a centrifuge, and an ebf. although it is longer, it offers a much better conversion ratio (75%, rather than 25% in the chemical plant). instead of borax, it requires 100 l of fluorine per dust; the nitric acid can be fully recycled, so this path scales better than the borax route. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Your First Naquadah Ingot
text:
your first naquadah ingot you may have noticed that you can't get naquadah dust from the naquadah ore, it will only give you the naquadah oxide mixture (nom) dust, annoying.

the full naquadah processing line is too complex and does not fit in iv. i believe you won't want to set up another line after finishing platinum, pbi and lanthanide lines.

lucky, you can directly smelt the nom dust into naquadah nuggets in ebf, but it is inefficient and you will lose the byproducts in it.

name: Behold: The Netherite Line
text:
behold: the netherite line you didn't seriously think you only needed to do the naquadah line in luv did you? well if so; better brace yourself for the netherite line!

don't panic, it's a relatively straight-forward line so long as you can wrap your head around minor processing loops and percent based output. fortunately you have a quest book to guide you through your initial setup.

be warned- you will need at least grade 1 purified water and naquadah coils to make it through this entire line.

this questline will start you off with the three primary things you must prepare in order to begin:

- milled netherrack
- nether air
- ancient debris collection

for at least one and likely two of those you will need to journey into the nether, so make sure you're prepared equipment wise!

[warn]if you already created the line and do not wish to complete the individual quests, hold one of these three item sets in your hand after completing this quest: [/warn]

- 1 dense netherite plate
- 64 intensely bonded netherite nanoparticles
- 16 netherite ingots  {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Fetch Quests
text:
fetch quests to make the circuit assembly line imprints you'll need a bunch of new materials.

to start, let's get some raw materials, prasiolite, cubic zirconia, and tellurium.

you also need some other materials, but i don't need to explain those, do i?

name: Fetching Cubic Zirconia
text:
fetching cubic zirconia for cubic zirconia, you'll need to combine zirconium and yttrium oxide in the ebf as well. fortunately you only need the dusts.

you can get zirconium from:
1) the red zircon ore on ross128b <- do this one
2) sifting cassiterite, tin, or ilmenite <- do this one if you hate ross

oxygen isn't hard to get, but the yttrium more than makes up for it. you have a couple options:
1) make rare earth (i) out of rare earth (see the mv quest)
2) make rare earth (ii) out of rare earth using a stronger acid and get it from yttriaite
3) when you have a t6 rocket, you can pick some yttrium ore up from triton, making you cry at how much easier it is
4) in zpm you can try going to the toxic everglades to grab weird gt++ ores, some of which have yttrium in them (yay rng ore worldgen!)
5) process almandine ore (found in twilight forest) in an isamill grinder & flotation cell for the froth, then set in a vacuum furnace.

to get rare earth you can use redstone or skystone, but you can also get it out of monazite directly or some other ores as a byproduct. hopefully you saved it up? {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 2, "damage": 4, "oredict": "", "id": "bartworks:gt.bwmetagenerateddust", "resolved": {"id": "i:bartworks:gt.bwmetagenerateddust:4", "name": "cubic zirconia dust", "mod": "bartworks", "registry": "gt.bwmetagenerateddust", "icon": 16282, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 4, "shard": "3f301c5cbaa096b0", "recipes": 19}, "label": "cubic zirconia dust"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Fluid TP for Magic-Haters
text:
fluid tp for magic-haters hate magic (and fluid p2p), but still want to tp fluids? tt has your back with the ender fluid link cover!

place one on a tank and open the gui.
channel: covers with the same text will connect.

public: links to any of the same color not set to private. use an internet program to find out what the numbers mean, and get colors you like.
private: does not link to public version of that color. meaningless in sp.

export: fluid moves from attached block -> cover network
import: fluid moves from cover network -> attached block

you can use multiple as inputs and/or outputs. it runs at 8000l/t.

you can send from an output hatch or to an input hatch for multis. probably won't work well for anything with multiple i/o, like a singleblock chemical reactor. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 2, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "tectech:item.tm.enderfluidlinkcover", "resolved": {"id": "i:tectech:item.tm.enderfluidlinkcover:0", "name": "ender fluid link cover", "mod": "tectech", "registry": "item.tm.enderfluidlinkcover", "icon": 51546, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "1324677954ce87cb", "recipes": 1}, "label": "ender fluid link cover"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Fusion Rocketry
text:
fusion rocketry so you completed your fusion reactor and made your rocket, great! now time to get some new ore! (like that isn't getting old) you don't need your hand held anymore, so i'll just list what's new.

enceladus, miranda, oberon, ross128ba and titan are the new planets. miranda is the 1st moon of uranus, while oberon is the last. enceladus is the 2nd moon of saturn, while titan is the second last. ross128ba is ross128b's moon in the ross128 system to the south.

the new veins are nickel, tungsten, and vanadium. the ores are: chrome, deep iron, iridium, gold, magnetite, nickel, osmium, silicon, shadow iron, tungsten, and vanadium.

you can get neutronium from small ores on enceladus, oberon, and titan.

and grab some planet blocks while you're at it too.

you can get the schematic for t6 on enceladus.

[note]i'm sure you can tell by now, but it's not like every planet is required, so go to the ones you want to, and skip the ones you don't want to go to. use nei to figure out where you need to go.[/note] {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Imprint Supporting Boards
Imprints, They're Important
Intensely Bonded Netherite Nanoparticles
text:
intensely bonded netherite nanoparticles at long last... the final ingredient needed before making netherite materials.

through the combination of the netherite nanoparticles and hellish metal in the ebf, you can create intensely bonded netherite nanoparticles. as an added bonus for those who have invested in bees, using the combs from a netherite queen, will reward you with 2x the product.

these are not only the primary pre-requisite ingredients for the dense netherite plate that you need for the fusion reactor, but also the pre-requisite material for making the rest of the netherite parts after you have created one; so be sure to stockpile and manufacture as many of these nanoparticles as you can.

name: King of Acid
text:
king of acid this is the fluoroantimonic acid, the strongest acid in the world currently. it can dissolve almost everything on earth, so it is the best choice to dissolve our nom dust.

text:
mutating things is cool when making raw crystal chips, you have two other options if using europium constantly is too expensive for you: bacterial sludge, and mutagen.

mutagen is obviously better than the sludge, but how do you get it? i'll teach you how.

first, get the bacterial sludge you got from mars, and run it through a brewery along with some u-238 to get enriched bacterial sludge. then ferment it to get fermented bacterial sludge. and finally you distill it to get mutagen.

but is a single bucket enough for you? hardly! but now that we have some, we can make more with the vat. use the mutagen you got along with some of that mysterious crystal dust to make a culture. unfortunately the chances are pretty low, so you'll almost certainly have to do it several times.

once you have your culture you can use it in the vat along with some of the dust again to make more. you'll need luv-tier glass, and plutonium rods.

if you want to get more bacterial sludge more easily, you can use the vat to make that too! the culture is much easier to make.

name: Netherite Scrap
text:
netherite scrap netherite scrap is an integral part of the netherite refinement process and fortunately you don't need very much of it. technically you only need two pieces of scrap, as they will constantly cycle from hot to cool while never actually being used up in the process (though, having more scrap handy could improve your setup efficiency).

you can obtain netherite scrap by either smelting ancient debris or using a forge hammer on it. though considering the forge hammer offers a 25% chance at gaining an additional scrap, you would be a little crazy to choose the former.

if you're wondering where you can find ancient debris, try scouring the nether. it's more likely to spawn lower near the lava, and is found sporadically like small ores are rather than being in large veins like usual gt ores. miners can also collect it!

[warn]if you don't feel like leaving home, or are lacking blocks within your nether dimension, there is also a meteor that can alleviate your ancient debris woes.[/warn] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, name: Starting Fusion
text:
starting fusion nuclear fusion is the next major step in your progression, and to accomplish it you will need a fusion reactor mark i. you will unlock new materials across the next few tiers with fusion, making this a required multiblock. europium is what you will need first to make it to zpm.

at the same time, fusion can generate power for you, primarily via helium plasma in this first tier. the speed of the reactor can make for significant eu/t, but actually consuming this plasma fast enough at this early stage is difficult. you will have large plasma turbines, which can run a buffered dynamo for 4 output amps. this might require a lot of spam compared to powergen setups you might be using, such as ucfe, vac nukes or other options. later, you will unlock xl turbines and a fusion line for them. 

for your first reactor, you will need a controller, 1-16 fluid input hatches, 1-16 fluid output hatches, and 16 luv+ energy hatches. each energy hatch has an energy capacity of 10m eu and draws up to 2048 eu/t.

that means you can do any fusion recipe with a start cost of 160m eu or less, and takes 32768 eu/t or less. using more fluid hatches means you need less fusion casings. while this doesn't matter as much for the mk1 reactor, this principle helps tremendously with the higher reactor tiers.

[note]you'll notice that there is an option to create a compact fusion reactor mki instead of the normal size. this is available as an option for every tier of fusion reactor. they are not required by name: Configuring TecTech Multiblocks
text:
configuring tectech multiblocks many tectech multis can be customized by adjusting certain internal numbers called parameters. you can directly adjust them in the gui.

if there are lit up sections in the parameters part of the multi interface (see the tectech multiblocks quest), you can configure the multi, otherwise there is nothing to do.

we'll be using the quantum computer as our example, since that is what you probably want it for.

first we need to understand the parameter naming, like id:0:1:i. the first number represents the parameter block. for the qc only block 0 is used. each such block can have up to 4 used parameters, 2 inputs and 2 outputs. the letter at the end specifies if a parameter is an input or output with i or o and the number in the middle distinguishes the 2 parameters of this kind in the block. it is either 0 or 1.

inputs are something that is either set or is a default. outputs give information that the machine sends to you, that indicates things. (like heat or computation)

and lastly, the parametrizer memory card lets you copy settings from one machine to another easily. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "tectech:item.em.parametrizermemorycard", "tag": {}, "resolved": {"id": "i:tectech:item.em.parametrizermemorycard:0", "name": "parametrizer memory card (copy mode)", "mod": "tectech", "registry": "item.em.parametrizermemorycard", "icon": 51545, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "367808dec69350c1", "recipes": 1}, "label": "parametrizer memory card (copy mode)"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Data Bank
text:
data bank by now you probably feel overwhelmed with the number of data sticks needed for your assembly line. tectech has a solution for you: the data bank. it allows you to store more than just 16 data sticks and can be connected to multiple assembly lines at the same time.

place the controller one block above the ground and use the multiblock structure hologram projector to see how it is built. you will need a maintenance hatch and at least an ev energy hatch, though the power requirements can be much higher if you use many data access hatches and data bank master connectors, for now you should start with an luv energy hatch. trying to run the data bank and then scanning the controller will tell you how much eu/t is needed.

you will need more blocks than what is asked for in this quest, as the number of data access hatches and connectors is up to you. you can have a maximum of 15 combined.

the assembly line reception connector replaces your old data access hatch on the assembly line. connect it to a master connector on the data bank with optical fiber cable and make sure to color the hatches and the cable.

name: Prismarine!? What Do I Need That For?
text:
prismarine!? what do i need that for? prismarine is an ancient material long rumored to have originated from structures found deep within the ocean. learning how to create this is extremely important, and may lead to advancements in technology with further exploration into the substrate.

you can get prismarine in a few different ways as shown resource-wise by the optional tasks:

1. through botania by transmutating nether quartz directly to prismarine via an alchemical catalyst or the fountain of alchemy

2. using red algae biomass and certus quartz dust in an autoclave

3. using red algae biomass and prismatic combs in an autoclave.

which method you choose is entirely up to you and dependent on what infrastructure you have setup thus-far. either way you would be wise to make a robust setup as you will be needing a decent amount of prismarine in the future.

name: Superdense
TecTech Multiblocks
text:
tectech multiblocks tectech multiblock common functionality

multiple ampere and laser hatches compatibility - to ease power distribution.

power pass - allows connected dynamo hatches to take power from the controller and output it, just like the active transformer does (and that is why the controller always need it in its recipe if that function is enabled...). [warn]be sure to turn off power pass if you want to edit your machine and don't want it to explode![/warn]

constructable interface - allows visualizing the structure with blueprints (there is an api to implement that for any block, but almost nothing does).

from left to right is 1, then clockwise for the rest in tt multi interfaces.

1) parameters - they are the way of the controller to communicate with player and parameter hatches. lights indicate status but more detailed information can be seen when moused over. the tooltip contains id in form of hatchid:parameternumber:direction, current status, current value, and short description.

2) uncertainty status - these 9 blocks indicate uncertainty status of the machine. if the lights are on, this machine requires an uncertainty resolver. red = bad, green = good. you need to do the absurd puzzle before using the machine.

control buttons - buttons might change their behavior and appearance depending on machine but usually they work like this, starting from top:

3) power pass - toggles power pass.

4) safe void - currently unused.

5) power switch - soft mallet with your finger...

6) input slot - standard functionality. {"0": {"index": 1, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

text:

there's only two new planets this time, proteus and triton. they're both moons of neptune.

the new veins are neutronium, niobium, and thorium. the ores are: adamantium, gallium, naquadah, neutronium, niobium, plutonium-241, titanium, uranium 235, uranium-238, and yttrium.

you should pick up some planet blocks while you're visiting.

name: Wormhole Generator
text:
wormhole generator the miniature wormhole generator uses quantum entangled singularities to transmit power over any distance, including across dimensions.

to use it, you must link two generators together using ae2 entangled singularities by placing one in each controller. once linked, both wormholes must be started by placing a full (non-entangled) ae2 singularity into an input bus on each machine. the wormhole will continue running as long as power is being transferred between them. if power transfer stops, the link will shut down and must be restarted using another singularity on both ends.

power is transferred through laser source hatches and laser target hatches. each wormhole can support up to 4 laser hatches. these must be placed in the center block of one of the side faces, excluding the controller side. hatch pairs link based on relative position between the two wormholes, not cardinal direction. for example, a source hatch placed on the top of the sending side must connect to a target hatch placed on the bottom of the receiving wormhole.

additionally, unlike ae2 p2p tunnels, this does not come with a 5% power loss but rather a much more manageable 0.5% loss. 

[note]the glass and input hatch must be tiered accordingly with the tier of the laser hatches. but remember, there is no amperage limit on this machine, so use whatever makes it cheapest for name: Actually Copying Cultures
text:
actually copying cultures to copy a culture, you'll need:

1) a sterilized petri dish
2) a plasma membrane (made from stemcells, or gotten while making enzymessollution)
3) stemcells
4) a data orb with the appropriate data on it
5) liquid dna
6) a uv bio lab
7) a clonal cellular synthesis module

you can change out the data orb for one with whatever culture you wish to copy. keep in mind that it might be easier to make a second culture the normal way, and that there's generally an alternative recipe that uses the fluid it produces to make it with a higher chance.

name: Advanced Crystal SoC Production
text:
advanced crystal soc production we can process crystal processing units in a laser engraver to get the crystal soc. but as our demand for circuits gradually increases, this method of production is becoming untenable. we need a more advanced way to mass produce crystal socs!

for that we use a new material, cerium-doped lutetium aluminium garnet (ce:luag). luag has better performance when making crystal socs - in fact it is a laser crystal material.

first, mix lutetium, aluminium, oxygen, and a little cerium to get the material blend. then put the blend with molten lutetium into an autoclave to get a regular luag gem. if you have already got oganesson you can also directly use that. as the second step, use the luag gem and more of the blend to produce exquisite luag gems.

after you get the first gem, you can also use your autoclave to grow crystals. using the vacuum furnace might be a better choice to produce exquisite luag gems.

lutetium, lutetium, it needs a lot of lutetium. how will you get a lot of lutetium? check out the powerful nuclear physics quest tab! {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, name: All Good Things...
text:
all good things... so you've built your t7 rocket. great, there's only one more left. until then, the new places you can visit are: haumea, the kuiper belt, makemake, and pluto.

pluto is just before the kuiper belt, and haumea and makemake are just after.

the new veins are black plutonium, garnet, red garnet. the ores are: black plutonium, borax, chrysotile, garnet sand, nether star, realgar, red garnet, and yellow garnet.

don't forget the planet blocks!

the last schematic is on pluto. this is also the last dungeon. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Elastic Singularity
Extract what you want
text:
extract what you want directly dissolve and chlorinate lanthanide ores in digester to get the concentrated solution of the corresponding ore. then use the corresponding extracting nano resin to extract the main material in the solution. the rest (chlorinated rare earth concentrate) is still rich in useful lanthanides.

you can use any type of extracting nano resin to extract the useful things in the rest. what nano resin you use, what lanthanide you'll get. every bucket of chlorinated rare earth concentrate can do this extraction 3 times. first concentrate to enriched solution, then enriched solution to diluted solution, then waste liquid.

after extracting, the nano resin will be "filled". put them "filled" into electrolyzer then nanites will transfer the "particles" out from the resin under the influence of electric field. and you can get the nano resins and let them go into the next work round, again and again without breaks.

yes, rare earth will not be rare. bless the nano tech. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": name: Fluids for Copying Cultures
text:
fluids for copying cultures ok, so let's say you've made some kind of culture, but you want more of it? you only need one per vat, but they're consumed when making dna samples, so you should probably learn how.

to start off, you'll need to get an ecoli culture.

use that to make the ecoli bacteria fluid. [note](i know the name is completely different, deal with it)[/note]

centrifuge that to make liquid dna.

and combine it with radon in the mixer to make fluorecentddna.

ecoli bacteria fluid can also be centrifuged for plasma membranes and enzymessollution, so do that as well.

and then centrifuge the enzymessollution again for polymerase.

you should expect to need a significant amount of ecoli bacteria fluid if you plan on copying a lot of cultures, or making the hard to make ones.

[note]to search for items related to copying cultures, search for 'culture', 'dna sample', or 'plasmid'. you can't do this for the data orbs, you have to check the uses of dna samples.[/note]

name: General Purpose Fermenting Bacteria
text:
general purpose fermenting bacteria so if you looked in nei and tried to figure out how to make this, you were probably confused by the fact that you use the fluid it produces to make it. this is where nei is lying to you. like the previous recipe, nei doesn't show it correctly (they should be around the same page in nei, they both also appear to produce sterilized petri dishes, (even if that's not true) and both use unique modules).

in order to make this, you'll need to make the rotten flesh bacteria culture, get the dna sample, and then get the data orb. it changes its name to beta-lactamase, that's normal.

then, do the same thing for common yeast (get the right yeast!).

then you need to use the recipe to combine the information from the data orbs and get the common yeast plasmid from that.

lastly, use the rotten flesh bacteria culture, the common yeast plasmid, penicillin (make it by centrifuging common yeast fluid), and distilled water. you want the transformation module for this. it's a 100% chance.

you'll want to use the normal recipe to make more cultures, since it also becomes beta-lactamase once you turn it into a dna sample. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, name: Quantum Computer
text:
quantum computer the quantum computer (qc) is an incredibly complicated machine used to generate computation for the research station and a few other multiblocks. there are a few things you need to understand before using one.

construction. much like an assembly line, the qc is built as a series of slices. the first and last slice are the only valid locations for hatches. the slices in between are primarily for computer racks. the multiblock structure hologram projector shows the minimum length qc, but holding multiple in a single stack will show/build longer versions up to the maximum length of 16. there is also a mandatory air block in front of the computer heat vents.

output. computation is nothing more than an integer input for certain recipes--much like eu. there may exist a minimum throughput requirement, a threshold to reach, or both (nei will tell you everything). computation is generated every second by the qc, transmitted by an optical transmission connector, received by an optical reception connector, and "consumed" by the machine or process that needs it. there is no storing computation and there can only be one transmission or reception hatch connected to the same optical fiber cables at a time. if absolutely necessary, the network switch with qos can split/join connections but know that it takes both power and maintenance to run.

additional qc can be chained together using another set of optical transmission and optical reception connectors between machines, but they cannot wallshare the same optical transmission connector.

uncertainty. the qc has a unique maintenance requirement that can only be corrected by balancing the schrödinger matrix inside an uncertainty resolver- an additional hatch that must go on either the first or last slice of the machine. start with the uncertainty resolver x, but know that there is another tier unlocked later on (uncertainty resolution) that will solve the puzzle on its own.

the interface of the uncertainty resolver x has the schrödinger matrix in the middle and two sets of 8 buttons on the left and right. clicking on one button and then another will switch the states of the two corresponding cells in the matrix. this means switching their shade/color. the goal of the puzzle is to balance the states of the matrix around the glowing led lights, turning all of them green.

parameters. in the gui of the controller, there are two configurable parameters, overclock and overvolt, that change how computation and heat are generated. higher overclock values contribute the most to computation and higher overvolt values contribute the most to heat. alone, this would encourage the player to make overclock as high as possible and overvolt as low as possible, but there is a penalty to computation for large differences between these two parameters. furthermore, overvolt values <1 will cause the qc to randomly drop computation proportional to its distance from 1. it is highly encouraged to play around with these parameters, as all the best setups do.

see the adjacent quest for more information on computer racks and generating computation. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, name: Quantum Mechanics is Hot
text:
quantum mechanics is hot the qc has 2-24 computer racks depending on the length of the machine. each rack has four total slots for either circuits (to generate heat and computation) or vents (to dissipate heat). although conceptually similar to a nuclear reactor, the location of the components inside does not matter at all. every rack is also completely independent from every other rack which means it is not possible to have one rack with all circuits and another with all vents.

the computation of a rack is the sum of all the components' individual computation. for example, two apu (tier 3) and two cooling cores have 240 + 240 + 0 + 0 = 480 base computation per second. however, computation changes significantly depending on the values for overclock and overvolt:

[note]computation = base * (1+overclock^2) / (1+(overclock-overvolt)^2)[/note]

the heat of a rack is a value between 0 and 10,000 and is reported in the interface of the qc or by using a portable scanner on the rack. every component has a certain heat limit which if exceeded will void that component. breaking or wrenching a rack while it is hot (>2000) will similarly void the components inside. the qc will explode if the heat exceeds 10,000 but no component has a heat limit greater than that, so don't worry too much about ruining your base.

[note]heat α heatconstant * overclock * overvolt^2[/note]

the power consumption of a rack is 1a zpm regardless of the components inside. this is in addition to the 1a zpm of the qc itself. however, these eu/t values are directly proportional to overclock and overvolt which should increase as you unlock better circuits. be sure to turn on the qc before the research station and only when you need it.

[note]eu/t = 131,072 * overclock * overvolt * (racks + 1)[/note]

to get you started, craft 4x apu (tier 3) and 4x cooling cores. place two of each component in the two racks and the qc will safely produce 1,920 computation/s for just 393,215 eu/t (0.75a uv) which is more than enough for researching the wetware mainframe. if you would like to further increase the computation/s at the cost of power, adjust the overclock and overvolt values to 1.44 and 1.03, respectively. this will generate 2,526 computation/s at a cost of 583,217 eu/t (1.11a uv).

if the apus are too bothersome to craft, try crystal mainframes instead but you will need different overclock and overvolt values to get the most out of them. that goes for every unique combination of circuits and vents. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 4, "damage": 103, "oredict": "", "id": "opencomputers:item", "resolved": {"id": "i:opencomputers:item:103", "name": "accelerated processing unit (apu) (tier 3)", "mod": "opencomputers", "registry": "item", "icon": 9513, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 103, "shard": "548bad8315074a6a", "recipes": 1}, "label": "accelerated processing unit (apu) (tier 3)"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:optional_retrieval"}, "1": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 1, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 4, "damage": 2, "oredict": "", "id": "gravisuite:itemsimpleitem", "resolved": {"id": "i:gravisuite:itemsimpleitem:2", "name": "cooling core", "mod": "gravisuite", "registry": "itemsimpleitem", "icon": 8175, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 2, "shard": "85d25a537aa3a9b9", "recipes": 4}, "label": "cooling core"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: Space Elevator
text:
space elevator the space elevator is a modular structure. it can be equipped with space elevator modules, which then can take on different tasks.

initially, your space elevator has 6 module slots that can be used. you can later upgrade that to up to 12 with mk-ii and mk-iii motors. the motor tier also determines the module tier that you can use. the i/o is not shared between modules, each module only sees their own i/o slots. energy is only provided to the central structure of the space elevator and then automatically distributed to all modules.

after a module has been inserted and supplied with the right i/o, it can be configured further using parameters.

you can see in nei which fluids are pumpable with the space pumping module. it consumes 1a uhv to work. the gas type and planet type are parameters.

nei also has an overview of all the ores you can obtain with a space mining module. it needs to be supplied with a drone, which will act as catalyst, a set of input items, computation and either helium, bismuth or radon plasma. the plasma will boost both the recipe time and the amount of bonus stacks you get out of a recipe. with its parameters you can adjust parallels, overdrive, and distance. when multiple recipes have the same input and you have the distance set to a value that they share, the module will pick a random one, taking the recipes weights into consideration.

the space elevator also lets you travel to other planets, but it doesn't get you back though so better keep that in mind!

the mining module also got a cycle mode. in static mode it will hold its distance while in cycle mode it will change its distance after each recipe check (and you can configure the range and step size of that).

[note]teleportation can be accessed though the controller.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 14003, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.blockmachines", "resolved": {"id": "i:gregtech:gt.blockmachines:14003", "name": "space elevator", "mod": "gregtech", "registry": "gt.blockmachines", "icon": 23625, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 14003, "shard": "5d497a0cb75f149e", "recipes": 2}, "label": "space elevator"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {}

name: The Board that Keeps Life

name: This is Not How You Make Cheese
text:
this is not how you make cheese in order to make wetware circuits, you'll need sterilized growth catalyst medium and stemcells.

to begin, you will first need bacteria which you can get through the bacterial vat or the brewing machine. the vat recipe is more efficient, but you need a culture for it so you need to start with the brewing recipe. the bacterial vat needs at least bismuth rods in the radio hatch for the proper sievert and at least ev-tier glass to make bacteria. there are also 3 different recipes, so you can use a higher tier one later if you like.

you'll also need mince meat and agar. you'll want a stable supply of meat such as a fish farm, a standard animal farm, or meatrose/goldfish farm.

agar has a more complicated processing chain, but it's nothing compared to platinum. you'll need even more meat for it.

use some of the bacteria to create an ova evolutionis culture (15% chance), and then place that in the bacterial vat's controller. the bacterial vat also needs at least uranium rods in the radio hatch for the proper sievert and at least iv-tier glass to make raw growth catalyst medium. there are higher tier recipes for this as well.

name: A Blast to the Past
text:
a blast to the past now that you have the bioware mainframe, you have unlocked the first of the stargate trophies!
yes, there's multiple of them, one for each major iteration of the stargate recipe.
these trophies are just that, trophies, and you can try to craft them if you want to compare the costs to today's stargate standards.
to complete these quests you have to submit two stargates' worth of materials.

now, let me bestow upon you a short history lesson about this point in gt:nhs past.

the year is 2020. the bio mainframe was pretty much the end of gtnh progression at the time, not much above uhv existed or was craftable. this was also the point in the pack where you'd start scaling for stargate, as that too was tiered at uhv. technically uev parts were craftable, but their only uses were singleblocks for pas (which only held up to 16 uev machines) and the deep dark portal. uev-umv energy hatches were craftable, but their recipes were simple hull + wire crafting table recipes
...and that was about it for uhv+ content.
with the recent addition of void miners, the previously thought to be impossible started to seem actually attainable, a set of stargates. specifically, to craft a set of them, not just find them like others have before.

one group in particular, known as the gigaplex, gave it their all and actually managed to do it, to prove that crafting stargates is possible with enough determination.

thus, on the 16th of february, 2021, the first set of crafted stargates had been born.

p.s.: if you want to be as faithful to the challenge as possible, try completing this quest without using any of the modern functionality that didn't exist back then.
here's a non-exhaustive list of major things that didn't exist (in no particular order):
-pcb factory, space elevator, component assemblyline, aal, prass, eec, eig, compact fusions, mcr, mabs
-any bee related gt machines
-any uev or above multis
-xl turbines, naq fuel, leg
-sub 1-tick oc, batch mode, inbuilt void protection on multis
-level maintainer, ae fluid crafting, stocking buses/hatches, crafting input buses, me output buses/hatches, non-recursive ae component recipes
-shift-clicking recipes into ae patterns (pain)
-early-midgame qol such as ghost circuits, visual prospecting, reprogramming circuits with a screwdriver, seeing assline recipes in nei before having crafted them, and more

p.p.s: this quest is missing the chaotic capacitors on purpose, because the chaotic core recipe requires spacetime now, but the chaotic capacitor recipe did not change at all since then. all in all the cost for these banks was completely negligible back then and still is today, they only serve as a magic gate for sg. {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 1, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, name: Compressing the Core of a Star
text:
compressing the core of a star the next material is infinity catalyst. infinity catalyst needs to be compressed with insane amounts of force. the only machine capable of doing that is a neutronium compressor. check out the neutronium compressor quest in multiblock goals if you haven't made one yet.

to make the catalyst, go to vega b to get the dust. then use the neutronium compressor to make infinity catalyst with 64 of the dust.

you can also do the insane avaritia recipe to make the infinity catalyst, if you want a challenge :p

[note]the compressor can also be used to make singularities, culminating in the eternal singularity, used in the alternate recipe.[/note]

name: It's Not Going Bad, I Swear!
text:
it's not going bad, i swear! to make your next tier of circuits (bio circuits), you need to make raw bio medium. there are three ways of making it.

the first one requires stemcells, unknown crystal and t-ceti seaweed extract at luv voltage and 94 sievert (plutonium level) in a bacterial vat. it makes raw bio medium at 4:1 ratio.

the second one is basically the first one, but it requires infinity catalyst instead of tritanium at zpm voltage and 140 sievert (enriched naquadah level) in a bacterial vat. it makes raw bio medium at 1:1 ratio.

the third one is the most efficient, but it requires biocells (which you don't have yet), and 4 dust of infinity catalyst at uv voltage and 150 sievert (naquadria level) in a bacterial vat. it makes raw bio medium at 1:2 ratio.

name: Soldering's Not Working Anymore
text:
soldering's not working anymore after all these advancements, it looks like some things just aren't meant to be. every machine that your assembly line has crafted works, but the most advanced ones so far seem to be... a bit rough around the edges. further inspection revealed that indalloy just isn't good enough. it seems that infinity's neverending vibrations destabilize the joints where the soldering happens, your living circuits have been offering resistance to this crude soldering alloy, however that happens...

it's likely that new materials will completely break indalloy's ability to get pieces soldered together. because of that, it's about time for a new development in this technology, and the previous rejection by your living circuits has given you an excellent idea. any new material can have some new behavior that will ruin assembling for you, but what if the solder itself learns about these complications and learns how to adjust to them, mutating for them?

that's right: mutated living solder.

this sort of chemistry is only possible in a full-scale chemical plant, equipped with the most advanced casing: botmium. on top of that, the catalyst you need to use has been consumed so thoroughly that you were forced to use infinity for it, on top of the mutating naquadria. your infinity will be lost to the crafting, still, unless you manage to put [note]tungstensteel pipe casings[/note] and [warn]awakened draconium coils[/warn] in your chemical plant, which prevent the catalyst from losing durability. any better coils also have the same effect.

the new solder itself is a different story. wetware technology is too primitive for this, and your bio cells have refused to bond with any fluid that would serve as its carrier for soldering. when you tried a mixture of hot tin and bismuth, it finally worked, but the soldering didn't actually work. it looked like the bio cells hadn't learned how to fulfill their new job, which could be fixed by adding an example material as a test subject, something simpler like infinity catalyst... but it seemed impossible to bond the cells to the dust. you need more energy... not just loads of eu, something concentrated, hot, fizzling with energy!

yes, everything alive died instantly when you decided to add plasmas instead of hot fluids. no surprise there. however, bio cells did survive inside hot fluids, so we just need some temperature control here, and some separation between cell and plasma... yes, gravi stars can be used for this. we still need to cool down the plasmas, so that the enhanced cells can mix with them in liquid form, and eu alone would be too expensive. gelid cryotheum has proven to be surprisingly efficient, perhaps due to its origins, as a component of a living being, the blizz.

there we go! the mutated living solder is now complete. the highly intelligent bio cells are energized by the concentrated heat of the plasmas, while keeping a distance from them due to the gravi stars' influence, and they analyze the infinity catalyst dust to learn about material instability. this is a very slow process, but it happens at the same time as the plasmas are slowly cooled, using cryotheum and eu, until the learning process is complete and the bio cells fall into the tin and bismuth, now in the liquid form that was shown to work before. finally, armed with their new knowledge, the cells flow through the naquadria-based, infinity-reinforced catalyst so that they can mutate in real-time after researching the material they're soldering.

this should work for any future soldering need, regardless of material. let's hope so, at least... {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 1, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "miscutils:itemcellmutatedlivingsolder", "resolved": {"id": "i:miscutils:itemcellmutatedlivingsolder:0", "name": "mutated living solder cell", "mod": "miscutils", "registry": "itemcellmutatedlivingsolder", "icon": 49630, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "d97d52e0b5c720c1", "recipes": 1}, "label": "mutated living solder cell"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:optional_retrieval"}, "1": {"index": 2, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: The Final Frontier?
text:
the final frontier? the last of the normal rocket progression. after this is there is only the mothership for the t9 system and the deep dark, which has all the ores+more.

although you get access to six new planets, there's only two new veins. and don't complain that barnarda should be barnard, we can't fix it.

the barnarda system is to the nnw, and you can visit barnarda c, e, and f.
the α centauri system is to the ne, and you can visit α centauri bb (proxima centauri is not visitable). [note]remember to wear your spacesuit![/note]
the t ceti system is to the ssw, and you can visit the habitable planet t ceti e.
the vega system is to the wnw, and you can visit the planet vega b.

the new veins are cadmium and samarium. the ores are cadmium, caesium, cerium, lanthanum, neodymium, samarium, and tartarite.

you can get awakened draconium from small ores on barnarda e, barnarda f, t ceti e, and vega b.
you can get bedrockium from small ores on barnarda f.
you can get infinity catalyst from small ores on vega b.

in addition to planet ores and blocks, grab some barnarda c saplings and dirt so you can grow some more if you need it for radox (lol). you can also grab some more unknown crystal shards from the rainbow crystals lying around.

more importantly you should collect seaweed from t ceti e. you need it to make uev circuits, and though you can make it as well, you need some to begin with. the unknown liquid to grow these is however found in lakes and underground on barnarda c. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Xenoxene Xenoxsis
text:
xenoxene xenoxsis to make the next tier plastic, radox, or the next tier of smds, you will need xenoxene.

getting the xenoxene xenoxsis culture is a bit tricky. the recipe is similar to the general purpose one. remember that all recipes in this chain are low probability recipes.

your first step is to make the barnardafis culture, then the dna sample, and then the data orb. if you didn't grab the saplings and dirt previously (to grow more trees for logs), head back to barnarda c.

use the same recipe as for the general purpose one, but use the data orb for barnardafis instead of common yeast. you should get the barnardafis plasmid.

again, it's the same recipe for the next step, but with the tcetieis fucus serratus culture and the barnardafis plasmid, this should produce the xenoxene xenoxsis culture. it's a 7.5% chance.

you should probably use the normal alternative recipe to make more cultures, since it's easy to fail copying it too.

you should be able to figure out yourself how to make xenoxene once you have the culture.

name: Automating Power On/Off
text:
automating power on/off once you have a gt boiler or large combustion engine with a long startup time, you may wish to automate turning it on/off to save fuel, since extra power or steam will just be voided. additionally, the bigger your steam/eu buffer is, the less time your generators will spend heating up, which makes them more efficient.

use a machine controller cover on the controller for that. you can put it on top, bottom, or sides next to a casing - casings will transmit the redstone signal. you can use a soldering iron and fine soldering alloy wire to set the redstone output of a controller block to strong. when set to strong it can go through a casing, but not hatches, buses, or other blocks. use it with an activity detector if you want to receive a signal from the controller rather than turning it on/off with one.

with a machine controller cover, you can use redstone to turn the machine on and off. this is handy if you don't want to use a soft hammer to disable a machine yourself constantly.

the best way to do that is with an rs latch. one input will turn the machine on, and one input will turn the machine off. use a comparator attached to a valve to measure the steam level in your multiblock iron or steel tank. invert the signal to turn on your boiler when the steam level is low. when the steam level signal is high, turn your boiler off. use a trail of redstone to lower the signal strength. because of boiler/turbine warmup, try to set the on strength to 30 percent of capacity and off strength to about 90 percent.

red alloy wire will hold a redstone signal for a longer distance than normal redstone, while redstone conduits will go indefinitely. you can also use amplified redcrystal to improve the strength of the signal for a long distance, repeating as necessary.

you can use an energy detector cover in normal electrical storage (including batteries) mode to monitor the power in a battery buffer and use it to enable/disable generators in a similar way. change mode using a screwdriver. if you use a dense redcrystal, it will only allow signal through at a certain level, perfect for automating this kind of thing.

name: Build Your Own Keep Inventory
text:
build your own keep inventory the ender io mod adds one of the handiest enchantments in the game: soulbound. an item enchanted with it stays in your inventory when you die, while everything else drops into your grave.

the best part: it works on almost anything, even items that normally reject enchantments:

- backpacks (both normal and adventure backpacks) - including everything inside them
- the mantle of the raven and the rod of the skies
- even tinkers' construct tools, which normally ignore vanilla enchantments completely

how to get it:

1. the ender io enchanter crafts soulbound books from a book and quill and an ender crystal. see the [questlink]aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaqg==[/questlink] quest.

2. loot bags regularly drop enchanted books, soulbound among them - higher tiers give better chances. see the "do you feel unlucky?" quest.

3. found an item that already has soulbound? strip it off with the draconic evolution disenchanter to get the book. see the [questlink]aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaifa==[/questlink]quest - surrounding the disenchanter with bookcases reduces the damage it deals.

applying it is easy: use a vanilla anvil, just like any other enchantment.

[note]ps: put soulbound on your backpack itself - the backpack and everything inside it stays with you on death.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 0, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "minecraft:enchanted_book", "tag": {"storedenchantments": {"0": {"id": 8, "lvl": 1}}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (minecraft:enchanted_book, metadata 0)"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"choices": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 6, "oredict": "", "id": "enhancedlootbags:lootbag", "resolved": {"id": "i:enhancedlootbags:lootbag:6", "name": "lootbag (tier 3 hv)", "mod": "enhancedlootbags", "registry": "lootbag", "icon": 21274, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 6, "shard": "4351b75552afb0b2", "recipes": 1}, "label": "lootbag (tier 3 hv)"}, "1": {"count": 2, "damage": 8, "oredict": "", "id": "enderio:itemmaterial", "resolved": {"id": "i:enderio:itemmaterial:8", "name": "ender crystal", "mod": "enderio", "registry": "itemmaterial", "icon": 5413, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 8, "shard": "7a02f75b28b56912", "recipes": 1}, "label": "ender crystal"}}, "ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:choice"}}

name: Covering Up
text:
covering up this quest goes over all of the covers, just in case you forgot or they weren't mentioned. if they have their own quest, look at it for more info. you can put them on basically any gt block, pipe, machine, tank, etc. though that doesn't consider whether it will work right or be useful. shift-right-click will open a gui for many of them. for covers that you can adjust the amount of, clicking the left side with a screwdriver goes down, and right goes up. all covers block rain on the side they're attached to. generally you can adjust covers with a screwdriver, whether they have a gui or not. you can remove them with a crowbar if you forgot.

fluid-related covers:
pump: transfers fluids at the speed specified on the tooltip.

fluid regulator: regulates the rate that fluid can go through it, as well as pumping it. can work x/s or x/t.

steam valve: moves more, but is only for steam. only goes to iv. does not work on sh steam.

overflow: voids anything over the specified amount in the tank.

fluid detector: will emit a redstone signal (rs) based on fluid fill rate of the tank it's on. by default, empty=15, full=0. use inverted mode to swap. useful on tanks and hatches.

ender fluid link: cover version of ender tanks to tp fluid around. doesn't connect to ender tanks though.

drain module: protects from rain on that side, and will fill the tank with water from rain if it can. useless.

fluid filter: filters fluid going through it. click with a cell to set it.

shutter: blocks items/fluids when active. use it with a machine controller and rs. does not visually disconnect/block. you place it between the pipes, and put the mc on the same pipe.

item-related covers:
conveyor: sends items. use an item pipe in import mode or on a gt block/machine.

robot arm: sends from a specific slot in the machine it's on (internal) to another specific slot in a block next to it (adjacent). keep going through numbers until you get it right, it seems to change per machine. if the output slot is full, it won't output. there needs to be a valid block with slots to send to, or the settings won't save.

item detector: will emit rs based on item fill rate of the block it's on. by default, empty=0, full=15. detects by filled slots, so doesn't work right with the super/quantum chests. probably better for buses.

filtered conveyor: filters up to one type of item (whitelist/blacklist) and acts as a conveyor module. locked to either export or import.

eu-related covers:
energy detector: will emit rs based on eu fill rate of the batbuff/tank it's on. by default, empty=0, full=15. make sure to set it to include batteries. can also detect steam for some reason.

power pass upgrade: read the tooltip, then ask bart how it works, he didn't bother telling anyone. he'll probably just tell you the code is the best documentation, just like the tectech guys. may not actually be finished/work, either.

tesla coil/tesla coil rich edition: use with the tesla tower to send eu wirelessly or something.

other covers:
player detector: detects players. about 10 block range. [warn]currently owner/other is inverted on non-pipes due to some bug or another.[/warn]

activity detector: detects either recipe progress or idleness. 0%=0 rs, ~95%=14 by default. in idle mode, idleness is 15, and is 0 when running by default.

machine controller: turns machine on/off based on rs. disable machine will keep it off regardless of rs state. safe mode only works on mbs. if a mb runs out of power, it will normally turn off, but a mc will turn it back on, continuing to void stuff. this will set it to the disable machine state instead. you will also get a notification. [warn]safe mode is currently broken?[/warn]

needs maintenance: emits rs if it meets the condition specified. rotor=turbine?

redstone transmitter/receiver (in/out): ok, these things are confusing, so listen closely. first, set a frequency, either by using the gui, or using the original way: right-clicking it with an item. empty hand = 0, other items = their item id. be careful not to reset it to 0 by accident. honestly, just use the gui. you can set it to private or not, it's the same kind of thing as enderstorage, so you don't blare rs across the server. channel state = rs level.

rt(o) sets the channel state based on the redstone level sent from outside to the specific side. you can tp an rs from this to the rr(o).
rt(i) sets the channel state based on redstone level that would be emitted from the machine itself. [warn]always sends 15, so it's useless.[/warn]
rr(o) outputs redstone level based on channel state. you can tp rs from the rt(o) to here.
rr(i) controls whether a machine can work based on channel state, just like a machine controller cover does. if it has 0 rs, it stays off. at least 1, and it turns on. you send the signal from elsewhere with the rt(o).
rr(i) can also be used in conjunction with other covers whose states talk about conditional.

ic2 heat vents: speeds up machines a tiny amount? also looks neat. todo: someone please look at the code to see what it actually does.

crafting table: adds a crafting table to the block you can use. mostly cosmetic.

planks/plates/foils: blocks i/o on that side. use a screwdriver to set allowed types of stuff through. blocks everything by default. set the output to another side first to avoid changing its settings too. you'll probably 'use' this by accident at least once.

computer monitor: adds a visual look. cosmetic-only cover.

lens: cosmetic-only cover.

you can also use ae2 facades as cosmetic covers. {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 20, "oredict": "", "id": "gregtech:gt.metatool.01", "tag": {"gt.toolstats": {"maxdamage": 51200, "primarymaterial": "steel", "secondarymaterial": "steel"}, "ench": {"0": {"id": 16, "lvl": 2}}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (gregtech:gt.metatool.01, metadata 20)"}}}}

name: Lootbag Uptiering
text:
lootbag uptiering in gtnh, the lootbags are quite useful tools for boosting your resources. there are a wide variety of lootbag types, and those types all have upgrade paths to get better resources.

there are two paths you can take when it comes to upgrading your lootbags, you can either enchant it with fortune, or you can upgrade the bag itself. enchanting the lootbag with fortune will increase the chances of more rare drops being given to you on opening, while upgrading the bag itself will change the item pool to that of the upgraded bag. notably, if you uptier the bag itself, it will cost 3 of the previous bag tier, so make sure it's worthwhile to upgrade before you do so!

if you're looking to maximize your advantage it's recommended you both uptier your lootbag and apply the fortune upgrade. 

[note]be sure to use nei to see all of this information. use 'u' on your lootbag and you will be able to see the potential drops, the drop chances based on fortune levels, and you will be able to see recipes for uptiering the bag.[/note] {"0": {"index": 0, "taskid": "bq_standard:checkbox"}} {}

name: Modular Meddling
text:
modular meddling interested in powerful, customizable armor that you can modify as you advance? look no further than &z&zmechanical armor!

in order to begin tinkering, you'll need a workspace for modifying modular equipment along with a set of mechanical armor. the armor is essentially useless on its own, but gains additional features through modification. each piece of armor is composed of three parts:

augments: augments add a wide variety of useful features to the armor. augments are categorized into one of three types: protection, movement, and utility. augments can only be inserted into slots corresponding to their category.

frames: the armor's frame determines the protection value of the armor along with how many slots it contains for augments.

name: Sometimes Life is Scary and Dark - Bring a Backpack
text:
sometimes life is scary and dark - bring a backpack now that you are mv, you can make an adventure backpack. this very useful backpack can do many things. it can store 2 tools for quick access, has internal tanks for containing liquids - use the hose to access them, a built-in crafting table, and storage.

when placed on your back, it can be accessed using the quick-access key; the default is b. check your controls for details.

when placed on the ground, it can be accessed with a right-click. while on the ground, the bedroll can be deployed and used.

they can also be upgraded to add special abilities. for a full list, visit [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/adventure_backpacks[/url].

[note]it uses up the same slot as the coal jetpack and the copterpack, so you'll either need to choose one, or swap them around.[/note] {"0": {"autoconsume": 0, "consume": 0, "groupdetect": 0, "ignorenbt": 1, "index": 0, "partialmatch": 1, "requireonlyoneitem": 0, "requireditems": {"0": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "adventurebackpack:blockbackpack", "tag": {"wearabledata": {}}, "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (adventurebackpack:blockbackpack, metadata 0)"}}, "taskid": "bq_standard:retrieval"}} {"0": {"ignoredisabled": 0, "index": 0, "rewardid": "bq_standard:item", "rewards": {"0": {"count": 64, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "harvestcraft:beefwellingtonitem", "resolved": {"id": "i:harvestcraft:beefwellingtonitem:0", "name": "beef wellington", "mod": "harvestcraft", "registry": "beefwellingtonitem", "icon": 47058, "nbt": null, "kind": "item", "unit": "items", "damage": 0, "shard": "308073bc491cf18b", "recipes": 1}, "label": "beef wellington"}, "1": {"count": 1, "damage": 0, "oredict": "", "id": "adventurebackpack:backpackhose", "resolved": null, "label": "unknown item (adventurebackpack:backpackhose, metadata 0)"}}}}
